title: Premierement.
text: roast a whole lamb, half spit-roasted, half barded. to prevent the belly side from cooking too quickly and burning, it must be barded all around with a large sheet of well-buttered white paper and tied neatly. a quarter of an hour before removing the meat from the spit, remove this protective covering that has shielded it from the initial heat. to finish cooking, don't forget first of all to place a piece of fresh butter, salt, and pepper inside the body, because lamb, being inherently bland, needs to be seasoned well. this seasoning will cook with it, moistening and penetrating it so that it absorbs all the flavor. also, baste it from time to time with the juices that emerge.

title: Agneau gras.
text: to make a fine tart with apples and spice take good butter, a pound, and beat it well with a quarter pound of powdered sugar until it is light and fluffy. then add four eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. sift in a pound of flour and a teaspoon of mace, mixing gently until just combined. roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface and line a tart pan. trim the edges neatly. for the filling, peel and core six large apples, such as cox or ribston. slice them thinly and arrange them in the tart shell. sprinkle with a quarter pound of powdered sugar, a teaspoon of ground cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. dot with a few knobs of butter. bake in a moderate oven until the crust is golden and the apples are tender, about 45-50 minutes. when cool, dust with powdered sugar and serve.

title: 1) Eine Citronen=Suppe.
text: take water and add breadcrumbs from milk bread to your liking into the water, and let it cook until the breadcrumbs are very soft and well-cooked. then add wine, as much as you like, a little whole cinnamon, a little whole nutmeg, and sweeten it with sugar, and let it cook a little more. if you want to serve it soon, grate the yellow zest of a lemon into it, let it come to a boil a few times, then stir it, and strain it through a sieve. when you want to serve it, add the yolks of 3 or 4 eggs.

title: 2) Eine Bier=Suppe zu machen.
text: one takes 1 measure of beer and lets it boil, then allows it to foam well, and adds a quarter pound of sweet butter. then one takes black bread and cuts it into small cubes, roasting it golden yellow in hot butter. one takes the yolks from 3 or 4 eggs and whisks them in a bowl with boiling beer. one can also add a few spoonfuls of cream. afterwards, one takes a little ground cloves and cinnamon, and then combines it all together in a bowl over the cubed bread.

title: 3) Eine Wein=Suppe zu machen.
text: first, combine half a measure of wine with a cup of water and bring to a boil. then, stir in a quarter pound of sweet butter, a little mace, and as much sugar as you like. next, cut milk bread into small cubes and toast them in butter until golden brown. in a bowl, whisk together the yolks of 3 or 4 eggs with a little boiling wine, and combine everything in a serving bowl. if desired, add a pinch of saffron.

title: 4) Eine braune Wein=Suppe zu machen.
text: make it as above, except instead of milk bread, use rye bread, grated on a grater and nicely toasted yellow in butter. also add a little sugar and cinnamon.

title: 5) Eine Kalbfleisch=Suppe zu machen.
text: take the calf's shins from the hindquarter, place them with cold water and a little salt, when it has foamed well, take 2 dry milk loaves, peel off the crust, and add the crumbs to the shins. then take celery, parsley root and onion, and add a few generous handfuls to the shins, until they are completely cooked, then strain them through a sieve, and add a little nutmeg and a little butter therein, and when you want to prepare it, take the yolks of 3 or 4 eggs and an equal number of spoonfuls of cream and stir them in you must also toast slices of milk loaf if you wish, you can make balls or dumplings from calf meat with a little kidney fat, milk loaf and a few eggs and a little cream mixed in, and cooked in water, and add them underneath.

title: 6) Eine gelbe Suppe zu machen.
text: take veal shank from the hindquarter, and put it in a pot with cold water and a little salt. when the shank is quickly cooked, take a bit of salted butter and melt it in another pot, adding a generous spoonful of flour and letting it toast slightly. then take some of the shank broth and add it to the flour, stirring the flour until smooth. when it has cooked a little, strain it and add it to the shank in the pot, and let it cook well. if you want to serve it quickly, take a little saffron, mix it with a bit of broth, and add it to the soup. then serve the soup over milk bread slices, with the shank placed at the bottom of the bowl, and the yolks of 3 or 4 eggs added as well.

title: 7) Eine Krebs=Suppe zu machen.
text: take half a hundred crabs, boil them until beautifully red. remove the tails, then put the shells from the tails along with anything else remaining from the crabs into a mortar and grind it very finely. take a quarter pound of butter and let it melt. once melted, add the ground crab. roast slowly, adding some meat broth, as well as crumbs from a dry milk bread. a little salt and mace can also be added. when this red broth or butter is well cooked, strain it through a fine sieve. when you want to serve it, add the yolks of 3 or 4 eggs along with a spoonful of cream. the bread must be toasted beforehand, and when it is served, place the peeled crab tails and the red butter on top.

title: 8) Eine Schoccolade=Suppe zu machen.
text: one and a half quarter pounds of flour are taken, and the same is put into a whole new pot and roasted dry until it looks brownish it must be stirred constantly so it doesn't burn. afterwards, one and a half measures of milk, which has been scalded, are added and when the flour is roasted, stir it with the milk. great care must be taken to ensure the flour doesn t form any lumps, but becomes perfectly smooth. then, it is placed back on the fire and allowed to cook well, adding cinnamon and sugar so that it is sweet enough. when it has cooked strongly, it is strained through a sieve, and the yolks of 4 or 5 eggs are stirred in. the soup must be as thick as chocolate.

title: 9) Eine Reiß=Suppe zu kochen.
text: take rice as you wish, add water and salt to it, and when it has been cooked for about an hour, take half a hundred crabs. cook them in water, then crush them finely in a mortar, and melt a quarter pound of fresh butter. afterwards, add meat broth and let it simmer, then strain it through a sieve and pour the strained broth into the rice, allowing it to cook well. the red crab butter must be skimmed off beforehand, then the rice is put through a sieve, and when it is prepared, the crab butter is poured over the soup. you must also cook some mace flowers with the soup.

title: 10) Eine Rüben=Suppe zu machen.
text: one takes white turnips, the same cut into cubes and washed clean, then one lets butter heat up, the turnips are thrown in and roasted very slowly until they are nicely yellow, then one adds meat broth and lets it cook well. one can also use goose fat instead of butter and roast the turnips in it, which gives the soup a good flavor. also, one can roast a duck and add it to the soup a moment before serving, then arrange it and place the duck in the bowl. one must also roast slices of milk bread in the soup. if one wants to make the soup really good and hearty, one takes 1 or 2 pounds of beef, depending on how much or little soup, cuts it into thin pieces, doesn't wash it, but beats it well, puts it in a pot with a little butter, and a whole onion, and a few crushed cloves, and lets it simmer slowly

title: 11) Eine braune Suppe zu machen.
text: you take 5 pounds of beef from a piece suitable for pies, cut into thin slices and well pounded. from this, you take about a quarter pound and scrape it with a knife, removing the skin and sinew. the scraped meat is set aside. the sinew, skin, and the remaining pounded beef are placed in warm salted or fresh butter, along with a whole onion and a few crushed cloves, and allowed to simmer over the fire. as soon as it has a little broth, you pour it into another pot, and add water or meat broth to the meat, allowing it to simmer again until you have drawn off approximately 1 measure of these ingredients. then, add meat broth to the extracted meat, and add celery, onion, and various spices, straining it into the broth so that the meat comes out. you can also add the spices to the broth first. when the soup has simmered, add sweetbreads and thymus, cooking them well and adding them to the

title: 12) Eine gute Milch=Suppe zu machen.
text: take milk, as much as you like, when it is boiled, then for 1 measure, take the yolks from 3 or 4 eggs and stir them in. add a measure less than 1 kronesworth of rosewater and as much sugar as needed, and cut slices of milk bread into it.

title: 13) Eine Kerbel=Suppe zu machen.
text: take parsley, pick it over and wash it well, then chop it. roast it in a little fresh butter, and as soon as it is well roasted, pour meat broth over it. then add the crumbs from 2 milk loaves and let them cook until the milk bread is completely smooth. when serving, add 3 or 4 egg yolks along with an equal number of spoonfuls of cream, stir it, and add a little nutmeg and salt. if desired, you can chop an onion with the parsley, and if you don't have milk bread, you can also roast a little white flour with the parsley.

title:
14) Eine kalte Milch=Suppe oder
Eyer=Milch zu machen.
text: take milk, as much as you like, and let it boil. then, measure out milk, 4 eggs, beat them well, and gradually pour in the boiling milk and 1 spoonful of rosewater. set it aside and let it cool, then add pieces of milk bread.

title:
15) Eine grüne Suppe zu machen, wie 
es die Jahreszeit mit sich bringet.
text: when sorrel, burdock, or other tender herbs are available, sauté them in a little butter or meat broth fat. then pour meat broth over them and let it cook well, adding 3 or 4 egg yolks and an equal amount of cream. if it is lamb's lettuce or asparagus spears, they must first be blanched and then thrown into the hot meat broth. a little salt and nutmeg should not be forgotten. if it is herbs, they must first be finely chopped and then pieces of milk bread added.

title: 16) Eine Kirschen=Suppe zu machen.
text: to begin, take sour cherries or sweet cherries, leaving the pits in or removing them. simmer them in a little fresh butter. add one part wine and three parts water, and stir it in. add sugar and a little whole cinnamon until it is sweet enough, and let it cook well together. when serving, crumble toasted milk bread into it but the cinnamon must be removed. if you don't like to simmer the cherries, you can add them directly to the wine.

title: 17) Eyer=Gerst=Suppe zu machen.
text: make meat broth boil, grate 2 or 3 crusts of stale bread into it and let them cook well, add a little salt and a piece of butter. when it is to be prepared, add the yolks of 3 or 4 eggs.

title: 18) Eine Wasser=Suppe zu machen.
text: cut 3 to 4 slices of milk bread into a bowl, place it in a frying pan, and pour boiling water over it to soften the bread. then, beat 5 to 6 eggs on top with a little salt. pour a bit more boiling water over, add butter, and sprinkle a little flour on top. it is then ready.

title:
19) Eine Lerchen= oder 
Krammets=Vögel=Suppe zu machen.
text: take larks or bramblings. when roasted, pound them very finely in a mortar and then brown them in butter. when they are slightly roasted, add meat broth and let it cook well. strain it and arrange it, and add the yolks of some eggs, along with several spoonfuls of cream. macaroon recipe in a cream broth. take 1 pound of almonds, pound them finely. add rosewater, 3 grated slices of milk bread, a spoonful of sugar, 3 eggs, and the grated yellow zest of a lemon, and mix everything well together. bake them in clarified butter.

title: Die Brühe dazu.
text: take half a measure of cream, half a spoonful of sugar, a little rosewater, and the yolks of 5 eggs stir all of this over the heat for as long as it takes to boil, then pour it into a bowl and place the macarons inside. for decoration, you can also stick powdered sugar on top.

title: 2) Einen Spannischen Brey zu kochen.
text: take a pound and a half of milk, a quarter pound of rice flour, along with the yolks of 8 eggs, a quarter pound of sugar, and a small amount of rosewater. beat the eggs with a little milk, then mix in the rice flour and sugar. afterwards, cook and stir diligently until it is thick enough.

title:
3) Einen guten Mandel=Brey zu
verfertigen.
text: take three cups of milk, a pound and a half of almonds, finely ground, a quarter pound of rice flour, the yolks of four eggs, a farthing of rosewater, and sugar as much as you like, and one cup of milk with which to mix the almonds, rice flour, and rosewater. then let the milk simmer in a pot, and stir the almonds gradually into the hot milk, and let it cook like baby s porridge. when it is cooked, add a little butter and let it come to a boil once more, and it is ready.

title: 4) Einen Buteng zu machen.
text: take the crumbs from eight dry milk loaves, soak them in water, then press them hard. take a quarter pound of fresh butter and stir the crumbs gently with it. then add seven eggs, a generous cup of cream, half a pound of small raisins, a farthing of rosewater, the yellow zest of a lemon, grated, and a little sugar, well mixed together. pour into a mold and place in a pot of boiling water, cook for 2 hours. afterwards, remove from the mold and pour the broth over it. for decoration, you can place sliced almonds on top.

title: Brühe von Rahm zum Buteng.
text: take half a measure of cream and, to your liking, sugar until it is sweet enough, along with the yolks of 5 eggs and a little rosewater, all stirred together over the heat until it boils.

title: Eine rothe Brühe dazu.
text: take two good handfuls of cranberries, and a few cherries, and cook them in water. when they have cooked for about half an hour, add a little wine and sugar until it is sweet enough, then cook well until it is quite thick and smooth. pour it over butter. you can also add a little raspberry or cherry juice instead of white wine, or use red or cherry wine, which will give it a beautiful color. you can also add a little cinnamon.

title:
5) Auf eine andere Art einen Buteng 
zu machen.
text: grate the crusts from 5 loaves of milk bread. combine with about one cup of cream that is not too thick, stirring until the grated bread is well blended. add a quarter pound of ox-cheek meat, allowing it to melt completely, then grate the zest of a lemon over the mixture. add 10 ounces of sugar and a quarter pound of small raisins that have been sautéed in fresh butter, and 7 whole eggs. stir everything together thoroughly. grease a mold or cloth with butter and cook in boiling water for 2 hours, maintaining a steady simmer.

title: Eine Brühe dazu.
text: take the yolks from 4 eggs, a spoonful of finely sifted flour, well stirred, a cup of wine and half a cup of cream, a quarter pound of large raisins, a quarter of sugar, a piece of whole cinnamon, stir this constantly over the charcoal fire, and when it begins to boil, remove it from the heat and arrange it over the pork loin. for decoration, you can stick elongated sliced almonds on top.

title: Noch eine Brühe dazu.
text: take half a measure of cream, and sugar until it is sweet enough, along with the yolks of 5 eggs and a little rosewater. stir all of this over the fire until it boils, and then serve over butter.

title: 6) Einen Nieren=Buteng zu machen.
text: take the kidneys of a roast calf, along with a little meat, and chop them finely. take 2 milk loaves, peel them, and soak them in milk, pressing them out firmly, and add them to the kidneys. take 6 eggs, a little spice and salt, and a quarter pound of small raisins, well washed and added as well. then take the cloth or mold in which you want to cook it, grease it with butter and put the filling inside. place it in a pot of boiling water and let it cook for two hours, and it is good.

title: Die Brühe dazu.
text: bring broth to a gentle simmer and add stale bread, allowing it to soften. add a little wine, lemon slices, salt, and spices. when serving, take the yolks from 2 or 3 eggs and a little cream, and pour over the top.

title: 7) Einen Schüsselfladen zu machen.
text: take 12 eggs, beat them well, add a measure of milk, and a farthing of rosewater. pour all of this into a tin bowl, and place a pastry lid on top. cook over a low heat from below and above, but do not let it boil at first, or it will collapse.

title:
8) Einen Citronen=Schaum zu 
machen.
text: take 14 eggs with the wise, whisk them well in a bowl, then rub the yellow zest from 4 lemon peels and add it. from the 4 lemons, press out the juice and add that as well the lemons must be juicy. afterward, add half a measure of wine, 1 pound of sugar. stir all of this well and strain it into a new pot. place the pot over the fire or a charcoal pan, take a twig from a new broom and use it to beat the mixture in the pot until it thickens and rises. you can test it with a drop on the back of your hand when it's quite hot, it s ready, but it must not boil, and it must be constantly whipped, otherwise it will clump together. if you don t like it too sweet, you can save a quarter pound of sugar it s sweet enough even then. this portion yields two large bowls full.

title: 9) Crembule zu machen.
text: begin with 4 loth of fine flour, carefully weighed, 6 egg yolks, measured precisely with a maas of milk, and stirred together. grate the yellow zest of a lemon and add it, as well as a small piece of whole cinnamon. then place it over the fire and stir constantly. when it has boiled up with a few bubbles, strain it through a sieve into a bowl, where it should remain as it cools. if you want to bring it to the table quickly, put the fire shovel into the fire until it is completely glowing. sprinkle a little sugar over the cream, and then press the glowing shovel over the entire cream so that the sugar turns brownish.

title:
10) Junge Hühner mit Auskern=Erbsen
zu machen.
text: first, cook the chickens until thoroughly done, then melt butter and add shelled peas, sautéing them well. next, add meat broth, grated milk bread, salt, and mace, and let it simmer gently until tender. then, cook the crabs until done, remove the noses, peel the tails so the crabs remain intact, and add them as well. take the noses, tails, and shells, pound them, and lightly toast in butter. pour a little meat broth over them and let it cook. then, take the crab butter from the top, strain the remaining liquid, and pour it over the peas. when serving, add three egg yolks and a few spoonfuls of cream, and place the red crab butter on top. serve immediately you can also add it briefly to the broth.

title:
11) Hühner mit Stof=Salat zu 
machen.
text: boil the chickens alone. the stock salad is stirred and pressed hard. take meat broth and cook bread gently in it. afterward, add a little salt and seasoning, then the stock salad as well, and cook thoroughly. when you want to serve it, take some egg yolks and a few spoonfuls of cream, and arrange them over the chicken.

title: 12) Gebacken Weißkraut.
text: chop about 2 heads of white cabbage very finely and sauté in butter. afterwards, take 2 heads of milk bread, soaked in water and pressed hard, 6 eggs, 6 spoonfuls of cream, a little seasoning, and salt, and mix well together. grease a tin bowl with fresh butter, scrape the crust off the milk bread and sprinkle it on top. then place the bowls on a cabbage pan, put a pie lid on top, and apply heat above and below until it looks like a sugar glaze.

title: 13) Gekochter Blumenkohl.
text: once the cauliflower is cleaned and washed, cook it in water and salt until tender. then, make a broth over it, stir in grated bread flour until it dissolves in meat broth, and add a little salt and cauliflower when serving. add the yolks of 2 or 3 eggs and several spoonfuls of cream on top.

title: 14) Boeuf a la mode zu machen.
text: you take the pastry piece, split it in half, beat it well so it becomes tender, then prick it through and through with a finger's thickness of bacon, which has previously been mixed with finely chopped parsley, and a little spice blend. if you wish, you can let it sit in vinegar for several days, then place it in a small pot, add a little water, crushed cloves, a little salt, a few onions, a whole stalk of celery, a piece of black bread, and a few bay leaves. then let it simmer slowly over the fire. if you wish, you can place it on warm ashes or a few coals the evening before and let it sit overnight this will make it even more tender. when it is well-cooked and the meat is tender, remove it. skim the fat from the broth, strain the broth through a sieve. then take a spoonful of flour, toast it with the skimmed fat until lightly browned, then add a little

title:
15) Gehackt Kalbfleisch mit 
Limonen.
text: take a piece of veal from the rear quarter. peel the skin from the thick meat, then chop it finely along with a lemon. add water and salt, and let it cook well. once it is properly cooked, add a little wine and seasoning. if there is too much water, pour some off. when it begins to simmer again, just before serving, stir in 2 to 3 egg yolks and several spoonfuls of cream.

title:
16) Einen guten Eyerkäs zu 
verfertigen.
text: to make it, take 12 eggs, beat them with a wooden spoon until they become frothy, then gradually add a measure of milk, along with a small coin s worth of rosewater. pour this into a tall pot, roughly 2 measures in size. then take the pot and place it in a kettle or another pot of boiling water, but be careful to prevent any water from leaking in. when the milk and eggs are firm, take them out with a large tin spoon and pour them into earthenware egg molds. let them stand until the next day. afterward, loosen them in a bowl and pour cream over them, a little thick but still sweet. you can also add sugar to the cream if you wish, or each person can add it to their plate if they prefer it sweet. the cream should not be poured over the cheese, but rather alongside it then it is ready.

title:
17) Eine gelbe Brühe, kalt zu 
essen.
text: take half a measure of good wine. and 18 egg yolks, beaten very small. once this is done, pour half a measure of wine over it, a quarter of a cup of vinegar, and peeled pine nuts, as much sugar as is needed to make it sweet. then put it on the fire and stir constantly until it boils. after that, set it aside. you can put half the sugar on the fire with it, and when it's done, add the other half with candied citron. you can put in young welsh chickens or veal, which must all be well-cooked and cut into portions before pouring the broth over it. the meat must be well drained so that no broth remains on it, otherwise the pastry broth will be spoiled.

title: 18) Gestoft Kalbfleisch zu machen.
text: cut the veal into pieces and let it sit in vinegar for a day. then, brown it nicely in butter. after that, toast a spoonful of flour in the butter until quite brown, then add water, bay leaves, a few slices of lemon, a little spice, and a little vinegar. let this cook with the meat. when it's ready to serve, add a little sugar to make it taste sweet.

title:
19) Eine frische Rindszung zu 
kochen.
text: take the tongue and cook it thoroughly in water and salt, then drain it. split it in half lengthwise, make a broth over it, roast a spoonful of flour in butter, then add meat broth, a glass of wine, a handful of small raisins, a little whole cinnamon and sugar until it is sweet enough, a little peeled almonds, whole or sliced lengthwise. let all of this cook well and serve over the tongue. for decoration, you can place sliced almonds on top.

title:
20) Ein Spanferkel weiß zu 
sieden.
text: take the young pig, cut off the head, and cut the rest into pieces. place it in cold water as soon as possible. once cooked, transfer it to a pot of cold water, rinse it clean, and place it in salt water, where you can keep it for several days. however, it must be eaten cold and must have vinegar on it.

title: 22) [>21)] Gelbe Glösger in einer Brüh.
text: take half a pound of raw veal, a quarter pound of kidney fat, dried milk bread, the crumbs of which must be pressed hard in water, take a few eggs, 2 tablespoons of cream, a little spice, and salt, along with a little dried saffron, which must be finely ground, then mix everything together, and make gloezers from it, which are stirred with water, a little thicker than in a soup, and then cook them in water until thoroughly done. then take the crumbs of a milk bread and simmer them in meat broth, then pass through a sieve, and add a few slices of lemon, wine, mace, and a little saffron, let it cook well with them. when they are to be served, place the gloezers in a little, and add them covered with a few egg yolks and a few tablespoons of cream.

title:
22) Eine gute Scheele oder Galera 
zu machen.
text: take 6 veal shanks, or as many as your portion requires you can also add some pork shanks. place them in water and let them cook well until you see the shanks detaching from the bones. then, transfer the broth to a large, foot-shaped pot. add a piece of veal shoulder that has been previously soaked in vinegar, and make sure it is well-seasoned with salt. once the meat is in the broth, add a few whole cloves, a little whole pepper, some mace flowers, 4 or 5 bay leaves, and a few whole onions. let it cook well. if the broth becomes too short, add water. when the meat is cooked through, remove it and place it in a tinned pâté mold. continue cooking the broth, adding a few slices of lemon. be careful not to overcook the lemon slices. if it's not sour enough, add a little vinegar and salt. once this is done,

title:
23) Einen wilden Schweinskopf 
zu machen.
text: take the head and let the hairs be singed off until it is completely black. afterwards, place it in water and soak it for a night, then scrape it clean and pull out the tongue. at the front of the trunk, cut a cross and carefully peel the skin so that it doesn't burst during cooking. then, where the tongue comes out, insert thinly sliced onions, crushed juniper berries, and 2 or 3 handfuls of salt. place the head in a tall pot and sprinkle it generously with the aforementioned herbs, onions, and fine spices. cook it for at least 4 hours in a mixture of one part wine, one part vinegar, and one part water. allow it to cool, gild the ears and trunk, and eat it cold with vinegar.

title:
24) Einen Kalbskopf mit einer 
Butter=Brüh.
text: wash the head very clean and split it in two, place it with water and salt and cook it thoroughly. afterward, take salted or fresh butter, a good amount, and put it in a pot with 1 spoonful of flour, along with the yolks of 4 or 5 eggs, a little meat broth, and a little vinegar, and stir it over the fire. when you want to serve it, cut milk bread into cubes and toast it brown in butter and sprinkle it over the head, then pour the broth over it.

title: 25) Ein Kalbsgrös zu kochen.
text: once the veal is thoroughly cleaned, put it in a pot or cauldron. add several handfuls of salt and rub it in well, then wash it clean. afterwards, place it with water and salt and let it cook. when it has properly foamed, take the crusts from a milk bread and add a little flour, letting it cook completely. when you want to prepare it, add the yolks from three or four eggs and several spoonfuls of cream. you can also add a little nutmeg.

title: 26) Einen Leberkuchen zu machen.
text: take a calf s liver, chop it finely, having removed the sinew. soak breadcrumbs from three or four milk loaves in water until hard, add 8 eggs, a half pound of small raisins, three-quarters of a pound of rendered kidney fat, six spoonfuls of cream, a little nutmeg, and salt. mix all together well and bake in clarified butter.

title: 27) Gebackene junge Hühner.
text: clean the chickens thoroughly, remove the head and neck, and cut the remainder into four or more pieces. dry them well in a cloth so they are not too wet. then sprinkle with a little salt, coat them in flour, and bake in melted butter. make a butter broth to serve over them.

title:
28) Capaunen in einer 
Austern=Brühe.
text: clean the oysters well of their beards and brown them in fresh butter. then take a large pinch of flour, a little salt and mace, and pour in meat broth, allowing it to cook well, then straining it. if you want to serve it quickly, put the oysters in and let them come to a boil, then stir in the yolks of three or four eggs along with lemon juice. the broth must be well thickened. the capon is roasted, and the broth is served over it.

title: 29) Gefüllte Kohlraben.
text: take the brussels sprouts, not too large, peel them and boil them in water until very tender. hollow them out on the side where they are greenest, make a filling. take the crumbs of a milk bread, squeeze them well in water, take two spoonsful of cream, two eggs, a little salt and nut, together with the scooped-out portion from the brussels sprouts. mix these ingredients well, and fry in butter, then stuff them into the brussels sprouts, and make a broth, namely, cook bread crumbs in meat broth, a little salt and spices added, and simmer the brussels sprouts in it for a moment when you want to serve them, add a few spoonfuls of cream and the yolks of some eggs. one can prepare turnips in the same way.

title: 30) Gute Weck=Klös.
text: take fresh butter as much as an egg, and beat it until foamy. then take the yolks of 2 eggs, a little mace, and salt, gently rubbed in, and as much wheat flour as you need for a pastry crust instead of wheat flour, you can use white flour, it's both agreeable.

title: 31) Eine Fricasee zu machen.
text: take young chickens, wash them clean, then cut off the necks and the rest into quarters. brown them in butter with a pinch of flour. if you want to serve them quickly, take a piece of butter, the yolks of four or five eggs, and a few spoonfuls of cream, a generous amount of lemon juice, and a little chopped parsley. if you lack lemon juice, you can use a little vinegar, then add the broth from the chickens as well, and stir this over the fire until it boils, then pour it over the chickens. when browning, you can also add a little whole parsley, a whole onion, and a few whole cloves, then remove them again afterward. you can also proceed in this way with pigeons and veal.

title: 32) Einen weissen Ragou.
text: take bread soaked in milk, cook it very gently in meat broth. then pass it through a sieve, and add a few slices of lemon, a little mace, peeled ox tongue, boiled crayfish, and if you have them, calf's milk as well, but these must first be boiled in a little salted water until they turn white. next, prepare the dumplings in clean, boiling water. when they are cooked, add them to the ragout. when serving, add the yolks of a few eggs and a few spoonfuls of cream. this ragout can be served with old or young chicken, capons, a welsh chicken, veal, ox tongue, and pigeons.

title: Braune Ragou.
text: roast one or two ducks on a spit. afterward, take salted butter, toast a spoonful of flour in it until very dark brown, then add water, a little wine or vinegar, and some slices of lemon. let it simmer well you can also add ox throat, sweetbreads, mushrooms, tripe, and capers if you want to serve it quickly. when you want to serve it, place the duck in the broth to warm it, as you can roast it beforehand if you wish. also make dumplings from veal, bake them brown in melted butter, and if you want to make the ragout really good, add the strained gravy or broth from beef, as you would for a brown soup, which will make it quite rich. if you don't add gravy, you must add a little pepper and salt. you can use tame or wild pigeons, veal, or a lamb roast instead of the ducks.

title: Klösger zu obigen.
text: take as much ox kidney fat as veal, finely chopped, with the skin removed. then take crumbs from a stale milk bread, soak them in water, and squeeze them dry. chop them with the veal, a few eggs, a few spoonfuls of cream, a little salt, and mace. form into small dumplings and bake in rendered butter.

title: 1) Wildpret zu braten.
text: to begin, one takes a deer, skins it well, and soaks it in vinegar for several days. then one skews it and covers it with boiling vinegar or wine, according to how one likes it sour. afterwards, one melts butter and drizzles it over the roast, continuing until it is cooked through. one arranges it nicely, decorates it with sliced lemon rounds, and puts the sauce from that into a separate dish. in this manner, one can also prepare a hindquarter from venison.

title: 2) Eine wilde Ente zu braten.
text: one takes a wild duck, cleans it thoroughly, draws it, and dresses it nicely, then pours boiling wine over it, skewers it, and lets butter melt and bastes it with it until it is cooked then one sets it upright, and the sauce is served separately. in the same manner, one can prepare partridges and pheasants.

title: 3) Einen welschen Hahn zu braten.
text: one takes a foreign goose, cleans it, draws it, washes it, and rubs it well with pepper and salt. then it is trussed, and the same is stuffed, allowing butter to melt, basting it occasionally until it is cooked. then one arranges it on a dish, garnishes it with lemon slices. in this manner, young chickens are also prepared.

title: 4) Einen Kalbskeul zu braten.
text: one takes a fine veal shank, seasons it with salt, then places it on a spit. add some water to the pan, sprinkle salt over it, let butter melt, and baste the roast with it frequently until it is cooked through. then arrange it on a platter.

title: 5) Eine Kalbsbrust zu füllen.
text: one takes a veal lung, when cooked, and chops it finely with a milk bread. then, one adds a little parsley, 4 or 5 eggs, some cream, seasoning, and a little salt. all of this is roasted over the fire with butter, and then sliced veal breast is filled with it and sewn up, and roasted on a spit.

title: 6) Einen Rindsbraten zu braten.
text: take a nice piece of beef from the hindquarter, skewer it and roast it. if you don t want to skewer it, you can make a sauce of sardines or shallots. the sardines must be washed clean, the innards removed, then well crushed. roast a little flour and add some of this sauce, stirring in the sardines as well. if you want to make the sauce of shallots, you must also finely chop them and soften them in butter. then, apply the sauce to the roast.

title: 7) Einen Hammelskolben zu braten.
text: take a sheep's knuckle, pound it well, then put it in a pot, add a generous half measure of water, and salt. let it cook until it browns in its own juices. if desired, you can add wine, or you can stud it with shallots. when it is nicely browned, arrange it on a platter.

title: 8) Ein gut Spanferkel zu braten.
text: one takes a fine suckling pig. once it is prepared, one puts it in a trough, sprinkles it on both sides with a little pitch. then one takes boiling water and pours it over it gradually until the hair comes off easily. when it is thoroughly cleaned, one takes it out, washes it well in water and lets it drain properly. then one takes pepper and salt and rubs it well inside, cleans it well, and then skewers it. one coats it with bacon fat or butter and lets it roast. one must pay close attention to the fire, otherwise it will blister. when it is done and nicely crisp, one serves it.

title: 9) Gefüllte Tauben zu braten.
text: melt butter in a pan over heat. then take the crumbs from a milk loaf, press them hard in water, and add them to the hot butter. add 4 eggs with their yolks, a little parsley, salt, and seasoning, and as much cream as eggs. place this mixture over the heat and let it dry slightly. then fill the pigeon carcasses and roast them in a pot or on a spit. if you wish to make them in a ragout, simmer them after they are filled, and make a broth for the ragout as you normally would.

title: 1) Eine Mandel=Torte.
text: take one pound of almonds, three-quarters of a pound of sugar, and the rinds of two lemons, which are grated into the almonds. use 18 eggs, but only the whites from 9 eggs the eggs must be well beaten, as must the almonds with the sugar. afterward, combine them and stir well until bubbles form. add 4 spoonfuls of cinnamon water, and then bake in a cake pan or a special tin form.

title: 2) Eine Zungen=Torte.
text: take a beef tongue, a half pound. mark, a quarter pound of pine nuts, a glass of wine, a good spoonful of sugar, a quarter pound of small raisins, 2 or 3 eggs, a little cinnamon, a quarter of candied citron. mix all these together, cook the tongue thoroughly and chop it finely, then add it to the dough and bake.

title: 3) Eine Brod=Mandel=Torte.
text: take 12 loth almonds, a half pound of sugar, a half quarter of cinnamon, 8 loth grated black bread, mostly crust, then a little ground cloves, mace flowers, 8 whole eggs, and a little rosewater. mix all of this well together, then put the dough into the tart pan, add the filling, and bake. it must not have a lid.

title: 4) Rahm=Törtger zu machen.
text: make a dough with as much flour as butter, then add enough cream to fill a mug, and 3 eggs, and a spoonful of rosewater. beat the eggs well and pour in the cream and rosewater. this makes 8 tarts. you need a quarter pound of butter and a quarter pound of flour for the dough.

title: 5) Marck=Törtger.
text: take half a pound of almonds, grind them with rosewater. then, take a quarter pound of ox marrow, melt it, and pour it over the almonds. add 4 eggs, separating 2 egg whites, a quarter pound of finely ground sugar, and the grated yellow zest of one lemon. combine all of these ingredients and pour them into the dough in the tart pan and bake. this yields 8 tartlets.

title: 6) Nieren=Torten zu machen.
text: make a good dough with as much flour as butter. afterward, take veal kidneys and a little meat from roast, chop these very finely. then add a milk roll to the water, press it dry and add it. add a little wine, cream, small raisins, and a little sugar, stir everything well together, and pour it over the dough. put a lid on it and bake.

title: Man kan sie auch sauer machen.
text: take capers, finely chopped, and add a little vinegar. if you don't have kidneys, you can also make it with cooked beef or veal, but you must add ox marrow.

title: 7) Eine gute Eyer=Torte.
text: take 1 pound of almonds, when ground with a little rosewater, add 3 4 pound of sugar, 16 hard-boiled egg yolks removed and finely chopped, the yellow zest of one citron, 10 loth of fresh butter well washed, made warm throughout, and then thoroughly beaten like a cream. when these are well combined, beat the whites of 2 eggs into a foam and stir that in as well, then pour into the dough and bake. there should be no lid, and the top crust should look like sugar blossoms.

title: 8) Eine Rahm=Torten.
text: take one and a half pints of cream, the crumbs of 3 milk loaves, 2 pounds of almonds finely ground with a little rosewater, 10 whole eggs, the grated zest of a lemon, and a little cinnamon and sugar to taste, ensuring it is sweet enough. the milk loaves must be weighed in water, thoroughly pressed and gently mixed, then the cream poured in underneath, the eggs beaten in gradually and well mixed with the above, poured into the dough and baked. there should be no lid on top and it must look like a sugar pastry.

title: 9) Eine Kerbel=Torten.
text: take 3 loaves of milk bread and crumble the crusts. soak them in water and press them firmly. then, take 8 whole eggs, half a measure of cream, a little cinnamon, a pound of small raisins, a quarter cup of rosewater, sugar to taste, and a generous portion of finely chopped parsley. sauté the parsley with the raisins in fresh butter until it releases from the pan. combine everything and bake.

title: 10) Eine Citronen=Torte.
text: take 8 fine lemons, grate the yellow peel from them, then take a good handful of almonds, peel these and crush them finely, peel 2 or 3 apples and chop them small, and mix the almonds and apples with sugar and cinnamon. let the peeled yellow peel from the lemons cook briefly in water. cut the remaining lemons thinly into long strips, and place these in a bowl, sprinkling generously with sugar so that the sugar draws out the juice. afterwards, make a puff pastry, place the pastry in a pan, and spread the mixed apples and almonds evenly on the bottom. add a quarter pound of candied lemon peel, thinly sliced, over the almonds, then arrange the lemon strips next to each other on the candied peel. sprinkle generously with sugar, and on top of the sugar, the yellow peel and more sugar. cover with a lid and bake. you will need 2 pounds of sugar for this, and if it is not too sweet, it must be baked quickly.

title: 11) Eine Brod=Torte.
text: take 1 lot of black bread crumbs, one and a half lots of semolina, three-quarters of a pound of sugar, and one and a half quarter lots of almonds, which must be ground with rosewater. add 11 eggs and a grated nutmeg, and some cloves. mix well for an hour and then bake.

title: 12) Eine Aepfel=Torte.
text: take good cooking apples or cabbage apples, peel them and cut them into quarters, removing the cores, then slice them thinly. add sugar to taste, a little grated cinnamon, and if you wish, you can add small raisins. when making the tart, layer the apples, then sugar, cinnamon, grated lemon peel, and small raisins. repeat the layers of apples and the other ingredients until the tart reaches the edges of the pan. you can also add the juice from the grated lemon. then, place a lid on top and bake.

title: 13) Eine Kirschen=Torte.
text: you take 6 or 7 pounds of sour cherries, put them into a pan, and remove the pits. then, for one pound of cherries, use half a pound of sugar. if you want to make them really good, use three-quarters of a pound of sugar per pound of cherries. put the sugar into a clean pot with a little water and let it simmer gently. then add the cherries along with their juice and let it simmer slowly. afterwards, remove the cherries into a bowl and sprinkle a few almonds onto the bottom of the tart pan. then add the cherries, and you can add a little ground cinnamon. then put a lid on top. note. currant, raspberry, and monastery berry tarts are made in the same way.

title: 14) Eine Apricosen=Torte.
text: one takes apricots, separates them, and removes the kernels. they should weigh one pound of apricots and three-quarters of a pound of sugar. put the sugar into a clean pot and let it cook slowly with water. afterward, clarify it with egg white, then cook the apricots very slowly. when the juice has thickened, gently remove the apricots so they remain whole. once cold, place them in a tart pan. you can also crush the kernels with a little peeled almonds and rosewater and sprinkle them on the bottom. if you fear the juice might penetrate too strongly, you can add a little biscuit to the kernels and almonds, which can be done with all fruit tarts. afterward, place a lid on top. in this way, one makes a tart with mirabelles, peaches, and quinces.

title: 15) Einen guten Raton.
text: take half a pound of butter, gently mixed with the yolks of 9 eggs. from those nine eggs, take only the whites, and from three more eggs, add the yolks and whites to the whites and beat into a foam, then add a little sugar and rosewater, a few spoonfuls of yeast mixed with a cup of milk. afterwards, slowly stir in a pound and a half of flour, beating well, and fill into a prepared form. the form must be well greased with butter, and sprinkle a quarter pound of ground almonds at the bottom, then bake slowly.

title: 16) Eine Brunellen=Torte.
text: make a good dough, then cook small raisins, sugar, cinnamon, and lemon peel in a little water until dry. spread ground almonds on the bottom, then layer with candied citrus peel, sugar, and cinnamon. cover with a lid.

title: Schales zu machen.
text: take a quarter pound of candied orange peel, a quarter pound of citron, three-quarters of a pound of almonds, 12 ounces of sugar, one egg, a generous pat of foreign butter, a spoonful of fine flour. cut the orange peel into two parts, one half finely chopped and the other half cut into pieces, and do the same with the citron. grind the almonds, but not too finely. then mix everything together well, grease the bottom of a tart pan with fresh butter, and sprinkle with a little breadcrumbs. spread the mixed ingredients on top as thickly as possible, then arrange the lengthwise-cut orange peel and citron, as well as the whole almonds, on top. brush with egg white and sprinkle with a little sugar, and bake. it must be baked with heat from above, and it should look a fine yellow color.

title: 1) Eine gute warme Pastete.
text: take half a pound of sweet butter, wash it clean, take a tail or pie crust piece, beat it well and roast it on the grate, afterwards skewer it and lay it in vinegar, add bay leaves, golden onions and all sorts of spices and let the meat lie in the vinegar for eight days, afterwards prepare the dough and lay the meat in it with golden onions, anchovies and lemons, chop it all finely and sprinkle it over the meat, put the lid on and brush it with egg yolk, and bake it but the meat together with its accompaniments must be cooked the day before.

title:
2) Den blätterichten Teig zu obiger
Pastete.
text: take a pound of flour, a pound of butter. half of the flour is mixed with a half cup of water and some salt. as it's mixed, it is kneaded. then take the butter, place it on the dough, knead again, and add more butter, and so knead until the whole pound of butter along with the flour is worked into the dough. then form the dough.

title: 3) Eine Olopoterie=Pastete.
text: take chickens, cut off their necks, quarter them, and brown them in butter. afterwards, add maccaroni, mushrooms, and ox tongue everything must be previously boiled. then make dumplings, which must be made from veal, and from the filling, one makes crab noses and boils them in water, as well as adding boiled crabs and water frogs.

title: 4) Einen krachenden Teig.
text: take measured sugar and as much flour as the whites of several eggs, depending on whether you want to make a lot or little dough, and add a drop of orange blossom water. knead the dough thoroughly and prepare it well, but so that it is not too soft. make a crust from it as thin as paper, if possible, but always dust it with flour underneath and rub it around with your hand. this dough will almost stretch by itself after you have rolled it out a few times with a rolling pin. grease a plate or tart pan lightly with butter, place the stretched dough inside, trim it around the edges, and prick it here and there with the tip of a knife so that it does not puff up in the oven. let it dry in the oven, and when it is baked, place it in a bowl or plate and just before serving, add some jam of your choice, such as apricot, peach, lemon, or preserved fruit. from this dough, you can prepare

title:
5) Mandel=Teig zu Torten und
kleinen Boden.
text: combine the previously described dry almond dough in a mortar with good fresh butter, finely chopped lemon zest, some preserves, a little sugar, and the yolks of four or five raw eggs. mix well. on meat days, you can add beef marrow this dough is used for large and small cakes.

title: 6) Nägelein=Pastetger.
text: take a pound of flour, half a pound of sugar, eight eggs, half an ounce of cloves, stirred for a small hour, the form half full, and baked.

title: 1) Karpfen mit einer braunen Brühe.
text: clean the carp thoroughly, cut it into 4 or 6 pieces. when cutting, save the blood and wash the fish well inside with vinegar. pour the bloody vinegar over the blood. then take flour or stale bread, grate it and toast it in butter until it turns light brown. add water, a whole onion, bay leaves, a few slices of lemon, and a little ground cloves, and salt. let the blood and vinegar cook well until the broth thickens. then add the cut carp and cook until it is done it must look nicely browned.

title: 2) Karpfen mit einer weisen Brühe.
text: wash and gut the carp, then cut it into cubes. remove the gills and brown it in butter. add meat broth, a glass of wine, a few slices of lemon, and some seasoning. let it simmer. meanwhile, in another pot, melt a generous amount of butter, add a half tablespoon of flour, the yolks of 4 or 5 eggs, a few spoonfuls of cream, a little seasoning, and a quarter of a small jar of anchovies, finely chopped. add a little vinegar as well. place the pot over the heat and stir until it boils, then strain it through a sieve. when serving the fish, add it to the sauce a moment before. the head and tail can be boiled or baked and placed in the center of the dish.

title: 3) Gefüllte Karpfen.
text: one takes a carp as large as one wishes, but it must be a milchner. after it has been scaled, gutted, and washed, it is dried a little. it is then placed in a bowl. next, one takes the milt from the fish and two more herring milt or a quarter of a sardine, chopped together very finely. then, one takes the crumbs of a dry milchbrot, soaks it in water, and squeezes it out. add to the milt a good tin spoon full of cream, a little salt and seasoning, the grated zest of a lemon, and stir everything well together. then, fry it in butter and place it in the fish, sewing it up. after that, one can roast it on a grill or in butter. it s best to leave it overnight so that it dries out properly.

title: 4) Eine Brühe dazu.
text: take a quarter pound of anchovies, wash them clean and chop them finely, then put them in a pot with a generous piece of butter, the yolks of 3 eggs, 3 spoonfuls of cream, a little salt, mace, a little lemon juice and a little vinegar. stir this over the fire until it boils, then strain it through a sieve and serve over the fish.

title: 5) Ein blau gesottener Karpfen.
text: take a carp and cut it into as many pieces as you like. wash it clean, then pour vinegar over it and let it stand for a while. then put water into a pan, add salt, some peppercorns, a few bay leaves, a whole onion, and some vinegar. bring it to a boil, then add the fish and boil until it is cooked through. transfer it to a dish and garnish with parsley.

title: 6) Einen Hecht mit einer Butterbrühe.
text: take the pike, scale it, clean it thoroughly, and wash it well. then put water in a pan, add salt, and let it boil. afterwards, put the pike in, and cook it until it is done. place it on a dish, let butter melt, add parsley to it, and pour it over the fish.

title: 7) Einen Hecht mit einer Eyer=Soos.
text: prepare this like the previous one. once it is boiled, take the yolks from 3 or 4 eggs, a little meat broth, some salt, mace, 2 to 4 pieces of citron, and a piece of sweet butter, and pour this broth over the pike.

title:
8) Ein Hecht mit einer 
Sardellen=Soos.
text: cook it in this manner, then arrange it on a dish. afterwards, take a quarter-pound of anchovies, wash them clean in water, remove the small bones, mash them with a little meat broth, add the yolks of 4 or 5 eggs, a bit of nutmeg, and some salt, and mix it into an anchovy sauce. let it simmer over coals, and then pour it over the pike.

title: 9) Einen guten Ahl zu braten.
text: take one fowl, pluck it, cut it into pieces. then take breadcrumbs, mace blossoms, a little clove, a little salt, and mix these together. then, take a piece at a time and turn it in the breadcrumbs, skewer it, placing a few bay leaves between each piece. roast it, basting it with sweet butter occasionally, and sprinkle it with breadcrumbs until it is cooked through. arrange it on a dish, then place some lemons in a bowl and set it alongside on the table.

title: 10) Gekochte Salmen.
text: bring water to a boil, then add a few whole flowers, whole peppercorns, a little salt, and several bay leaves, a whole onion, and a little vinegar. once everything has cooked well, add the salmon, which must first be washed. when it is cooked through, remove it from the heat and let it cool. add a little parsley while it's cooking.

title: 11) Gebratene Salmen.
text: wash the salmon, let it drain well, then place it on a grill, on paper or a wooden spit. it must also be basted with butter so it doesn t stick, turning it often and baking it over a low heat. when it's done, place it on a dish and make a sauce for it melt butter and add a few capers, seasoning to taste.

title: 12) Gestofte Salmen.
text: cook the salmon until done, then take meat broth and let stale milk bread soften in it. strain the mixture and add a little lemon, salt, seasoning, and wine. let this simmer. you can also add a bit of the water the salmon cooked in. if you wish, you can add the salmon to the broth to cook for a few moments. then, serve, adding the yolks of 4 eggs and several spoonfuls of cream.

title: 1) Waffeln.
text: take 3 pounds of flour and half a maas of milk, 30 eggs, one and a half pounds of butter, half of which must be salted, half a cup of rosewater, 6 spoonfuls of yeast and a little salt. the milk must be lukewarm, and when you want to make it, put the yeast in a sieve and beat it well with the 3 pounds of flour until it is very smooth, then slowly pour in the milk and beat well, and also beat in the eggs gradually, and set it near the oven to rise. if you want to bake it in the evening, you can make it after dinner, and when you want to bake it, you must make the iron quite full and warm beforehand, and grease it with bacon.

title: 2) Gute Zimmet=Waffeln.
text: take 2 pounds of flour, half a pound of sugar, 1 pound of salted butter, 3 pinches of good cinnamon, 3 eggs. let the butter melt and pour it in gradually into the flour, until everything is well combined. make small cakes from the dough and bake them.

title: 3) Berlingot zu machen.
text: take 8 eggs, three-quarters of a pound of finely ground sugar, 2 spoons of rosewater, and a little salt, beat these together for three-quarters of an hour. afterward, add a half pound of melted butter, and beat it again until it has been beaten for a total of an hour. then add flour until it begins to form a dough. shape it into round pastries or crescents, they must look beautifully white, and bake them in a cake pan.

title: 4) Gebackene Mandeln.
text: take a quarter pound of fresh butter, a quarter pound of sugar, 5 eggs, beaten with the sugar, the yellow zest of a lemon grated in, and the butter melted. add flour as needed until the dough looks moist, then cut out shapes and bake.

title: 5) Gefüllte Brunellen.
text: take plums and cut them slightly open at the top. then make a filling of ground almonds, sugar, cinnamon, and rosewater, well mixed together. fill the plums with this mixture, and then make a dough from flour, rosewater, sugar, cinnamon, and wine, slightly thicker than pancake batter. dip the plums into the dough and bake them in butter, sprinkling sugar on top.

title: 6) Mandelschnitten.
text: take half a pound of almonds, half a pound of sugar, 3 eggs, a splash of rosewater, and slices of milk bread, then bake in lard or other butter.

title: 7) Nierenschnitten.
text: take the kidneys of a roasted veal roast, you can also add a little veal, and chop it very finely. crumble two slices of stale milk bread in water until hard, and add 5 or 6 eggs. combine all of this thoroughly, add a little cream, about a quarter cup of small raisins, a little salt and spices, and mix everything well. spread this mixture on milk bread slices and bake in rendered butter, then sprinkle with sugar.

title: 8) Eingeweicht Milchbrod.
text: take milk bread, grate the crusts, and place them in a bowl. add eggs, half a measure of milk, and a kreuzer of rosewater, stirring everything well together. let the milk bread soak in this mixture, and then bake it in clarified butter. finish with a raisin broth poured over it.

title: 9) Gefüllte Milchbrod mit Mandeln
text: take the milk bread, cut a hole in the bottom the size of a gold coin, scoop out the crumbs and grate them. then make a filling from a quarter of almonds, finely ground, with rosewater, dry milk bread, the crust peeled off, dipped in cold water and squeezed out, then put into a bowl with 4 eggs, a cup of cream and a little sugar, gently whisked until sweet enough, along with a pinch of ground cinnamon. combine all of this with the ground almonds and mix well. then place it on the fire with the pot and stir until it thickens, then let it cool. once it s cold, put it into the milk bread, placing the piece that was cut out at the bottom on top. if it's too small, take another piece and bake it in clarified butter. for decoration, you can stick sliced almonds on top, if you wish, and you can add the yellow peel of half a lemon along with a handful

title: 10) Kugelhopfen oder Nonnenfürz.
text: take three-quarters of a pound of flour, a tin spoon full of yeast, or a little brandy, a little fresh butter, mixed with a cup of boiling milk, then beat in 6 eggs one after another, and then add it slowly with a spoon to hot clarified butter and bake slowly before you beat in the eggs, however, you must let the dough cool down a little.

title: 11) Maultaschen.
text: make a good dough, rolling it out a little thick, cut square pieces from it and take preserved raspberries or cherries, and put them inside, fold it over the edges, and brushed with egg yolk, then baked in a tart pan, or filled with filling like an almond tart.

title: 12) Zwieback zu machen.
text: take a glassful of eggs, both yellow and white, a glassful of milk, two glassfuls of the finest flour, and a little salt. stir the flour with the milk and put it into a tinned bowl. bake over heat, both above and below, until it dries out. then cut into rectangular pieces, about 3 fingers wide, and bake in clarified butter, basting constantly with a spoonful. when you put them into the butter, remove the pan from the heat so that it isn't too hot, so that they don't brown too quickly. if you wish, you can cut a cross into them. this portion requires two spoonfuls of the finest brandy.

title: 13) Rübenschnitten.
text: take half a pound of almonds, 2 spoonfuls of rosewater, half a pound of sugar, and 5 eggs. add flour until the dough can be kneaded. cut this into oblong shapes and bake.

title: 14) Nürnberger=Gebacknes.
text: take 12 pounds of sugar, 3 spoons of butter, 1 and 1 8 pounds of flour, 2 eggs beaten with rosewater, then stirred with sugar and flour, and afterwards the butter added, along with the yellow zest of a lemon, to make a dough. press out shapes, brush with egg yolk and bake in a cake pan. afterwards, let it cool slightly and brush with sugar and lemon juice, and bake a little more until the sugar is dried.

title: 15) Gute Macronen.
text: take 1 and 1 2 pounds of grated almonds, one pound of sugar, and a little rosewater, mixing them well together. roast slowly over the fire in a casserole or new pot. afterward, separate four eggs, taking the whites and beating them well, then add them to the mixture. place onto wafers as large as you desire, and bake in a cake pan they must look a beautiful yellow.

title: 16) Gute Spritzen.
text: take a pound of finely ground flour, half a measure of milk heated and cooked, and a little fresh butter. afterwards, take the flour and add it to the milk, letting it become completely dry over the heat. then add 1 dram of rosewater and 12 eggs, well beaten, and bake.

title:
17) Gebackene Mandeln oder
Bubenschenkel.
text: take 1 pound of ground sugar, previously 1 cup of rosewater, three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter, melt over the fire, and stir in 10 eggs, the yellow zest of a lemon. mix all of this well, then add flour until it forms a soft dough, then bake in clarified butter.

title: 18) Gute Plamey.
text: take apples and rosewater. chop the apples finely and make them into a purée, squeeze in the juice of a lemon, the yolks of 2 eggs, and sweeten well. then, take the zest of a lemon, grease a bowl with sweet butter, add crumbs of milk bread, sugar, and cinnamon, mixing them together and sprinkling a little thickly into the bowl. add the purée and sprinkle more on top, then bake in a charcoal pan over heat from above and below, but not for too long.

title: 19) Eyerküchelger zu machen.
text: take 12 eggs well beaten, a cup of milk, and a pinch of rosewater. set over a few coals and let it thicken. afterward, make a crust from eight milk loaves, grated on a grater, and place it underneath. form round cakes and bake in melted butter.

title: Die Brühe dazu.
text: combine two parts wine with one part water. simmer a handful of small raisins with sugar and cinnamon, then drizzle over the küchel and sprinkle with sugar.

title: 20) Reis=Küchelger.
text: take 1 pound of rice, 1 measure of milk, eggs, sugar, and cinnamon. grate milk bread on a grater, add it underneath, and bake in rendered butter.

title: 21) Macronen=Küchelger.
text: take a pound of almonds, finely ground with rosewater, three slices of milk bread grated on a grater, one spoonful of sugar, three egg whites, and the yellow zest of a lemon, all well mixed together and baked in clarified butter.

title: 22) Die Brühe dazu.
text: take half a measure of milk, half a spoonful of sugar, a little rosewater, the yolks of 5 eggs. stir all of this over the fire until it boils, then put it into a bowl and place the macarons on top, and sprinkle granulated sugar over the macarons.

title: 23) Weck=Klösger.
text: take a fresh milk bread, press it hard in water and stir it gently with the yolk of an egg, a spoonful of cream, and about as much butter as a half chicken's egg. stir all this together until it is smooth, and add a little salt and mace. afterwards, form into balls and cook in water these can be used in soups and ragout.

title: 24) Weck=Klösger auf andere Art.
text: make them similarly to the previous ones, only slightly larger. when cooked in water or meat broth, prepare a sauce over them of cream and egg yolk, a tiny pinch of flour, stirred over the fire until it boils, and served over the dumplings. sprinkle with bread grated on a grater, fried brown in butter, and placed over the dumplings.

title: 25) Aepfel=Küchelger.
text: take apples, peel them, and slice them about as thick as half a finger, removing the cores. make a dough with a cup of beer, roughly as thick as a foreign walnut, and throw in some rendered butter. when the beer boils, melt the butter, then take some good flour and mix it with the beer until it forms a dough slightly thicker than a pancake batter. press the apples into the dough and bake in rendered butter.

title: 26) Gebackenes von Milchbrod.
text: take 4 milk loaves, grate off the crusts, then cut the milk loaves in half lengthwise, and then cut each half into 3 pieces. place all these pieces in a bowl or frying pan. afterwards, take 8 eggs, half a measure of milk, and a pinch of rosewater, stir everything well together and pour over the sliced milk loaves, let it soak for an hour. then bake in rendered butter, as soon as they are baked, roll them in sugar and cinnamon they must look finely browned.

title: 27) Fricatellen zu machen.
text: take 2 pounds of raw veal, 1 pound of ox kidney fat, 2 or 3 dry milk rolls, peeled and pressed hard in water, beaten with several eggs, a few spoonfuls of cream, a little seasoning and salt. work these ingredients together and make patties, then fry them brown in clarified butter. you can also make them from beef, but you will need more kidney fat and a bit more of everything, as beef is very dry. alternatively, you can make them from sausage filling, in which case you won't need any fat.

title: 28) Brühe dazu.
text: take meat broth, add grated bread to it, and let it cook until very tender. add a little seasoning and salt, a few slices of lemon. if you wish to arrange it in this way, add the yolks of a few eggs and a few spoonfuls of cream. or you can make a butter broth with it for that, take a good piece of butter, a few pinches of flour, a little vinegar, and a little water, along with the yolks of four eggs, and stir it until it boils.

title: 29) Gebackene Kalbsfüs.
text: boil the feet in water and salt. afterwards, make a dough from flour, eggs, and rosewater, with a little salt. remove the bones from the feet, dip the meat in the dough, and bake in rendered butter.

title: 30) Gebackene Kalbsleber.
text: clean the liver and remove the skin. cut it into pieces and coat them in flour and salt, then fry them golden yellow in rendered butter. afterwards, melt butter and roast a spoonful of flour until lightly golden. stir in a little water, add a few slices of lemon, some spices, and let it simmer. pour this sauce over the liver. alternatively, you can make a different sauce by browning a spoonful of flour in butter. add a little meat broth or water, a glass of wine, a few lemon slices, a handful of small raisins, a few peeled almonds, either whole or sliced lengthwise, a whole cinnamon stick, and sugar until it s sweet enough. once everything is well cooked, pour it over the liver.

title: 31) Fricanton zu machen.
text: take a cut of veal roast, cut pieces from the thickest parts, about a hand's breadth long, longer than wide, skin it and lightly pound it, then nicely studded with fat, and press the pieces together so they look nicely thick. then take a calf s kidney and two calf s feet and simmer them. next, take the studded veal, place it in an earthenware pot, pour calf broth over it so that it covers the pieces, add an onion studded with cloves, a little mace and salt. you can also add a slice of bacon cut very thinly, and let it cook slowly until it turns yellowish. then take another pot, toast a spoonful of flour in rendered butter until finely browned, then add some calf broth, a glass of wine, an onion studded with cloves or seasoning, a little salt, a few slices of lemon, and a little asafetida, and let it cook together well. then pour the extracted juice from

title: 32) Gute Kugelhopfen.
text: take three-quarters of a pound of fresh butter, 10 eggs, a spoonful of rosewater gently mixed, then add 1 pound of fine flour gradually. add 3 spoonfuls of good yeast mixed with half a cup of milk, which must be warm, and slowly add it to the rest. beat for three-quarters of an hour until it pulls away from the spoon. then grease the molds with melted butter and put the dough in, filling them only halfway. let it rise near the fire until it reaches the shape of the mold, then place in a tart pan and bake in the oven. you must also add a little sugar.

title: 33) Muscheln zu machen.
text: take as much flour as milk. for each spoonful of flour, add one egg. beat the flour, milk, and eggs well. add two spoonfuls of rosewater and some sugar, if desired. you can add a quarter pound of ground almonds, well beaten, to the mixture. dip a seashell spoon into the batter and bake in rendered butter. when cool, sprinkle with sugar.

title: 34) Wasser=Küchelger.
text: take a pound of fresh butter, and pour a pound of fresh water into it, place it in a pot with coals so that it warms together and the butter melts, then slowly add a pound of flour, and 6 eggs, one after the other poured in, and 3 silver spoonfuls of rosewater, beat everything for about an hour, then take a small spoonful of dough, about the size of a foreign walnut, and put it into rendered butter, and constantly stir with a spoon. the butter must not be too hot when the dough is added.

title: 35) Böffertger zu machen.
text: take 5 eggs, well beaten, and slowly stir in flour until it is smooth, along with half a measure of milk and enough flour to make it thick enough. then add a quarter pound of fresh butter, melted, and a few pewter spoonfuls of yeast, large and small raisins, and a little sugar. let it rise for 3 hours and bake in an egg pan.

title: 36) Zuckerbrod zu machen.
text: take 6 eggs, half a pound of sugar, 10 lots of yeast, 10 lots of white flour, beat the eggs for half an hour, then add the sugar, and make a fire underneath so it burns brightly, afterward, combine the flour and add it, and stir it until it forms bubbles, then grease the pan with butter, put it in, and bake it.

title: 37) Bisquit=Kuchen.
text: take 1 pound of canary sugar, finely ground and sifted, so that it is like flour. in a tall pot, beat this sugar with 16 eggs for an hour until it forms a foam. add a little rosewater and three-quarters of a pound of the best starch flour, gradually incorporating it and beating well. afterward, grease the pan or mold with fresh butter, pour the batter into it, and bake slowly.

title: 38) Gerührte Waffeln.
text: take 1 pound of fresh butter, beat it for an hour, then add 12 eggs, which have previously been warmed in water, beating one after the other in, but mixing each one well until all the eggs are combined. afterward, add half a pound of flour, a cup of sweet milk, and a generous spoonful of yeast, mixing it all together. then add the butter that has been beaten, and let it rise. when it has risen well, bake it. add some salt.

title: 39) Dampfnudeln zu machen.
text: take 1 pound of fine flour, put it into a deep bowl, 4 spoonfuls of yeast mixed with milk through a sieve, until the flour is well combined and well beaten. then let the dough rise for an hour, and add 6 eggs, one at a time, and a little salt. afterward, shape the dough into balls about the size of an egg, and place them on a board to rise a bit. then take a wide-bottomed pot with half a measure of water you can also use half milk. when it boils, put the steamed dumplings in, let them cook gently, and well covered, so that the steam cooks them. the broth can be made with butter if it is too fatty, you can add a little meat broth. you can also bake the steamed dumplings beautifully yellow in butter.

title: 40) Mandel=Sylben.
text: take half a pound of flour, half a pound of finely ground sugar, half a pound of finely ground almonds, the yolk of one egg, half an ounce of cinnamon, pepper as much as you like, and a little rosewater. the sugar must be stirred well with water, then all combined together. the iron pan must be freshly prepared and greased with fresh butter, and baked.

title: 41) Gefüllte Eyer.
text: scald a large egg, about half-cooked, then soften a roll in milk and stir it well. afterward, add eggs, sugar, cinnamon, ground almonds, and raisins, and make a batter. bake the batter in butter until it is as thick as you desire. to achieve the desired thickness, incorporate more eggs into the batter and then bake again in butter. repeat this process of adding eggs and baking in butter as many times as necessary until the batter is thick enough. finally, cut it into four portions and arrange them over a bowl.

title: Suppen.
text: a lemon soup. a beer soup. a wine soup. a brown wine soup. a veal soup. a yellow soup. a crab soup. a chocolate soup. a rice soup. a beet soup. a brown soup. a good milk soup. a lovage soup. a cold milk soup or egg milk. a green soup, as the season provides. a cherry soup. an egg barley soup. a water soup. a lark or blackbird soup.

title: Bey=Essen.
text: macaroon in a cream broth for the broth cook a spanish broth. prepare a good almond broth. make a butter broth. cream broth for the butter broth. a red broth for this. another way to make a butter broth. for this, a broth. another broth for this. make a kidney butter broth. for this, a broth. make a schüsselfladen. make a lemon foam. make a crembule. prepare young chickens with pea puree. prepare chickens with lettuce. baked sauerkraut. boiled cauliflower. to make boeuf à la mode. minced veal with lemons. prepare a good eyerkäse. eat a yellow broth cold. make gestoofed veal. cook a fresh ox tongue. simmer a spanish suckling pig white. yellow klösger in a broth. a good scheele or galera.

title: Gebratenes.
text: roasting game 39 roasting a wild duck 40 roasting a foreign rooster 40 roasting a veal shoulder 41 stuffing a veal breast 41 roasting a beef roast 41 roasting a lamb shoulder 42 roasting a fine suckling pig 42 roasting stuffed pigeons 43

title: Torten.
text: an almond cake a tongue cake a bread almond cake to make cream pastry marc pastry to make kidney cakes a good egg cake a cream cake a lemon cake a bread cake an apple cake a cherry cake an apricot cake a good ratatouille brunnen cake to make shells
ingredients: lemon cake bread cake apple cake cherry apricot cake

title: Pasteten.
text: a good warm pastry. roll out the puff pastry. potato pastry. a crisp pastry. almond pastry for tarts and small bases. small nail pastry jars.

text: carp with a brown broth carp with a white broth stuffed carp a broth to serve with it blue-braised carp pike with a butter broth pike with an egg sauce pike with an anchovy sauce how to roast a good ahl boiled salmon fried salmon stewed salmon

text: waffles good zimmet waffles to make berlingots roasted almonds stuffed brunellen almond slices kidney slices soaked milk bread stuffed milk bread with almonds hop cakes or nun s froth maultaschen to make zwieback beet slices nuremberg baked goods good macronen good spritzen roasted almonds or boy s shanks good plamey to make eyerküchelger the broth for it rice küchelger macronen küchelger the broth for it bread dumplings bread dumplings another way apple küchelger baked from milk bread to make fricatellen broth for it roasted calf s feet roasted calf s liver to make fricanton good hop cakes to make muscheln water küchelger to make böffertger to make zuckerbrod biscuit cake
ingredients: roasted almonds brunellen almond kidney milk bread milk bread
