title: Neues Hannöverisches Kochbuch 1800 (Auszüge)
text: to prepare two portions. first, take a pound of veal, cut it into small pieces, and put it in a pot with half a pound of bacon, chopped. add a quarter pound of butter, a bunch of parsley, two onions, finely chopped, and a little salt and pepper. let it simmer over a gentle fire until the meat is tender. then, add a pint of good broth, a spoonful of flour, and a few cloves. simmer until the sauce thickens. serve with buttered toast.

title:
1. 
Empfehlung der Reinlichkeit.
text: as what every cook deserves to be recommended first is cleanliness. it is the first thing by which they commend themselves and their art, and their dishes. a dish that may less entice our palate will nevertheless be preferred over another, more palatable one, because it comes from clean and pure hands. conversely, the best skill and the most enticing dish often lose their deliciousness and evoke disgust. therefore, whoever cooks should ensure the utmost cleanliness of their own ingredients, their utensils, their vessels, and equally so for the cleanliness of their own body and clothing. one rightly infers the one from the other, and cleanliness secures the cook the first recommendation.

title:
2. 
Etwas über die Gefäße beym Kochen.
text: the vessels in which we stir, beat, cook, roast, bake, and also store our food are far from equally good for our palate, and especially for our health. they can be very harmful to human health, and therefore one must be very careful regarding them. vessels made of copper and brass are more dangerous than those of tin, which are not as good as those of iron, and earthenware, stone, glass, and porcelain vessels are better than all. one can still cook in tin and iron, but nothing should be stored in them, or kept only overnight, especially anything acidic. cooking in copper or brass is so dangerous that it can be fatal to those who eat from it. where one cannot entirely do without copper and brass equipment, one must at least ensure that they are constantly kept in good condition internally with tinning. vessels made of clay or earth, of stone, of glass, and porcelain are the best, and should at least be used exclusively when something is to be preserved

title:
3. 
Bouillon zu kochen.
text: the meat intended for the bouillon is washed well with cold water and placed in a well-tinned kettle with cold water over the fire. as soon as it begins to boil, the scum is diligently skimmed off, and some peeled and washed celery, carrots, yellow roots, and onions, along with a bay leaf, are added. it is then allowed to simmer slowly over a gentle fire until the meat is tender. half a pound of lean ham, cut into cubes, thrown in, improves the flavor. the broth is then strained through a hair sieve, and the fat is carefully removed, and you have bouillon. a good bouillon requires a good piece of beef, one or two calf shanks, and an old hen.

title:
4. 
Braune Bouillon oder Jus zu machen.
text: one takes lean beef, that is, beef which is not fatty and contains no bones, and cuts it into finger-thick slices, lightly pounding them with the back of a knife. then one greases a casserole dish with cold butter, places the beef slices in it, along with any trimmings from cutlets or the like, if one has them, and also some lean ham cut into cubes. next, one places the casserole dish over a low heat, letting the meat brown slowly until it is brown, but not too dark. then one adds broth, or if one does not have it, boiling water, which is of course not as good as broth. add some herbs and roots as used in white broth, and don't forget a little salt. when the meat is cooked until very tender, one strains the broth through a hair sieve and removes the fat the jus is then ready. the slower the brown broth cooks, the clearer and better it will be,

title:
5.
Braise zu machen.
text: to braise means to set something in a copper pan or dish. it is, incidentally, a very excellent thing because it obtains a fine flavor if one wants to cook, for example, a capon, or chickens and chicks, ducks, a lamb, veal shank, or whatever it may be, one takes a casserole, according to the size of the ingredients so that they can lie neatly within. one slices bacon and lines the bottom of the casserole with it. one takes a good portion of fresh kidney fat, chops it up a little, and sprinkles the bacon with it. add various herbs, such as bay leaves, basil, whole onions, a little whole pepper, thyme, a few whole cloves, and a few pieces of ginger. then, place whatever one wants to cook within, covers it, and sets it on a low tripod, making a gentle charcoal fire underneath, so that it slowly simmers in its own broth with the fat turn it occasionally, and

title:
6.
Braune Coulis zu Saucen.
text: a good spoonful of butter is put into a casserole with some slices of lean beef, onions, yellow root vegetables, celery, bones from mutton and veal, and an old hen that has been cleaned and chopped with skin and bones. the casserole is then placed over the fire and allowed to simmer or fry together in the butter. it must simmer until it turns brown. however, one must be careful that it does not burn, otherwise it will become bitter and therefore unusable for sauces. once it has acquired its proper brown color, broth, or, in its absence, even just water, is poured over it and allowed to cook thoroughly so that all the flavor comes out. once this is done, a piece of lean ham is cut into cubes, put into a small casserole with some butter, placed over a gentle fire, and allowed to sweat until it turns yellowish-brown. then, it is stirred with a good spoonful of flour, added to the first mixture, and allowed to cook

title:
7.
Weiße Coulis zu Saucen.
text: one takes a few old chickens, cleans them and minces them, veal from the neck, and the legs from the bones, a spoonful of butter, parsnips, yellow carrots, and celery root, slices all of these, puts it into a casserole with onions, bay leaves, a little salt, and a ladleful of broth, and lets it cook together until it wants to thicken. now one fills the casserole with more broth, lets it cook until done, and pours it through a sieve into an earthenware dish. from this one makes hachee sauce, pistache sauce, and morgels sauce. it can also be added to roasted poultry, fricandaux, and all fine meat and wing pastries.

title:
8.
Eine braune Fischcoulis.
text: to prepare fish forcemeat, the backbone is removed. this and any other fish trimmings are finely chopped. then, melt a piece of butter in a saucepan until browned, add the chopped fish trimmings along with some yellow turnip, celery, onions, and a bay leaf, and let it simmer until it turns brown. next, stir in a small spoonful of flour, add stock as needed, and let it simmer gently for half an hour, then strain it. this coulis is used for fish sauces. a white coulis of this type is prepared in the same way, but it is not allowed to brown it is filled up with white bouillon, and then white sauces are made from it.

title:
9.
Glace zum glaciren verschiedener Fleischspeisen.
text: to enhance the appearance of certain meat dishes, one must glaze them. to achieve this, combine equal parts broth and a good meat glaze made from beef bones. simmer over a strong heat until it reduces to a syrup-like consistency. this glaze is then brushed onto the meat to be glazed using a pastry brush when serving.

title:
10.
Einen weißen Guß, oder eine weiße Glace
über Bäckereien.
text: finely ground 1 4 pound of white sugar is sifted. then, it is placed in a deep earthenware bowl, and the whites of one egg are beaten into it, along with the juice of a lemon, but without the seeds. it is stirred with a wooden spoon, always in one direction, until it is completely white and stiff. if it is too thick, it is thinned with lemon juice. it is used to coat pastries, then sprinkled with colorful sanding sugar, and allowed to dry in a moderately warm oven.

title:
11.
Krebsbutter.
text: cook a dozen crabs in water, but without salt. break off all the red shells, the pincers, and legs, and grind this finely with a pound of butter in a mortar. then place it in a saucepan over a gentle heat, and let it simmer, stirring constantly, for a good while until the butter is completely red. add boiling water, let it cook down, strain the broth through a fine sieve, and let it cool. now remove the butter from the top, melt it together, and use it it can also be kept for a long time.

title:
12.
Krebscoulis.
text: to begin, proceed as with crab butter. once it has sweated sufficiently, add some flour, let it sweat a little longer, then pour in good broth and simmer for half an hour. afterward, strain the broth through a fine sieve, but do not let it boil again, otherwise the red butter will form on top.

title:
13.
Vom Legiren.
text: to begin, take more or less egg yolks, according to the size of your bowl roughly three to four for an ordinary bowl and whisk them after the food to be coated has been prepared. add a little cold broth, vinegar, lemon juice, milk, etc. next, add a small amount of the incorporated sauce and stir it through, then let it slowly run onto the simmering pigeon, young chicken, veal, or lamb. but be sure to stir the casserole constantly. as soon as it just begins to simmer, remove it from the heat, taste for salt, and adjust as needed.

title:
14.
Eine Klare anzurühren.
text: to begin, take four spoonfuls of fine flour and beat in three whole eggs. once this is done, gradually add as much milk as needed, along with mace and a little salt, until you have the consistency required for pancakes. it must be slightly thick. if you need more or less, you can adjust the ingredients according to the proportions given. you can also stir in wine or wheat beer, as appropriate. this batter can be used to bake various items, as described below.

title:
15.
Eine andere Klare mit Milch, worinnen
Obst ausgebacken wird.
text: take four to five good spoonfuls of fine flour, four to five whole eggs, a good spoonful of leaven or yeast dissolved in water, grated lemon zest, finely ground cinnamon, some grated and sifted sugar, and stir it all well. then, as before, stir it with milk and let it rest so that the yeast works its way through.

title:
16.
Butter abzuklären.
text: melt as much butter as you need for frying in a saucepan over a low heat, allowing it to simmer gently until it is completely clear. remove from the heat, let any sediment settle to the bottom, and skim off any foam. strain the butter through a fine-mesh sieve into another saucepan, being careful not to let any sediment pass through. when ready to fry, place the butter over the heat and allow it to get hot enough that a small piece of dough dropped in will immediately float to the surface. then you can begin frying.

title:
17.
Farce von Kalbfleisch oder Rindfleisch.
text: to begin, take cutlets or meat from the shank, remove the sinew and finely chop it. then, sprinkle with breadcrumbs and wrap them around the chopped meat. once this is done, melt a quarter pound of butter in a saucepan, beat in six to eight eggs, stirring well with the butter, then add a spoonful of milk. set over low heat and stir constantly until a thin scrambled egg mixture forms. spread this over the chopped meat, mix it thoroughly, and combine it with the breadcrumbs until it forms a dough-like consistency. return the mixture to the saucepan, add a little salt, finely ground nutmeg, finely chopped thyme, and two or three whole eggs. stir well to combine. if the farce becomes too stiff, thin it with milk. this farce is suitable for fine pastries, stuffed dishes, and dumplings served in white and brown soups.

title:
18.
Farce von Kalbsbraten.
text: remove the tendons from the roast and cut them out. then, chop the roast finely. soak breadcrumbs in milk, place them on a sieve to drain, then squeeze them completely dry and spread them over the chopped meat. after that, in a casserole, whisk six egg yolks and four whole eggs with butter, and stir until they form a scrambled egg mixture. add this next to the roast and breadcrumbs, along with salt, a little nutmeg, and finely chopped thyme, and mix everything together thoroughly. now, return everything to the casserole and stir in four raw egg yolks. finally, whisk the whites of ten eggs until they form a snow-like consistency and gently fold them in. this farce is baked and added to brown soups, crab soups, and lentil soups. it can also be baked in molds. grease the molds with butter, rub fine soup croutons between your hands briefly, sprinkle them into the molds instead of breadcrumbs, pour the mixture

title:
19.
Farce von Hechten oder Karpen.
text: once the fish is scaled, gutted, and clean, wash it, then cut it into small pieces. place it in a saucepan with a generous quarter pound of butter, add one or two chopped onions, a few bay leaves, and a little salt. set it over low heat and let the fish sweat until cooked. remove the fish with a slotted spoon, carefully fillet it, ensuring all the smallest bones are removed, and then finely chop the fish. to the remaining butter, add six to eight whole eggs and stir over the heat until it forms scrambled eggs. now, add grated breadcrumbs to the fish, place the scrambled eggs on top, and mix them thoroughly. leave the bay leaves behind. finally, return the mixture to the saucepan, stir with a wooden spoon, and stir in two or three whole eggs, finely grated nutmeg, salt, and finely chopped thyme. if the farce becomes too stiff, stir in a little good milk to thin it out. this farce is suitable for

title:
20.
Farce von Krebsen.
text: once the crabs have been cooked in water with salt and caraway seeds, remove them from the water and let them cool. then, break off the tails and claws. pull out the intestinal tract from the tails and finely chop the meat. grind the crab shells finely and sweat them in butter over low heat until the butter turns red. strain it through a sieve into a small casserole, allowing only the clarified butter to drain through. beat six to eight whole eggs into this clarified butter, stir well, place over low heat, and cook into a scrambled egg mixture. immediately spread this over the chopped crab tails, adding grated breadcrumbs, mace, salt, a little finely chopped thyme, and finely chopped parsley, mixing everything together as finely as possible, and finally stir in two whole eggs in the casserole until well combined. if it becomes too thick, thin it out with a little good milk. use this to make dumplings for crab soup, and also to stuff and bake the crabs. furthermore,

title:
21.
Eine Marginade.
text: pour a half measure of vinegar into a casserole, add some salt, whole thyme and marjoram, a few peeled and sliced onions, whole cloves, and mace, and let it simmer. in this marinade, one can pickle or preserve anything. all meats for coarse pies. game of all kinds, including turkey, ducks, lamb, and beef, if one needs it in coarse pies in the absence of game. the game and everything else is cut as needed and placed in the marinade. poultry is first trussed, then placed in an earthenware vessel so that the back is up and the breast down, and the marinade is poured hot over it. the items in the marinade must be stirred daily. sometimes they lie too long and draw out too much acid. in this case, before use, they are placed in fresh water to draw out the acid. let them lie in the water for half an hour, then take them out, press them with your hand, and dry them with a

title:
22.
Braun gebranntes Mehl.
text: melt about 1 2 pound of butter in a saucepan over the fire, stirring in enough flour to form a stiff paste. cook this over a low heat, stirring constantly, until the flour turns a light brown color. you can then use it immediately, or store it in an earthenware bowl until needed.

title:
23.
Weiß gebranntes Mehl.
text: melt the butter, stir in the flour, and cook over low heat until it begins to rise. store as before if not used immediately.

title:
24.
Einen Rand auf eine Schüssel zu setzen.
text: make a very stiff dough on the table with flour and boiling water, roll it out about two finger-widths thick and as long as the bowl's curve, but fairly thin, and cut it evenly all around. then, brush the bowl, where the edge will be set, with lightly beaten egg, place the dough on it, press it firmly all over, make some decorations on it, and let this edge dry a little in a pie dish or a slightly cool oven.

title:
25.
Schnee von Eiweiß zu schlagen.
text: crack the eggs that are intended for this purpose. put the whites into a large, flat tin bowl, being careful to ensure that no yolk gets mixed in. then, using a long, two-finger-wide whisk, beat the egg whites until they form a very stiff foam.

title:
26.
Von Blanchiren.
text: poultry, or other meat that needs to be blanched, is placed whole or in pieces in cold water over a strong fire. when it boils, it is immediately removed and rinsed and cleaned with cold water. in this way, large pieces of veal, older chickens, and young chickens, as well as lamb and veal cut into small pieces, are not allowed to come to a full boil. however, when blanching veal brisket, it should be boiled for a short while, as it then becomes stiff and easier to handle. if you have stuffed items to blanch, bring the water to a boil first, then add the meat, let it boil over a few times, remove it, and rinse it. if you put stuffed items in cold water, the water will seep into the stuffing, making it soft and tasteless. it is also to be remembered that one must not leave meat in either cold or warm water unnecessarily, as the water draws the strength from the meat.

title:
27.
Abgeriebene Butter.
text: clarify the butter as instructed in recipe number 15, and place it in an earthenware bowl. then, stir it with a wooden spoon until it is cold and stiff again.

title:
28.
Torten, Bäckereyen und Craims zu glaciren.
text: once these items have been sprinkled with sugar, hold a glowing shovel over them until they develop color. when the area is properly colored, take another and continue in this manner until everything has a fine glaze.

title:
29.
Craim zu garniren.
text: cut long biscuits, or sugar cookies, into triangular shapes, sprinkle these pieces with sugar, and brown them as before with a glowing spatula. arrange these pieces around the edge of the bowl, so that the points face outward. chop the scraps from the biscuits or sugar cookies finely, sprinkle them with sugar, brown them in the same way with a glowing spatula, chop them again, sprinkle them with sugar, and brown them again. once it is all chestnut brown, grind it finely, like flour, and sprinkle the cream with it in patterns of flowers, trees, and other designs.

title:
30.
Von eingeweichtem Weißbrodt.
text: to use white bread or rolls for forcemeat or the like take stale bread that is well-baked. remove the crust from this, soak it in cold milk until soft. then, press the milk out with clean hands, and crumble the bread.

title:
1.
Eine ordinaire Hühnersuppe mit Perlgraupen.
text: combine 1 4 pound of barley in a well-tinned kettle with cold water and a little butter, then set over heat and let it cook for a short while. next, add an old hen, which has been simmered one or two days prior, drawn, and blanched according to instruction 25 in the previous book, to the barley in the kettle. pour in enough boiling water to make soup, add a little salt, and let the hen simmer slowly until it is almost cooked through. then add some cream, and finely chopped celery, parsley root, and leek, and let it cook together until done. just before serving, add a pinch of grated nutmeg to the soup.

title:
2.
Hühnersuppe mit Reis.
text: one takes an old chicken, prepared in the previous manner, and places it in a pot with water over the fire, adding a little salt, and lets it simmer slowly. approximately 3 4 of an hour before serving, one takes 3 4 pound of rice, rinses it briefly with boiling water, and adds it to the soup, as well as some soup herbs as before. then one lets everything cook slowly until done, and adds a little nutmeg to the soup when serving.

title:
3.
Hühnersuppe mit Reis auf eine andere Art.
text: an old hen is slowly cooked with water and a little salt. add some soup herbs and a bit of seasoning, as in the previous soup. separately, rinse 1 4 pound of rice with boiling water, then cook it with a little broth, butter, and salt over low heat. add a handful of carefully selected raisins and let it cook until it thickens. serve the soup with the hen, but place the rice on a separate plate.

title:
4. 
Krebssuppe.
text: cook one shock of crabs in water without salt, crack the shells, and make a crab coulis as instructed in the 11th instruction in the previous section but not too thick. into this coulis, if the season allows, add green peas, cauliflower, or finely cut asparagus, as well as the broken crab tails, some of the largest crab claws, and small dumplings, or some of the crab shells filled. these ingredients must be pre-cooked with a little broth, and the filled shells baked in the oven or in a tart pan. make a farce as described in the 18th instruction in the first section, using some of the crab meat, and fill the shells or make dumplings with this farce. after straining, the soup should not be boiled again.

title:
5. 
Eine Karpensuppe.
text: once the carp have been scaled and cleaned, the flesh is cut from the bones and a forcemeat is made from it. the meat is first fried in butter, then stale white bread is soaked in 6 eggs and milk, squeezed dry, and stirred into the meat over the fire. this is chopped very finely, then seasoned with mace and salt, and 2 raw eggs are added. it is shaped like a carp and baked in the oven until done. the bones are simmered with yellow roots, beets, parsley, and celery in a casserole until slightly thickened and browned. then, broth is added, it is brought to a boil, and strained through a hair sieve. the baked carp and toasted white bread are placed in soup bowls and served.

title:
6. 
Suppe von Hechten, Forellen, 
Karoutschen u.s.w.
text: fish, such as trout, char, and other fish, are prepared in the same manner.

title:
7.
Suppe a la Sante, oder Kräutersuppe.
text: you take sorrel, lovage, parsley, and purslane, chop them finely, and sauté with butter, adding a handful of flour. then, pour broth over it, bind it with five or six eggs, place toasted white bread in the soup bowl, and serve.

title:
1.
Enten a la Braise.
text: once prepared, they are braised and served with a creamy sauce and lemon. see introduction. regulation 11.

title:
2.
Gefüllte Enten.
text: dress the ducks by cutting along the back, remove the bones, stuff with a forcemeat, sew them back up, cook them braised, and serve with a coulis sauce and lemon.

title:
3.
Enten mit Cappern.
text: the ducks are cooked either in a braise or on a spit, and served with a capper's sauce.

title:
4.
Enten mit Sardellensauce.
text: the ducks are cooked in a braise and served with a sardine sauce.

title:
5.
Enten a la Daube
text: to make a fine tart with apples and spice take a pound of fine flour, a quarter of a pound of butter, a quarter of a pound of lard, a half-pint of water, and a spoonful of rosewater. work the flour, butter, and lard together until it s like fine breadcrumbs. then add the water and rosewater, and knead it well until it s smooth and pliable. let it rest for an hour. roll out the pastry thinly and line a deep tart pan. prick the bottom with a fork. for the filling, take a peck of apples, peeled, cored, and sliced. mix them with a quarter of a pound of butter, a quarter of a pound of sugar, a spoonful of ginger, a half-spoonful of mace, and a little salt. pour the apple mixture into the pastry-lined pan. cover the top with a thin layer of pastry. cut slits in the top

title:
6.
Kalkuten a la Daube
text: they are made in the same way as goose à la daube.

title:
7.
Kalkuten mit Kastanien.
text: peel 1 pound of chestnuts, add coulis to them, and simmer gently. serve this sauce with roasted turkey.

title:
8.
Gefüllten Kalkuten mit Austern.
text: remove the bones from a turkey, fill it with sauce, sew it back together, roast it until cooked through, and serve with oyster sauce.

title:
9.
Kalkuten mit Trüffeln.
text: roast the turkeys on a spit after they have been wrapped with bacon and paper. when serving, add a sauce of coulis with truffles underneath.

title:
10.
Farcirten Kalkuten.
text: take a roasted turkey, remove the breast meat, and chop it finely for the stuffing. mix with 4 beaten eggs and 2 raw eggs, grated white bread, salt, and spices. stuff the mixture back into the breast cavity, score the surface decoratively with a knife. place the turkey in a casserole dish with bacon, broth, onions, and salt. cover and cook over heat from both above and below until done. finally, serve with a coulis sauce and lemon.

title:
11.
Grillade von Kalkuten.
text: take the shanks, turn them in butter, sprinkle them with grated bread and salt, roast them on a rack until browned, and add a brown sauce with onions and lemon.

title:
12.
Poupeton von Kalkuten.
text: first, make a ragout of roasted turkey. then, create a border of forcemeat around the dish, place the ragout inside, and bake it in the oven until cooked through and browned.

title:
13.
Junge Kalkuten mit einer englischen Sauce.
text: these are nicely roasted on skewers and served with english sauce.

title:
14.
Gefüllte Kalkuten.
text: when the turkey is cleaned, beat a spoonful of butter with two eggs until frothy. then add grated breadcrumbs, currants, lemon zest, muscat flowers, and a little suet, mixing everything together. fill the turkey's crop and interior with this mixture, and roast it on a spit until cooked through. next, make a sauce from coulis with morels, truffles, meat pieces, stomach, livers, and lemons, like a ragout. pour this sauce over the dish and arrange the turkey on top.

title:
15.
Aspic von Kalkuten.
text: from a roasted turkey, tender slices are cut from the breast, and an aspic is made, just as one makes it from veal.

title:
1.
Holländische Sauce zu Fischen.
text: take a little flour, mix it with the yolks of 6 eggs, vinegar, and water. add a piece of butter and sugar, and cook the sauce over the fire until it is about to boil.

title:
2.
Braune Robertsauce.
text: make a little browned flour, add browned broth, a little vinegar, a few spoonfuls of jam, and a little sugar, and let it all cook together.

title:
3.
Gelbe Robertsauce.
text: a spoonful of flour is whisked with 3 egg yolks, a little vinegar, white broth, a few spoonfuls of sempf, a little butter, and sugar into a smooth sauce.

title:
4.
Eine grüne Rockensauce zum Lammbraten.
text: take a handful of green sorrel, pound it in a mortar and combine it with roasted breadcrumbs, wine, vinegar, sugar, and pepper, straining the mixture through a hair cloth.

title:
26.
Zitronensauce.
text: simmer a little white flour with broth, and stir in the juice of 2 lemons, then enrich the sauce with 2 egg yolks.

title:
27.
Zitronensauce anders.
text: whisk together a little flour with 4 egg yolks, the juice of 3 lemons, along with their grated zest, water, sugar, butter, and cinnamon over heat until just before boiling.

title:
28.
Morchelsauce.
text: one takes a handful of morels, boils them in water, cleans them, and chops them finely. furthermore, one prepares a white sauce, adds the morels to it, lets them simmer for a while, and enriches the sauce with 2 egg yolks.

title:
29.
Champignonssauce.
text: to make this sauce with dried mushrooms, proceed as with morels. if the mushrooms are fresh, however, clean them, cut them into cubes, sauté them in butter until tender, cook them through with a white sauce, and enrich the sauce with 2 egg yolks.

title:
30.
Sauce a la Reine
text: one takes the breast of a cooked chicken, the yolks of 4 hard-boiled eggs, 1 8 pound of sugar, and 1 2 loth of bitter almonds, and grinds all of this finely in a mortar. then one pours white coulis over it, lets it cook together, and strains the sauce through a fine sieve which must not be cooked again.

title:
31.
Dragonsauce.
text: chop the dragon coarsely, add brown or white sauce to taste, and let the sauce simmer.

title:
32.
Zwiebelsauce.
text: peel some medium-sized onions and boil them in water. then add brown sauce and cook the onions until they are completely tender.

title:
33.
Sauce Remoulade.
text: whisk the yolks of 3 hard-boiled eggs with finely chopped capers, provence herbs, mustard, vinegar, and ground pepper, and serve this sauce cold.

title:
34.
Chocolatesauce.
text: melt 1 2 pound of grated chocolate with half wine and half butter. stir in a little butter and sugar, then thicken the sauce with 4 egg yolks, and serve with puddings and other pastries.

title:
39.
Melirtes Gemüse.
text: you take green peas, diced yellow root vegetables, kohlrabi, cauliflower stems, markische beets, celery, parsnips, runner beans, half-ripe shelling peas, large beans, and very small potatoes. you cook all of this in salted water, then drain it. you make a sauce from white, burnt flour and broth, add the vegetables, season with salt, and let it cook through. serve with cutlets, sausages, or grilled sausage.

title:
1.
Eine Pastete von Hasen.
text: once the hare is skinned and the pelts removed, it is chopped into pieces and seasoned with bacon, cloves, pepper, and salt. these pieces are left overnight in vinegar, salt, spices, and bay leaves. then, a forcemeat is made from veal, onions, bacon, salt, spices, and some white bread. next, a baked dough is prepared using 6 pounds of flour. it is worked quite stiff with boiled water on the kneading table, like for bread. when it is well prepared, half a finger's thickness is rolled out, and cut to the size and shape of the pie, round or oblong. from the cut-off dough, the border is made. it is rolled out by hand until it is long enough to go around the pie. then, it is rolled out with the rolling pin to a width of one hand, and again as thick as a finger. this is trimmed off with a knife and placed on the bottom crust, brushed with

title:
2.
Eine Wildpastete.
text: the meat from a venison or roe deer haunch is skinned from the bones and cut into neat pieces, and interspersed with seasoned bacon. the remaining ingredients are prepared as with hare.

title:
3.
Pastete von Feldhühnern.
text: the field hens, but not too old, should be cleaned and drawn, and then placed in a marinade. otherwise, proceed as with the rabbit pie.

title:
4.
Pastete von Fasanen.
text: it's made like this just as well.

title:
6.
Pastete von wilden oder zahmen Enten.
text: duck, whether old or young, are cleaned, eviscerated, and marinated. the rest is well known. this pie is served with a caper sauce.

title:
1.
Hecht blau zu kochen.
text: the pike are cleaned without skinning. they are bent or chopped into pieces and washed. then they are poured over with vinegar so they turn blue. they are cooked in salted boiling water until done, skimmed, and served with a sauce of chopped parsley and butter, or a yellow wine sauce.

title:
2.
Gestofte Hechte.
text: the pike are cleaned, scaled, and washed, then placed in a casserole dish. add butter, salt, onions, bay leaves, grated white bread, nutmeg, wine, lemons, and a little water. simmer until cooked through.

title:
3.
Gestofte Hechte auf andere Art.
text: the pike is cut into pieces, cleaned, and then cooked thoroughly with butter, chopped parsley, salt, grated white bread, and water.

title:
4. 
Gespickten Hecht.
text: to make a fine almond tart, take a pound of fine wheat flour, a quarter of a pound of butter, a quarter of a pound of sugar, and four eggs. mix the flour and butter together until it resembles breadcrumbs. then add the sugar and eggs, and knead until you have a smooth paste. roll out the dough thinly and line a tart pan. prick the base with a fork. for the filling, take a pound of sweet almonds, blanched and ground, a quarter of a pound of sugar, and four egg whites. beat the egg whites until stiff, then gently fold in the ground almonds and sugar. pour the filling into the prepared tart shell. bake in a moderate oven until golden brown. when cool, sprinkle with powdered sugar.

title:
44.
Laberdan zu kochen.
text: the laberdan must be soaked for 2 days, and then cooked thoroughly in water. a sauce of butter and mustard is added during cooking.

title:
45.
Schmerlinge blau gekocht.
text: the snails are cleaned, soaked in vinegar, and cooked until tender in water and salt. a yellow sauce is made with butter, flour, 2 whole eggs, lemon, water, wine, and sugar.

title:
46.
Stinte zu kochen.
text: remove the heads and entrails from the cuttlefish. then, place a pot of water and salt over heat when it boils, add the cuttlefish. as soon as they come back to a boil, they are cooked and served with mustard and butter.

title:
47.
Gebackene Stinte.
text: the sprat are scaled, heads and innards removed, dredged in flour and salt, and fried until done in brown butter.

title:
48.
Seezungen gekocht.
text: skin the plaice, cut off the heads and wing bones, remove the innards, and simmer the tongues with salt and water, serving with a watercress sauce.

title: Seezungen gebacken.
text: once the tongues are prepared as before, score them and sprinkle with salt. then dry them, brush with egg, sprinkle with grated breadcrumbs, and fry in clarified butter. serve with green peas, or simply with browned butter.

title:
1.
Compotte von Johannisbeeren.
text: pick the currants and set them over a low heat with sugar. once cooked through, remove them with a slotted spoon. cook the juice with plenty of sugar until it becomes very thick, like syrup, and pour it over the currants. sprinkle with crushed cinnamon and sugar.

title:
2.
Compotte von Kirschen.
text: one takes sour cherries, removes the pits, and cooks them with plenty of sugar, cinnamon, and lemon peel. then, one removes the cherries, and cooks the juice as above until it is thick like syrup, and pours it back over the cherries.

title:
3.
Compotte von Aprikosen.
text: once the apricots are peeled, cook 1 2 pound of sugar and skim off any foam. add the apricots and cook them in the sugar until they are tender but still hold their shape, then arrange them nicely.

title:
46.
Auflauf.
text: make a little white burnt flour, then add 1 quarter milk and 8 eggs, along with some crushed sugar, cinnamon, grated lemon peel, and salt. pour this into a buttered dish, bake it, and serve it immediately.

title:
15.
Französische Würste.
text: for 1 pound of ground pork, add 1 2 pound of finely diced bacon, along with 1 slice of bread soaked in milk, 3 egg yolks, a little nutmeg, and salt. once thoroughly mixed, stuff it into a sausage and simmer it gently in water for an hour, then brown it in butter and serve with the butter.

title:
16.
Englische Würste.
text: for two measures of bread, soak the bread in milk. take 1 pound of finely ground almonds, 1 pound of sugar, lemon zest, canella, mace, ½ pound of cubed dried plums, and 12 eggs. mix all ingredients well. fill this mixture into casings like andouillette sausages and cook in a mixture of half milk and half water until done. then, fry them in brown butter and serve.

title: 1. Kartoffel-Suppe.
text: melt some butter or lard in a pot. add a cooked, grated potato and let it steam slightly. then thin it with 1 8 liter of water and let it simmer a bit longer. cut small cubes from half a bread roll and fry them in lard. arrange the fried cubes over the soup.

title: 2. Flädchen-Suppe.
text: for 1 8 liter of water, take 1 4 egg and 1 teaspoon of flour, stir it with a little milk and let it run into boiling water. after 3 minutes, the soup is ready.

title: 3. Butter-Suppe.
text: in a small pot, melt some butter. add cubed white bread and let it steam slightly. pour in broth seasoned with salt and let it simmer for a bit longer.

title: 4. Gries-Suppe.
text: in a small pot, melt some butter. stir in a teaspoon of semolina and let it brown slightly. then pour in the soup, diluted with water or meat broth, and season with salt. serve over toasted bread. you can also whisk in an egg.

title: 5. Süße Rahm-Suppe.
text: heat 1 8 liter of milk. stir in 1 2 teaspoon of flour and 1 4 egg yolk. add sugar and cinnamon to taste. bring to a boil, then pour over cubed bread.

title: 6. Chocolade-Suppe.
text: heat 1 8 liter of milk, then stir in 1 spoonful of grated chocolate and some sugar. bring to a boil a few times, stirring constantly. now, stir in 1 2 beaten egg yolk and pour it over toasted bread.

title: 7. Aepfel-Suppe.
text: to 1 8 liter of wine and an equal amount of water, take 1 sliced apple, cored. let it simmer with sugar and a small piece of cinnamon in the water and wine until it softens. then strain it and bring it to a boil again. stir in 1 4 of an egg and serve over diced white bread.

title: 8. Nudel-Suppe.
text: combine 3 teaspoons of flour with 3 teaspoons of egg and mix thoroughly until a firm dough forms. then, place the dough on a floured board and knead it briefly. roll it out with a rolling pin into two thin sheets, and when they have dried slightly, roll them together and cut into noodles. first, bring 1 4 liter of meat broth to a boil, then add the noodles and let the soup cook for a bit longer.

title: 9. Semmelmehl-Suppe.
text: combine 1 tablespoon of grated white bread with half an egg, a little salt, and whisk into boiling meat broth. stir well, grate some nutmeg over it, and let the soup simmer for a bit longer. when serving, sprinkle with chopped chives.

title: 10. Bier-Suppe.
text: take a pinch of flour. stir it in a pan with 1 8 liter of milk, mix in 4 teaspoonfuls of egg yolk, a small piece of cinnamon, some beer, and sugar until the soup is very sweet, and let it come to a boil while stirring constantly.

title: 11. Omeletten-Suppe.
text: take 1 8 liter of milk, the same amount of flour, and 1 2 an egg. add a little salt and mix it all together into a very thin, smooth batter. then, heat a little lard in a flat pan, pour in some batter, and bake the omelet golden yellow on both sides. if you have batter left over, bake another one, roll it up, and cut it slightly wider than noodles. when the meat broth is boiling, add the noodles and let them boil only once. you can then prepare the soup.

title: 12. Milch-Suppe.
text: heat 1 8 liter of milk with sugar, cinnamon, and a little lemon juice. meanwhile, whisk 1 2 an egg and pour it into the milk, letting it cook for a bit longer. then, pour the mixture over finely sliced white or black bread.

title: 13. Eingebrannte Suppe.
text: in a small pot, melt some butter until hot, then add a spoonful of flour and roast it until dark brown. next, add a little water and stir well, then pour in the remaining water. season the soup with salt and serve it over thin slices of white or black bread.

title: 14. Butter-Klößchen.
text: cream 17 grams of butter with 1 2 an egg, adding a little salt and breadcrumbs, but not so much that the dough becomes too firm let it stand, then drop very small dumplings into simmering meat broth or water.

title: 15. Schwemmklöße.
text: in a saucepan, whisk together 1 egg, 1 spoonful of milk, and 1 spoonful of flour until well combined. melt 1 spoonful of butter in a frying pan over heat, then pour the whisked mixture into the pan and let it steam until the dough releases from the pan. once completely cool, beat in 1 egg and add a pinch of salt, mixing thoroughly. using a metal spoon, cut out elongated dumplings and drop them into boiling salted water. they are ready when they float to the surface. alternatively, you can add them directly to boiling meat broth and serve as a soup.

title: 16. Gebackene Erbsen.
text: make a fairly thick dough with 1 spoonful of flour, 1 egg, a little salt, and milk, and let the whole thing drip through a small sieve into hot lard and bake until golden yellow. then pour simmering meat broth over it.

title: 17. Fleisch-Klößchen.
text: you chop up a small piece of leftover meat with a bit of onion very finely and pour some hot lard over it. cut half a bread roll into thin slices and soak them in milk. add the meat, 3 teaspoonfuls of egg, salt, and a little pepper. form small dumplings and put them into boiling meat broth. they can also be fried in lard.

title: 18. Kartoffel-Klößchen.
text: rub a cooked potato, which is already cooked, with 4 teaspoons of egg, a little salt, and stir well. then form small dumplings, place them on a spoon, and fry them in hot lard until golden.

title: 19. Weißbrot-Klößchen.
text: soak half a stale bread roll in milk, squeeze out the excess milk, then stir in 1 egg, some salt, and chives. form small dumplings and bake them in hot rendered fat.

title: 20. Kartoffel-Klöße.
text: grate one boiled potato, then dice 1 4 of a roll and roast the cubes in rendered fat. add 1 4 of an egg, some salt, and a little flour, and form a firm dough from the mixture. shape into dumplings and cook in salted water for 5 minutes.

title: 21. Aepfel-Klöße.
text: peel an apple and remove the core, then cut it into small cubes and place them in a bowl. next, add 2 tablespoons of milk, 1 egg, and enough flour to form a dough that isn't too stiff. using a teaspoon, scoop out small dumplings from this dough and drop them into boiling water. cook for a few minutes. once they are done, place them in a bowl and pour hot melted butter over them.

title: 22. Birnen-Klöße.
text: the pears, after being cored, are prepared in the same way as the apple dumplings, but a teaspoon of grated white bread is added to the dough.

title: 23. Mehl-Klöße.
text: cut one half of a roll in thin strips and the other half into cubes. moisten the strips with 1 tablespoon of milk and sauté the cubes in lard. beat 1 2 egg with a little salt and then stir in 1 tablespoon of flour. it s good to taste a dumpling first. if it doesn't hold its shape, add a little more flour. place the dumplings in boiling salted water, 1 tablespoon at a time, and cook for 5 minutes.

title: 24. Kartoffel-Spatzen.
text: grate one cooked, cold potato. mix with 1 teaspoon of egg and 1 tablespoon of flour, and a little salt. then, drop small dumplings into boiling salted water and cook for 5 minutes. afterwards, toast 1 tablespoon of breadcrumbs in a little rendered fat and sprinkle over the dumplings when serving.

title: 25. Brot-Klößchen.
text: half a roll is grated and moistened with a little milk, then 1 2 egg, 1 tablespoon of flour, and some salt are stirred in. small dumplings are put into boiling water and simmered for 5 minutes. when serving, they are also sprinkled with toasted breadcrumbs.

title: 26. Karthäuser-Klöße.
text: rub off the outside of one bun. slice the bun into thick pieces. soak them in milk and beaten egg, coat them in the rubbed-off breadcrumbs, and fry them in hot lard on both sides until golden yellow. when serving, pour a wine or hip sauce over them.

title: 27. Mandel-Klöße.
text: sweet almonds and a few blanched bitter almonds are scalded with boiling water, peeled, and ground finely in a mortar. these are then placed in a bowl. next, add one spoonful of sugar, 1 2 spoonful of butter, 1 egg yolk, and 25 grams of grated white bread, and finally, the beaten egg whites. mix everything well together. from this mixture, form small mounds onto a baking sheet or in a buttered pan and bake until nicely golden brown in a hot oven.

title: 28. Kartoffel-Nudeln.
text: a boiled, cold potato is grated, then mixed with one good teaspoon of egg and one large tablespoon of flour and a little salt. next, form small noodles about the thickness of a pencil. heat some lard in a frying pan, lay the noodles next to each other, and bake them until golden yellow all around. when serving, sprinkle with sugar.

title: 29. Holländische Sauce.
text: melt 34 grams of butter, then add 1 weak spoonful of flour and 1 egg yolk, and let it steam slightly. next, pour in some cold water, stir vigorously, and gradually add more water, allowing the sauce to come to a boil while stirring constantly. once boiling, add 1 spoonful of vinegar and 1 small piece of sugar, and continue to cook until the sauce begins to thicken.

title: 30. Hüften-Sauce.
text: one small teaspoon of bone marrow is mixed with one small glass of wine and an equal amount of water, then brought to a simmer.

title: 31. Wein-Sauce.
text: a glass of water and an equal amount of wine are heated with a piece of sugar and a piece of cinnamon, then stirred with half a beaten egg.

title: 32. Butter-Sauce.
text: melt a small piece of butter, add 1 egg yolk, 1 spoonful of flour, a few drops of lemon juice, and a pinch of mace. pour in some meat broth and let the sauce cook for just a few moments.

title: 33. Zwiebel-Sauce.
text: take a small onion, cook it with some salt and milk into a mash. pour this over grated white bread and then cook it further with some butter and flour, after you have already added some meat broth.

title: 34. Senf-Sauce.
text: take some mustard and cook it with butter in meat broth. if you add some roasted flour, the sauce will be even better.

title: 35. Erdbeer-Sauce.
text: take some strawberries, press them through a clean cloth, cook the juice with 1 spoonful of red wine, sugar, and cinnamon, and thicken the sauce with flour that has been previously mixed with cold water.

title: 36. Himbeer-Sauce.
text: it is prepared the same way as the strawberry sauce, and so is the gooseberry sauce.

title: 37. Vanille-Sauce.
text: whisk one egg with a little milk. add about one teaspoon of ground sugar. then, heat about one cup of milk with some cinnamon and a small piece of vanilla until it simmers. remove the cinnamon and vanilla, and pour the milk into the egg while stirring constantly.

title: 38. Chocolade-Sauce.
text: melt 25 grams of grated chocolate with 1 2 cup of milk, stirring constantly, and then set aside. meanwhile, whisk 1 teaspoon of flour with 2 teaspoons of milk until smooth. add 1 2 egg yolk, then pour in the melted chocolate mixture and bring it back to a boil.

title: 39. Eine süße Speise.
text: rub off half a roll, cut the rest into small, delicate strips. grease a dish with butter, sprinkle with some raisins, arrange the strips on top. beat together some sugar and cinnamon with 1 egg, pour 1 spoonful of milk over the strips, place thin pieces of butter on top. mix a few thinly sliced almonds with a little sugar, sprinkle over the dish and bake in the oven.

title: 40. Chocolade-Koch.
text: combine 1 2 tablespoon flour and an equal amount of cream with a little butter to make a thick paste. then, whisk in 1 2 an egg, 1 tablespoon of ground sugar, and an equal amount of grated chocolate. stir the mixture into the clarified paste. bake the whole in a buttered baking dish over moderate heat.

title: 41. Schwarzbrot-Koch.
text: grease a baking dish with some lard, then sprinkle a layer of grated black bread. next, add a layer of thinly sliced apples, some sugar, wineberries, cinnamon, and if desired, ground almonds. then another layer of bread, and so on, until the dish is full. top with some butter or lard and bake.

title: 42. Pudding.
text: cream 9 grams of butter until foamy. add 9 grams of sifted sugar, 9 grams of flour, and 1 2 an egg. after stirring well, bake in a buttered form or pudding mold. a wine sauce can be served with it.

title: 43. Reis-Pudding.
text: 35 grams of rice are steeped with boiling water and left to stand for 1 4 hour, then the water is drained off, and the rice is steamed in 1 4 liter of simmering milk over low heat, covered, for 1 2 hour, after which time it should be firm, soft, and dry. now stir in 1 2 tablespoon of flour several times, stir in 26 grams of butter, and then remove it from the heat and let it cool. next, add 26 grams of sugar and 1 1 2 egg yolks. beat everything together until frothy, add a little vanilla and lemon zest, and fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites. pour the mixture into a buttered mold and simmer in boiling water for 1 2 hour. serve with wine sauce.

title: 44. Englischer Pudding.
text: rub the outside of half a roll. cut the inside into fine strips and moisten them with hot milk. then, cream 17 grams of butter until fluffy, add 6 teaspoonfuls of egg, 6 ground almonds, 9 grams of sugar, and some currants. mix everything thoroughly with the moistened bread. now, grease a pudding mold with butter or lard, pour the mixture into it, seal the mold tightly, and hang it in boiling water for 1 2 hour.

title: 45. Brot-Pudding.
text: beat an egg lightly with 15 grams of sugar, then add 136 grams of ground almonds, as much soaked breadcrumbs, and grate in some lemon zest. once everything is well combined, whip some egg whites until stiff peaks form, and fold them into the mixture. pour into a buttered pudding mold and proceed as with the previous pudding.

title: 46. Chocolade-Pudding.
text: beat 30 grams of finely ground sugar with 1 egg yolk until frothy. add 5 grams of flour, 5 grams of finely ground chocolate, and the whipped egg white. mix everything well and proceed as with the previous pudding.

title: 47. Citronen-Pudding.
text: cream 15 grams of butter until light and fluffy. then, whisk in 1 egg yolk, the zest of a lemon, 15 grams of sugar, and the juice of a lemon. place the mixture over heat and bring it to a boil, stirring constantly. let it cool, then add whipped egg whites and prepare the pudding as before.

title: 48. Gebackener Pudding.
text: cut 1 2 a roll into fine slices, moisten them with a little boiling milk, and press them firmly together. meanwhile, melt 15 grams of butter gently, beat in one egg yolk, a little ground cinnamon, grated lemon zest, and 9 ground almonds. mix everything together well for 1 4 of an hour. beat one egg white into stiff peaks, and gently fold it into the mixture. bake the pudding in a buttered and breadcrumb-coated pudding mold.

title: 49. Gebackene Nudeln.
text: make a noodle dough with 1 2 an egg, 3 coffee spoons of flour, and a little salt. roll it out on a board and cut it into wide strips. cook the strips in 1 8 liter of milk with a little sugar until thick, and set aside to cool. in a pan, heat some butter. add the noodles and turn them frequently with a flat spoon until they are nicely yellow. season with sugar and cinnamon.

title: 50. Auflauf.
text: whisk together 1 tablespoon of flour with a little milk until smooth, then stir in 1 2 an egg and another 1 tablespoon of milk, and season with salt. grease a pan with some lard and bake the mixture. if you mix in a finely chopped apple, it's even better.

title: 51. Aepfelmännlein.
text: to 1 4 cup finely breadcrumbs, add a little milk, let it soften slightly, then mix in 1 4 egg and 1 finely chopped apple, and salt lightly. heat a little lard in a frying pan, pour in the mixture, and let it bake slowly.

title: 52. Kapuziner-Auflauf.
text: rub off the crust from 1 4 of a roll, slice the inside into thin pieces, place them in a baking dish, pour a small spoonful of milk over them, let it cook until dry, and then allow to cool. beat 9 grams of butter lightly, add the remaining bread, beat in one small egg, a little cinnamon, sugar, and currants. fill the mixed mixture into a baking dish and bake in a roasting pan.

title: 53. Kirschen-Auflauf.
text: pit 1 handful of cherries. then take 1 8 liter of flour, add some milk, and stir it into a dough. add 1 egg and a little salt, and mix well. add the cherries along with some sugar and cinnamon, and bake the bake in a baking dish greased with butter.

title: 54. Zwetschgen-Auflauf
text: to prepare it like a cherry bake.

title: 55. Brot-Auflauf
text: boil 1 8 liter of milk. rub a grated roll into a thick paste. then, cream 68 grams of butter until fluffy, gradually adding 6 coffee spoons of egg, 9 grams of crushed sugar, some crushed almonds, and measured lemon zest along with the paste. grease a frying pan with butter, pour in the mixture, and bake.

title: 56. Chocolade-Auflauf.
text: cream 17 grams of butter until light and fluffy. add 25 grams of sugar and 1 1 2 egg yolks, then mix well. stir in 17 grams of grated chocolate. meanwhile, cut 50 grams of white bread into thin slices and soak in milk. squeeze out the excess milk and add the bread to the mixture. beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold them into the batter. grease an ovenproof dish with butter, pour in the mixture, and bake slowly.

title: 57. Nürnberger Lebkuchen-Brei.
text: rub one piece of nuremberg gingerbread, add some wine and water, and let it cook. if it's not sweet enough, sweeten it with some sugar.

title: 58. Aepfel-Brei (Muß, Purée).
text: peel one large apple and thinly slice it, then cook it gently with a little sugar, a pinch of cinnamon, and a bit of water and dried cranberries.

title: 59. Zwetschgen-Brei.
text: ripe sweet plums are pitted and cooked gently with sugar and cinnamon.

title: 60. Mehl-Brei.
text: whisk 1 tablespoon of flour and 2 tablespoons of milk together, slowly, until smooth. then, cook the mixture in a copper pan until it thickens.

title: 61. Milchreis.
text: take 3 teaspoons of rice, wash it, and set it over the heat with one cup of water. when the rice is soft, drain the water, then add salt, sugar, and milk. let it come to a boil again, then pour the mixture into a bowl. sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon, and arrange small raisins around the edge.

title: 62. Citronen-Brei.
text: the finely weighed zest of a lemon, a pinch of flour is stirred smooth with some wine, then 1 2 an egg, a little more wine and water are added, along with a bit of sugar, and the whole thing is allowed to come to a boil, stirring constantly. now add some lemon juice and, if not sweet enough, some more sugar.

title:
63. Schwarzbeer-Brei.
(Heidelbeer-Brei.)
text: wash the blackberries and cook them thickly with some grated and toasted black bread and sugar.

title: 64. Mohnpillen.
text: grind 1 to 2 tablespoons of poppy seeds in a mortar. add 3 tablespoons of milk, a little sugar, and some grated white bread, and mix everything thoroughly. transfer to a bowl, smooth the top, sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon, and serve with small anise crumbs.

title: 65. Mandel-Brei.
text: in a pan, melt 1 piece of butter and toast one teaspoon of flour until golden. add 8 blanched, finely weighed almonds. whisk 4 teaspoons of egg with 9 grams of ground sugar and 1 8 liter of milk until smooth. add the toasted flour and cook the whole mixture, stirring constantly.

title: 66. Gestürzter Kartoffelbrei.
text: four peeled potatoes are sliced thinly, placed in a pot, and covered with water to halfway up the potatoes. set over the fire and let the potatoes cook until soft. then, mash the potatoes with a wooden spoon into a purée, season with salt and pepper, and add a small piece of butter, mixing everything well. next, grease a metal or porcelain mold with butter, sprinkle it with grated breadcrumbs, add the purée, and bake the whole thing in a hot oven until heated through.

title: 67. Haschee.
text: chop a bit of leftover roast with some onion very finely and mix it with a spoonful of grated, in lard-roasted white bread. pour the whole thing with some hot meat broth, add vinegar and salt, and let it cook.

title:
68. Uebriggebliebenes Rindfleisch
zuzubereiten.
text: slice the meat thinly and brown it slightly in butter. add 1 tablespoon of vinegar and 2 tablespoons of meat broth. then, add some lemon zest, salt, pepper, and onion, and let it come to a boil together.

title: 69. Abgebräuntes Rindfleisch.
text: slice leftover beef into thin strips, season with salt and pepper. heat some rendered fat or butter, then add the strips and brown them on both sides. you can also whisk half an egg with a little water and stir it into the cooked meat, which will make it even more flavorful.

title: 70. Geröstete Kartoffel.
text: in a pan, heat some butter or lard. meanwhile, slice some boiled, still warm potatoes, season them with salt, sprinkle with caraway seeds, and fry them in the hot lard. you can also use pepper instead of caraway seeds.

title: 71. Omelettes.
text: for 1 teaspoon of flour, take 1 4 of an egg, a little salt, and milk to make a thin batter. heat a small amount of lard in an omelet pan, pour some of the batter in, let it spread to form neat, round shapes, and cook until golden yellow on both sides.

title: 72. Gefüllte Omelettes
text: once all the bases are prepared, spread a little jam on each, roll them up, place them on a small plate, and sprinkle with sugar.

title: 73. Milchspätzle.
text: cream 17 grams of butter until it is frothy, then add 1 2 an egg and 1 tablespoon of flour. add a little milk to form a proper sparrow dough, and salt it slightly. then, grease a small pot with butter, add 1 8 liter of milk and bring it to a boil. using a spoon, drop small dumplings into the boiling milk and cook until done.

title: 74. Omelettes mit Aepfeln.
text: first, make an omelet batter as in recipe number 71. peel one apple and finely shred it, then stir it into the batter. bake spoonfuls of the batter and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon while still warm.

title: 75. Omelettes in der Milch.
text: the omelets were baked, then rolled and placed in a bowl. 1 8 liter of milk is heated with sugar and cinnamon, the omelets are poured with it, and the whole mixture is brought back to a boil.

title: 76. Waffeln.
text: one piece of butter, about the size of a walnut, is whipped until foamy, then 1 4 of an egg is added. next, 17 grams of flour, a little salt, and lukewarm milk, like an omelet batter, are stirred in. now, the waffles are baked in a waffle iron that has been coated on both sides with lard until golden yellow.

title: 77. Untereinander.
text: whisk together 1 8 liter of flour and 1 8 liter of milk, then add one egg and a little salt. pour this batter into hot lard and cook, stirring constantly, until golden brown.

title: 78. Spritzküchlein.
text: in 1 8 liter of milk, scalded with a little sugar and butter, gradually stir in white flour until the dough is very thick. then add 1 2 an egg, pipe the dough into hot lard, and bake until golden yellow.

title: 79. Fastnachts-Küchlein.
text: beat half an egg, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and an equal amount of sweet or sour cream with flour. roll 2 loaves very thinly, place the 2 cakes on top of each other, roll out again, then cut the pastry into small squares and bake until golden brown in hot lard.

title: 80. Schneeballen.
text: combine 1 2 an egg, 1 teaspoon of sweet milk, a little salt, and a bit of butter with flour to form a firm dough, then shape into small cookies. make cuts in them, not too close together, nor quite all the way through. then take a strip with a skewer, leave the next one, take the next one again, and so on. fry them in hot lard until nicely golden yellow.

title: 81. Aepfel-Küchlein.
text: a small apple is sliced, peeled, and cored, then dipped in an omelet batter and fried golden yellow in hot lard, and finally sprinkled with sugar.

title: 82. Chocoladezwetschgen.
text: wash 35 grams of dried plums, simmer them gently in water, then drain. remove the pits. heat 9 grams of butter or lard. add the plums and roast them slightly, stirring constantly to prevent burning. mix 9 grams of grated chocolate with 6 grams of sugar. while the plums are still warm, toss them in the chocolate mixture and arrange them neatly on a plate.

title: 83. Sträubelein.
text: take 1 2 tablespoon flour, 1 2 egg, 1 teaspoon sour cream, a little salt, and enough milk to make the batter flow. then, drop it in a round shape through a funnel or perforated spoon into hot lard and bake the strips until golden yellow. sprinkle with sugar.

title: 84. Hirschhörnchen.
text: a small piece of butter is thoroughly mixed with 1 egg, 20 grams of sugar, and 60 grams of flour, small wreaths or rings are formed from this, and they are baked in hot lard. they are generously sprinkled with sugar.

title: 85. Butterteig.
text: sift together 17 grams of flour and a walnut-sized amount of fat. add 1 small teaspoon of egg and a few drops of milk.

title: 86. Süßer Butterteig.
text: 17 grams of butter or lard, 1 teaspoon of sugar, 1 1 2 teaspoons of flour, 1 teaspoon of milk, all stirred together and combined.

title: 87. Käferszipfelein.
text: melt 9 grams of butter, 1 spoonful of flour, 17 grams of sugar, and 1 2 egg, then form small spätzle. bake in hot rendered fat and sprinkle with sugar.

title: 88. Versoffene Jungfern.
text: beat 1 egg with 1 tablespoon of sugar until frothy, then add 1 tablespoon of flour. once everything is well mixed, add the whipped egg whites. with a small spoon, form small dumplings from the dough and fry them golden brown in hot lard. when done, make a wine sauce with a glass of white wine, some sugar, cinnamon, and 1 2 clove. after the sauce has cooked, pour it over the dumplings and serve.

title: 89. Gelbe Rüblein.
text: melt 17 grams of lard. stir well, then add 1 2 egg and 1 teaspoon of sugar. add flour until a dough can be formed into small dumplings. these dumplings must be continuously stirred in a pan with hot lard using a spatula. while still warm, make a small opening on top and stuff with chopped fresh yellow beet.

title:
90. Aepfel- oder Zwetschgenkuchen
von Butterteig.
text: make a puff pastry and roll it out into a circle. top it with fresh or cooked plums or apples if using apples, create a lattice pattern with strips of rolled-out dough and bake the cake in the oven.

title: 91. Propheten-Kuchen.
text: 9 grams of butter, 1 2 egg and 17 grams of sugar are stirred for 5 minutes, then enough flour is added to form a rather firm dough, which is rolled out, spread with butter on both sides, and baked in the oven.

title: 92. Käse-Kuchen.
text: roll out a puff pastry. then, combine 2 tablespoons of grated cheese and 1 teaspoon of flour, stirring until smooth. add 17 grams of melted butter, 1 2 an egg, 1 1 2 tablespoons of milk, some cranberries, and sugar, mixing everything well together. spread the mixture over the puff pastry that has been brushed with lard and bake it in the oven.

title: 93. Baumkuchen von Brot.
text: cut off a loaf-high piece of bread, remove the crust, and cut a pointed cone in the shape of a sugar cone from the remaining bread. now, in a glass, combine white wine, 3 tablespoons of sugar, and two cloves, and bring to a simmer. slowly pour it over the bread form, ensuring it soaks in thoroughly. what drains out at the bottom is poured back over the top, until the bread cake is well saturated but not too soft. then, sprinkle it with grated chocolate until the outside is dry again cut slivered almonds into elongated pieces, decorate the cake with them, and sprinkle the whole thing with finely sifted sugar.

title: 94. Kartoffel-Torte.
text: a small boiled potato is grated. then 3-4 almonds are peeled and finely ground. to this, 1 tablespoon of ground sugar is mixed with 1 strong teaspoon of egg and combined with the almonds. finally, the potatoes are added. the mixture is baked in a baking dish greased with lard and sprinkled with bread.

title: 95. Blitz-Torte.
text: take one egg, as much finely ground sugar as the egg weighs, and an equal amount of butter. then add as much fine flour as half an egg weighs, and a little grated lemon zest. rub the butter lightly, add the sugar, then add the egg gradually. after stirring everything vigorously for a while, mix in the finely sifted flour. pour this mixture into a buttered and breadcrumb-strewn cake tin or baking dish and bake the cake in a moderately heated oven until golden brown.

title: 96. Sand-Torte.
text: cream 17 grams of butter, then add 1 4 of an egg, 1 tablespoon of ground sugar, and 2 tablespoons of flour, stirring slowly until combined. do not grease the baking pan too heavily, and bake the mixture slowly.

title: 97. Sand-Törtchen.
text: cream 35 grams of butter with 1 2 an egg, then vigorously mix in 25 grams of ground sugar, a little lemon zest, and flour. drop small spoonfuls of the mixture onto a floured baking sheet and bake until golden yellow.

title: 98. Biscuit-Torte.
text: beat 17 grams of sifted sugar with 1 2 an egg and 1 2 a yolk until light and fluffy, then stir in 21 grams of fine flour. pour the mixture into a mold coated with butter and bake.

title: 99. Mandel-Torte.
text: to 34 grams of peeled, ground almonds, take the same amount of sugar and 1 egg, mix the mixture well, and bake it in a buttered cake tin.

title: 100. Rahm-Torte.
text: make a simple sweet shortcrust pastry. butter a round, shallow cake tin, line it with the pastry. whisk 1 8 liter of cream with 1 2 an egg, 9 grams of sugar, a little cinnamon, and grated lemon zest. pour this mixture into the tin and bake the cake in the oven.

title: 101. Aepfel-Torte.
text: a peeled half apple is sliced thinly and sprinkled with sugar and cinnamon. a grated bread roll is soaked in milk 17 grams of butter is creamed until fluffy, then 1 2 an egg and 9 grams of blanched, ground almonds and the same amount of sugar are mixed together. next, the apples and the squeezed-out bread are folded in. a cake pan is greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs, and the mixture is poured in and baked in a hot oven.

title: 102. Becken-Brot.
text: cream together 34 grams of butter, 1 2 egg, 34 grams of sugar, and 68 grams of flour until smooth, then knead into a dough. from this dough, form pretzels, loaves, pointed rolls, etc., brush them with egg yolk, and bake them on a floured baking sheet.

title: 103. Brief-Couverts.
text: make a thin sheet of puff pastry, cut it into square pieces, and fill these with apple or plum purée. fold the four corners of each piece together. place a small red ribbon in the center instead of a seal. brush the pastries with egg yolk and bake them on a flour-dusted baking sheet.

title: 104. Wiener Plätzchen.
text: beat the egg white of one egg until it forms stiff peaks. add 34 grams of sugar and continue beating for a while. add a little grated lemon zest, a little lemon juice, and 15 grams of flour, mixing well. then, using a small spoon, drop small cookies onto a buttered baking sheet and bake until golden yellow.

title: 105. Anis-Kräpflein.
text: from 17 grams of flour, 9 grams, ½ loth butter, 1 teaspoon of egg, and a little anise, prepare a dough. let it rest for ¼ hour, roll it out to about a knife-edge thickness, and cut out small round cookies with the tip of a finger. brush them with egg yolk and anise, and bake them on a flour-dusted sheet until golden yellow.

title: 106. Zimmt-Plätzchen.
text: set aside 17 grams of coarsely chopped, unpeeled almonds. in a small bowl, whisk the egg white from 1 2 egg with 17 grams of finely sifted sugar until frothy. add a pinch of cinnamon and the almonds. drop small mounds of the mixture onto wafers and bake the cookies until golden yellow.

title: 107. Dotter-Plätzchen.
text: whisk 2 egg yolks, 34 grams of sugar, and 68 grams of flour. sprinkle a baking sheet with anise and flour, place small cookies on it, and bake.

title: 108. Gebackene S.
text: whisk 2 egg yolks, 15 grams sifted sugar, 27 grams butter, and 34 grams flour together well. shape a narrow strip of the dough, cut it into small pieces, roll each piece lengthwise by hand, and form them into s shapes. brush with egg yolk, sprinkle with sifted sugar, and bake on a buttered baking sheet.

title: 109. Butterzeug.
text: cream together 35 grams of butter and 35 grams of sugar until light and fluffy. then add 1 4 of an egg, 1 teaspoon of arrack, and enough flour until the dough can be rolled out nicely with a rolling pin. first, sprinkle flour on a pastry board, place the dough on it, and knead it well. then roll it out to a knife-thickness with the rolling pin and cut out small shapes with butter molds. place these on a baking sheet and bake in the oven until a rich golden-yellow color. knead and roll out the scraps together repeatedly until there is no dough left. once they are done, sprinkle them with mixed sugar and cinnamon.

title: 110. Blitz.
text: cream 17 grams of butter with 1 egg yolk until frothy, then add 17 grams of sugar and the same amount of flour. beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold them into the batter. spread the batter evenly, about 1 8 inch thick, onto a buttered baking sheet, sprinkle with raisins, and bake in a preheated oven. once the pastry has set slightly, remove it from the oven, cut it into shifted squares, and finish baking.

title: 111. Anis-Schnitten.
text: beat half an egg with 17 grams of sugar. then add measured lemon zest, 17 grams of ground almonds, some cinnamon, anise to taste, and 17 grams of flour, mixing well together. place the dough on a pastry board, form it into a roll, cut small pieces from it, place them on a buttered baking sheet, and bake until golden yellow.

title: 112. Anisschnitten auf andere Art.
text: beat 3 4 egg and 35 grams of sugar until frothy, then add a little lemon zest, 1 teaspoon of anise, and 35 grams of flour, mixing everything well. now, roll into small sausages and place them on a buttered baking sheet. bake in a cooled oven until golden yellow.

title: 113. Chocolade-Häuflein.
text: combine 5 grams of chocolate with 26 grams of sifted sugar beat the egg white from half an egg until stiff peaks form, quickly fold it into the mixture, drop small mounds onto a wafer, and bake in a moderately cool oven.

title: 114. Chocoladeplätzchen.
text: whip 1 1 2 egg whites with 35 grams of sugar. combine with 70 grams of chocolate and 70 grams of almonds. form small balls from the mixture and place them on oblaten wafers. dry in a warm oven.

title: 115. Macronen.
text: beat the egg white of 1 2 egg into a light snow. add 17 grams of sifted sugar and an equal amount of blanched, ground almonds. beat vigorously for 20 minutes. form small cookies from this mixture onto a wafer and bake in a not-too-hot oven.

title: 116. Nußplätzchen.
text: beat 35 grams of sugar with 1 4 of an egg until frothy. add 20 chopped walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon, mixing well. roll the dough into small balls, place them on oblaten, and bake slowly in the oven.

title: 117. Citronenplätzchen.
text: one-quarter egg and one-half egg yolk are thoroughly beaten with 35 grams of sugar, then some lemon zest and 35 grams of flour are added. small cookies are formed from the dough and placed on a buttered baking sheet and baked slowly.

title: 118. Chocolademacronen.
text: combine 35 grams of almonds with 1 teaspoon of egg white. place the mixture in a bowl and stir in 9 grams of grated chocolate, 35 grams of sugar, and 1 4 of beaten egg white. form the mixture into small balls, place them on wafers, and bake in a moderately warm oven.

title: 119. Chocolade.
text: heat 1 8 liter of milk to a boil, stirring constantly. add 17 grams of grated chocolate, and let it simmer gently while continuing to stir. then, pour it into a jug where you have previously whisked 1 2 an egg.

title: 120. Eier-Milch.
text: in 1 4 liter of milk, add a little sugar, vanilla, or cinnamon and bring it to a boil. then, whisk in 1 egg yolk, stirring it very slowly with the milk, and continue to heat over the fire while stirring constantly.

title: 121. Mandel-Milch.
text: grind 17 grams of washed almonds finely in a mortar, pour 1 4 liter of water over them, press the mixture through a cloth, and add sugar to taste.

title: 122. Reformirter Thee.
text: bring 1 8 liter of milk to a boil, then add a tiny pinch of tea, some cinnamon, lemon peel, and as much sugar as you like. after it has simmered a bit, whisk in 1 egg yolk, pour the boiled milk through a sieve, slowly over the yolk, and fill into a pitcher.

title: 123. Cheaudeau.
text: you boil 1 8 liter of wine with 34 grams of finely weighed sugar, the zest of a lemon, and a little lemon juice. in a pot, you beat an egg and stir it slowly with the wine. now, the whole mixture must be stirred vigorously, but not allowed to boil. it must be very frothy when you pour it into the cups.

title: 124. Punsch.
text: pour 1 8 liter of tea over 34 grams of sugar, which is in a bowl. add 1 tablespoon of arrack or rum and a little lemon juice. stir everything together and the punch is ready to serve.

title: 125. Roter Punsch.
text: dissolve 35 grams of sugar with 1 tablespoon of arrack and warm it. then add 2 tablespoons of warm red wine and an equal amount of boiling water, and the punch is ready serve hot.

title: 126. Warmes Bier.
text: a measure of beer is brought to a boil with a small piece of rock candy and poured over a lightly beaten egg.

title: 127. Warmes Bier auf andere Art.
text: heat 1 8 liter of beer with sugar, a little cinnamon, and lemon peel. whisk in half an egg, stir into the simmering beer, and let it steep for a bit.

title: 128. Eier-Crême.
text: beat one egg white and 15 grams of sugar until foamy. cook with 1 2 teaspoon of flour and 1 4 liter of milk, then set aside to cool. stir the flour with a little cold milk beforehand.

title: 129. Mandel-Crême.
text: grind 30 grams of sweet and 15 grams of bitter almonds with a few drops of water, combine this paste with 1 4 liter of milk, squeeze in some lemon juice, sweeten to taste, beat everything until frothy, strain through a sieve, fill glasses with the liquid and top with the froth.

title: 130. Aepfel-Mark.
text: bake three apples in the oven, then peel and core them and place them in a bowl. add some vanilla and sugar, plus 1 4 of an egg white, and beat it vigorously with a wooden spoon until frothy. arrange the whole thing on a platter, garnish the pulp with colorful sugar decorations from the confectioner, and serve. it is excellent.

title: 131. Rühreier.
text: take 2 eggs, whisk them with a little salt, pepper, and milk. heat a piece of butter in an omelet pan, pour the eggs in, and stir them over the heat until they begin to set.

title: 132. Ochsenaugen.
text: take 2 eggs, pour them into a pan with hot lard and let them fry undisturbed you can cut the finished eggs into small, round pieces.

title: 133. Eierkuchen.
text: take 1 2 roll, slice it into thin pieces, pour a little milk over it, add 1 egg and some salt, and mix everything together. heat a generous amount of lard in an omelet pan, spread the mixture in it, and bake it until nicely browned on both sides.

title: 134. Eierkraut.
text: melt 15 grams of butter in a pan and brown a spoonful of grated bread and 1 teaspoon of flour in it. then whisk 2 eggs with 1 4 liter of milk, pour it over the toasted flour, and let it come to a boil while stirring constantly. finally, sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.

title: 135. Kartoffel-Salat.
text: boiled potatoes are peeled while still hot and sliced, then salted and thoroughly mixed with oil. next, add some vinegar and sliced onions, and stir well again. sprinkle the salad with pepper and chopped chives.

title: 136. Gurken-Salat.
text: the peeled and sliced cucumbers are sprinkled with salt and left to sit for a while. then they are lightly squeezed, seasoned with a bit more salt, and mixed with oil. vinegar is added, and after stirring well, pepper and chives are sprinkled on top.

title: 137. Rettig-Salat.
text: it is prepared the same as the cucumber salad.

title: 138. Bohnen-Salat.
text: take some beans, cook them until soft, remove the fibers, chop them smaller and then prepare them like potato salad.

title: 139. Endivien-Salat.
text: the endives are cleaned of their outer green leaves and the inner yellow leaves are finely cut lengthwise and washed after the water has drained in a sieve, the salad is seasoned with salt, oil, and vinegar and sweetened with sugar as desired.

title: 140. Rote Rüben-Salat.
text: beets, with their leaves not trimmed too neatly, are cooked tender in salted water, peeled, and sliced. these are immediately sprinkled with salt and pepper, then drizzled with vinegar and oil, and mixed together.

title: 141. Gebackene Sardellen.
text: for 3 or 4 sardines, per child, place them on a wooden platter and run fresh water over them. then, cut off the tails and open them along the belly with a knife. remove the long bones and rinse the sardines a bit more. now, sprinkle them with flour and bake them golden yellow in hot lard.

title:
142. Junge Gänschen aus Wallnüssen
bereitet.
text: take good, large walnuts, carefully remove them from their shells. to ensure they remain whole, cut them in half with a knife and blanch them in hot water. peel off the yellow skin, and you will have small, charming little ducks. arrange these on a plate and pour cooked sugar over them to create a glaze. now arrange them in a circle on a dish and decorate the edges with finely sliced apple slices.

title: 143. Mausebraten.
text: take a piece of ham, pound it quite tender with a knife, cut pieces about the size of coins from it, roll them in beaten egg yolk, sprinkle them with grated breadcrumbs, and bake them golden brown in hot lard.

title: 144. Gekochte Zuckerglasur.
text: 70 grams of fine sugar is moistened with one tablespoon of water and placed over low heat until the sugar is warm and begins to melt on the side. the glaze can then be immediately used to cover cakes and pastries.

title:
<<55>>
Register.
text: to make a fine almond milk take sweet almonds, a pound. soak them in water overnight. then drain them and grind them finely with fresh water, using a quarter of their weight in water. strain the milk through a linen cloth. add a quarter of a pound of fresh butter, and stir it in well. season with a little sugar and cinnamon. heat it gently, but do not boil.

title:
