Nachtrag.
Neue Kochrezepte:
text: apple cake ingredients 6 medium-sized apples 125g butter 125g sugar 3 eggs 125g plain flour 1 teaspoon baking powder 1 2 teaspoon cinnamon a pinch of salt butter and flour for the baking tin optional raisins or chopped nuts instructions preheat the oven to 180 c. grease and flour a round baking tin. peel, core, and quarter the apples. cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the cinnamon and salt. sift the flour and baking powder into the mixture and gently fold in until just combined. if desired, fold in raisins or chopped nuts. pour the batter into the prepared baking tin and arrange the apple quarters

title:
Shakespear theatralische Werke. Aus dem 
Englischen übersetzt von Herrn Wieland,
4 und 5ter Band, groß 8. Zürch, bey Orell,
Geßner und Compagnie, 1764. 4ter Band
hält 31 und 5ter Band 27 Bogen.
text: one should, by legal right, not translate a man like shakespeare. without knowledge of the english language, english customs, and english humor, one can find little enjoyment in the majority of his works therefore, whoever understands the above should read this excellent writer in english, and whoever does not understand it should rightly not read him at all. the present translation will certainly give rise to many poor judgments about shakespeare, and to even poorer imitations. moreover, we cannot overlook the fact that at many points it seems as though mr. w. has not sufficiently studied his author his style is also very rigid and full of provincial words, so that his translation, which is otherwise quite faithful, is rarely pleasant to read.

title: (PRAESCRIPTIO)
text: thus far, victor, bishop of the church of tunnensis, has arranged the order of the preceding years we have taken care to add those that followed.

title: (INTRODUCTIO)
text: after eusebius, bishop of the church of caesarea, jerome, throughout the world known presbyter, and also prosper, a religious man, and victor, bishop of the african church of tunnena, who were seen to have woven together, with great brevity and diligence, the history of almost all the nations, and have brought it down to our time, transmitting the events of the world and the deeds to our knowledge, we, in the aid of our lord jesus christ, those things which have been done in our times, partly because we have foreseen them with the faith of our eyes, and partly because we have learned them from the accounts of faithful people, have endeavored to transmit to posterity in a concise style. 1. therefore, in the fifteenth indiction, as has been said, after the death of justinian, justin the younger, his nephew, is declared emperor of the romans. 2. justin

title: ANNO II MEMORATI PRINCIPIS //a.568\\
text: in the royal cities of aetherius and addaeus, patricians, while attempting to bring about justin's death by poison rather than sword, were discovered and ordered to be punished with capital sentence the first was devoured by wild beasts, the second perished in flames. justin, son of a german patrician and nephew of emperor justin, was killed in alexandria as part of sophia the august's faction. at this time, athanagild, king of the goths in hispania, met his end, and liuva was advanced to the throne in his stead.

title: ANNO III IVSTINI IMP. //a.569\\
text: the garamantes, desiring to associate with the peace of the roman republic and the faith of christians, request those who can obtain both immediately. theodorus, the prefect of africa, was killed by the moors. the tribe of the macucaritans received the christian faith during this time. in the third year of this reign, liuuigildus, a german, while the brother of the king of the liuvians still survived, was established in the kingdom of hispania citerior, marries the abandoned gosuintha of athanagild, and wonderfully restores the province of the goths, which had previously been diminished due to the rebellion of various factions, to its former boundaries.

title:
ANNO IV IVSTINI IMP. QVI EST LIVVIGILDI REGIS
SECVNDVS ANNVS //a.570\\
text: teoctistus, military commander of the province of africa, perished after being defeated in war by the moors. liuwigild, king, devastates the lands of bastetania and the city of malacita with repelled troops, and returns victorious to his throne. justinian, emperor, through tiberius, the count of the excubitors, instigates war against the abars in thrace, and tiberius returns victorious to constantinople. in the province of gallaecia, miro is made king of the suebi after theudomir.

title:
ANNO V IVSTINI IMP. QVI EST III LIVVIGILDI REGIS
ANNVS //a.571\\
text: the emperor justinian repelled the persians and secured the roman provinces of armenia and iberia. the persian emperor prepares war through his generals. amabilis, the master of military affairs in africa, is killed by the moors. liuuigildus, king, seizes the strongest city of asidona through the treachery of a certain framidanci at night, and, having slain the soldiers, restores the rights of the goths to the aforementioned city. donatus, abbot of the monastery of seruitani, is renowned as a celebrated worker of miracles.

title:
ANNO VI IVSTINI IMP. QVI EST LIVVIGILDI REGIS
{70} IIII ANNVS //a.572\\
text: the kingdom of the gepids came to an end, and king cuniemundus, defeated in battle by the lombards, fell on the field, and his treasures were brought whole to emperor justinian in constantinople by trasaricus, bishop of the arian sect, and reptilanus, cuniemundus nephew. king leovigild captured corduba, a city long held by the goths, at night, slaughtering his enemies and establishing his own dominion, recovering many cities and castles through the multitude of slain rural inhabitants and restoring the goths' rule. king miro of the suebi waged war against the runcones. dominus, the bishop of helena, was considered renowned.

title: ANNO VII IVSTINI IMP. QVI EST LIVVIGILDI V ANNVS //a.573\\
text: the king of the lombards, aluinus, is killed at night by his own men, influenced by his wife however, his treasures, along with the queen, fall under the control of the roman state, and the lombards remain without a king and treasure. at this time, king liuva met his end, and all of hispania and narbonensian gaul came under the kingdom and power of liuvigild. emperor justin is shaken by a severe illness, which some attributed to a great commotion, while others believed it to be the harassment of demons. in the royal city, mortality from a groin plague flared up, and we witnessed many thousands of people dying. king liuvigild enters sabaria, devastates sappos, and restores the province to his control, making his two sons, hermenegild and reccared, who were born from his deceased wife, co-rulers of the kingdom. emissaries from the macc

title: ANNO VIII IVSTINI, QVI EST LIVVIGILDI VI ANNVS //a.574\\
text: the romans break the peace treaties with the persians and, having conquered the powerful city of daras through a congress, enter the remembered city with a large multitude of roman soldiers and lay it waste. at this time, king liuvigild enters cantabria, kills the invaders, seizes amaya, plunders their wealth, and brings the province back under his control. justinian the emperor makes tiberius, whom we mentioned above as the count of the guards, caesar and shortly thereafter invests him with imperial dignity, designating him as the leader of the republic. on the first day of this tiberius caesar s reign, he is struck by an inguinal wound in the royal city.

title:
ANNO VIIII IVSTINI IMP. QVI EST LIVVIGILDI REGIS
VII ANNVS //a.575\\
text: the persian emperor, with an excessive army, advances to devastate roman territories. to this, justinian, roman military commander and master of soldiers of the east, appointed by tiberius, prepares for war and, meeting in a fierce battle in the fields between the daras and nisivians, having with him the strongest tribes who speak the barbarian language called herinians, overcomes the aforementioned emperor. with his army turned to flight, he penetrates the emperor's camps and, victorious, justinian ravages the borders of persian provinces, directing their spoils for a triumph to constantinople, among other things, twenty-four elephants which displayed a great spectacle for the romans in the royal city. indeed, a multitude of spoils from the roman persians were sold at a very high price for the public treasury. liuigild, king of the goths, enters the mountains of aregenses, leads aspidium, the elder of the place, with his wife and children captive, and brings his wealth

title:
ANNO X IVSTINI IMP. QVI EST LIVVIGILDI REGIS VIII
ANNVS //a.576\\
text: 1. justinian's general, badurius, is defeated in italy by the lombards, and shortly thereafter meets his end there. 2. the roman, anagast's son, patricius, the master of the military of the suebi people, captured the king of the suans alive, and brought him to constantinople along with his treasure, wife, and sons, returning his province to roman dominion. 3. liuuigildus troubles the borders of the suebi in gallaecia, and at the request of king mirone through envoys, granted them peace for a short time. 4. the slavs invade many roman cities in thrace, leaving them depopulated and deserted. 5. the abares harass the coast by surprise and are very troublesome to ships sailing along the thracian coast. 6. after benedict, pelagius the younger is ordained bishop of the roman church and presides for eleven years. 1

title:
ANNO ERGO I IMPERII TIBERII, QVI EST LIVVIGILDI
IX REGNI ANNVS
text: the thracians besiege abare and the royal city from a long wall. liuuigildus, king, enters orospeda and occupies the cities and castles of that province, making it his own province. not long after, the local farmers rebelling are suppressed by the goths, and afterwards orospeda is held entirely by the goths.

title:
ANNO II TIBERII IMPERATORIS QVI EST LIVVIGILDI 
REGIS AN. X //a.578\\
text: gennadius, master of the military in africa, devastates mauros, garmulem, the very strongest king, who had already slain three generals, previously named, of the roman army, overcomes him in war and slays the king himself with his sword. tiberius establishes mauricius, count of the watchmen, master of the military in the east, and sends him to confront the persians. the romans wage a lamentable war against the lombards in italy. liuuigildus, king, having extinguished tyrants on all sides and overcome the invaders of hispania, retired with the people to his own rest, and founded a city in celtiberia, named after his son, which is now called recopolis he established privileges for the new city, adorning it with remarkable works both in the walls and in the suburbs. john, a priest of the church of emerita, is considered renowned.

title:
ANNO III TIBERII IMP. QVI EST LIVVIGILDI REGIS 
XI ANNVS //a.579\\
text: the borders of thrace are being pushed back, and parts of greece and pannonia are occupied. king liuvigild marries his son hermenegild to the daughter of king sisebert of the franks and grants him a portion of the region to rule. therefore, liuvigild, while enjoying a peaceful reign and the security of his enemies, is disturbed by domestic strife. for in the same year, his son hermenegild, taking power with the faction of queen goswintha, initiates a rebellion in the city of hispalis, and incites other cities and fortresses to rebel against his father. this caused the province of hispania greater destruction than the attacks of its enemies, both among the goths and the romans. novellus, the bishop of complutum, is considered a man of great renown.

title: ANNO IIII TIBERII QVI EST LIVVIGILDI XII ANNVS //a.580\\
text: mauricius, master of soldiers of the east, wages war against the persians and, due to the persians' great numbers, spent the winter in the east. livygildus, king, gathers a synod of bishops of the arian sect in toledo and amends the ancient heresy with a new error, saying that those coming from roman religion to our catholic faith should not be baptized, but only cleansed through the laying on of hands and the reception of communion, and that glory should be given to the father through the son in the holy spirit. through this seduction, many of our people, more through greed than conviction, turn to the arian doctrine.

title: ANNO V TIBERII, QVI EST LIVVIGILDI XIII ANNVS //a.581\\
text: the longobards in italy choose a king from their own people, named autharic, during whose time the roman soldiers are utterly defeated and the longobards seize the borders of italy. the slavic people devastate illyricum and thrace. liuuigildus, king, occupies a part of vasconia and founded the city, now called victoriaco. emperor tiberius gives his daughter in marriage to mauritius, the master of soldiers of the east.

title: ANNO VI TIBERII, QVI EST LIVVIGILDI XIIII ANNVS //a.582\\
text: tiberius laid down the authority of life and mauricius is declared emperor of the romans. the emperor mauricius ruled for twenty years. liuuigildus gathers an army to attack the tyrant s son.

title:
ANNO ERGO I MAVRICII IMPERATORIS, LIVVIGILDI 
REGIS XV ANNVS //a.583\\
text: king liuvigild gathers an army and besieges the city of hispalis, confining his rebellious son with a severe blockade. the king of the suebi, miro, arrives to capture hispalis and brings about his final day. eburicus, his son, succeeds him in the province of gallaetia. meanwhile, king liuvigild completely disrupts the aforementioned city, now with famine, now with the sword, now with the closure of the baetis river.

title:
ANNO II MAVRICII IMP., QVI EST LIVVIGILDI XVI
ANNVS //a.584\\
text: liuigi restores the walls of the ancient italian city, a matter which presented the greatest obstacle to the people of hispalis. at this time, audeca seizes tyrannical power in the suebian kingdom of gallaecia and receives the abandoned kingdom of siseguntia from the late king miron in marriage. he deprives eboricum of its kingdom and makes its monks into a monastery. liuigi, the king, enters hispalis to fight against his son hermenegildo, as the latter is entering public affairs. he captured the cities and castles that his son had occupied, and not long afterward apprehended the aforementioned son in the city of corduba, stripping him of his kingdom and sending him into exile to valentia. emperor mauritius moves against the lombards and franks through a treaty, a matter that brought considerable damage to both peoples. eutropius, the abbot of the monastery of seruitania, a disciple of saint donatus

title: ANNO III MAVRICII, QVl EST LIVVIGILDI XVII ANNVS //a.585\\
text: mauricius, through his generals, inflicts war upon the persians. liuvigildus, king of the gallaecians, devastates, deprives audecan, the king, of his kingdom, returns the suebi people, their treasure, and their homeland to his power, and makes the province of the goths. hermenegildus is killed in tarraconensis by sisbert. the franks, desiring to occupy narbonensis gaul, enter with an army. liuvigildus, sending his son reccared to meet them, repels the frankish army and liberates the province of gaul from their infestation. two camps are occupied, one by peace, the other by war. the camp called ugerno is placed very safely on the bank of the rhone river, which king reccared attacked with a fierce battle and, victorious, returned to his father and his homeland. audeca, deprived of his kingdom, is tonsured and,

title:
ANNO IIII MAVRICII IMPERATORIS, QVI EST 
LIVVIGILDI REGIS XVIII ANNVS //a.586\\
text: the longobardic king authari, after a meeting with the romans, overcomes and cuts down a great multitude of roman soldiers, occupying the borders of italy. this year, king leovegild died, and his son reccared peacefully assumed the royal scepter.

title:
ANNO V MAVRICII PRINCIPIS ROMANORVM QVI EST 
RECCAREDI REGIS PRIMVS FELICITER ANNVS //a.587\\
text: mauricius theodosius makes his son caesarius, born from his daughter tiberius the emperor's daughter. upon the death of pelagius the younger, gregory succeeds as bishop of the roman church. the romans, with the help of the franks, devastate the lombards and bring a portion of the italian provinces back under their power. sisbertus, the slayer of hermenegild, meets his end in a most disgraceful death. in the first year of his reign, in the tenth month, reccared is converted to catholicism with god s help, and having approached the priests of the arian sect in wise discussion, he brings them to the catholic faith rather by reason than by force, and he restores the entire people of the goths and suebi to unity and peace within the christian church. the arian sect, through divine grace, comes to christ in doctrine. desiderius, a

title:
{300} ANNO VI MAVRICII, QVI EST RECCAREDI SECVNDVS 
ANNVS //a.588\\
text: a certain group from the arians, that is, sunna the bishop and segga, are exposed for attempting to seize tyranny sunna is banished, and segga, having his hands cut off, is exiled to gaul. mauricius makes theodosius, the son, whom we mentioned above as caesar, emperor of the romans.

title:
ANNO VII MAVRICII QVI EST RECCAREDI REGIS 
TERTIVS ANNVS //a.589\\
text: bishop uldida and queen gosuintha, who had been plotting against reccared, are revealed and publicly renounce their communion with the catholic faith, which they had feigned under a christian guise. uldida is condemned to exile for this wickedness, while gosuintha brought an end to her life, always hostile to catholics. a frankish army, sent by king gontramnus and led by boson, arrived in narbonnese gaul and pitched camp near the city of carcassonne. claudius, the duke of lusitania, directed by king reccared, met them there. a battle ensued, and the franks were routed, and the frankish camp and army were plundered by the goths. therefore, in this battle, the divine grace and the catholic faith, which king reccared and the goths faithfully embraced, are recognized as having been at work, for it is not difficult for our god to grant victory to a few, even when

title:
ANNO VIII MAVRICII IMPERATORIS, QVI EST 
RECCAREDI REGIS IIII ANNVS //a.590\\
text: a holy council of bishops from all of spain, gaul, and galatia convened in the city of toledo at the command of king reccared, with a number of seventy-two bishops present, including the aforementioned christian reccared. he presented a written document containing the order of his conversion and the profession of all the goth priests, and he explained all matters pertaining to the orthodox faith. the holy council of bishops decreed that this document should be applied with canonical authority. however, the main business of the council rested with saint leander, bishop of the church of hispalis, and the blessed eutropius, abbot of the monastery of seruitani. the aforementioned king reccared, as we have said, attended the holy council, renewing, in our times, the ancient example of emperor constantine the great, who illuminated the holy council of nicaea with his presence, and also of christian emperor marcian, whose insistence confirmed the decrees of the council of chal
