title: 1. Wie man die trubel erkennen sol.
text: recognize the signs of trouble not only by the taste, but also by how they feel. test whether they are sweet, and when you press them, if they release the husk from the grains and are sticky, and draw your fingers together, and whether they are full and soft. if they are as described beforehand, then they are good. you can tell by their appearance that they will not grow larger, and if they wrinkle and shrink away, know that their time has passed.

title: 2. Wie man den win dretten sol.
text: also, those who press the wine should wash their feet, and also those who drain the wine, and one must separate the coarse sediment from the good. do not neglect this, or great harm may come to the wine. if the wine is drained, it should be carried in clean vessels so that it remains strong. but if it stands for a while before draining and also over the pulp and in the pulp undrained, it will become sickly and red. also, some people often leave the red wine for a long time in the pulp undrained, because they want it to become thicker and to increase in quantity. i do not approve of this because of the impurities they seek in it, which spoil the wine's flavor and make it bad. you should also instruct those who drain the wine not to stand too close to it or the press, because too many spices are not beneficial for the wine, and there should be few of them. also, be diligent when you want to

title: 3. Wie man die faß bereiten sol.
text: to make good salt, use fresh walnut leaves or peach leaves and fresh herbs. wash them thoroughly so they do not smell. when the herbs are pressed, take smoke and infuse them well. you should also know that spice merchants and others use a method to prevent the smell, the mold, or any other bad taste and bitterness from the vessels. it happens that the bad taste of the vessel clings to the wine, and that causes many people trouble. they make the brain boil and water the eyes. you should also know that this previously mentioned wine cannot last long put it in an unblemished vessel, and that is why they often use beechwood to make their vessels.

title: 4. So der win girt.
text: to make fine wine, when you see the juice is still warm, pour juice into it as if it came from the press. begin to ferment it first. and if it does not want to ferment, do as before. and pour more juice into it and do that four or five times. you should also be careful not to fill the vessel too full at any time, lest it overflow.

title: 5. Wie du wasser vz dem win bringest.
text: even when the weather is harsh and rainy, and your wine is diluted with water, and the water remains in the wine, if you want to achieve this skillfully, you should rack your wine after the first fermentation into another vessel. this leaves the watery portion and anything that has settled at the bottom, along with anything harmful to the wine, behind. know that each wine is best in the middle of the vessel, whether it's above or below. ale is better at the top, and honey is better at the bottom than at the top. therefore, pour different types of wine from a vessel through a cloth, from the middle and from the top.

title: 6. Von gefürtem win, wie man den versuchet.
text: also, some people would offer or sell wine. they deceive those who taste it by adding licorice, nuts, old cheese, or salted food to it. then the wine has a sweet taste.

title: 7. Wie man wine versuchet.
text: also do this again, when you eat something sour or bitter, the wine will not taste good. therefore, vintners try the wine in the morning, after they have washed their mouths, and then eat three or four mouthfuls of bread soaked in water, because no one can taste properly who is on an empty stomach or too full.

title: 8. Wie man den win besehen sol, so man in verkauffet.
text: whoever wishes to sell wine should observe whether the north wind blows, for at that time the wine is at its healthiest and has been well preserved. but whoever wishes to buy wine should test it when the east wind blows, for then the wine readily transforms and reveals whether any sickness is present within it.

title: 9. Obe wasser in dem wine sy.
text: if someone wants to buy wine, they should not be satisfied with a single tasting, but should thoroughly taste the wine and hold it in their mouth for a long time. and if they want to detect whether water has been added to the wine or the must, as the crows learn, throw in some spelt. if it floats on top, the wine is without water. other experts say, if you throw an eye into it and it floats on top, the wine is without water. but if it sinks to the bottom, water is in it. if you want to test it that way, take a small reed that has been dried in water, or a piece of wood, or a sedge, or a sprig, or any other dry thing and smear it with oil. then wash it off and put it into the wine. afterwards, draw it out from the wine. if the wine has water, water droplets will hang from the reed. if you want to try it another

title: 10. Zu weler zit sich der win aller gernest verkeret.
text: the wine changes and transforms most of all when the sun doesn't shine on it or doesn't touch it, that is around saint lucy's day and during frost. it also changes from great heat and frost, and especially from rainy weather, wind, thunder, lightning, and from the blossoming of the vine.

title: 11. Daz dem wine donre noch blixe nit geschaden mag.
text: if you wish the wine to not be harmed by thunder or lightning, lay iron over the vat. it is also not unpleasant if the wine is altered by the thunder and lightning, when there are gusts of wind that sweep across the land, destroying it so that it is no longer useful for brewing or beer. you can also well preserve and protect the wine so that it is not altered by rain or wind. let the cellar be constructed so that there are no windows, and the door should be sealed against the wind that blows in the afternoon. if you want to have windows in the cellar, make them small, so that you can open and close them when necessary because of the cold and heat.

title: 12. Die zeichen, obe sich der wine verkeren wil.
text: to learn the signs by which one can recognize if the wine will spoil, when the wine has been drained, one should carefully prepare the sediment at the bottom of the vessel. afterwards, wait for an hour to see if the sediment smells. if it smells, the wine will spoil, and the stronger the smell, the more the wine has spoiled. and when you want to remove the sediment from the vessel, take a stick and poke into the sediment, and retrieve it, testing it both by taste and by smell.

title: 13. Wiltu wissen, waz gesmackes eyn win gewinnen wil.
text: try it differently as well. take the wine in the middle of the cask and simmer it, letting it cool, and then taste it. and whatever flavor it has, the wine will also take on in the cask. try the same thing again take a small twig or a straw and make a ring on it, and poke it into the wine, and then it will appear like a little bubble. if you skim it off quickly, the wine is fresh but if you let it linger, the wine will change.

title: 14. Welher win sich nit verkeren wil.
text: also, when the wine has a fresh taste and bubbles in the glass or cup, it remains. whoever does not notice this will be mistaken.

title:
15. Wie du dun solt, daz sich der win nit verkert vnd daz

er gut blibet.
text: to also preserve and protect the wine so that it does not spoil at the time you want to keep it, take a piece of wood about a span long, when the beech trees are growing, and put it into the wine while it is still sweet, and let it sit there for a while, and the wine will become lasting. also add the fruit of the tree called myrtle to it, and let it sit there for a while, and the wine will gain a good taste, be pleasant, and strengthen the stomach and the brain. and also fenugreek, so that it does not spoil. add also the roots of the vine to the must, and the wine will become lasting. also add the blood of the vine to it, and the wine will become lasting, fresh, and strengthen itself. note also that when the must begins to ferment, hang hops that are of the season in a small sack. this will not only protect the wine from spoiling, but it will also make

title: 16. Wie der wine werhafftig blibet.
text: another time, simmer wine and add a measure of must to it, so that the wine becomes substantial. it is also good to hang some buckwheat grains in it.

title: 17. Wie du faße bereiten solt.
text: when you put wine into your barrels or at any other time of the year wish to pour wine into them, you should wash your barrels well with salt water. let them dry thoroughly. afterwards, treat them with pitch and seal the smoke within the barrel, so the wine will keep well throughout the entire year, without spoiling.

title: 18. Wie man die win machet geren.
text: when the weather is cold, or if the wine doesn't please, you should add nettle root and wine stone, finely crushed, and it will work well.

title: 19. Daz der win sich nit verstoß.
text: when you brew your wine in a wooden vessel, add briar, or buckthorn, or hops, or cornflowers, in a linen cloth. each separately, so that it holds the wine, so that it does not spoil, unless it is heated. whatever wine is drawn off at the time, it will be sicker or weaker, and it cannot last long and readily changes, when it has suffered too much of heat and frost.

title: 20. Wie man den win abeloßet.
text: let the wine settle in winter, or in spring or summer. whoever lets the wine settle, if his moon is favorable, will gladly turn it into vinegar or something sour. let the wine settle in rainy weather, or when a new month begins or rises and be careful that the moon is not in the path of the sun. that is, when it is not wedded. when it is useful, check the moon when you want to let the wine settle, when the moon is the lowest planet and is nearest to us all. also, do not let the wine settle when it thunders or flashes, or when the east wind blows strongly. be wary of the wind with the path of the sun, which most often damages the wine. the wind that comes from the south is good for the wine and makes it fresh.

title: 21. Win wider bringen, der sich verstoßen hat.
text: to restore a wine that has become cloudy when the wine becomes cloudy while still in the cask, let out about three-quarters of the wine and leave the rest in the vessel. stir the dregs well and turn the cask back and forth, then let it settle. if the wine has already been drawn off and becomes cloudy, take the whites of 44 eggs and beat them well, then add wine to them. add a headful of stale meal, a quarter of a headful of alum, and a headful of luter sand, along with the wine from the cask. mash everything together and add it to the wine, stirring it with a split stick that has many holes. the holes should be plugged with a cobweb. this will clarify and brighten the wine. alternatively, take bran husks and mash them with the same wine, then pour the mixture back into the cask and stir well. or, add a good amount of juniper berries to the wine and

title: 25. Witu [!E] roten win wiß machen.
text: to make red wine that becomes pale and white, take to the white of an egg and some fine flour and as you have been instructed a quarter of a pint of cow's milk and a little salt, mix them together and pour them into the wine, and stir it well with it, so that it becomes white and beautiful. some also make their wine white with finely grated herbs or with chalk. the two are very bitter, and whoever drinks much of this wine will have it in his head.

title: 24. Wiltu seigern win frische machen.
text: to make your wine better, do this take a headful of elderberries and as much oak bark as elderberries, and half as much crushed wine stones. let it sit in the wine vessel for a quarter and mix it well. then pour it into a mortar and stir the wine thickly until it foams. skim off the foam and return it to the wine. if you stir it well together, the wine will be fresher. or put a good bunch of nettle roots in the wine, or put ground mustard in a linen cloth and put it in the wine it will make the wine fresher.

title: 25. Wiltu eym schymmeligen win helffen.
text: if you wish to help mellow wine so that it loses its harshness, put it in a clean vessel and add a handful of sage and a few small thyme sprigs, crushed and boiled, and strained through a linen cloth. the wine will then taste very good.

title:
26. Wie du den win by siner farwe behaltest, so du in

<<125>>

drinckest.
text: even if you serve wine, add a few sprigs of thyme or cornflowers, so that the wine retains its color. spread a linen cloth over the serving vessel and place two fingers' thickness of ash upon it. then lay a good green sod of earth on top of the ash, which should be the thickness of a dry finger. prick through it with a spindle point in three places, so that the foul odors may escape. thus, the wine will remain stable. if you use a wide-mouthed vessel or a tub, like those used for windows, be sparing with the wine.

title: 27. Do wine rot ist worden.
text: roast the bones of beef, which is particularly good with red wine. roasted wine makes a clear wine, both bad and good.

title: 28. Wie man kranckem win helffen sol.
text: to help a sick wine recover, take alum and as much sugar and burnt horn as you like, all together in a linen cloth, and put that into the vessel. then the wine will improve. if you don t have that, take lees from where good wine has settled, take them and stir them into the sick wine well, and the sick wine will improve.

title: 29. Do ein win sin farwe verlorn hat.
text: the wellich has lost its color, add it to a feed. two pounds of almond kernels, a small handful of blanched almonds. prepare milk from the same wine and then, for over two hours, make another milk with half a pound of cream using the same wine, and pour the other milk out and let the wine settle until the next day it will become clear and fine.

title: 30. Von trübem wine.
text: to clarify muddy wine, take barley with herbs and roots and nettle roots, but not the herbs. take 2 liters and sink it to the bottom. then take a quarter of water and a fifth of alum and stir the alum into the water. pour it into the vat and mash it into the vat and seal it. let it sit for a day.

title: 31. Von seigerm wine.
text: to prepare a wellich wine sausage, take fresh rind and fresh wood. remove the black skin and grate it very finely. grind two pounds of meat into a bowl and let it lie thinly for seven days, so it will become fresh and beautiful.

title: 32. Suren wine suße machen.
text: to make wine sweet take a pound of licorice and grind it finely in a mortar until it is soft. then put it in a thin linen cloth and hang it in the middle of the vessel. when you want to add to the vessel, hold the licorice in your hand and then put it back in the vessel and let it remain in there for as long as it loses its strength then the wine will be sweet and flavorful.

title: 33. Smacket der win nach dem vaße.
text: to make a small cake, take a loaf of bread. when hot from the oven, press the bread warm onto a surface and cover it with a cloth or a cushion.

title: 34. Wilt du wine starcke machen.
text: to make wine stronger than it was, take grains of paradise, nutmeg, ginger, cinnamon, and galangal, and grind them. put them in a small linen cloth and place it under the wine in the vessel. when you cover the vessel, stir the cloth or the sack back and forth, and it will be stronger than it was before.

title: 35. Wilt du swartzen nuwen win wiß machen.
text: to darken the new wine, or to make it white, take for each barrel a pound of alum and a pennyweight of salt, and three measures of milk, and beat them together in a clean vessel, vigorously until it foams. then leave the vessel against an ewer and beat the must vigorously with a stick, and pour it under each other into the must, stirring it together very well. then take a pound of glass, finely ground, so that it is like fine meal, and pour that on top into the vessel and stir it well together and fill it full, so it gains color on the third day.

title: 36. Win schöne machen.
text: to make wine look beautiful, take grape skins and wash them well. once you ve drained the wine from the lees, put the skins into the wine. the wine will become clear and beautiful. or take chalk and place it in a clean cloth, then put it in the wine. the wine will become clear, but this is a trick. another trick take a little burnt wine and pour it into the wine. the wine will become clear because of it. some consider this a trick. or fry peppercorns in oil and peel the rinds finely, then put them in the wine the wine will become clear and beautiful. another method take a little sediment and pour it over the wine, and when you ve let it settle, the wine will become clear and beautiful.

title: 37. Wiltu roten win wiß machen.
text: to cleanse the elderberries, wash them and place them in red wine the wine will become colored. if you wish to make white wine red, take red elderberries and place them in white wine.

title: 38. Bucken win.
text: to make bucken wine, take the red bucken and place it in the herbarium, and let the wine simmer over it. the wine is good for women.

title: 39. Sertzen win.
text: to make wine clear and good, take fresh rushes and sprinkle them over the wine, stirring them in together and let it stand.

title: 40. Wiltu win zu essich machen.
text: if you wish to make wine palatable, lay it in the sun and two measures of warm milk, and let the wine settle well. it will soon become good to drink.

title: 41. Daz essich wider zu win werde.
text: to make the cheese again take bran and lay it in the cheese it should lie for two days and two nights.

title: 42. Daz win zu essich werde.
text: to make a drink take barley grains and roast them, and place the roasted barley in wine or roasted bread broth.

title: 43. So der wine jm gist ist.
text: to make wine agreeable, take blossoms of beans and cornflowers, and wine blossoms like them, a great deal. put them in a linen bag and hang it. then put the bag with the blossoms in a vessel so that the wine is in the infusion. this will strengthen the wine and make it taste very good.

title: 44. Drüben win luter machen.
text: to clarify your wine, take bottled flour and fresh eggs and make a cake with them, and throw it into the wine and let it settle. if you want to clarify your wine, take a pound of winestone and half a pound of salt and burn it in a pan and then rub it finely and throw it into the wine. and beat the wine with a wooden stick and let it settle, and it will become clear.

title: 45. Essich machen.
text: if you want to make a good drink, take a quart of water and a quintin of honey and a quart of wine, and simmer them well, then put it in a vessel and let it sour.

title: 46. Win schone behalten.
text: take a root of agrimony as large as two fists. wash it well and wrap it in a cloth, then hang it in white wine in a vessel and cover it with honey. the wine will remain pleasant and stable as long as one drinks from it.

title: 47. Gebrochen wine.
text: take broken almonds, soak them in wine, and wash them well with clear water, then let them dry. after that, put the almonds in the wine, and take a little burnt wine and pour it under the wine. then take woad and put it in a cloth, and hang it over the wine, not in the wine. seal the vessel tightly above, and the wine will become fine and clear, and will do no harm.

title: 48. Verdorben wine wider bringen.
text: if you want to restore spoiled wine or beer to a pleasant taste, take sage, betony, borage, and bay leaves, each in equal measure, and place them in a bag in the vessel.

title: 49. Wißen win rot machen.
text: if you wish to make wine red, take the best elderberries and press them through a clean cloth, so that the juice flows out. then take honey and let the dregs and foam settle into clarity, and take then the aforementioned juice and simmer it in the honey, making a sweet confection. and if you wish to make wine red, take a little of the confection and put it in the wine, and it will become red and no one who drinks it will suspect it, and it will also be harmless to no one.

title: 50. Wiltu wissen win rot machen.
text: dry cornflowers and poppies until they are withered. then add the dried cornflowers to white wine. it will turn red for a short time.

title: 51. Rotfarwen win luter machen.
text: to clarify red wine, take two pounds of honey and a handful of salt, and grind them together with a pestle. then take wine, about a quarter of a barrel, and strain it through a cloth and pour it into a large vessel, and stir it together with a stick. do the same with powdered gypsum. you can find this at the apothecary. throw it into the vessel, and it will settle to the bottom.

title: 52. Fulen win gut machen vnd frisch.
text: whoever wants to make good and fresh wine should take a quarter of a bushel of rind and scrape off the top and the skin, likewise a handful, and mix that together in the vat for four days, which is not too much.

title: 55. Seigern win frische machen.
text: to make sugared wine fresh, take a red fir tree, the middle bark as large as a cask and a handful, and put it in a vessel for a while, so that it doesn't become too limp.

title: 54. Summertzen win wider bringen.
text: to make spiced wine, take three pennyworth of ginger and two pennyworth of saffron, pound them together, and put them in a vessel in a small bag for four days.

title: 55. Daz der win nit breche.
text: if you want the wine not to break, add a few grains of wormwood or rue to it.

title: 56. Salbey win.
text: to make wilted sorrel wine, take the sorrel and break off the pointed ends, and loosen the leaves so they are clean. let them dry in the sun. afterwards, when they are dried, soak them in water for two hours. then lay them in the sun again to dry, and when they are dried, put them in a clean linen bag and hang it in the wine it will be flavorful and healthily infused.

title: 57. Daz win, der rot worden ist, wider schon werde.
text: to restore wine that has turned red, proceed as follows take dregs from white wine and pour them into the red wine, stirring the dregs well in the vessel with a stick. let it settle until the wine becomes clear. when the wine is clear, you should drain it off. if it is a large cask, add a measure of good burnt wine to the vessel, and the wine will remain clear and pure. or take noble grape pomace with the stems and the small cuttings and the small clusters, wash them clean, and put them in the vessel. then the wine will become clear and pure and remain beneficial in the end.

title: 58. Schön win biz an daz ende.
text: to obtain a fine wine, first take unripe grapes those that are not ripe and still have a firm texture. place these grapes in a clean vessel and pour clear water over them, allowing them to sit. then, take the grape pomace from the third pressing and wash it thoroughly. put it in a bowl and pour water over it. if you want the wine to be especially fine, take some of the grapes from the vessel and squeeze them well. also, take some of the pomace and let the wine drain over the grapes and pomace, allowing it to sit. the wine will then remain clear and not leak a single drop in the vessel, and it will be beneficial to no one.

title: 59. Daz win nit seiger werde.
text: to keep wine from becoming sour, take fresh cream and wash it clean and pure, then put it into the wine while it is still unfermented and warm. let the wine ferment over it. after you have strained it, remove any sediment that you should have broken or cut a month before the harvest, and put it in clear water in a vessel. put the sediment in the vessel with the wine, and you will be well assured that the wine will not become sour let it stand for four years.

title: 60. Daz essich nit seiger werde.
text: if you don't want the broth to become too strong, take some whey. wash it well and then add it to the broth. also take some bear's paw and chop it finely, then put it in a small bag. and then add the small bag to the broth the broth will not become too strong, unless the dish is prepared differently, with the broth inside.

title: 61. Daz din wine schone werde.
text: once the dough has risen, take a wooden griddle and peel. remove the top crust and take two stalks of rosemary or thyme, and throw them into a greased vessel it will become fragrant and softened.

title: 62. Win, der in einer buden verderben wil.
text: if the wine becomes spoiled, to restore it, uncover it and add another wine, choosing as much as will warm the other wine in the vessel or in the spoiled portion, and then seal the vessel or spoiled portion tightly it will be good.

title: 65. Druben wine luter machen.
text: once the must is ready, make the wine as follows lay out well-heated oven stones, and you will need a beakerful in the wine it will quickly become clear and pure, without a doubt.

title: 64. Daz wine zu essich werden.
text: if you want your wine to be edible, take barley grains and roast them. then put the roasted barley into the wine, or add roasted bread.

roast grape vines. when you place the grape vines in a warm oven and melt them therein, which in latin is called passo, that is roasted grape vines. the grape vine's blood stops the bleeding, and the grape vine's sap, which flows out when you cut it, overcomes roughness and bitterness. its root overcomes uncleanness in the ears when it is pounded. its juice breaks up the stone in the bladder. take the green grape skins, when they are cut off, and roast them in a furnace and then extract the water from it, and that water is good for watery eyes and sick eyes, when you put it in them.
aristotle says, one should try new wine or beer, whether water has been mixed in or not. if an egg is put in it and it sinks to the bottom, then there is no water in it.

title: 67. Seiger win.
text: to make wine stronger, take some wood and put it inside. make pegs from sour wood and stick them into the bottom. it will become fresh again.

title: 68. Drüben wine schone vnd luter machen.
text: to quickly clarify and purify cloudy wine, burn beechwood. grind the ashes through a sieve and then strain a double layer of fine cloth over a container. spread a hand s thickness of the ashes on the cloth. then take three measures of good, clear wine and pour it through. next, take half a measure of the same wine and add it to the cloudy wine it will quickly become clear and fine.

title: 69. Gebrochen win schone machen.
text: to cleanse broken wine, take half a measure of its lees and add the white from twenty eggs, beating it well together and setting it aside. on the third day, fill the vessel with clear spring water, let it stand for eight days, and it will be cleansed and pure without doubt.

title: 70. Seigern wine balde frisch machen.
text: to refresh stale wine, take of the same stale wine from the vessel a full kettle and let it settle well. while it is settling, break it with a wine breaker and pour it into the vessel while still hot, and let it stand for eight days, and it will be refreshed.

title: 71. Wilt du essich machen.
text: to make a good wine essence, whether for yourself or others, place alum in good wine essence for fourteen days, ensuring the essence always covers the alum. afterward, let it dry in the sun, but not too hard. then, place it in heated wine for a day and a night, and allow it to dry well and grind it into a powder. take a handful of this powder and add it to a whole barrel of wine it will become a good essence overnight. test this with a measure of wine. do not take more powder than you can hold between two fingers.

title: 72. Wissen win rot machen.
text: if you wish to make red wine, then take a woolen cloth and dip it in mulberries and let it press. when you drink, let the cloth be in it.

title: 75. Drüben wine luter machen.
text: to clarify beer wine, take bottled beer and fresh eggs, make a cake, throw it into the wine and let it lie in it.

title: 74. Essich machen.
text: to make essence, take one quarter of water, one fifth of honey, one quarter of wine, simmer it well, then put it in a vessel.

title: 75. Schymmelig wine.
text: take a slightly sour wine, and lay in it a loaf of bread. put it in a vessel or a sack, and in it, wine. and take savory spices, bind them in a small cloth, and let them lie in it for three days. then, on the fourth day, it will have very good wine and be pleasing.

title: 76. Seiger win.
text: to make a fine, sparkling vessel, first crush some almonds until they are small, then pass them through a cloth or sieve, beat twenty-eight egg whites, add a handful of salt to them, and strain them through a cloth. you should mix the almonds and the egg whites together in a quarter of the wine. let the vessel stand for a span, and stir the wine with a whisk, breaking it up. then take the mixed wine and add a half measure of water to it every morning for eight days. this will keep the wine fresh, beautiful, and well-made.

title: 77. Vor die wine mutter.
text: to make mother wine, break a barrel of wine, take two pounds of saffron. a glass and a mirror glass. and you should stir them together. then take the same wine and put it with each other in the vessel and pour it in and for three mornings into each other in the vessel and every day a half measure of water, and you will have a good wine in three days.

title: 78. Wie man drüben vnd gebrochen wine wider bringen sol.
text: to restore spoiled wine take ash from vine shoots, chop it finely, and strain it through a cloth. take fifteen eggshells, also strain them through a cloth. then take the vine ash and the eggshells and a quarter of the spoiled wine, mix all together, pour the mixture into the vessel, and it will have clear wine again.

title: 79. Smackender win.
text: take a barrel of must, cut it with lye until it separates into pieces, then put it into a sackcloth, hang it in a vessel and add a bush of sallow, each as large as an egg. let it hang until the fourth day, then three mornings every morning a measure of water in it, and after that one has already a fine wine.

title: 80. Drüben wine.
text: take a barrel of good wine. take hen's egg whites, let them stand. beat them together in a bowl until frothy, strain them through a cloth. take a spoonful of salt, a quarter of the wine, and beat it with a whisk until it foams. add wine to the vessel until it is about a hand's breadth empty, and then add the frothed wine to it. this will produce a fine wine.

title: 81. Von essichem win.
text: to make a batch of wine, or to begin with, prepare small balls of leek and onion seeds, each about the size of an eye. take boiling water as much as a man can hold in his hand, pour it into the bowl, and it will be a fine, good wine.

title: 82. Von fulem win.
text: to make a barrel of wine, take peeled grape skins as many as a man can hold under his arms, scrape them with a knife, place them in a press vessel, and let the wine through a filter into the vessel. keep the filter agitated, and place it in a limestone or quartz vessel. in eight days, you will have good wine.

title: 83. So win nit winfar ist.
text: if you make a batch that is not wine, but rather a small amount, use saffron on the third day, and you will have wine.

title: 84. Drübe wine.
text: to make wine palatable and improve its flavor, grind ox gallstones into powder and add the powder to the wine. afterwards, add half a measure of water to it, and it will be a better wine.

title: 85. Born win.
text: to make good born wine, take two white ashes. place them in a bowl, filling it to a quarter of its capacity. then add fresh wine to the bowl and pour more wine over it. this will make the wine good for mixing with other wines to a great extent. if you do not wish to do this, take a supple ash stick, ensuring it is as long from the base as it is to the tip. remove the bark from the top of the stick, warm the stick over a fire, and then place it in the bowl. let it remain in the bowl, and it will become good and even better than other wines, and also very good.

title: 86. Wie man von rotem wine wissen wine machen sol.
text: to make wine from red berries take red berries, ensuring no grain has sprouted, take as many as you wish, spread the berries on a cloth, place them in a press with the wooden beam. the wine will be as clear as knowing, truly clear and fine.

title: 87. Guten essich machen.
text: to make good vinegar from good wine take wine and grind it finely in a stone mortar, as into an earthen vessel. pour it onto the middle part of the vessel, then fill the vessel with strong vinegar, add the powder and cover the vinegar with it well, so firmly and for so long, that the powder has drawn the vinegar to itself. then let the powder press well on a clean board. then pound it with your hands, throw it thus pounded into the earthen vessel, but also well with good vinegar. let it stand thus filled, unboiled, until the powder has drawn the vinegar quite to itself. then let it press, but pound it with your hands, so that it is well covered in the vessel, fill it well with good vinegar, let it stand unboiled until the vinegar has quite dissolved into the powder. then take the powder unboiled,

title: 88. Gestendig wine.
text: to make wine take a wooden trough as long as a bushel and one span wide, and place it in the wine. in the first draining, let it remain there. in the second draining, fill the wine every friday.

title: 89. Verdorben win.
text: to cleanse spoiled wine, crush small stones. strain the wine through them, pressing it firmly into a cloth. let it drain, allowing the sediment to settle and the wine to clarify. then place the wine stones in the cloth into a vessel. when the cloth is burned away, take the wine stones from the vessel, grind them into powder, and place the powder in a small bag in a cool cellar, and wait to see what drips from it that is, the oil from which the wine will be restored.

title: 90. Essich.
text: put hazel or red alder wood into the wine, to be eaten.

title: 91. Von zehem wine schone machen.
text: to make wine clear, take birch bark and strip off the outer bark, then peel off the inner bark and soak it in the wine. this will draw out the sediment and the dregs. do this repeatedly until the wine is clear.

title: 92. Von smackendem wine, daz er wolsmacken werde.
text: to make tasty wine, take monk's wort and pound it and put it in, and it will taste good. or if the wine is cloudy or tastes bad or is bloody, take nettle root and mandrake and put the two together in the wine for a day and a night, and the wine will be good and tasty.

title: 93. Wann trübe win luter wil werden.
text: if wine turns cloudy and wants to become red and clear, take the white of an egg, salt, and a little alum, mix them together, and put them in it will return and become fine.

title: 94. Win, der nach essich smacket.
text: when you want to make a tasty dish, take beans and bacon. put them in a bag in the middle of the wine.

title: 95. Win, der nach dem vaße smacket vnd schimmelt.
text: when the yeast has settled and appears murky, take yeast from fresh wine and white clay, and a little sand, and wash the must, and mix the grape skins together. shake it into the wine and stir it through, and let it rest. it will settle and become clear.

title:
96. Obe du wilt, daz din win balde luter werde, so er vff

den trusen lit.
text: if you wish your wine to be clear, whether it is cloudy from sediment or not sweet enough, take goat's milk and make it thin, then pour it over the wine. take a measure for a barrel it will clear the wine, but not for long.

title: 97. Wilt du, daz der win lange luter blibe.
text: to ensure your wine remains long, pure, and good, take 40 eggs to a full barrel, and they should be fresh, and crush them well and mix them with the wine as you beat them. then take a measure of honey and dissolve it, and throw a chalk stone, finely ground, into the eggs, and stir everything together until the chalk is well dissolved. and then add a measure of goat's milk or cow's milk, and pour it all into the vessel gently and evenly. stir it vigorously for a good while and then let it rest for a day and a night. afterwards it will become pure and clear.

title: 98. So der win weich ist, zehe oder seiger.
text: if the wine is sour or musty, take small pebbles from a green or cold spring and wash them well. place them in cold water and throw them into the vessel, and wash the bottom with cold spring water every night. the wine will then be good, clear, and fine.

title: 99. So win verderben wil vnd dannoch sin farwe hat.
text: if the wine should spoil and still retain its color, keep it cool, and let there be much wine. if the wine should become cloudy, take warm bread and throw it in pieces into it, so it binds the sediment together. and taste the wine in the middle, to see what it needs. whatever flavor it lacks, add that. and let the bread hang in it for half a day.

title: 100. Wann der wine siech vnd krang ist.
text: if the wine is sick and spoiled, take a measure of burnt wine to a barrel and pour it in it will then be good and fine and not bubble.

title: 101. Wann der win kon hat oder ein hut gewynnet.
text: when the wind has blown or a hat has been won, hang it in the middle part, and it will be right.

title: 102. Waz dem win gebristet.
text: take broken wine, then take wine stone and put it in a tub with juniper in a sack and beech wood, add the bruised to it, and it will be good and right.

title: 103. Bruchig win.
text: you will need approximately two or three pounds of alum. put it on a hot hearth, or in a new dish over embers, until it melts. then, brown it to a powder and grind it very finely. afterwards, place it in a small cloth bag.

title: 104. Wann der win dicke vnd trübe wirt.
text: when the wine is thick and watery but still has color, take wild lemon, as much as will fit above the pot, hang it in, it will draw out the wateriness and the slime and make it fine.

title: 105. Wiltu machen roten win.
text: to make rotten wine, take red flowers that grew in the field. grind the petals off the stems and pound them well on a mortar stone. press the juice from them and strain it through cloth, and put it into the wine. it will become red as much as you see it needs.

title: 106. Ronen win luter machen.
text: to make wine clear, if it is cloudy, take to four gallons a quarter of a pound of egg white and beat it very well in lukewarm water and strain it through a clean cloth and pour some wine into it and beat it and pour it then into the vessel and stir it well together, and it will be clear, etc.

title: 107. Seigern win frische machen.
text: to make fresh wine, take from a barrel, measure out, and pour into a container, cover it, and set it back in the barrel and let it simmer gently and foam. when it no longer foams, cover the container, but let it simmer well. once it has simmered well, take a straw or a small stick and lift it up into the container, so that the wine ignites. let it burn for a short while, then take it from the barrel and let it splash slightly, and pour it into the vessel while still hot, and it will be quite fresh.

title: 108. Win, der vff den trusen lit, daz er sich nit rege.
text: if the wine appears cloudy and unsettled, take four handfuls of vine branches and put them into two barrels of wine. if you don't have vine branches, take oak wood and burn it to ashes, stir it well, and take a quarter of the ashes to two barrels and stir it with a measure of lye water, then add it to the ashes, etc.

title: 109. Lutern win machen.
text: to make a gentle, pleasing luter wine, take a glass and pound it in a mortar, and then add a large handful of yolk to a barrel of wine and twenty eggs. beat this well with five yolks, then add 1 2 measure of water and 1 2 of wine, and beat it very thoroughly together, and pour it in until it fills a beaker. then take a work and anoint it within, and lift the glass with it onto a bushel, and throw it in, and stir it very well before and after.

title: 110. Daz sich wine nit verstoße.
text: if you don't want the wine you let stand to sour, take one measure of water and a large handful of salt and beat them together and shake it in.

title: 111. Goltfarwen wine.
text: if you want to make golden-colored wine, take twelve measures of wine into a vessel and boil it well. then take a few grains of myrrh and crush them in a mortar and put them into the boiling wine. when it has been well boiled, let the wine cool slightly and then pour it into the wine and stir it very thoroughly, both before and after.

title: 112. Win, der nach schymmel smacket.
text: to make wine, which has a pleasant flavor, take bark from trees and grind it very finely, and put it in a sack and hang it. and take wheat bran and grind it also, and put it in a sack and hang it as well.

title: 115. Wilt du win luter haben.
text: to have boiled meat, put bay leaves in the wine.

title: 114. Wilt du, daz kein bier nymmer sure werde.
text: if you want your beer to never go sour, take bog myrtle with seeds and everything, and throw it into the beer.

title: 115. Wiltu machen guten essich.
text: to make a good dish, put in the wine wood sorrel and parsley.

title: 116. Wilt du druoben win wieder schon machen.
text: to revive wine that has turned sour, or wine that is black, you should take a large bowlful of salt and fill a pan with it. then heat it until it is very hot in the vessel. you should have almond milk prepared, which you should strain through a cloth and pour into the vessel with the salt. first, let about a third of the wine drain off, and then stir the wine almost entirely in the vessel with a skimmer, made with nails or holes. then fill the vessel and cover it, and let it sit for eight or fourteen days, and it will be good again.

title: 117. Wilt du:o seiger win schon vnd fresch mach. [!E]
text: to make wine clear and fresh, take what has holes or is made with nails, and pour the wine almost entirely into the cask. let it stand for two hours or more, and then seal the cask again. add half a measure of fresh water to it and stir it in, and let it sit for eight days, and it will become fresh.

title: 118. Wilt dv dicken roden win machen.
text: to make a thick red wine, as the rotten grapes do, which are washed in the grain, and take two leaves from them and cut away the blackness from the leaves and pound the leaves and put them in wine, it will become thick red.

title:
119. Wan du wilt win ym herbest fassen, daß er schon

blib.
text: to prepare your wort, so that your beer remains sweet and does not break, take half a cauldron as large as a loaf of bread. add a quarter or a third of a bushel of malt and two or three bushels of water into a kettle, and place the mash in it, and let it boil, and brew your wort.

title: 120. Zuo seiger win oder druober win.
text: to make sweet wine or wine over wine take nettles. roots also a bushel, two or three. wash the herbs thoroughly to a half bushel and put them in a morning in wine, so that they sink to the bottom by a span. and in the evening, take them out again and wash them, then put them back in the cask and let them stay for three days one after another, until the wine is sweet and fresh, and then take it off and strain it, and let it sit, and it will become sweet and clear.

title:
121. Item wan dv schon win an siechen wilt zue
drincken.
text: to make a drink that remains pleasantly sweet until the end, take the leaves as large as a fist and string them onto a length of cord. draw three or four firkins of wine from the cask and add as much gebundil as will not disturb the wine s flavor. stir it in and drink it. it should be consumed with faith or with honey.

title: I. Lapis Aëtites.
text: it is a great protection from nature god gave this stone first to humankind as a safeguard of salvation. the eagle carries it from the farthest parts of the world to its nest to guard its eggs. aëtites is a stone of a reddish-purple color, very rough in appearance and it has another stone beneath it, as if pregnant. it is useful for pregnant women when bound around the left arm, it prevents a woman from miscarrying. it is also very suitable for a quick delivery. if a woman is in danger, when introduced and ground up and placed upon her lower back, she will be delivered quickly. furthermore, it will protect the bearer, making them sober and capable of overcoming everything it will increase familiar affairs, spread a good reputation, and be most pleasing. whoever carries this stone will have the easiest entrance to all things, to god and to people. it also preserves infants and young girls. this stone causes lymphatic ailments and wicked terrors to cease,

title: II. Lapis Heliotropius.
text: the heliotrope stone is born in ethiopia, cyprus, and libya. it is emerald in color, with veins of blood. it is called heliotropius because it turns the sun. when placed in a silver basin filled with water and set against the sun, it turns the sun and makes the water appear bloody and dark. you will see its divine power, for the basin will begin to stir the water, becoming cloudy like the air with thunder, lightning, rain, and storms, so much so that even the inexperienced are terrified and disturbed by its power such forces and divine qualities this stone possesses. furthermore, it foretells the future through perennial streams and vocally through songs. it also preserves the ability to live and keeps the body unharmed, and it brings a good reputation to pregnant women and removes all kinds of poisons and it removes terrors of all kinds. for whoever carries this stone is never deceived, so great is the grace of this stone granted to humans by god.

title: III. Lapis Adamas.
text: this stone, harder than adamant, is best found in india, second best in arabia, and others in cyprus. similar ones are also found in the philippines, all nearly equal in color and size. they are suitable for all magical workings and possess the same powers. but this stone is said by some to be anactites, because it brings about and completes everything you desire. having obtained this stone, enclose it in a silver pouch, and a consecrated gate will render you invincible and unconquerable against enemies, foes, evildoers, and all proud men, causing you to be feared by everyone. it repels all fear, uncertain dreams, shadowy visions, poisons, and disputes. therefore, make a bracelet from gold, silver, iron, and brass fashion a torquel and wear it around your left arm, for great help from the gods is associated with this stone.

title: IV. Lapis Memnonius.
text: indeed, memnon's stone is the greatest and most powerful. it expels poisons, illnesses, weaknesses, tumors, and enmities it makes one faithful, truthful, steadfast, eloquent, modest, and pleasing in appearance to all, and moreover, invincible in every matter and every contest. and do not be surprised that i write to you about it having such powers many kings praise it they have tested it against enemies and in great battles. brave men and gladiators in the arena, and athletes seeking a pleasing victory, have followed it. but truly, many have used it before judges in important cases this stone has such power to be always a great defense in winning. however, you will surpass through its use all that i say, you will avoid all angers, and after being shipwrecked, you will swim and despise neptune, the god of the sea. indeed, many people wearing it for the sake of victory have obtained it. the syrians are stronger.

title: V. Lapis Diadochos.
text: the lapis lazuli is like a diamond it is most useful for divinations through water and for summoning shadows, as no other stone. furthermore, it diligently shows the likenesses of demons do not use it for the dead, for it resists the deceased. for this stone is both downward and holy, and it is consecrated by perpetual consecration.

title: VI. Lapis Smaragdus.
text: the most beautiful and powerful emerald is excellent for all divination concerning water. it has influence in every undertaking, and when carried, it adds substance and propriety to both body and speech. above all, it aids and delivers from storms. for whoever has perfected and consecrated it, will certainly obtain freedom. however, it must be perfected thus having obtained the stone, order a scarab to be carved, then with isis standing beneath it, afterward it should be lengthened. then, inserting a golden brooch into the said opening, consecrate it and prepare a certain good place, and adorn yourself and all that is yours, and you will see the glory of the stone, which god has granted it.

title: VII. Lapius [!Ed] Corallius.
text: coral possesses great power and magical protection, and aids in important endeavors. it is steadfast and repels all the tricks of dreams with its remedy. the greatest protection against the wrath of lords is an inscription of noctiluca, that is, the sign of hecate or the image of gurgon whoever carries it will never be captured by any medicine, nor by a lightning strike. it is also a great aid in war and battle, making the carrier invincible, effective, and impenetrable, without fear or sadness, and secure, allowing easy acquisition and access. furthermore, when consecrated, crushed, and sown with wheat, barley, or any fruit, it removes hail and every harmful storm from the land and when scattered in vineyards or olive groves, it repels every destructive onslaught of the winds. placed in a house, it protects against all witchcraft, the shadows of demons, empty dreams, and lightning strikes. if you have it on a ship, you will be much more effective

title: VIII. Lapis Exebenus.
text: the white stone of exebenus is fair and pleasing, with which goldsmiths often purify gold. however, it greatly soothes the stomach when sprinkled with water in a drink. furthermore, it restores the insane or the weary in a drink. and you should also give it to lovers in a drink moreover, it wonderfully suits the delights of venus those who drink it do not suffer from fatigue. it also alleviates the pain of the bladder, indeed it is most helpful. for carried, it preserves childbirth without distress, and when bound around the right thigh, it hastens the speed of labor. consecrated with perpetual consecration.

title: IX. Lapis Haematites.
text: hematite is the best gift of nature it is given to all by god. it is useful for all bodily health it is also a good safeguard of health, for this stone is permanent and especially suited to the eyes. when ground and applied with attic honey that has not been smoked, it heals eye conditions and when infused with a woman's milk, it cures all eye pain, as well as eye sores and snake bites. when drunk with water, it wonderfully heals all snake wounds and continuous bleeding when wrapped around the navel, either with ointment or through a potion, you will give the stone for healing. furthermore, it dissolves and heals with declining drops.

title: X. Lapis Chelidonius.     10
text: swallows stones are found in the crops of swallows. there are two kinds, black and red. take swallows and remove the stones from their crops they will be useful to you the red one heals lunatics, madmen, and the weak. make it so take a linen cloth, pure, and tie it on, encircling it around the arm of the sick person, and it will be cured on the third day. furthermore, it makes those who carry it agreeable and eloquent, even lovable and suitable. the black one, carried similarly, brings the best conclusions to all business matters, and also withstands all threats and wraths of kings and lords. for whoever has it with him will please all people and lead them to his will for it adapts itself to their beliefs. but if someone has sore eyes, grind it with water and apply it, and he will be healed

title: XI. Lapis Chelonites.
text: the tortoise stone is for foretelling the future having it under your tongue, you learn whatever you wish. when you have received it, dilute your mouth beforehand. it is effective for prophecy up to the sixth hour. in the first moon, it is effective for the whole day, as is the fifteenth but as the moon wanes, it is effective before sunrise. this stone is extracted from the eyes of the tortoise. if you want to know if it is true, put it above a brazier with three glowing coals and offer a sacrifice with the incense, placing this stone on top, confounding it it is not harmed at all.

title: XII. Lapis Ceraunius.
text: the ceraunian stone, which the egyptians call an emerald, is found in those places where lightning strikes. it is said, however, that it is formed from the grinding together of clouds and for this reason deserves this name. if anyone carries it with purity, they will never be struck by lightning, neither in a house nor in a villa where they are present. moreover, if a sailor possesses it, he will not be endangered by lightning or storm. furthermore, whoever carries it will surpass all others in every victory and contest. it also gives oracles to those who implore it, good dreams in sleep such is the power of this ceraunian stone.

title: XIII. Lapis Iaspis.
text: jasper is found in many places and comes in many colors. the best and most powerful is the one with the brightest color. this stone is only perfect when consecrated and carried with care. for it is a perfecter of rains and summons the rains.

title: XIV. Lapis Sapphirus.
text: the sapphire is indeed highly esteemed by the gods. some call it ormisus. kings often wear this stone around their necks, for it is the greatest protection. it possesses these powers it keeps a man free from all jaundice, makes him pleasing to the gods, and provides a body that is healthy and of good color. when worn, it restrains excessive sweating and removes all internal heat from the one who carries it. furthermore, when crushed with milk and applied to old sores, it provides great healing, and it cures weeping eyes and forehead spasms. and if anyone has twisting pains in their internal organs, it heals when drunk with milk. if anyone has a wound in their intestines, grind the stone with milk and apply it around the intestine, and it will be healed. if anyone s tongue is afflicted, similarly, anoint the tongue with the crushed stone and it will be cured. it heals all wounds, whether fresh or old, in the same way when crushed and applied

title: XV. Lapis Epistites.
text: the stone is red and translucent. it is truly found in corinth, near the temple of the god. it possesses these great virtues when placed in boiling water, it continuously makes it warmer but if you allow it to remain in the water, it removes all heat and makes the water cold. those who have this stone will ward off blight from fruits, mists, harmful whirlwinds, and locusts. it also appeases the gods through its power. furthermore, when someone holds it in their right hand against the sun, it emits rays and vomits forth fire at its will, so that those who see may marvel. it is suitable for the powerful and rebellious, for whoever carries it as a safeguard around their left arm, will scorn all difficulties and all disturbances.

title: XVI. Lapis Orites.
text: this stone is of a dark color, round in shape, which others call siderite. it is useful for healing bites of wild animals. when crushed and mixed with a rosy ointment, applied to animal wounds, it heals very powerfully, and when bound, it joins and strengthens the nerves. whoever carries it with him repels the attack of all wild beasts. those who carry this stone travel through lonely places without being troubled by wild animals. there is also another stone called orites, green and slightly pale, with markings. you will know if this stone is genuine if you place it upon a brazier with many burning coals, and upon them many different kinds of stones, and this one among them, and let it burn for an hour. then, if you see it whole and unharmed, you will have it as a safeguard, and it overcomes all danger and drives away all fear. there is also a third kind, like an iron plate, smooth on one side, sharp on the

title: XVII. Lapis Achates.
text: the jasper stone possesses excellent powers, but the one with a lion s skin-like color is effective against scorpion stings when bound or steeped in water, it immediately alleviates pain. ground and sprinkled on wounds, or given in a potion with wine, it heals viper bites. carried as an amulet, it makes the wearer persuasive, powerful, pleasing, and robust, and it gives them a good appearance, making them beloved by both gods and people.

title: XVIII. Lapis Odontolycius.
text: the teeth of a wolf, they are fortunate and useful to soldiers and hunters and those wishing to seize something and those who divine through water or by means of divination, placed beneath the bottom of a cup. they provide a firm safeguard for infants. they are especially suitable, however, for thieves who desire to steal another's property.

title: XIX. Lapis Alectorius.
text: a stone of the fowl is found in the ventricles of chickens, sometimes like a bean, sometimes crystalline in appearance, or like clear water. whoever carries this stone will be invincible against all men, though he will be tested and proven by many. for a gladiator or fighter having it in his mouth will remain unconquered, without thirst, and will defeat any athlete and charioteer in every way. milo of croton, carrying this stone, was never defeated. furthermore, many others, having it during battles, fought bravely and remained invincible. and kings, exiled from their kingdom, regained their dominion, not only their own, but also that of others. it also makes those who carry it secure, pleasing, and agreeable. moreover, it restores concerning sexual pleasures. but it will also benefit women who wish to please men for it is a common stone. it also provides firmness in speech. it makes the carrier appear majestic, generous, virtuous, and

title: XX. Lapis Gagates.     5
text: indeed, the stone agate is found in a river called gagano. it is of a pale color and rather long. however, it possesses great and excellent powers. if women have not had their monthly flow, if this stone is crushed and placed upon burning coals, then let the woman be ordered to walk around so that her womb may be vaporized, and thus it will be cleansed, without harm and without pain. if anyone is buying slaves and wants to know if they are unstable or lunatic, heat the stone, and if anyone has such a defect, they will fall upon that very defect this stone has such power. it resolves all deceit and bonds, and when heated, it drives away all snakes, vipers, and serpents from the place.

title: XXI. Lapis Medius.
text: the black stone is of a middle size when ground, it emits a yellow color. it has many good and bad powers. if anyone compares joy to revenge against enemies or robbers... so people should be ready both for good things and for bad, if fortune has led them. you will know that those who act well will not reach the place of the impious... therefore, this stone, ground on a cutting board with a woman's milk, which she once produced in her first childbirth of a boy, applied as a salve, cures white spots in the eyes and removes all eye pain even if someone has despaired of seeing, it heals. furthermore, for those suffering from gout, it is ground in the same way with the milk of a sheep that once bore a male fetus, and it is applied and healed. it also cures the kidneys, shortness of breath, and internal organs. this medicine is the greatest and has been tested by many. indeed, you will prepare this medicine

title: XXII. Lapis Syrtius.     20
text: the lapis syrtius, also called sapphirus, is found in the furthest parts of libya, cast up by the sea during storms, and also occurs in the region of apulia, near lucania. damigeron writes this stone would have conquered all the power of other stones, possessing the greatest power and being foremost among protective charms. therefore, whoever possesses this stone is armed against all deceit, and resists all witchcraft and the plots of other stones. its natural power is said to be divine. if someone is sent into bonds by a king or magistrate because of misdeeds, and if someone wishes to release him, if it can be done, touch the heads of the bonds, and they will immediately break. once freed, go to the enemy and touch this stone, and the enemy will open before him, and he will go wherever he pleases, for no one will notice him. it is also best for cultivating favor and friendship.

title: XXIII. Lapis Capnites.
text: this stone resembles crystal but is quite different from it. it is best for travelers. it renders the wearer pleasing to both gods and people, and makes him handsome and shapely. it cures those suffering from dropsy when bound around the left arm. it is also useful for removing fears and threats. for whoever possesses it comes into favor with all peoples and softens threats.

title: XXIV. Lapis Optallius.
text: an obsidian stone is effective around the eyes for whoever wears it will never suffer from eye strain. it is also useful for thieves, so they may not be caught for it obscures the sight of those nearby, so they cannot see them stealing. thieves used to wear this.

title: XXV. Lapis Obsyontes.
text: indeed, the philosopher's stone, as our ancestors say, seems to be of varied power. it is, in fact, the best and with great effort resists uncertain dreams, like no other stone. furthermore, it aids those who wish to harm. if someone carves the sun and moon on it and carries it consecrated, it demands a good life.

title: XXVI. Lapis Hieracites.
text: the black stone, first numbered and approved by many, is moderately black and suitable. you will have it. however, do this when you wish to know something beforehand, wash your mouth with the best honey and place the stone under your tongue, and you will learn what is within you, or what someone thinks or considers, all future events. but it is most suitable for requests for when you ask for something, carrying it, no one will contradict you. truly, it also works for love affairs and persuasion by necessity, more than other stones. therefore, tie the stone to yourself, and go to boys or to a woman, and they will not contradict you. if you wish to know that this stone is true, you will be able to recognize it thus mix it with milk and honey, pour it around the stone, and place it, and a fly will not sit there, thus driving it away. let this not be considered a jest. from the same mixture, pour

title: XXVII. Lapis Carsydonius.
text: a consecrated and water-bound lapis lazuli, 15. it protects. furthermore, whoever has carried it from childhood will never sink or be troubled. it also makes the bearer handsome, faithful, powerful, and capable of accomplishing everything. it should be carved with mars in armor, or a veiled maiden scattering laurel. consecrated with perpetual consecration.

title: XXVIII. Lapis Lychnites.
text: a beautiful, translucent blue lapis lazuli, suitable for placing around the neck against night birds, protects against them. furthermore, when placed in a linen cloth and bound to the forehead, it stops the flow of blood. whoever carries it knows how to predict the future, prevents the sick from speaking of other things, and drives away illnesses. when wrapped around, it also heals nerves and warts on the body, applied to the area where there is pain. moreover, if someone has this consecrated stone in a house that is on fire, if it happens by chance, the fire is immediately extinguished. this stone is consecrated to vulcan.

title: XXIX. Lapis Topatozontes.
text: the finest topazos are excellent for divination. if anyone drinks sea grape wine and becomes mad, grind a stone upon a small wooden bowl, mix it with water, and give it to the madman to drink. then, apply the stone around his neck, and he will be healed. it is also useful when sacrifices are made and the gods are appeased. it carries persuasion with it, secures favors, and makes those who are pregnant grateful. it is sanctified by perpetual consecration.

title: XXX. Lapis Magnitis.     10
text: the magnet stone has great powers. it is full of spirit, that is, it attracts and holds whatever iron is placed upon it. it is found in colchis. they say it was used in magic indeed, a man named medon is to be sought after. from him, medi, who used it every hour by the brightness of twelve signs..... truly, all magicians have confirmed the power of this stone, as if they possessed the greatest powers, and so they discovered how to test their wives' affection towards them, whether they always maintained goodwill, and they diligently learned if they had done so. while their wives were sleeping, they placed the stone secretly beneath their heads, and if she was chaste from all other men, she approached her husband in her sleep, rolling about, and embraced him as if moved by someone. but if she had lain with another man, the stone emitted a stench of a most foul odor, so that she fell from the bed to the floor. it

title: XXXI. Lapis Lyngurium.
text: heather honey is the best protection in the house, and is safe for pregnant women and children. it also resists the regional plague when drunk with wine.

title: XXXII. Lapis Daphnea.
text: make a stone of sea lavender for those with lymphatic issues, demonic possession, or to promote blood flow, or for those suffering from dropsy.

title: XXXIII. Lapis Charcedonius.
text: a pierced and iron-covered jasper stone whoever carries it will prevail in the matter.

title: XXXIV. Lapis Galactites.
text: the stone called galactites some call it anachites, others leucographites the egyptians call it smaragdus, others galbatites. the magi and egyptians call it synechites, for it contains within itself all that you intend, being the only stone of its kind. but ostanes, master of all the magi, called it lethargum, as if it brings oblivion of all evils, for it makes even useful business productive. he praised it as having greater power than any other. the magi, not from hearsay, but from scripture, were astonished and experienced every magical action. they adorned this stone, the aforementioned galactites, as the most effective and powerful of all, with extreme praise. it is said to be called galactites because it causes milk to flow in women who lack it. do this thus the woman is ordered to fast then you give her the powdered stone with gruel, or barley, or water,

title: XXXV. Lapis Berillus.
text: a beautiful stone this is a great stone it is bright, serene, clear, like the oil of apollo. carve a marine locust upon it and a small horn beneath its feet, and place savory herb beneath the gem, enclosed in a little gold. consecrated and carried, it unites love and makes it greater than all. furthermore, this stone is good for eye ailments and for all health, if you put it in water and give the water to drink. it removes belching, sighs, and pain of the liver.

title: XXXVI. Lapis Selenitis.
text: a stone resembling jasper, known as selenite. strong and heavy, bright, wondrous, sacred. its splendor waxes and wanes with the moon. it is truly useful for many things, bringing love and fulfilling desires. it also helps those suffering from consumption when worn during the waxing moon or when carried during the waning moon, it works wonderfully.

title: XXXVII. Lapis Panchrodes.
text: a five-layered cake possesses every color, purple, red, black, pale, rose, and green, all diverse colors. having it in the morning, green is beneficial. it brings about victory, for it is unconquered and sacred, that is, holy. carve into it images of latinus, hippocrates, and three recipients from behind it aids against all magical arts.

title: XXXVIII. Lapis Collurus.
text: blue lapis lazuli it is similar to sapphire it has a pale marine color. suitable for the adornment of kings and powerful people. wear it around the neck as a pendant.

title: XXXIX. Lapis Trisutes.
text: a cake resembling the sky's arch here strong, weighty, having in its center a peak like a white tiara. here great, carried with ceremony, it is offered for a cause without right.

title: XL. Lapis Melas.
text: the black stone contains small stars. it is also called syrtis. when someone speaks of its cause, it brings blessing, attainment, and victory, and expels every disturbance of the enemy, their damages, and sorceries, and magical pollutions, and the incantation of ancient potions and prayers, and hatred, and all other evils from the body. it is a consecrated stone. use it when the moon is waning from the seventeenth to the thirtieth day when it is waxing, until the fifteenth day, not beyond.

title: XLI. Lapis Gagatromanes.
text: it is similar in color to a goat, that is, a wild goat. if anyone has used this stone, it is useful. however, in stories, it is also powerful against enemies who possess it. hercules used this stone, and after he laid it down, he was defeated.

title: XLII. Lapis Phoenicites.
text: like a phoenician date, reddish or blood-red, a wonderful stone. carried in the left hand, it is useful against melancholy and for undertaking actions.

title: XLIII. Lapis Lyncis.     10
text: dry in two parts in honey and milk, then remove and enclose in a ring, and thus you will carry it, and wherever you go with it, you will have joy and merriment as you wish.

title: XLIV. Lapis Narcissites.
text: take a moderate amount of green malachite. it has the scent of crushed narcissus flowers, a magnificent bloom. whoever uses this stone will conquer all.

title: XLV. Lapis Steatites.
text: it is like a lion's fat. this one is brighter in color than a lion's. whoever uses it on the left arm will be victorious.

title: XLVI. Lapis Camptine.
text: to gain favor with both gods and people, and to bring joy to the body, and to restrain the fears of ancestors or their fury, and to secure commendations. it cures dropsy when bound to the left arm. consecrate this one from any consecration.

title: XLVII. Lapis Chrysolithus.
text: it is thick, bright, and golden in appearance. this, when applied to a gold shaving, is a protective charm against nightly fears. pierced and passed through with donkey hairs and fastened to the left arm, it conquers all demons.

title: XLVIII. Lapis Chrysolithus alter.
text: golden stone it is indeed like the eye of a turtledove. it is also an aid to desire, love, and justice. it makes one well-received, articulate, gracious, lovable, and friendly to those who see them. it opens every entrance it also softens the gaze of anger.

title: XLIX. Lapis Apocheamus.
text: we prepare a large stone, which is longer than a goat's eye, having within it a shape that is oblong and white, not very pale. held in the left hand, it brings about minor injuries.

title: L. Lapis Sardius.     5
text: this color appears light, or mottled it is well-regarded by women, and pleasing. carve a vine and ivy into it.

title: (I. LATIN II.)
text: if physicians fail you, use a good diet by the counsel of me, -- measured feeding and moderation in travel, -- and be not malicious for anyone's departure, but be meek in trouble, glad in plenty, not pensive nor thoughtful for any sudden chance, not grumpy, but merry after your degree. if physic lacks, make this your guidance.

title: (II. LATIN I.)
text: keep from cold your feet, your stomach, and your head eat no raw meat, take good heed thereto, drink wholesome drink, and feed thee on light bread, and with an appetite from your meat look that you go. lead your life in chastity, you shall find it best so drink not upon your sleep, but do as you teach, and bear no wrath to friend or foe use not to sup late, nor to drink much.

title: (III. LATIN IV.)
text: do not eat on the morrow before appetite. clear air and walking make good digestion. do not drink between meals for any frivolous pleasure, but if thirst or travel occasion it. and over-salted food does great oppression to feeble stomachs that will not restrain themselves from things that are contrary to their constitution, for they do to their stomachs often much pain.

title: (IV. LATIN VII.)
text: avoid all late suppers, neither by day nor by night, nor any rich, excessive meals and be wary of nodding heads and candlelight, and also of long sleep and idleness. for she is the porter of all these vices. avoid all drunken people, liars, and lechers, and all those who indulge in such unprofitableness, and also jesters and revelers.

title: (V. LATIN III.)
text: to serve well, do not give credence be not too hasty, nor too eager to please do no violence to poor people be gentle in speech, and moderate in feeding. at many meals, he does not greedily eat a long sleep after food does much harm. blame no condition which is worthy of praise but to say the best, set all your pleasure.

title: (VI. LATIN VI.)
text: use fire by the morrow, and to bedward at eve. to dispel black mists and air of pestilence and arise thou early if thou be in health, and first by the morrow do god reverence. to visit the poor do thy diligence, and on the needy have compassion, for good deeds cause mirth in conscience, and in heaven to have great possession.

title: (VII. LATIN V.)
text: do not be extravagant in your clothing beyond your station be guided by moderation while you are alive and with three kinds of people, do not be in debate first, with your superior, be wary to strive, avoid quarrels with your equal, with your inferior to strive, it is but shame therefore i counsel you, while you are alive, to live in peace, and gain yourself a good name.

title: (VIII. LATIN X.)
text: to maintain a man's well-being, both in body and soul, is a worthy goal for anyone who wishes to pursue it. moderate feeding preserves a man's health, and likewise charity is due to the soul. do not disregard this diet, for it is good and true though it may seem the work of no apothecary, nor any other master who can demonstrate great skill, i counsel you to be guided by this dietary plan.

title:
Albrecht Dürer an Willibald Pirckheimer in Nürnberg

Venedig, 6. Januar 1506
text: to the honorable master wilbolt pirkamer, citizen of nuremberg, my esteemed lord. i wish you much health and a blessed new year, and all that is good for you. my willing service to you, dear pirkamer. i inquire about your health i desire much good of you from god. furthermore, as you commanded me to acquire some pearls and stones, i inform you that i could not obtain anything of good quality or worth its price, for it is scraped from the germans. those who trade on the rhine at gand want to gain four gulden from it, but they are deceitful people who live there. one must not trust anyone to serve you faithfully. therefore, some other good fellows have advised me to be wary of them, for they cheat people. one can buy better things in frankfurt for less money than in venice. and regarding the pewterer you wished me to order, the people at im hoff have already procured it. but if you need anything

title:
Albrecht Dürer an Willibald Pirckheimer in Nürnberg 
Venedig, 7. Februar 1506
text: to the honorable master wilbolt pirkamer in nuremberg, my gracious lord. i willingly offer you my service, dear sir. if it pleases you at all, i heartily wish you, from the bottom of my heart, as i do myself. i have recently written to you let the messenger be welcome to you. in the meantime, my mother has written to me and scolded me for not writing to you and for not telling you why you have caused me displeasure by not writing to me i must almost account to you for it and she is very worried about how things are. so i will not hold myself accountable for failing to write and for you not being at home. but as soon as i learned that you were home or would be coming home, i wrote to you immediately, and also instructed the steward to tell you my service. therefore, i beg you to forgive me, if i have not found anyone else on earth so dear as you. i do

title:
Albrecht Dürer an Willibald Pirckheimer in
Nürnberg Venedig, 28. Februar 1506
text: to the honorable and wise master wilbolt pirckheimer in nuremberg, my esteemed lord. it pleases me greatly to do what i can for you, dear pirckheimer. i also receive divine favor, and i earnestly pray for it. however, i will not be finished before pentecost. i have sold all my paintings, one by one. i gave two for 24 guilders, and the other three for the three rings, which were valued at 24 guilders. but i had them appraised by good craftsmen, who say they are worth 22 guilders. as you write about buying some stones, i thought i would also send you the rings through franz im hoff. let him show them to you, as you understand them. if you like them, have him say what they are worth. he will keep them for that amount. but if you need them no longer, send them

title:
Albrecht Dürer an Willibald Pirckheimer in
Nürnberg Venedig, 8. März 1506
text: to the esteemed master wilbolt pirkamer in nuremberg, my gracious lord. my willing service to, dear pirkamer. i send you a ring with a sapphire. i had previously written to you separately about it. and i have not been able to acquire it due to a journey, as i spent two days in the city with a good companion, whom i entrusted with all the goldsmiths both german and foreign to find it. they made appraisals, but none found one equal to it or for such a price. through great luck, i bought it for 18 guilders and 4 marcells from a man who had carried it on his own person, who promised to serve me if i first gave him the ring. and as soon as i bought it, a german goldsmith offered to give me 3 guilders profit if he set it for me. therefore, i hope he will please me. everyone says that it is a found

title: Ein essen von dreyssig ayeren
text: to make a dish of thirty or forty eggs, take two sow plums, one smaller than the other, and soak them well with water inside. then take the eggs and shell them, separating the whites particularly and the yolks particularly. then take the smaller plums and stir the yolks through each other, placing them in the plums so they are full and bound. then season them well and throw them into a pot, letting them cook until they are firm. then shell the plums from the yolks and take the plums and cut a hole in them so that the yolk may enter. then put the yolks in the plums, and beat the whites through each other. take then a funnel and press it into the hole and place the whites on the yolks so that the plums are full, and then bind them. place them then in the pot and let them simmer until the whites cook around the yolks. add a bit of salt and give it, and a little vinegar to it.

title: A dish made from 30 or 40 eggs
text: to make a dish from 30 eggs or 40 in the form of one large egg, take two pig's bladders, one smaller than the other. rinse them carefully inside. then take the eggs, remove the shells, and separate the whites from the yolks. take the small pig's bladder, mix the yolks and put them into the smaller bladder until the bladder is full. tie the bladder up carefully and place it in a pot. let it boil until the yolks become solid. then remove the bladder from the yolks. take the bigger bladder and cut a hole in it, big enough to put in the yolks. sew up this hole in the bigger bladder with the yolks inside. then mix the whites of the eggs. take a funnel, put it into the opening hole of the bigger bladder and pour the whites on top of the yolks within the bigger bladder, so that the bladder is filled. tie it up, put it into the pot and let it boil once
