title: References
text: to make a fine sauce of almonds. take fresh almonds and grind them finely. then take sweet water or wine and boil it, and strain it through a cloth. then add the ground almonds and let it simmer until it thickens. add saffron and sugar and salt to taste.

title: Ein osterfladen zu pachen
text: to make a pie, first prepare the dough as usual. then, take 12 eggs and beat them well. add a grated semolina, as you would for a simple pastry, but not too stiff. add half a handful of wine pearls and some melted butter. spread this mixture onto the prepared pie crust. if the mixture spreads evenly, it is properly done.

title: To bake an easter cake
text: beat three eggs and prepare a pastry base as usual. then, whisk together twelve eggs until well combined. add breadcrumbs, as you would for fritters, to lighten the mixture. incorporate half a pound of dried raisins and the best butter available. pour this mixture over a thinly rolled pastry base and bake until crisp.

title: Some notes
text: a bottom make a dough from eggs, so that you can roll it out finely like paper, lay it double, and roll it again with a roller. cut the pastry into small pieces with a small wheel, dip them in butter.

title:
Dumplings of fishes. From: Anno Christy
1609 in Nürnberg. Ein schön künstlich Kochbüchlein
von vielen vnd manchen Richten.
text: dumplings of fishes take one pound of fresh fish, such as carp or trout. clean it well and remove the bones and head. grind the fish very finely. take half a pound of stale bread crumbs, a quarter pound of butter, two eggs, salt, and a little mace. mix all these ingredients together thoroughly. form the mixture into dumplings, then boil them in salted water until they float to the surface. serve with melted butter.

title: Knödlein von Fischen Zumachen.
text: first, prepare the fish as they should be, gut them. then chop the fish finely and season to your liking. wrap in pastry and place in hot fat. bake slightly and make a broth with wine, and verjuice. add that too, it is good.

title: Dumplings of fishes
text: first, boil the fish properly, then remove the bones and flake the fish into small pieces. season to your liking, add saffron to give it a yellow color, and coat it in flour. fry in hot fat and bake gently. prepare a wine sauce, adding a spice mixture and saffron. the dish is then complete.

title: Bubenpfulbe
text: to make a boy s pulse, take one calf s tongue and lungs, and cut them well, and cut bacon underneath. grind it small, and beat eggs into it, and saffron, and pepper. then make egg leaves and wrap them around it, and cover it over with eggs, and bake it in lard.

title: A rough translation
text: to make a pastry for a young boy, take calf s tongue and lungs, cut into pieces and chop with lard. add eggs and season with saffron and pepper. then, make thin sheets of pastry and roll them loosely around the chopped filling. brush the ends with egg and bake or fry in fat.

title:
Parallel texts from other manuscripts with the same or a similar
recipe
text: to make a baked puff pastry take a calf s lungs and cook them well, then slice bacon underneath and chop it finely, add onions and pepper and saffron, and bake them with mint leaves and butter inside, and cover with onions, and bake in lard. to make a puff pastry take a calf s lungs and cook them well and slice bacon underneath and chop it finely and add onions and pepper and saffron and bake them with mint leaves and butter inside and cover the edges with onion. bake in lard. a puff pastry. take a calf s tongue and the lungs, cook them well, then chop them and bacon underneath, add onions, saffron, and good herbs, and long leaves of good dough well kneaded, and butter inside, and cover the edges with a thin onion dough, and bake in lard.

title: A rough translation:
text: to make a good pie, take calf s or buck s liver and boil it over a grill according to its size. then cut it into small pieces and pound them very finely in a mortar. add a little honey and spices, along with raisins or plums and two eggs, and mix everything well with the liver. shape the mixture back into a single liver shape. place this piece into a pot with clear fat and turn it frequently. let it bake in the pot, then put it on a spit and baste it with ordinary lard. sprinkle with honey and spices and roast until cooked through. this dish is called pie liver.

title: A rough translation
text: make a thick paste from the peas, pounding them well if you wish to create a castle-like appearance. sweeten lightly with sugar. shape the pea paste into a shallow dish, about a hand's breadth high and wide, and place it in a serving dish. decorate the outside with two crosses, each about a hand's breadth high and a short span long. build a surrounding wall around the dish, also a hand's breadth high, using more of the pea paste. fashion small cones from the paste to serve as towers, and arrange them along the wall as desired. pour a generous amount of broth into the pea dish. serve with fried, baked, or roasted herring.

title: Some Notes:
text: prepare the peas by boiling them in lye, then washing them in fresh water until they lose their shells. next, boil, dry, and pound them in a mortar. they can also be mixed with honey and strained. the two crosses should likely be prepared from the peas as well.

title:
Regimen sanitatis editum pro Friderico palatino Rheni
per doctorem Minsinger in fluxu catarrali ad pectus.
text: most illustrious and high-born prince as your princely grace experiences a great flow from the heart into the chest, which has initially burdened your grace on the right side of the chest with tightness and shortness of breath, and now has brought a remarkable heat with a mixture of fever, something your grace has not had before, so that such a flow with the heat in future times may not bring a severe illness internally to the chest and also to the lungs, i have, according to your grace s request and to my ability with god s help, described how your grace should conduct himself with the six necessities that a person needs to maintain life and health, if he holds himself properly within and uses them well, namely air, exercise, rest, food and drink, sleep and wakefulness, excesses and purification thereof, and too much of the mind, anger, sadness and worry etcetera.

title: Von dem lufft.
text: to protect yourself from the air, you should avoid foul, coarse, misty, windy, and intensely cold and damp air. when the air is like this, you should stay indoors during the day and in your sleeping chamber at night. and you should make use of juniper, spruce, beech, or birch wood, or fragrant herbs, so that the air becomes dry, pure, warm, and fragrant. at these times, the head covering should be worn, but not too tightly, so that cold, damp, and foul air cannot flow in.

title: Regierung mit essen vnd trincken.
text: you should maintain yourself with food and drink as follows avoid all foods that are indigestible, that create excessive moisture in the head and brain, especially garlic, onion, lentils, peas, beans, radish, nuts and hazelnuts, cabbage, herbs, and rue. also avoid strong wine that quickly rises to the head, and milk and whey, and anything made from milk. however, goat s milk with sugar may be eaten or drunk if you wish, as it will strengthen the body.

title: Von fleisch
text: eat all old beef, pork, and such meat that is dried or salted. also eat game with four feet, called deer, hind, swine, bear, fox. but the lungs of the fox are good for your grace, as are the lungs of a hedgehog, if they have a special property to strengthen the chest and the lungs, as wise physicians say. your grace should also eat old hares, old doves, and geese, and other fowl that live in the water. your grace should eat brains, lungs, liver, milk, cauldrons from all large animals. your grace shall eat young hunner meat, hens and capons, young doves, roe deer, hazel grouse, pheasant, young calf meat, lamb meat, kitchen meat, rhine game well hunted, or a young deer well hunted, and small fowl, buntings, cranes, ground-tits, and larks, and thrushes. and such meat may your grace eat boiled or roasted,

title: von ops
text: your grace should generally avoid plums and cherries and pears when it is very hot. your grace may eat a little of plums and cherries and pears on an empty stomach before any other food, when they are mild for digestion. some physicians say that a spoonful of apples, gently fried with sugar, softens the chest and helps to expel humors. some women also say that fried onions are good for the humors. but i do not hold by that, when they give bad moisture and phlegm in the head, through which the flux is restrained. however, if your grace is healthy, then your grace may eat fried pears and fried quinces after a meal, when they dry the food from the stomach and help with the digestion. avoid other ripe fruits and other fruits that grow in these lands, such as mulberries and those that readily fall, and nespels, sperwers, and chestnuts. however, figs cooked and grapes with a brew of sennetted herbs may your grace

title: Von bewegung vnd der ruow.
text: after eating, avoid moving about too quickly, especially after a substantial meal. instead, relax and entertain yourself, perhaps by reading old histories of emperors and lords, or something amusing, or noble poems, or dice games. however, do not entirely abandon movement and exercise. each morning, upon waking, cleanse yourself, urinating and clearing any other bodily fluids from the nose and other passages. afterwards, exercise with bowel movements or riding, or some other way, until the passages are clear and relaxed and the skin feels warm. then, rest a while after the exercise and proceed to the table to eat and drink. during the meal, begin with easily digestible foods, such as broth and pottage, and then move on to coarser and more substantial fare, like beer. a person should not eat too much, and fewer dishes should be on the table than the stomach can comfortably hold. this aforementioned exercise can also be performed in the evening before dinner. if, due to inclement weather or some

title: Von der regierung des schlafens vnd wachens.
text: to rest well in the day, especially soon after eating, do not sleep, unless it is that your grace has not slept the night or your grace has felt the need to sleep during the day. especially in summer, your grace may sleep for two or three hours after eating, for a half or whole hour with a raised head and shoulders, with a pillow and with shoes taken off, but let the feet be covered with light cloths. and the right time to begin sleeping is two or three hours after supper. and the sleep should not occur on the back, for that sleep is very harmful, when it holds excess moisture in the head and brain and prevents it from having its proper exit. therefore, sleep should first occur on the right side for an hour or two, then on the left side until daybreak, and then it should end on the right side. and whoever feels, now that your grace is burdened with a flux in the head and the stomach, that your grace may

title:
Nun volgt regierung der vberflússekeit vnd reyngung

von der vberflússekeit.
text: take care to moderate your eating and drinking, and avoid excess, lest your stomach become displeased with the food and drink, and the resulting flux in your head may be driven into your chest. it is especially harmful at night, when the flux in your head occurs during the night and also affects the head. therefore, your grace should eat moderately and lightly at dinner. and your grace should strive to cleanse yourself daily for the purpose of digestion, with urine and to release the excess from the head through the nose, internally through the throat, and through the gums. if nature is reluctant to do this, you should force it with enemas, made with cumin and salt, or made with soap, and for the cleansing of the head through the nostrils, with plugs that you insert into the nose in the morning, as i have given your grace. your grace may loosen the head once or twice a week with herbs in a bath, as i have learned from wilhelm, and in the meantime

title: Regierung der zuvelle des gemüts.
text: to avoid sorrow, sadness, fear, and especially anger, which move the flow and the blood, and the heat in the head, and increase the flow in the head even more. therefore, your grace should be as cheerful as she can. and thus ends the regimen, as to how your grace should govern herself with the aforementioned six items. but if your grace should need to use something for the flow in the head, and for the closest part in the chest, and for the tightness of the breath, and how one should make and use it, i have described it in particular. i will, when it is necessary, faithfully give instruction as to how it should be used. and i have made this regimen for your grace as concisely as possible, so that even the simplest person can understand and remember it. and if anyone, learned or unlearned, wants to argue against it, i am ready to prove what is written here, with the respected writings of hippocrates, avicenna

title: Kaffee und Thee
text: once, young women with dark eyebrows, asked me, friend, why do you drink coffee and i replied to the young woman in honor of the brunettes the brunettes were boasting today in coffee time, as they disputed the preference away from the blondes. they quarreled over coffee, 10 and called me to mediate. come said a flirtatious young woman, and waved her fan, you once sang, you could mediate handel 15 now mediate our dispute as well. but first, i must ask you why do you drink the coffee treachorous brunette, my confession will be heard by the most well-behaved blondes, it will be heard by blonde doris,

title: Eÿer Tortte
text: make a milk porridge over the fire. put in a large egg. add some butter, also add a little wheat flour and a crumbled roll. let everything simmer together until it becomes thin, like a mush. let it cool afterward, make a crust two or three fingers high, put the filling inside, and bake until done. stir in plenty of sugar beforehand and when you want to eat it, sprinkle some sugar on top.

title: A platter from a batter? A sweet pancake?
text: pour creamy milk into a saucepan and heat over a fire. add fat about the volume of an egg then stir in egg yolks, wheat flour, and crushed breadcrumbs. simmer until the mixture thickens to the consistency of porridge or mashed potatoes. allow to cool, then shape the mixture into a thick pancake, roughly two to three finger widths deep. fill with stuffing and bake until cooked through. before baking, stir plenty of sugar into the batter. when serving, sprinkle with sugar.

title: Magen-Strützl.
text: one pound of sugar, 4 ounces candied citron, 3 ounces candied ginger, 5 ounces almonds, 1 ounce cinnamon, 1 quarter-pound of muscatel flowers, 1 quarter-pound of cloves. these pieces must all be cut uniformly. once this is done, the sugar must be crushed into small pieces and 1 goblet of water added, then simmered until it melts. remove from the heat, then add the candied fruit, followed by the spices, and finally stir in the almonds. when it begins to thicken, pour it into paper molds or jars. when cool and pressed, they will settle.

title: Muscatzin-Letzelten.
text: one pound of unblanched almonds, wipe off the dust, then grind them coarsely, but finely, and quite without adding any liquid. once ground, take one pound of powdered sugar, 8 ounces of fine flour, ground cinnamon until it darkens, and chopped mace as much as you like. mix everything well together and beat in 6 whole eggs, adding them gradually so as not to spill any. the dough must be properly combined. then place it on an oblate and bake as you would bread or pastry.

title: Bätzl zu machen.
text: one pound of sugar, one pound of fine flour, two ounces of cinnamon, one ounce of cloves. take the rinds of three lemons, add all of these together, then beat in six fresh eggs one by one, and work the dough well, but not too stiff. form into small balls, place them on a baking sheet previously greased with wax, but wiped clean with a cloth. bake until finely browned they will be beautiful and good.

title: Gute Mandl-Letzelt.
text: grind half a pound of almonds until they soften and the skins come off. then chop them coarsely. from six almond pieces, press them in an oven until they are browned. then take half a pound of sugar, twelve lots of fine flour, and a little water. beat them well together. add half a lot of ground nutmeg, finely chopped, and mix that in with the sugar and flour. then add the almonds and mix well. make a dough from this and bake it finely in a tart pan.

title: Gut Gewürtz-Letzelt.
text: one pound fine flour, one pound ground candied sugar, a pinch of cinnamon, a pinch of cloves, a pinch of nutmeg all the spices coarsely chopped 5 egg whites, 3 egg yolks, well beaten, and mixed into the dough. finally, shape it.

title: Hobelschaiten zu machen.
text: grind half a pound of almonds and one quarter of a nutmeg coarsely. chop the other quarter of a nutmeg finely, add a few drops of water and as much powdered sugar as needed to sweeten. cut square pieces from oblaten wafers. spread them thickly with the almond mixture, mixing in some lemon zest. bake until lightly browned, then brush with egg wash. bake again until the egg wash is well set.

title: Springerl zu machen.
text: take a pound of sugar, grind it and sift it, take 24 ounces of flour, and mix it in. add cinnamon, cloves, mace, and lemon peel, chopped as finely as you can. mix that in as well. begin with egg whites and lemon juice, making the dough as thick as you can. knead it well, roll it out as thinly as paper, press it onto a mold. let it stand for a few hours, then bake it until golden brown. let it cool, then brush it with an icing. place it back in tart pans so the icing will form flakes, and let it cool.

title: Das Zimmet-Brod zu machen.
text: in a bowl, cream together 12 egg yolks, 6 whole eggs, and 3 quarter-pounds of sugar for a good hour. then add 3 quarter-pounds of fine flour, mixing in a spoonful at a time. next, add a little bit of chopped muscat flower and half a quarter-pound of ground cinnamon, mixing the spices in as well. then add a quarter-pound of coarsely chopped almonds, ensuring they are incorporated last. grease the mold with butter and pour the batter into it. when it s baked halfway, remove the mold from the oven. dissolve some coarsely ground sugar in water and spread it over the batter, then return to the oven.

title: Wie man die Stiffteln-Letzelt macht.
text: sliced almonds, pistachios, cinnamon, cloves, orange peel, and lemon peel are combined. also, one takes egg whites and beats them very finely, then adds sugar, stirring it in as one would a small cake. with this dough, one covers the almonds. one adds sugar as sweet as one desires. then, one takes wafers and cuts them into squares, spreads a thin layer of water ice on top and bottom, and bakes them finely and beautifully.

title: Pasterial-Letzelt.
text: for one pound of almonds, use one pound of sugar, finely ground almonds, and finely sifted sugar. then, add half a pound of clarified sugar and mix it with the ground almonds, pressing firmly and allowing it to cool. afterward, knead with the remaining half pound of sugar, shape the dough, and roll it out very thinly. press letzelt molds onto the dough and let it stand for two hours so that it doesn't run apart.

title:
Wie man die Grün-Pätzl/ oder Letzelt-Lauber macht/
oder was man will von Pistatzy-Taig.
text: ground almonds, half a pound also, clarified sugar, half a pound. take a quarter of the sugar and mix it with the almonds, and press it in a bowl. then take the remaining sugar to work with and combine. also, add a beaten egg yolk underneath and mix it in. once mixed, make the dough with spinach. you must take good spinach and boil it. then drain the water, place it in fresh water, and rinse it. grind it and add it to the almonds, not too much, so that it has a good color. add an egg on top, and bake it. use more heat on top than below.

title: Wie man die Baurn-Krapffen macht.
text: beat two whole eggs and three yolks in a bowl, and whisk very well. add half a pound of sugar and beat for a good half hour. add coarsely chopped almonds, 4 lots, and thinly sliced candied citron peel, along with some muscat flower. add flour until a thin dough forms then stir no more. place on wafers, decorate with almonds, and bake, with more heat on top than below.

title: Ein gutes Convect.
text: add sugar as much as you like and let it boil very thick until it becomes hard. when a drop of water is added, take long-cut almonds, pistachios, candied orange peel, candied lemon peel, and lemon juice. when you remove it from the fire, press the juice in, and also stir the chopped pieces into the sugar. place the nuts in water and swirl them around, then pour the sugar over them.

title: Musquetirer-Brod.
text: take half a pound of honey, well clarified. add one lot of cloves, one lot of cinnamon, one lot of ginger, one lot of pepper, one lot of coriander, two measures of nutmeg, and the zest of two lemons, all coarsely chopped, and put them into the warm honey. simmer briefly with the spices. then add baker s yeast, mix it with the honey and spices to form a firm dough, kneading it well. the dough should not become cold, otherwise it will not come together. place it in a baking pan and bake for 3 or 4 hours, with more heat on top than below.

title: Piscotten zu machen.
text: beat one pound of clarified sugar into a bowl. remove all the bird's eyes from it. add the clarified butter to the sugar, and stir for two hours. afterwards, take half a pound of starch and half a pound of fine flour, and stir it into the butter and sugar until well combined. pour the batter through a sieve onto paper, shaping it like small fish cakes. bake in a flat pan, and cut while warm from the paper.

title: Geröste Mandel.
text: pound a pound of almonds in a copper bowl, set over the fire, and roast until completely dry and hard, turning them constantly so they don't burn. pour them onto a clean cloth and wipe them to remove any dust. take three-quarters of a pound of sugar into a bowl, add half a teacup of water, and let it boil until it foams well. add the roasted almonds and let them roast with the sugar until the sugar adheres to the almonds as if they were candied. then they are ready.

title: Letzelten von grünen Pomerantschen zu machen.
text: grate the zest from oranges. then bind the juice in a cloth and bruise it in boiling water, letting the heat work on it. afterwards, quickly transfer it to cold water, and do this for about ten minutes until the bitterness is gone. press the oranges until they are completely dry. grind them in a stone mortar. add lemon juice and gradually stir in sugar, a spoonful at a time, until it forms a dough. then make small pastries from it and press them onto a board.

title:
Weisse Lemoni-Letzelt zu machen mit Oepffel oder Kitten vermischt/
von Oepffeln werden sie schön weiß/ aber von Kitten
geschmächer.
text: peel a citron, using only the yellow zest. then, grate the white part into fresh water and let it soak for half an hour. after that, remove the grated citron from the fresh water, tie it in a cloth, and pound it in hot water until the bitterness is released. quickly transfer it to cold water, then stir it into half a pound of finely strained cream or oil. add half a pound of fine white sugar, crushed small. mix it in and simmer until it slides off the spoon. pour into a bowl and let it sit overnight. the next day, spread the mixture thinly onto paper, shaping it with molds and impressing a design as desired. you can beautifully extract the citron's sourness and mix it in just as you remove it from the heat. however, be careful that the heat doesn't add too much. when the pieces have rested on the paper for two days, they should be carefully pressed to ensure they bake evenly and remain moist inside.

title: Marillen-Pätzl.
text: boil apricots in water until the skin starts to split. peel them, clean them well, and remove the stones. press the pulp through a sieve. take 1 pound of sugar, pour 1 small pitcher of water over it, and boil until thick drops form. add the strained apricot pulp. continue to boil until it cleanly separates from the pot. add confectioner s sugar, press out large spots over the fire, and form the remaining mixture into round shapes.

title: Gute Citeroni-Letzelt zu machen.
text: first, take the citrons, cut off the yellow rinds, chop them very finely, wrap them in a cloth, and let them simmer until they are tender. then take the white part of the citrons, cut it like rhubarb, wrap it in a cloth, and let it simmer until it becomes soft enough to be mashed. then take a pound of coarsely ground sugar and three quarter-measures of the simmered citrons, and grind them together very well until very fine. then put the ground citrons into a bowl, set it over embers, add some citrus juice, and the yellow rinds as much as you like. then make a fine dough, and form small cakes from it. bake them near the oven they will surely be good.

title: Wie man die Weixel zu dem Gebratenen einmacht.
text: make fine, early gooseberries that are not too sour, wash them clean, remove the stems, and put them in a glass. add a spoonful of sugar, then a spoonful of gooseberries, until it is full but you must sugar it well. afterwards, pour good wine vinegar over it, so that the vinegar covers the gooseberries, tie it up, and prick holes in it with a skewer into the paper. let it stand in the sun the whole summer they will remain perfectly preserved and are very good with roasted meats, and also beneficial for digestion during fevers.

title: Pomerantschenblühe-Saltzen zu machen.
text: blossom, and burn it off afterward, place it briefly in fresh water, take it out again, and pound it in a stone mortar. afterward, simmer a thick sugar syrup, and then add the pounded blossom to it. let it simmer a little together, take it off the heat, and pour it into a glass thus it is finished. but you must add sugar to the blossom, otherwise it will turn completely black.

title: Die Rumel-Sultz gar gut zu machen.
text: to prepare a large pike, open it along the belly but do not split it, and cut out large pieces, then blanch them gently in blue water, but not fully cooked, and set aside. afterwards, take the finest and best wine, and for each quarter or measure of three loth of fresh sorrel leaves, wash them clean and finely chop them, and soften and simmer them in the wine. then take the same wine and add as much as you desire for the saltiness, always one quarter of wine per pound of pike, and a nice, clear broth, and as much vinegar as will create a fine tang. also add a few whole juniper berries and some unpeeled onion sprouts, which you must remove from time to time so they do not disintegrate. you can also squeeze in the sour juice of a few fresh lemons, and simmer everything in a glazed pot or a tinned kettle. afterwards, take the following spices ginger, very clean and coarsely chopped pepper,

title: Wie man das Weixel-Wasser macht.
text: take 2 quarts of finely cleaned, fresh apples. remove a good handful of cores and grind them in a mortar. add this to the remaining apples. crush them with a clean, wooden press until they are completely mashed and juicy. pour 3 quarts of water over them, stir well, strain through a linen cloth, and sweeten to taste.

title:
Wie man den Zucker läutern und clarificiren soll/ den
man zum Confect überziehen/ und andern Sachen brauchen thut.
text: for one pound of sugar, take half a measure of water. grind the sugar very finely into a copper bowl, and pour in one small cup of flowing water if you can. let it stand a while until the sugar dissolves before putting it over the fire. then, take the white from a freshly laid egg, beaten with half a small cup of water until frothy. when the sugar has been heated and is beginning to warm but not yet hot, add the froth to it and throw in the eggshells. stir finely and bring to a boil. when it boils quickly, the foam will all sink down. when it starts to rise again, have half a small cup of water on hand and pour a third of it into the boiling sugar to cool it down. this cooling process should be done three times, but the sugar must boil over. then, skim it clean and boil it to the right thickness, as needed.

title:
Wie man allerhand Sachen candiren soll von Gewürtz/ Früchten/
und auch Blumen.
text: to prepare candied fruits, one must cut them small or large, as desired, and press them finely. the nails must be pressed very finely. venetian almonds, peeled, should be rubbed finely on a cloth, and the blossoms of muscat grapes, cut coarsely. the fruits, such as citrons, lemons, orange peels, pears, and nuts, must all be previously preserved in sugar and then well pressed. herbs and flowers must all be pressed finely and smoothly in a book, and then pressed again to keep them smooth, or drawn through boiled sugar, pressed again, and reserved for candying. one can candy all the spices together or separately. whatever one wishes to candy, one should arrange it in a copper or tin dish of the same width, or slightly narrower at the bottom. then, for each pound of spice, take two pounds of fine, clarified sugar, the finest and best cononei sugar, and boil it until it can be drawn between the fingers like a thread

title:
Wie man das Confect weiß und krauß überziehen
soll.
text: to prepare the zimmet, cut the ginger and orange peels lengthwise. the cloves must be soaked in water overnight and carefully peeled apart with a sharp knife. the coriander should be soaked in wine vinegar overnight and then thoroughly dried. you must coat each spice generously. then, take a quarter pound of spices to a pound of fine honey sugar. clarify the sugar and cook it until it becomes slightly slippery between your fingers and has a slight pull. place the spices in a copper kettle and hang it over the oven. keep the sugar warm on a nearby charcoal fire, but do not let it boil. warm the spices in the kettle slightly, and pour in about a half spoonful of the clarified sugar through the appropriate funnel. the funnel must be opened over the kettle so that the first pour wets everything evenly. then stir in the kettle. afterwards, pour several times and stir again. then, place it on a lined sieve and let it stand in a warm room for two or three days. after that

title: Den Zucker-Pinat zu machen.
text: to make sugar spun candy, you shouldn't use hard sugar, as it won't draw out well and will become hard quickly. instead, take a pound of white confections' sugar, or soft sugar. pour a half and a half measure of flowing water over it and cook it over a coal fire. once the sugar thickens, have two round wooden sticks, about a finger's thickness and length, ready. place these in a bowl of cold water. when the sugar is thick, press one stick into it and immediately throw it into the cold water. after a short while, remove it again. when the sugar is quite hard, take the stick in your mouth and pull the sugar down with your teeth. the sugar should remain as thin as a small glass. dip it briefly in cold water and quickly take it into your mouth and bite it. if it shatters like glass, it's done. if it's still slightly soft, continue to cook it until

title: Allerley Kräutl- und Blümelwerck mit Zucker zu überziehen.
text: one should soak tragant in rosewater and press it through a cloth, stirring in a spoonful of sugar until it resembles a small child s porridge. herbs and flowers should be brushed with this, and then rolled in finely crushed and sifted sugar, so that they are coated on all sides. afterward, place them on paper and cool them in a shallow pan or near an oven. currants or elderberries can be treated in the same way however, the currants must be pressed very well, and the elderberries should be slightly dried, and they must be cooled only in a room, not in a shallow pan.

title: Das auffgeworffene Zuckerwerck zu machen.
text: one should soak fine white tragacanth overnight in orange blossom or rose water, and press it through a thick cloth until very firm. then, place it in a stone mortar and pound it with the finest, most beautiful sugar, ground three times, until a firm dough forms. from this dough, take out portions as needed, and spread strength flour on a sheet of paper, rolling it out to a thickness of one finger. press the model onto the dough and cut it out finely. then bake in a dutch oven, allowing them to rise, but be sure they do not brown. the heat should be even at the bottom and top. if you want to color them, take various coloring powders from the apothecary, soak them overnight in rose or orange blossom water, and mix them into the tragacanth. you can also cut them out using bent models they will be very beautiful as well. however, lay them on oblate paper, otherwise they will break. you can also make various

title: Wie man das durchsichtige Eiß macht.
text: to make a fine tragant, pound it well and add rosewater gradually until it dissolves. then press it through a cloth until it's as thin as a weak milk. after that, take the finest three-times clarified sugar and stir it in until it thickens like semolina porridge. let this stand. if you want to use it, make it a day in advance so the sugar dissolves. when you want to whip it, set it in hot water otherwise, it won't whip easily. don't stir it too vigorously, or it will become white and thick, but not light and translucent.

title: Die Kitten-Spalten einzumachen.
text: one should gently and well time the kittens to simmer softly, clean them, and peel the soft part from the top, not too deep towards the stony part. from that, take a pound and add five quarter-pounds of finely sifted white sugar. rub them well in a copper bowl for about an hour until they become beautifully white. then, over a well-smoldering fire, press and stir well, being careful not to let it burn, until it separates from the pan and looks like a good, thick custard. after that, stir until it nearly sets. then, beat into small, deep earthenware bowls, about the size of half a kitten, and let them stand for about an hour, pressing a spoon into the center to make them solid, and they will look like half kittens. let them sit until they firm up slightly and the top becomes pressed. then, using a white, red, mixed-brown, or blue juice, as desired, simmer and strain it finely

title:
Den weissen Kitten-Safft über die Spalten/ und in die
Mödl zu machen.
text: to begin, thinly slice the white part of a citron. take a generous handful of these slices, and cut up six or seven pieces of cooked quince, having first removed the good parts. add two handfuls of raw, unpeeled quince sprouts to this, pour fresh water over them, and simmer over a gentle heat until the quince sprouts and citron are tender. then add two handfuls of quince sprouts, and let it sit for a bit longer, allowing the sprouts to cool slightly. afterwards, strain the mixture through a strong cloth, then strain it again through a cloth to ensure it is clear and free of any solids. from this juice, take more than half a measure, but no more than three, per pound of sugar. once the sugar has dissolved, place it over low charcoal embers until it begins to simmer and clarify. let it simmer until it thickens, then remove it from the heat and let it stand over a small ember until it no longer simmers and is perfectly

title: Ein gar gutte Kitten-Salsen.
text: to begin, take half a measure or three generous spoonfuls of white wine and crush it. pour it into the pressed juice from boiled caper berries, and let it simmer until it turns a beautiful hazelnut brown. strain it through a cloth, and squeeze the pods well. then, for each cup of juice, add a quarter portion of sugar and simmer until it thickens. add finely chopped lemon peel and simmer briefly. pour into a tall glass. this sauce can be served with roasted meats if diluted with wine, or it can be placed on shells if you ve extracted a fine piece of marrow and sprinkled it with candied fruit.

title: Die druckene Kitt-Spalten einzumachen.
text: to prepare the quince halves, preserve them in syrup. boil large, beautiful quinces until they are tender but still hold their shape, not overly soft. clean them thoroughly and cut one into two or three wedges to remove any stones. arrange them in a jar and sprinkle with cinnamon. then, boil sugar in a pot until it thickens slightly and pour it over the quinces. afterwards, boil more sugar until it forms threads, but not so much as for candying. rub this sugar vigorously with a grater in the pot until it turns white, like a child s cooking. the quince halves must first drip well on a rack and dry thoroughly near a warm oven. then, turn them in the sugar so they are thinly coated, and place them side by side on the rack. quickly dry them in a baking oven or very warm room. this will keep them soft inside. before drying, notice when they are in the syrup, they should be simmered until slightly soft, and

title: Das schöne durchsichtige Kittenwerck zu machen.
text: one should take the most beautiful kittens, if not red, then pale, very soft, and well-formed. be sure to remove anything red, and only cut down the best parts, then quickly strain through a fine sieve, only what passes easily. while straining the kittens, boil sugar, so they don't have to stand for long. for half a pound of kittens, use a pound of the finest sugar, crush it very finely, and add a goblet of water. boil until a drop falling into cold water immediately sets and feels like wax between your fingers. then stir the kittens into this mixture until it is smooth. don't stir too long, or it won't be translucent. afterwards, pour into the appropriate molds, having first placed them in hot water. let them set in a room, but not a very warm one if you press them in a very warm room, they will get a coarse skin. it shouldn't be too cold either. you can

title: Das Citeroni-Kraut zu machen.
text: one should cut the lemon leaves of citron very thinly lengthwise and then cut them very narrowly along the grain, like herbs, ensuring a little of the yellow rind remains at both ends. the smaller and longer they are cut, the more beautiful they become. soak them in fresh water until they become beautifully translucent, then drain them on a rack and spread them on a cloth. place them in a vessel and make a syrup over them as described previously for the preserved lemons, then pour cold water over it. if it becomes watery, simmer it again until it thickens. do not measure the sugar precisely by weight, but ensure the syrup is finely made and covers the leaves. it will become beautifully translucent and spread with a lovely sheen, like beaten silver.

title: Das Genuesische in die Mödl von Zwespen.
text: pour boiling water over the wasps and let them stand for a quarter of an hour, so that their skins can be peeled off. then chop them into strips. for every pound of wasps, take a pound of clarified sugar and boil it in a pot over a coal fire until it separates from the pan. afterwards, beat it into shaped molds and press.

title:
Wie man die Ribesl und Weinscherling-Safft bereiten und behalten
soll über ein Jahr/ damit man allerley Sachen färbt.
text: one should break the ripe berries from the stems, crush them in an earthen dish with a wooden pestle, then set them over a coal fire and simmer for a quarter of an hour, stirring constantly. afterward, pour them into a woolen bag and let the clear liquid drip through. keep this in a linen strainer with a container at the bottom in a cellar, and pour tree oil over the top.

title: Ein Hetschebetschen-Salsen zu machen.
text: soak the chestnuts until they sprout, but make sure they are not too soft clean them well, remove the kernels and the skins. fill a large wooden bowl completely with water, enough to cover them generously. let the water flow over the chestnuts until the bowl is completely full. cover with a clean cloth and place another bowl on top to prevent steam from escaping. let it stand for two hours. afterward, when you see that they are finely and softly cooked, drain the water and strain them through a fine sieve. the first liquid will be thin and watery discard it entirely. then it will become beautifully thick strain it until you have a pound. next, take a pound of sugar and boil it until it spins. take the spun sugar and pour it into the chestnuts, stirring gently to avoid lumps. pour into a glass and keep it away from a warm oven throughout the evening. in the morning, place it in a well-ventilated spot it will keep as long as

title:
Wie man die Weixel/ Ribesel/ und anders Obst gemein einmachen
soll/ zum Dortenfüllen/ und dergleichen.
text: first, take one pound of fresh fruit and one pound of sugar, crush them together. afterwards, wash the fruit clean, remove the stones or pit it depending on the fruit. put it along with the sugar into a copper basin, and sprinkle a little fresh water over it. let it simmer gently over a low heat until the fruit pulp falls from the spoon. then remove it from the heat and let it cool. it is then ready.

title: Marillen/ Himbeer/ oder andere Saltzen.
text: simmer the apricots or raspberries, passing them through a sieve beforehand, ensuring the apricots are peeled. for every pound of fruit, use three quarter-pounds of sugar. combine these in a pot and cook together until it sets into a firm drop or becomes slightly thickened. it is then ready. while it simmers, stir constantly to prevent burning.

title:
Weixel-Safft/ oder Ribesel und dergleichen zu machen/ so man
zum Abgiessen braucht.
text: to a pound of sugar, add a quarter of pressed juice. let this stand for a few hours until it settles, then strain it through a clean cloth and pour it over the sugar. let it simmer together until it becomes a thick juice or syrup then it is finished.

title: Mandel-Krapffen zu machen.
text: one should prepare the almonds as finely as possible and sugar them well. then, take the clear whites from two or three eggs you make a lot with this and cook them with a little fresh or cinnamon water, stirring them into the almonds. afterward, make a dough with the egg yolks and fine flour, sweetening it lightly. roll out a sheet of dough, spread the filling on top, and use a cutter to make long, thin strips, about the length of a finger and the thickness of a small finger. turn the cut strips over and join them together with egg white at the edges, forming rings. bake them in a baking pan. when they are half-baked, beat an egg yolk with fresh water and sugar, brush the tops with this mixture, and finish baking.

title: Andere Mandel-Krapffen in dem Schmaltz gebachen.
text: one should prepare the almonds as finely as possible and soak a penny s worth of stale bread in fresh water, then press it out well and grind it with the almonds, and add sugar. after that, beat 3 or 4 eggs into it until it forms a fine batter if it is too thick, you can add a crushed breadcrumb to help. then, make small pastries, not thicker than a finger's width, shaping them like the small turnips called gefährter-rüben. bake them in fine, cool lard, and when you take them out, stick a rosemary sprig on top they look very pretty and are very good warm when served on the table.

title:
Den Taig zu den bachnen Oepfel/ [Oepel/] Weixel/ und andern
Sachen/ daß er gar hoch aufflaufft.
text: one should let the sweet, skimmed milk warm, and melt a little lard into it, and stir in some fine flour until it is as thick as a cook. then, press it well over embers, and two or three pears, after which one makes many, into the hot water, and beat one after the other into the dough, and beat it smooth or stir it until it is as thick as a strudel dough if one wants to bake pretzels from it, one should always take a pretzel with the stem half cut off, dip it into the dough, and bake it in lard, so they rise very high. thus, one can also bake apples, sage, wasps' nests, zucchini blossoms, and whatever one wants. if one boils pretzels, and presses them finely, and sticks them onto small skewers, and bakes them from this dough, they become very beautiful and good when one arranges them, one must take or pull the skewers out, if one wishes. then

title: Krauste Weixel- oder Oepffel-Strauben zu machen.
text: to make this pastry, combine a little warm milk and fine flour to form a dough. then, lightly toast some flour in rendered fat, add it to the dough, and beat the dough until smooth. heat some schmaltz in a pan, larger than a typical dumpling. using a pastry bag, pipe the dough into the hot schmaltz, as you would with regular fritters, but they don't need to brown much, and shouldn't be too thick. remove them when they are still white, then bake another batch, allowing them to brown slightly. after that, bake another batch of white fritters like the first. then, thin out the remaining dough with sweet milk, and pipe the apples into the dough, ensuring not too much dough clings to them. next, place a white fritter in the pan and arrange the dough-covered apples neatly beside each other, without letting them touch, so the fritters don't become translucent

title: Die runden Brand-Küchl zu machen.
text: to begin, place a generous amount of rendered fat in a beautiful water, and let it simmer. then, stir in enough flour to make the flour just moist. next, press it well on hot ashes until it becomes very dry. then, put yeast in warm water and beat it one after another, or pound it in a mortar, until the dough is as thick as a cook s thumb. then, place it on a greased board, and with a spoon, pull fine, round crumbs into the rendered fat. the rendered fat must not be too hot, and bake them finely and coolly, constantly turning, and pouring on with a spoon so they spread beautifully and become very round.

title: Spritz-Krapffen zu machen.
text: to make the dough as for brand-baked pastries, but instead of water, use sweet milk. when the dough is finely kneaded, pour melted lard into a bowl and add the dough to it. then, place it in the pan, ensuring the layers aren't too thick just two layers. the lard should be slightly warmer than for the pastries, but not too hot.

title: Spritz-Krapffen von Mandel.
text: to prepare almonds, grind them finely with fresh water and sugar. then, incorporate a generous amount of sifted wheat flour, and with clarified butter from fresh cream, mix to a dough as thick as it will stick to a spoon. afterward, add a little melted butter, but not too hot, and press the dough through a pastry bag just as you would with other filled fritters. bake them until they are not browned the whiter they are, the better. if you want them to be served warm, sprinkle with sugar.

title: Ein guten Spritz-Krapffen [Spitz-Krapffen] zu machen.
text: to begin, melt a generous amount of sweet cream or butter or rendered fat in a large vessel. add two spoonfuls of fresh yeast and 5 egg yolks, well beaten. then, using warm bread flour, make a dough that is sticky to the touch, and work it well with your hands. place the dough in a bowl, cover it, and let it rise in a warm place. once it has doubled in size, punch it down and divide it into three pieces, rolling each into a long, thin rope. grease a spit with rendered fat and let it warm. wrap the dough around the spit, twisting it evenly. brush with beaten egg yolks and bake over a hot fire until set, brushing frequently with melted rendered fat until golden brown. serve warm.

title: Zucker-Sträubl zu machen.
text: one should take fine flour and almost a third of sugar, then egg whites, and two spoonfuls of fresh water, and one spoonful of wine, beating everything well together. with this, make a thin pancake batter and stir it very well. let the schmaltz get hot in the pan, but not too hot, and draw the batter through a fine pastry bag into the pan, and bake it, not brown. when you take it out, roll it quickly over a small rolling pin like a tulip, and place it on the rolling pin in the bowl where you want to arrange it, and then remove the rolling pin from the bowl. they cannot be moved once placed, they will break in your hands.

title: Die Waffen-Krapffen mit Mandel zu machen.
text: to begin, take half a pound of finely ground almonds and 4 egg yolks, and a whole egg. mix these well together, and add sugar to taste. next, take a good piece of sweet marzipan and melt a good piece of butter in it, then pour this over the almonds and egg mixture and mix well. then stir in fine bread flour until the dough is as thick as a strudel dough. allow the corresponding eggs to warm, grease them with butter, and spoon the dough into the eggs. bake over low heat and, when removed from the eggs, quickly wrap them in a cloth to make them crumble like a holly pastry.

title: Sack-Kuchen zu machen.
text: to make them, take 8 ounces of good, sweet milk and beat it well. then, with fine flour, make a dough like a strudel dough. put this dough into a small bag, not full, and tie it closed. place it in boiling water and cook until firm. then, remove it and cut long strips from it, two fingers wide. bake them cool in fat, stirring the pan constantly and spooning the fat over them. they will rise beautifully and become very high.

title: Ram-Krapffen zu machen.
text: one should take approximately half a measure of sweet cream and place it in a pan, and cook it gently with a good amount of flour until it becomes as thick as a porridge. then, press it well over the embers, but first, soak four eggs in warm water that is warm enough to hold your hand in, and let them heat up a bit. then, beat one after the other into the dough and stir well. afterward, form the dough into small, fatty patties and immerse them in hot fat if the patties stick together, separate them, as it is difficult to form them into rounds.

title: Die drey Pfannen-Krapffen.
text: melt a small piece of lard in warm cow's milk, and keep it warm. with five eggs, previously soaked in warm water, and fine flour, make a dough slightly thicker than a strudel dough. beat in one egg at a time. then, take a little lard in a pan and melt it. pour the dough into the pan and press it over a low heat until it can be cut. afterward, place it on a greased platter and cut long strips from it, only a little at a time, and bake them cool in lard.

title: Ein gutes Essen so man den faulen Hannß nennt.
text: to begin, take about 3 kreuzer worth of fine white bread dough and a half-measure of the best milk whey, and 4 or 5 egg yolks, well beaten within. add two spoonfuls of fresh yeast and mix it all into the dough. if it is too thin, add more flour and mix, then let it stand in a warm oven to rise. once risen, knead the dough again, very well and strongly, until it is firm. shape it like a sugarloaf and place it in the oven to bake, until finely warm but not overdone, so that it can be sliced. then take a sharp knife and cut down the bottom to the thickness of a large finger, and cut the rest into slices as thick as a knife's edge, except for the top, which should be as thick as the bottom. mix fresh butter well with sugar and spread the slices generously on both sides. place them back on top of each other and return them to

title: Die Blättleten Golatschen zu machen.
text: to begin, take a bit of fine wheat flour, warmed, and a good yeast starter, about half a small pitcher. mix well until it becomes frothy. then, add warm milk, enough to make the dough as thick as a fritter dough. pour the warm milk into the yeast mixture, mixing well, and use this to knead the dough, adding sugar, and place it in the oven for two hours, but not too hot. once it has risen, remove it from the oven and gently press it down with your hands. then, take a piece about the size of two hands, and roll it out with a rolling pin to a length of a span, and as thick as a finger s width. grease it with melted butter or lard, and roll it up as before, but do not grease it further. repeat this three or four times. for the fourth time, roll it out thinner, about the thickness of a thumb, and grease it with lard, and

title: Die gar guten Böheimischen Gollatschen.
text: to make such a dough as follows with a quick knife stroke, cut out round leaves, a little larger than a thumb-sized patty. then, make a very good, sweet milk and cream batter, spreading it well on a cloth and a small board until it is quite firm. after that, brush the batter with a good, thick spoon, like a cook, so that it can be spread. then spread this batter onto the cut-out leaves, as thickly as the dough is, but don't spread all the way to the edges leave a finger's breadth of space. layer two leaves over each other, so that they are thicker at the edges, to prevent the filling from running out. before folding, brush with butter, and then spread the filling on top, when the pastry is on the oven-dish. when you want to eat it, warm it.

title: Pugatschen-Brod von Kockholkhy.
text: a little flour from the mill a little yeast a small amount of fennel a spoonful of lard two measures of milk about 2 pfennigs worth of skins a quarter pound of sugar a little salt a little fresh water. mix all of this well and knead it into a long roll then let it rise and bake. after it has baked cut it into warm leaves as thin as you like.
ingredients: amount fennel spoonful lard measures milk

title: Den Butter-Taig zu machen.
text: to make a bowl of butter-filled pastries or doughnuts, take two egg yolks and two whole eggs, and some very cold water. with fine bread flour, make a dough that is quite firm, working it well. then roll it out to a thickness of half a finger's width. cut thin sheets of butter and let them harden in water. drain them on a cloth and roll the half-sheet of dough over them. fold the other half over, then incorporate butter well. roll out again, and cover with the half-sheet of dough. repeat this three times, ensuring the butter is always as thick as a knife stroke. once the butter is well incorporated after the three folds, roll the dough out to a thickness of one finger and cut out butter-filled doughnuts or pastries using a hot knife. bake them in a doughnut pan.

title: Ein marben Taig zu machen.
text: one should take fine bread flour, so that it doesn t run away then, one should take good sweet cream and cut in some fresh butter, but there should be more butter than cream. one should let it melt in, finely cooled, and when it s warm, but not hot, stir in 8 or 10 egg yolks, and pour this into the flour, and quickly make the dough. one must not work it too much then, roll out a sheet about a finger s thickness, as large as the tarts or pastries should be, and fill it with whatever one desires.

title: Ein Mandel-Dorten zu machen.
text: take one pound of almonds, soak them overnight in water. in the morning, peel and grind them. melt half a pound of butter, but do not let it get hot. pour it over the almonds. beat in 12 egg whites, 8 whole eggs, and 4 yolks, adding them finely one after another. from the 8 whole eggs, take out the whites from 2 eggs separately and beat them well with a lemon peel, then pour them into the butter. stir constantly for two or three hours, adding as much sugar as you desire. stir again. then pour the mixture into small almond molds, place them in a baking pan, and bake over fresh embers when you wish. if desired, make an icing to put over it.

title: Zimmet-Dorten zu machen.
text: one should prepare the almonds finely, as appropriate, and sugar them generously. then, stir in very finely ground cinnamon, as much as will make it the color of deer-brown, and work in a piece of cinnamon-flavored butter. afterwards, moisten with ale until it is as thick as a cook, using only the yolks from half the ale and the whole of the other half. also, add finely chopped candied citron. pour into a tart mold and bake in a pastry oven, not too quickly, so that it bakes through nicely. afterwards, spread it on top with a beautiful, thick white icing before it is fully baked. one can also decorate the sides and top finely with a small brush using the icing. however, this must be done after it is fully baked, otherwise the icing will become hard. you must remove it from the mold before the icing sets, otherwise you will break the icing.

title: Ein gute Reiß-Dorten.
text: one should cook well-picked rice in good, sweet milk, as one usually cooks it, quite thick. then, one should pound it well in a mortar. afterwards, one should take finely ground almonds, about as much as the rice, and pound them in. also, a good knob of butter, and from two rolls, the crumbs soaked in milk, squeezed out, and pounded in. then, sweeten and flavor with saffron, as one would a large almond cake, and bake it thus.

title: Mandel-Dorten mit Zimmet.
text: to begin, take half a pound, or three quarters, of almonds, prepared and ground as usual, but not too finely. add a handful of hazelnuts, ground to the same consistency, and mix in a good knob of fresh butter. then, beat in seven egg yolks and incorporate a generous amount of candied citron, finely chopped and sugared. from a good, rich pastry, cut out circles two fingers high and place them on a baking sheet. fill the circles with the almond mixture, then arrange thin slices of citron on top. bake in a moderate oven until well risen.

title: Ein grüne Kräuter-Dorten zu machen.
text: one should take beautiful young spinach, scald it with hot water, and drain it well. then chop it very finely, and mix in some finely ground almonds and milk-soaked breadcrumbs. add egg yolks and sweet cream to achieve the right consistency, and season with fine salt. when serving in dormice, first butter the bottom and then the top, and bake it, serving warm. if desired, a little saffron can be added, as it tastes very good with it.

title: Ein Speck-Dorten zu machen.
text: take five pounds of unsmoked bacon and burn it. then scrape it, and grind it. next, take two handfuls of almonds and grind them as well, making sure to grind the almonds before grinding the bacon. soft two rolls in good milk, and grind them in too, ensuring the rolls are well pressed. once everything is ground, put it in a bowl and stir in three egg yolks. the longer you stir, the better it will be. then make a dough and add two egg yolks as if it were an almond dough. roll out a sheet of dough that isn't too thick. grease a bowl with butter and place the dough inside. pour the mixture into the dough-lined bowl, and finely spread a layer of butter over the top, crimping the edges. bake in a tart pan, just as you would bake an almond tart. this is how it should be done.

title: Von allerley Fleisch-Speisen.
text: to begin, take a good piece of beef from the haunch and finely chop the lean meat not in large pieces salt it, and pour hot vinegar over it, letting it sit for about two hours. then, burn it off on a rack until it is nicely browned. afterwards, add water, vinegar, and a little beer. next, cut two onions thinly and roast them well in fat, then add them to the beef and simmer everything together. finally, season with pepper.

title: Den Rindern Lung zu machen.
text: one should finely chop about a pound of roasted meat, and crumble half a pound of dried sausages. soak a small amount of bread worth a penny in milk, and chop it in underneath. finely chop two onions and roast them in butter. add four ounces of chopped parsley and half a broth. simmer for a little over a and a half cups, then pour the broth over it, and sprinkle with a little ginger. one makes it similarly with game, but one must season it generously with pepper.

title: Kälberne Würstl zu machen.
text: one should finely chop veal meat and veal tenderloin, and mix them together with a salted lemon. also, soak bread in milk, season with pepper and marjoram, then wrap the chopped meat in a piece of veal netting. form into sausages and tie with string, then roast over the grill.

title: Die jungen Schaffmägl zu sieden.
text: the shanks must be trimmed and then boiled until tender, ensuring they are not tough. afterwards, finely chop veal, beef, or lamb flaps, along with fresh bacon. add two handfuls of grated breadcrumbs, then fill the shanks with plenty of meat, a roasted onion, and parsley. beat in two or three eggs, add a splash of cream, and pepper, to create a fine, thick filling. secure the shanks onto skewers, then fry them and baste with melted bacon fat or butter.

title: Würstl von Kapaun- und Hüner-Lebern.
text: one should finely chop the liver and kidneys of a capon, pepper them, and season lightly with salt. pour good cream over them, fill the largest intestines from a sausage casing, and briefly sear them in hot water. then place on a rack.

title: Hirschen-Würstl zu machen.
text: to make a clean venison sausage, first reserve some venison. then finely chop a young hare sausage, cut beef tenderloin into small pieces, quite a lot, and mix them together. add venison until it becomes finely red. then add pure cream until it thickens like liver sausage. season with salt, pepper, ginger, and ground nutmeg. fill into a clean, prepared venison casing. poach in hot water, brown on a rack, and serve on green leaves.

title: Bachene Hüner und Dauben.
text: to prepare the chickens and duck, cut them into pieces. beat the legs well and soak them overnight in water seasoned with plenty of salt. afterwards, sprinkle with good vinegar and let them lie for a while. then, coat in flour and bake in fat. toss fresh, bright green parsley in hot fat and immediately remove it, then sprinkle over the meat.

title: Hünlein oder junges Fleisch in Agriß zu kochen.
text: once the chicken is cleaned and cut up, scald it with hot water and place it in a pot. finely chop a bread roll and roast it slightly in butter. add a pinch of muscat flowers and mild pepper, and a generous handful of sorrel or unripe grapes. pour in good beef broth and simmer until cooked. when serving, add butter if desired. it is also prepared this way with green peas.

title: Ein gefüllten Kapaun zu kochen.
text: to roast the capon, salt it first. then take the liver, as much as possible, and chop it into crumbs. roast a little finely chopped onion in the capon s fat. add finely crumbled stale bread and rosemary, parsley, marjoram, and pepper. combine all of this and stuff the capon with it. also, include boiled and seasoned oysters or mussels. additionally, finely chop a roasted veal kidney, mix it with toasted bread, and use that to fill the capon.

title: Ein Hünlein in einer schwartzen Suppen.
text: one should collect the sweat from a young piglet, or more, in wine or vinegar. shred the piglet and brown it in hot lard. then place it in a small pot, and finely chop a sour apple, roasting it in the lard. add a little grated semolina, then pour in water, wine, vinegar, and the sweat. let it simmer, then add pepper, sugar, cinnamon, and cloves.

title: Ein gutes Essen von Lebern.
text: to make it, one should finely chop chicken, veal, or lamb liver, along with a generous amount of onions or other herbs, and a soaked bread roll in milk, beaten with two egg yolks. add a little marjoram, parsley, nutmeg, pepper, and a bit of sweet wine. melt butter in a pastry pan, pour the mixture into it, place embers both above and below, and let it bake. it will become beautifully browned. serve in the pan on the table. it can also be made with veal kidneys.

title: Ein gute Carbanada zu machen.
text: one should roast a hindquarter, remove the meat from the shanks, and cut it into small pieces. leave the meat on the long shanks and place it in a bowl. sprinkle with a little vinegar, finely chop a fresh lemon with its zest, pepper it well, and add a little broth. place butter on top, cover, and let it become hot over embers.

title: Ein gutes Lämmeres [Lämmmeres] Dampff-Brätl.
text: to begin, take a nice strudel of lamb. brown it on a rack, first sprinkling it with salt. afterwards, place it in a small pot and add four slices of a sour apple they can be green or dried and a grated nutmeg roasted in melted butter. pour in a little meat broth, pepper, ginger, and muscat flower. add these ingredients, cover tightly, and let it simmer over low heat.

title: Ein Hünlein wie ein Hasselhünlein zuzurichten.
text: to prepare it, pour a spoonful of vinegar and half a spoonful of brandy directly into the hen's throat, sprinkle, and drain, leaving it hanging overnight. afterwards, pluck and singe it, and slightly burn the feet if desired. if you wish, you can add woodcock feet to it and season with bacon or spices, then roast. alternatively, you can wrap it in a pastry crust. you must take hot vinegar, season it, and pour it over, then enclose it in the pastry with butter and lemon.

title: Rauch-Würst.
text: combine two parts lean pork with one part lean beef, finely chopped. season with salt, a generous amount of ground cumin, a little ground cinnamon, cloves, ginger, a bit of dried rose petals, coarsely crushed nutmeg, and pepper, mixing thoroughly. add a small piece of smoked bacon, or if unavailable, a little fresh bacon, finely diced. moisten with a little red wine, fill into sausage casings firmly and tightly, using a wooden skewer to pack them well, ensuring no air pockets remain, otherwise they will burst. the casings should be dry, but finely pressed if filled well, tie them together at both ends with a piece of string and hang them by the string. let the ends of the sausages protrude. allow them to dry in the air for three days, then smoke them and let them cool completely. these sausages belong to the category of sour cabbage, throat, and olives they can also be eaten raw.

title: Die guten geschelten Kastraun-Schlegl zu machen.
text: first, take the two shanks and salt them very well, especially where the fat is there you must push the salt in properly. then put them in a tub and pour the brine over them every day, and again over it, and let them lie like this for 5 or 6 days, or even a little longer. after that, they must be hung in the smoke for 5 or 6 days as well, and seasoned with crane root or smoked, and you must often see to it that there is not too little or too much they will press and firm up when there is enough.

title: Wie man die Hammen selcht.
text: first, salt them finely and place them in a tub. press them down for eight days, or less if needed, and every day, turn them once and pour over them, and then again. afterward, take them and boil them in a pot until they are nicely plump, in well-salted water, for as long as you would boil veal. then take them out, drain the water, and hang them to smoke, smoking them with fresh green branches that shouldn't be older than six days a day or two more doesn't matter, you must see when they are done.

title: Spanische Ohly zu machen.
text: first, take a piece of beef, clean it well and trim it. when the beef is about half-cooked, add kastaner sausage, pork loin, pig's trotters, calf's breast, grilled or boiled bratwurst, a good piece of salted belly or ham, a crumbled sausage, and a salted tongue. this dish also includes good neck meat, white cabbage, celery, winter salad, onions, and garlic, parsley, white beets, pickled beets, chestnuts, and caraway seeds, and all other good spices as appropriate for a dish. boil everything together in a pot, then arrange the dish on a large platter so that everything can be seen.

title: Rindfleisch auff Englisch zu kochen.
text: take a good, sizable piece of beef and prepare it so that it isn't crushed take finger-length, finger-thick bacon and finely chop it. the bacon must be well salted and spiced, and insert the chopped bacon along its length. take a pot or kettle large enough for the meat, then let it simmer well, always keeping it well covered. when the meat begins to soften, add a handful of cloves stuck in a nail, and a piece of ginger broken apart, and coarse pepper, fine herbs such as rosemary, savory, and three bay leaves. half an hour before serving, skim off the foam and pour in a measure of good wine and half a measure of good vinegar. take sweetbreads and ox tripe, which must be cut small, and let it simmer until the soup is reduced. then arrange the meat neatly and adjust with the sweetbreads and ox tripe.

title: Ein gute Mandel-Suppen zu machen.
text: to begin, take a small amount of almonds and soak them in fresh water. then, squeeze bread that has been weighed in water and grind it into the almonds. stir with boiled water or meat broth until a thick almond milk forms. afterward, add sugar and bring it to a boil. while it boils, stir well with a spoon and spread it evenly on both sides. if you boil a piece of wheat groats, about the size of a bean, in water or broth to help it blend, do not add sugar. however, if you stir it with broth, you don't need to add sugar.

title: Schmaltz-Suppen von Maurachen.
text: cleanly roast a few pieces of pork cutting thick rings across them with a swift knife stroke, placing them in a pot. add parsley and chives, along with pepper and salt. pour over three or four spoonfuls of good meat broth and let it simmer. then, cut a little less bread than you would for a fat soup and arrange the boiled pork on top. the soup shouldn't be too thick or too watery. afterward, heat some fat, pour it over, and add a little pepper.

title: Ein Suppen mit kleinen Vögelein.
text: one should slice rye bread as for a schmaltz soup, pour good beef broth over it, and let it soak. afterwards, fry small birds finely and nicely, place them on the bread, and lay well-roasted zwiebel on top. pepper and sprinkle with a little vinegar, then burn hot schmaltz over it.

title: Die Jäger-Suppen zu machen.
text: to make house bread, slice it as you would for a fat soup. arrange the slices in a bowl. then, take a small amount of sausage whether veal, beef, or game and chop it very finely, spreading it over the bread. add another layer of bread, then more chopped sausage until the bowl is full. next, pour hot meat broth over it so that it is moistened, and then drizzle hot rendered fat over the top. sprinkle a little pepper between the layers occasionally, and serve in this manner it is very good.

title: Ein gute Bier-Suppen.
text: one should take good beer, and if it is particularly fine and strong, mix it with water, and stir in four egg yolks and a good amount of spice, beating them well together, and then simmer. if one wishes to serve it, melt a good piece of butter into it, and cut the bread on which one serves it into cubes.

title: Wein-Suppen zu machen.
text: to make it, take sweet and otherwise good wine, and add two spoonfuls of fresh water, three or four egg yolks, and a sweet syrup well strained. then heat some rendered fat in a pan, and pour the soup into it. add sugar, muscat flower, and saffron, and let it simmer for a quarter. wine soups are quite harmful if not well-boiled they are also not good if not properly cooked.

title: Ein gutes Süppel über bratene Hüner.
text: melt lard over heat, and roast sugar in it until it hardens. then add water, muscat flowers, pepper, ginger, and cinnamon, and a little grated breadcrumbs. simmer, then add fresh lemon peel and do not let it simmer any further.

title: Ein Süppel über gesottene Fisch zu machen.
text: melt some rendered fat over heat. cut breadcrumbs into small pieces and roast them in the fat. add vinegar and water, and season with pepper, cinnamon stick, and muscat flower. simmer briefly, then stir in a knob of butter.

title: Ein Süppel über Gebratenes.
text: melt some rendered fat and add vinegar and wine to it, along with sugar, cinnamon, and honey. simmer.

title: Ein Süppel über bratene Kapaun/ und Rebhüner.
text: cut or chop fresh lemon zest finely and blanch it in water to remove any bitterness. drain it well. then press the lemon juice into it, adding a little wine and water, as well as pepper, cloves, and sugar, ensuring the acidity remains prominent. in a small pan, heat some rendered fat, and toast a spoonful of grated breadcrumbs in it. pour the lemon mixture into the pan and let it simmer briefly. if fresh lemons are unavailable, use dried lemon or orange zest, and substitute rose vinegar for the lemon juice.

title: Ein Mandel-Gescharb über ein Rechschlegel.
text: one should roast some bread slices in butter until finely browned, then pour in a mixture of half water and half wine. let it simmer, thicken, and clarify. add ground cinnamon, pepper, muscat flower, sugar, wine berries, cloves, and sliced almonds, and let it simmer well.

title: Ein anders Süppel über Kapaun/ und Rechschlegel.
text: melt some rendered fat and roast a spoonful of flour in it. add fresh water and wine, along with a few sprigs of rosemary or marjoram, and finely chopped lemon peel. let it simmer for a while, then add a handful of gooseberries, pitted, or currants. season with pepper and cinnamon, and if it s too sour, add sugar. simmer and then serve over cabbage and roast pork shoulder.

title: Ein gutes Süppel über ein Zung.
text: one should roast flour until lightly browned in rendered fat. then add water and vinegar, and sweeten with sugar or sweet juice. add a little rosemary, cinnamon, and cloves, and let it simmer. pour it over tongue that has been previously boiled and browned on a grill.

title: Rosmarin-Süppel.
text: one should brown flour in lard until lightly brown. then add beef broth and finely chopped rosemary. add a sprig of muscat blossom and let it simmer.

title: Nägeln-Süppel zu machen.
text: one should brown flour well in rendered fat, add meat broth, small dumplings, and a little vinegar, and let it simmer.

title: Eine gute Königs-Suppen zu machen.
text: prepare a cabbage, either boiled or roasted, and take the white parts from it, making a good purée. add half a pound of almonds and a small amount of semolina, and grind them together with a good, warm cabbage soup until smooth. serve with bread that has been well browned over the embers, mixed with good soup and broth. pour the purée over the soup. to adjust the flavor of the soup, use a little sherry and nutmeg. if you want it to be more flavorful, add some crushed crawfish tails and veal broth, and adjust the soup accordingly.

title: Ein Supen über Hechten/ Eschling/ und Fehren.
text: chop apples and onions very finely and roast them with a handful of grated breadcrumbs in melted fat, not too much so they don't brown. then press the fat out, after which wash three salted lemons finely, remove the seeds, and chop them as well. pour half a glass of wine and water over them, carefully wipe the salt off the fish, place the fish in a pot, and pour the broth over it. add a little vinegar as well. when the fish is almost cooked, season with pepper, ginger, cinnamon, mace, saffron, and sugar. if serving with pike or roach, the fish should be previously cooked.

title: Ein gute Suppen über Hechten/ Rutten/ und Scheiden.
text: to make a bowl of broth, finely chop a handful of leeks and pour water over them. simmer until very soft. remove the leeks and pour the broth over them. when it has thickened, add a generous spoonful of rendered fat and let it simmer until well combined. season with ground pepper. serve on toasted bread. this is also how you prepare turnips and parsnips.

title: Das gute Citeroni-Koch.
text: take 5 or 6 large lemons and put them in a bowl. slice the rinds very thinly, then grate the lemons until you reach the sour part. put the grated lemon in a cloth or bag and rinse it several times with clean boiling water, always pouring fresh water over it each time, and press it well until all the firmness is completely gone. then press it very clean and well. crush it finely in a stone mortar. next, take half a pound of sugar and pour water from a red-dyed cloth that has been soaked in it over the sugar, and let it simmer until it becomes a somewhat thick syrup. then add the finely crushed lemon and let it simmer in the right proportion, stirring it with a little lemon juice to taste. it must still have the consistency of a good quince paste. after it has cooled, transfer it to a clean bowl. take 7 or 8 fresh pears, taking only the clear juice, discarding the pulp. stir the quince

title: Das gute Pistatzi-Koch.
text: take one pound of almonds and sugar into a bowl clarify the sugar, then pour the ground almonds into it, pressing off the liquid. the almonds must be colored with spinach and stirred like a marzipan, sometimes a whole egg, sometimes a yolk, and stirred until it has the right consistency. then bake it. 12 portions, 6 whole eggs, 6 yolks if it's still too thick, add two more egg yolks.

title: Krebsen-Koch zu machen.
text: soak the schmollen in good milk until softened, then bake thoroughly. take 40 crayfish, boil them, and peel them. in butter, sauté some sulfur and chives in a knob of butter, stirring well as for schmaltz-knödel. then, take the crayfish, softened schmollen, and coarsely ground almonds, along with butter, into a mortar and pound them very well. next, take cream into a small jug and beat it until frothy, then stir it into the pounded mixture in a bowl. if desired, you can sweeten it or not. when baking, spread with red butter on top.

title: Ein gutes Schmaltz-Koch zu machen.
text: one should take ground starch and when one makes it in a bowl, one should take 4 egg yolks and some good sweet milk. beat the egg yolks in the bowl well and mix them with the starch to form a dough. when it begins to heat in the melted butter, one can pour it in, stirring finely as usual. when the fat is clear, it is cooked enough, then one should strain it.

title: Wie man das gute Krebsenblat macht.
text: boil the crabs, then make a red butter. from live crabs, extract crab spawn and crab roe, finely chopped. also, add coarsely ground almonds and candied citron pieces, coarsely chopped pistachios, and confectioner's sugar to taste. incorporate two whole eggs and two yolks, then blend in a piece of soaked bread crumbs. combine all ingredients thoroughly, spread onto a pastry crust, crimp the edges, and bake.

title: Ein gar gutes Mandel-Koch.
text: to begin, take half a pound of very finely ground almonds, and pour fresh water and softened bread crumbs into good milk. next, take a wide, shallow bowl, crumble a generous piece of butter into it, and let it melt directly in the bowl. then add the almonds to the bowl and beat in two whole eggs and the yolks of seven eggs, well sugar and stir over the embers until it becomes fine, beautiful, and white. afterwards, heat a little rendered fat in a small pan and fry the mixture in it, stirring constantly. then take another bowl, melt a little butter in it, and pour the cooked mixture into it, so that it becomes finely browned on both sides. you may also add ice on top.

title: Mandel-Reiß Koch.
text: one must carefully pick and wash the rice, and dry it again, so that it will puff up. then one must sift it through a sieve, after which one takes the rice flour and almonds, and stirs them with a little milk into a smooth paste. one cooks it over embers, letting it simmer gently until it thickens. before serving, one adds a piece of butter and sugar, and then lets it rest.

title: Agreß-Koch zu machen.
