text: make a good mug full of elderberries, as much as the pot is large, and add a spoonful of water to it. let it boil until it has reduced and thickened, and when it has done so, take sugar and butter, and 4 egg yolks, and stir them together. grease a pot with butter, and pour the cooked mixture into it, and let it bake like that.

title: Ein gutes Oepffel-Koch.
text: to make sour apple dumplings, cut the apples into strips, toss them in flour, and bake them in lard. then chop them finely, add three parts sugar, a sweet plum, a little grated breadcrumb, sugar, and cinnamon. afterwards, heat some lard in a pot, pour the apple mixture into it, and place hot embers both underneath and on top.

title: Das auffgangene Kitten-Koch.
text: one should simmer the kittens in water until very soft, and beat them. put the same into a bowl and sugar them well, stirring long and well under the sugar. then take the clear from two or three newly laid eggs and strain it well so that it becomes clear, and one should add this to the kittens little by little, stirring constantly the longer one stirs, the more beautiful it becomes. finally, stir in a little finely chopped lemon peel. if one wishes to serve immediately, one should grease a bowl with schmaltz and arrange the cooked mixture therein, finely and high up like snow cream, and place it in a pastry oven or pan it bakes very quickly. the oven must not be hot, for if one bakes it too early it will collapse. sprinkle a lot of sugar on top.

title: Kapaun-Müßl zu machen.
text: one should take only the sausage and marrow from a boiled capon. chop these as finely as possible. then, add a good slice of buttered bread soaked in good meat broth, and chop that in as well. also add one or two fresh eggs, which should be well-boiled when you want to eat them, and chop them in along with the white, scraping it from the shell. the finer you chop it, the better. when you are about to eat, pour a good meat broth over it, but not too much, so that it thickens finely like a porridge. then place it over a low heat and stir constantly until it is finely hot it must not boil, otherwise it will become hard. it will be nicely white and very good.

title: Schüssel-Koch zu machen von Mandel.
text: one should prepare two handfuls of almonds as finely as possible, sweeten them with sugar, and beat four eggs in upper milk, then pour it over them, so that the mixture is as thick as a strudel dough. grease a bowl with lard, pour the mixture into it, and simmer over heat until it sets.

title: Ein gutes Müssel von Hüner-Leber.
text: one should finely chop the well-drained livers and add one or two onions, then pour in sweet milk and let it simmer gently in a bowl or pastry dish, not for too long, so that it doesn't dissolve.

title: Das May-Muß zu machen.
text: to make a good, simple custard, not too much like a potful as one makes for a one-year-old child, place it in a bowl while it s still warm, and stir in four kreuzer worth of shredded butter, stirring it very well. the butter must be added gradually, and it should be well sweetened, and a spoonful of fresh water poured over it. you must stir for longer than an hour the longer you stir, the better it is. then, place it again in a bowl, piling it up finely, and garnish with flowers.

title: Ein gutes Semmel-Koch.
text: first, take stale bread, soak it in water, press it dry, and crumble it finely. then take a spoonful of rendered fat, stir it until it turns white afterward, add three egg yolks and two eggs with yolk and white, stirring very well. next, add finely chopped lemon zest, ensuring you use the fragrant part. add sugar to taste, place a bowl over a hot ember, and put another ember above it it is a good dish.

title: Das Mandel-Milch-Koch zu machen.
text: take a handful of almonds, peel them, and grind them very finely. mix with as much fresh milk, or otherwise good, thick milk strained through a cloth, as you need for cooking. once the almonds are well ground, heat the mixture. sweeten the milk, and in a clean bowl, make a custard with fine flour. when the custard begins to simmer, stir in the ground almonds, as much as you like. sweeten again if you desire a richer sweetness, and be sure the custard doesn't become too thick.

title: Gesultzte Milch zu machen.
text: one should take 10 egg whites and with a whisk beat a spoonful of water until frothy. then add twice as much sweet syrup, previously boiled in a small pot and again let it foam. afterwards, stir the egg whites into the syrup, very well until it becomes finely thick, and sweeten it well. place on a bowl, arrange, and chill.

title: Die Spanische Milch zu machen.
text: one should take good, sweet upper milk, a good measure full, and let it boil for about a quarter of an hour, or a little longer. afterward, pour it into a low earthenware dish and let it stand overnight in a cool cellar, where it will form a skin. then, take fine slices of bread rolls and soak them in good milk, and place them on a bowl. sprinkle them well with sugar, remove the skin finely with a spoon, and spread it on top, thickly and evenly, sprinkling sugar in between each layer. serve cold.

title: Schnee-Milch zu machen.
text: to begin, take a bowl with half a, or three, measures of very good, sweet cream. from five freshly churned butters, take the buttermilk, and whip it well with a spoon until it's very frothy then, place bread slices in a bowl, sprinkle with sugar and a little cinnamon, and pour the frothy buttermilk over them, layering it finely and as high as possible the higher, the better. if the buttermilk doesn't froth as long as a spoonful remains, simply whip it again it will froth. however, the cream must be very good.

title: Ein Topffen-Milch zu machen.
text: to begin, take a good, sweet cream, and pound three whole eggs well, then strain them through a sieve into a pot. set over the fire, and when it begins to simmer, crush curd cheese in some milk, pour it in, and stir well, leaving it over a low heat until it begins to thicken and forms a mass. let it stand for a while, then strain the mass through a cloth, and shape it into small molds, finely formed like spoons and woven from reeds. when the whey is well drained, turn it into a bowl and add sweet cream you may add sugar or not.

title: Reiß-Milch zu machen.
text: one should take good cream and cook rice in it, not too much. when it begins to simmer, one must not stir it. if it cooks for an hour and a half, the thick part will settle at the bottom. then one should lift the skin off, and let it run through a fine cloth, so that no rice comes through. sweeten or not, and let it cool.

title: Die Spanische Milch/ Nates genant.
text: to begin, take two quarts of unclarified milk, the further it is traveled, the better then take a freshly drawn milk, as it comes from the cow, strain it, and put it into a pail. set it on glowing embers, place small glowing coals around the outside, and let it stand for four or five hours on the glowing embers. when it is quite extinguished, put a fresh batch underneath, so that it works steadily from below, only not too much heat, otherwise the skin will become hard and tough, but it must always be working, just so you can feel it simmering. when it has risen sufficiently, it must certainly stand for four or five hours. take it from the embers, cover it, and place it in a cellar overnight. take the upper thick skin down, lay it on a bowl over each other, and add sugar thus it is made.

title: Mehr ein andere gute Milch.
text: first, take a portion of the previous day's sweet cream from the milk and put it into a small bowl. add a little of today's milk, then two spoonfuls of sugar. mix all of this well in a clean pot or whisk, and pour it into a bowl. afterwards, let it sit over low heat until it s warm, but not scorched, and then serve it cooled on the table.

title: Ein guten Lungenbraten-Pasteten zu machen.
text: to prepare a fine lung roast, skin it well and pound it thoroughly with the flesh fibers using a broad surface and a dull knife. then season it with salt, craneberry wine, camomile, and pour a good vinegar over it so that it can lie well within. you must turn it occasionally and let it stand for two days, or overnight in summer, and season it again. afterwards, roast it on a spit, and take some of the vinegar in which it was marinated, and melt a modest piece of butter into it, using this to moisten the roast several times. when it is about half-roasted, you should remove the skin, and while it is still hot, season it well with pepper, ginger, and a few cloves on both sides. if you have time, let it lie covered for half a day. then, depending on the size of the roast, take some quince, as much quince as there is of the quince, a pickled lemon, and a good

title: Das Pfefferl zu der Pasteten oder andern Sachen.
text: take one head of cabbage and a sour apple, finely chop them. take also some stale bread, grated, and roast all of this briefly in a little schmaltz. drain the schmaltz and put it in a pot. add chicken broth or broth from pork trimmings, or whatever you have available. add vinegar, enough to make it quite sour, and simmer. then beat it well and add sugar, cinnamon, and cloves only as much sugar as is needed to balance the sourness. if it s too thick, add wine and water, or meat broth. if you don t have broth, use pickle brine or dried pickles.

title:
Ein gute Karpffen- und Ferhen-Pasteten/ da man die Gräten
auch darmit essen kan.
text: to prepare the fish, open it at the belly and remove the innards. cut strips of fish meat from both sides, starting from the head, and salt them. then pour three spoonfuls of brandy over the head and let it sit in a cool place for three hours. afterward, sprinkle the fish thoroughly with a very sharp vinegar, heat it, and stir in pepper, ginger, and cloves until it forms a thick sauce like a porridge. then, coat the fish inside and out with this sauce and sprinkle it generously with brandy, cover it, and let it stand overnight. when you are ready to bake it, first sear both sides with hot lard. when placing it in the dough, put plenty of butter on the bottom and top, and add the lemon slices. bake it slowly, for four or five hours, depending on the size of the fish. every hour, pour a panful of butter through a small strainer into the dish. the fish, and even the bones, especially

title: Krebs-Pastetel zu machen.
text: one must have a hundred crabs on a table, if they are not too large, and instead of boiling them, let them drain well on a cloth so they are not too wet. then open them, and the bodies and claws should be ground well in a mortar until they are like dough. afterward, soak two rolls of breadcrumbs in milk, press them dry, and mix them into the crab dough, along with a knob of butter and a little pepper. this will make a beautiful dough, from which one should form small pastries, serving eight or ten to the table. first, make small leaves from a common dough, so that one can place them on top otherwise, the base will not hold. then, make a good crab topping, as before with the dough, mixing it with the yellow crab meat and the parsley, a little pepper, and chopped green herbs, also adding some claws. pack this in, add plenty of butter, then cover with the pastry crust, bind

title: Aber ein gutes Krebs-Pastetl zu machen.
text: to make a pie, start with good dough. then, blanch the crabs in salted water and open them, taking the claws and tails and seasoning with pepper. next, finely cook and flake a hake. layer butter in the pie crust, then a layer of crab, followed by a layer of hake, and a layer of butter. repeat this layering until the pie is full. pour a good broth over it, cover, and bake.

title: Fleisch-Pastetel zu machen.
text: one should take a pound of calf s meat or chicken forcemeat, and a reasonable amount, but not too much, of calf s or beef lights, and chop all of this as finely as possible, seasoning it with salt. then soak a bread roll in milk or meat broth, squeeze it out well, and add two egg yolks, and grind everything well in a mortar until it forms a dough. from this dough one can make several pastries, or just one pastety. place a calf s netting or a pastry sheet on the bottom where one will place it. then one should blanch capon or chicken livers that have been rinsed in much water until they are a beautiful white, and throw them into very hot clarified butter, and immediately take them out again, and salt and pepper them slightly, and chop in some green herbs and a finely chopped pickled lemon. spread a lot of butter on the bottom, then the chopped lemon on top, and fill the livers inside. on

title: Ein gutes Pastetel mit Hechten-Kraut zu machen.
text: take some finely boiled, clean cabbage and, in its place, a herring, finely shred it so that the bones come out well. then lay a leaf of butter on it, then cabbage, then of the herring, and ground pepper, and so on, until there is enough to turn over, but moderately much butter. you can also make it in a french pastry crust in a raised pie, and again boil a herring that is cut into pieces, and throw the pieces into hot rendered fat, so they brown a little, and place them in between. when you want to serve it, cut it open and pour a good, thick milk sauce over it, and leave it in the oven for a little longer.

title: Mehr ein Fleisch-Pastetel zu machen.
text: roast the veal and beef well, and take also many giblets, finely chopped. beat in three or four egg yolks, a little cream, wine berries, and pepper, stirring everything together. then form it into a pastry. line the bottom of a calf s stomach, and inside, place lamb or chicken meat. add lemon, pepper, parsley, and muscatel flowers. seal it, brush with egg yolk, and bake. when you want to serve it, make a small hole in the top and pour in meat broth with butter through a funnel, but only immediately when serving, otherwise it will soften.

title: Ein Ungarisch überschlagenes Pastetel.
text: use a fine, unblemished flour and a good, sweet milk lamb. chop a good, fresh butter into it, using more butter than milk lamb. let a little melt over a gentle heat, until the butter is finely rendered. once it s well combined, beat in 8 or 10 egg yolks, mixing thoroughly. add this mixture to the flour and work the dough briefly. roll out a sheet of dough to the size of the pie, but not too thin it should be about the thickness of a good, plump finger. then fill with chopped meat, or finely roasted lamb pieces, sprinkled with vinegar. cover with the dough and bake gently. when the pie is about half-baked, brush with egg yolk.

title: Mandel-Pastetl zu machen.
text: grind almonds very finely in a mortar, adding a spoonful of fresh water. grind them until they are not oily. add two egg whites and plenty of sugar, stirring until the mixture is quite thick. then, shape it into a small pastry. fill it with whatever you desire. make a covering from this dough as well, and bake it in an oven or pan. when it is nearly baked, remove it and make icing. spread it over and over. if you don't think it's beautiful enough, you can spread it again and bake it thoroughly.

title: Ein gutes auffgesetztes Pastetel mit dem weissen Süppel.
text: to prepare a nicely seasoned veal or lamb, chop the meat into small, handsome pieces and parboil. afterwards, rinse it well and make a pastry crust from white dough. then, place the meat inside, layering with plenty of butter, a bit of pepper, and soaked parsley root. seal it up and bake. afterwards, take a good meat broth and whisk in three egg yolks, lightly cooked and strained. once the pastry is nearly baked, pour the broth over it and let it bake again. add a sprig of green herbs, such as marjoram or heartsease.

title: Ein gutes Fisch-Pastetel zu machen.
text: one should cut open a good, medium-sized pike along the belly and chop it finely, like an eel, salt it, and then skewer it onto spits and roast it on a grate, brushing it several times with vinegar and melted butter, and so roast it halfway then one should boil another pike and flake it. or one can take a fish that one has saved, whatever kind it may be, and in the pastry one should lay some thin slices of bread soaked in broth, and butter on top of that, and flaked fish, and more butter, and the roasted fish on top of that, and grated pepper, then more butter and fish, and so on, so that the pastry, which is made of white dough, is filled, and always the roasted pieces and the flakes are layered, and on top again slices and butter, and then close it and bake it and when it is nearly baked, pour in a little thickened broth. one may also place rosemary between

title: Die Allebatritten Pasteten zu machen.
text: to begin, take some crane or small birds, good capon, two pigeons, and two sausages, and cook them almost halfway through. cut the capon and pigeons, as well as the sausages. then take six veal birds and cook as many as you like until they are a fine yellow. add whatever else you wish to include. next, take a good, fatty kidney pudding and cut the pudding along with the kidney thinly and finely. toast a handful of grated breadcrumbs in fat until they are a fine yellow, and mix in mild pepper. then turn some bread slices in beaten eggs and bake them in the fat. afterwards, dip them briefly in meat broth and place them on the bottom of the pie crust. the crust must be made from a rock pastry. then add butter, the aforementioned veal, and finely chopped lemon. after that, layer the previously cooked pieces in, interspersed with a few roasted, peeled chestnuts. then another layer of butter, veal, and lemon, and so

title: March-Pastetel zu machen.
text: make a dough from butter, flour, yeast, and sugar, knead the dough well, and roll out small pastries. cut fresh beef into fine squares, add sugar and cinnamon, and place between the pastries. seal the tops completely and bake in rendered fat.

title: Ein Hechten in einer Polnischen Suppen.
text: one should prepare the anglerfish, cutting it into pieces and salting it. let it lie in salt for an hour or two, depending on the size of the fish. then, take a handful of sorrel, a handful of chopped onions, several parsley roots that are cleanly trimmed, and two or three celery stalks, sliced and roasted in butter. simmer in water until it thickens. strain through a clean sieve, then add wine until it is thin enough. season well with pepper, ginger, grains of paradise, and saffron. remove the fish from the salt and place it in the soup, simmering it. then add a piece of sugar and butter, and continue to simmer.

title: Hechten in Lemoni zu kochen.
text: one should clean and cut the fish into pieces, salt it, and simmer in wine and vinegar. afterward, take good wine, saffron, ginger, sugar, and finely chopped lemon, and simmer them together. add the fish and let it cook until done.

title: Hechtel-Köchel zu machen.
text: one should open the haunch at the back, remove the innards, and separate them. salt it, and then place it on a roasting spit. afterwards, take butter, vinegar, and spices, melt the butter in the vinegar, and add rosemary sprigs. baste the haunch with this mixture until it is roasted. then pour the remaining broth over it, and serve it in this way.

title: Hechten in Oel zu kochen.
text: to prepare the john dory, cut it into pieces and salt it. then heat oil in a pan and lightly fry it. chop a good handful of chives finely and roast them until they are fine, tender, and yellow. also roast a handful of grated breadcrumbs, and add enough broth to cover them. add a generous amount of ground pepper. beforehand, either simmer the fish or fry it in the hot oil until it sets. then transfer it to a clean dish, pour the broth over it, and let it simmer.

title: Ein gefüllten Hechten zu machen.
text: to begin, open a medium-sized pike along the belly like a fish to be roasted. remove the innards, wash it clean, and salt it. then take a piece from another pike, chop it finely, and place it inside with some softened breadcrumbs, a handful of roughly ground almonds, and a knob of butter, pepper, nutmeg, marjoram, and juniper berries. beat in an egg, fill the pike with this mixture, and roast it on a spit, basting frequently. finally, pour a rich goat broth over it.

title: Hechten in Krien zu machen.
text: prepare the herring by cutting it into pieces and salting it. sprinkle it with hot wine one or two times this will make it fine and grainy. then, bring good, full milk to a boil and add the fish. include a spoonful of crushed caraway seeds, muscat flower, and crushed pepper. simmer until cooked.

title: Ein gesottenen Hechten in Capra.
text: when the duck has been cleaned and is lying in fat, salt, you should simmer it with half wine and water, and place it in a clean pot. pour half wine and broth over it, then add a handful of finely washed capers. afterwards, heat a little oil in a pan and brown some breadcrumbs, add as much fat as you like, and roast a little zibbel finely chopped in it, then pour that over as well. add pepper, ginger, and muscat blossom, and let it simmer together.

title: Ein Hechten in einer Braun-Suppen.
text: to prepare the perch, first finely chop the sweat and wash it out with wine, reserving the liquid. clean the fish and salt it. then, toast two slices of bread in melted butter, and add plenty of parsley root. also, roast two finely chopped onion halves in butter, and add the perch liver to this mixture, along with a little wine. pour this over the prepared fish, season with cloves and pepper, and simmer.

title: Ein Karpffen in einer gar guten Suppen.
text: to make it, take two carp and sweat them in vinegar, stirring well. add enough wine so the fish can simmer in it, and use plenty of vinegar so it becomes quite sour. when it boils, add a good amount of sugar to make it finely sweet, but still letting the acidity shine through. season with various spices. if the fish has been cleaned and salted beforehand, put it in the simmering mixture. when it's almost cooked through, remove the fish and let the broth reduce a bit. when it s nearly done, put the fish back in, always only two pieces at a time. when you're ready to serve, cut a fresh lemon into small pieces, place them finely on the fish, and keep it warm under a lid over embers. the lemon shouldn't simmer in the broth, or it will be ruined. if you want to serve it as a salt fish, keep it in a cool place like that.

title: Ein Karpffen in einer gelben Suppen.
text: one should clean the carp and cut it into pieces, and salt it. afterwards, simmer it in good wine until it is cooked through. then add a handful of crumbled stale bread, along with saffron, sugar, ginger, pepper, and cinnamon. alternatively, let it simmer and then sprinkle cinnamon sugar over it.

title: Ein Aal zu bachen.
text: one should simmer the eel in salt, as needed, then coat it in flour and bake it in fat. when serving, add bay leaves and sour oranges.

title: Einen Aal [Aaal] zu braten.
text: once the eel has been skinned and its veins removed along the backbone, it should be washed clean and cut into pieces. season with salt, ginger, and cloves, and let it lie for about an hour. then, skewer the pieces lengthwise onto bird skewers and roast, basting frequently with melted butter and rose vinegar. when almost roasted, sprinkle with cinnamon, cloves, and rosemary. in the same way, one can roast a roe or a flatfish, but it shouldn't lie in salt for as long as the eel only as one usually salts them.

title: Rutten einzumachen.
text: to make turnip soup, pour it into a clean pot. add chopped parsley and pepper, and grated nutmeg. add a little wine as well, and let it simmer. peel and mash the turnips, then season with salt. add the soup, and simmer until cooked through. when serving, add plenty of butter.

title: Ein Huechen oder Scheiden zu braten.
text: one should cut a nice piece from the haunch or rump, above the spine, leaving it as thick as possible. cut the spine finely lengthwise, in the shape of a sausage. salt this and attach it to a spit with four thin slivers, and tie it to the spit with a skewer, otherwise it will fall off. then, roast it finely as one would a sausage. afterward, melt a piece of butter, pour in some lemon juice or rose vinegar, and pepper it, and baste it constantly until it is almost hard. when basting for the last time, sprinkle it with a little grated breadcrumb, arrange it on green leaves, and add slices of a sour orange.

title: Scheiden einzumachen.
text: one must soften the casings in hot water like rutabagas and make pieces from them, leaving the tail a half ell long, intact this is needed later for frying. the pieces should be salted, then take a generous amount of parsnip, parsley, and root vegetables, and a breadcrumb mixture. pour in a broth, and simmer until everything is tender, then beat it well, and season with various spices. add the casings and brown them when you want to serve, and put a good knob of butter in.

title: Den Scheiden-Schweiff zu braten.
text: if it has been previously salted, you must bind it tightly with a string, otherwise it will fall apart, and roast it on a rack, constantly basting with butter, rose vinegar, and pepper. when it is nearly roasted, stud it with cloves and cinnamon sticks, and when it is roasted, stud it with rose-mary. you may press it or place it on a soup plate.

title: Sälbling haiß abzusieden.
text: one should take fine sprats, because they are still fresh and not dull, and according to their size, open them either by splitting, or cutting into pieces, or leaving them whole, and boil them quickly in finely salted water. afterward, quickly blanch them in the best butter with wine vinegar, remove from the heat, and arrange on a platter.

title: Die Ferchen schön blau abzusieden in der [dir] Sultzen.
text: to prepare them, open them on the belly all the way to the tail, then separate them, stab the spine, but do not cut through the skin. afterwards, proceed as with the young suckling pig. when taking them off the fire, sprinkle them with cold vinegar and a little alum. when removing them, cover them with a clean, thick cloth so that no steam escapes they will then become a beautiful blue color. then, lay two of them against each other on their bellies, as if they were swimming, and serve the soup alongside.

title: Ferchen in Oel zu kochen.
text: one should open the birds on the belly and cut off small bits. afterwards, take fresh oil into a pan. when it is hot, sprinkle it with a few drops of cold water, and heat a whole peeled onion with it. this will take away the coarse taste. add rose vinegar or sour orange juice to it. one should salt the birds as before, and place them on a roasting rack, often basting them until they are cooked through. one must also add spices, such as pepper, ginger, and pour the rest over a good wine, a handful of capers, and half a handful of wineberries, cinnamon, and cloves. however, the acidity must be tempered. boil all of this finely in a small pot, and pour it over the birds when they are prepared. add fine bay leaves for garnish.

title: Geselchte Fisch zu kochen.
text: one should take parsley root, cook it until very soft in a broth soup. afterwards, finely grated bread crumbs should be roasted in the rendered fat, and add them to the soup. the fish must be washed so that it is not salty, and put into the soup, and cook it properly. then add a good piece of butter, ground pepper, and muscat blossom. there must be plenty of parsley root, but one shouldn't make too much soup with it.

title: Den frischen Hausen zu braten.
text: one should cut the cutlets thinly and season with salt. then, roast them on a rack and constantly baste with fresh butter. afterwards, sprinkle with cinnamon and cloves, and serve warm on a platter or in a dish.

title: Den frischen Hausen abzusieden.
text: cut the pieces not too thick, wash them clean, and let them soak in water for a while. then simmer in well-salted water until tender. afterwards, take them out and pour hot vinegar over them, sprinkle with crushed pepper, and serve warm. or, if you prefer to serve them cold, leave the vinegar on and garnish with parsley.

title: Ein Biber-Schweiff zu kochen.
text: one should boil the beaver tail with the paws until the upper skin comes off, then in salted water for about three hours until it turns white. if it has another skin, one should clean it. when it is almost cooked, add vinegar, saffron, sugar, and other spices salted lemons may also be added while simmering.

title: Die Schildkrotten gar gut zu kochen.
text: cut off the turtle's head, feet, and tail. boil it in water until the shell softens. then, divide it into four pieces and scrape the skin clean. add the liver and lungs, finely chopped. season with pepper, ginger, mace, and salt. chop parsley very finely and sprinkle it on top. melt butter in a pan, then add grated breadcrumbs until a thick mixture forms. add the seasoned turtle and stir until it is coated with butter. pour in some broth and simmer. if desired, add a knob of butter. if you wish, clean the deep shells of the turtle and place them on a dish, arranging the turtle within them.

title: Blatelte Plateisen zu kochen.
text: one should soak the codfish day and night, or longer, in cold lye so that it swells beautifully, and its skin comes off. afterwards, wash it thoroughly and let it lie in water for a while, cut it into pieces, and let it simmer for a good while as needed. peel off the skin and flake the fish, removing the bones. then place it in a pot and pour good broth over it, adding a spoonful of grated breadcrumbs fried in fat. if desired, you can roast a shallot as well, and add a pinch of ground pepper and grains of paradise. you can also add a little chopped parsley or marjoram, or whatever else you like. simmer, then add a piece of butter.

title: Den Hausen abzusieden daß er ein halbes Jahr bleibt.
text: one should wash the veal clean and cut it into pieces, and simmer it in well-salted water. afterward, lay it on a cloth and a rack to drain. then, take the broth and pour half wine and half vinegar into it, and let it simmer, then cool. afterward, place the veal in a small earthenware pot, scattering ground pepper and salvia leaves, or rosemary, between the layers. pour the broth over it, doing so repeatedly until the pot is full and the broth covers the veal. then, seal the pot and keep it in a cool place.

title:
Kunst allerley Vögel einzubeitzen/ und wie sie sich lang
behalten lassen.
text: first, you must pluck and clean the birds, cut off the heads and feet, and remove the entrails. afterward, put clean water in a pot or cauldron over the fire when the water boils, put the birds in and let them simmer. then take them out onto a board to let the water drain off. next, take a wooden tub, fill it with the birds, and salt them so they are well covered in salt. add a little crushed crowberry, then pour in enough vinegar to cover the birds, and preserve them. when you want to eat them, open the tub and fry them. it has been tested.

title: Die Schweitzer-Käß zu machen.
text: first, in the evening, one milks the cow, and pours the milk into bowls. it must be skimmed early the next morning but if it is winter, it can stand for three days until skimmed. afterward, one takes the same milk and puts it into a pot that can be hung, and makes a small fire underneath, so that the milk becomes a little warmer than it comes from the cow. afterward, one takes it off the fire, puts in the rennet, and then makes a great deal of cheese the rennet must also be there. but if the rennet is new, one takes less than if it is old. when one has put the rennet in, one stirs it together with the largest skimming spoon, but not on the fire. afterward, one lets the spoon float in it. when the spoon stands still, it is come together. afterward, one takes out with the spoon the undesirable substance that floats above, and the rennet is

title:
Wie man aber die Lup zu disen Käsen machen muß/
ist also:
text: first, take a calf's stomach, wash and clean it thoroughly. then, blow it up and keep it until you want to make a loop. take one or two of these stomachs, depending on how many you want to make, and put them in a small cloth bag that has a small opening at the bottom, so you can let the loop out when you use it. if you take two stomachs, use a handful of salt if you only take one, use half that amount. salt the stomachs and then add cheese brine. let them stand in a cool place, not too cold or too hot then it is ready. the cheese must be salted for three weeks, but only every other day, and cleaned with water afterwards, then salted again.

title: Ende deß Koch-Buchs.
text: roast chicken with apples and onions ingredients 1 chicken 1 tbsp salt 1 tsp black pepper 1 2 tsp dried thyme 1 4 tsp dried sage 2 tbsp butter, melted 2 large apples, peeled, cored, and quartered 2 large onions, peeled and quartered 1 2 cup chicken broth instructions preheat oven to 350 f. rinse the chicken inside and out and pat dry. in a small bowl, combine salt, pepper, thyme, and sage. rub the mixture all over the chicken, including under the skin of the breast. brush the melted butter over the chicken. place the apples and onions in the bottom of a roasting pan. place the chicken on top of the apples and onions. pour the chicken broth into the bottom of the roasting pan. roast for 1 hour and
ingredients: dried thyme dried sage butter apples

title:
Bartholomæus Hübner: New Speisebüchlein:
Darinnen kurtzer Vnterricht von allerley Speise vnd Tranck/ so
zur Menschlichen Nahrung dienlich (...). Erfurt 1603.
text: to prepare a healthful body and a good constitution, one must consider the nature of foods and how they affect the humors. it is essential to eat moderately and to choose foods that are suited to the season and one's own temperament. foods should be wholesome and easily digestible, and one should avoid those that are heavy, greasy, or overly stimulating. it is beneficial to eat at regular times and to avoid overeating, as this can disrupt the balance of the humors. drinks should be pure and refreshing, and one should avoid those that are strong or intoxicating. water is the best drink, but wine and beer may be consumed in moderation. the preparation of food is also important. foods should be cooked properly and seasoned with herbs and spices to enhance their flavor and digestibility. it is best to avoid overly salty or spicy foods, as these can irritate the stomach. finally, one should pay attention to the appearance and aroma of food, as these can also affect its digestibility.

title:
Das Erste Buch: Darin etzliche nothwendige vnd nütze
Regeln/ von der Diæt/ Speise vnd Tranck/ erzehlet werden/
etc.
text: first, one must pay utmost attention and care to the foods we consume, ensuring they nourish and preserve the body as much as possible, so that no harm or detriment arises to any member or part of it. the opinion of celsus, from lucretius, should not be approved, who claims it matters little what foods one eats, as long as one can digest them, because reason and common experience teach the opposite. for physicians and philosophers say nourishment is life. and aetius truthfully warned against avoiding foods that provide bad, harmful nourishment, even if they are easily digestible and the stomach can overcome them, because harmful moisture then gathers in the body and veins, which can subsequently rot from minor causes and provoke harmful fevers and other diseases. therefore, choose foods that provide good juice, blossoms, and nourishment, as galen says in de alimentis facultatibus. for bad humors of the body, from which most illnesses originate, come

title: Drei Kochrezepte, die bei Jean Paul erwähnt werden
text: baked cat dirt ingredients take fresh cat dirt, cleanse it well. mix with flour, eggs, and a little salt. form into small cakes and bake until golden brown. serve hot. saxon christscheit ingredients take a pound of pork, half a pound of beef, and a quarter pound of veal, all finely chopped. mix with breadcrumbs, onions, eggs, salt, pepper, and marjoram. form into small loaves and bake until cooked through. aborted wasp nest ingredients carefully collect a freshly abandoned wasp nest. gently wash away any debris. mix with flour, eggs, and a pinch of salt. fry in oil until crispy. serve immediately.

title: Fisch wol sieden.
text: always keep a good fire going with smoke underneath when the sausages are done, they are cooked enough clean them nicely and cut them to the right size season them well with spices and salt then drizzle them with vinegar and lay them in dry or wet storage carry them for a while. if they are stored dry, sprinkle plenty of good ground ginger on them.

title: Holbrahten oder Rechbrahten in der Fasten zu machen.
text: simmer figs and wine in good wine, chop them finely. add flour to this, mix well. season with salt and spices. dip your hands in dough water, wrap the figs around a skewer like a spit, with wet hands, and press firmly. set them on the spit to roast. once cooked, slice it lengthwise on both sides of the spit, making pretty pieces. decorate with almond kernels, either blanched or candied, and serve. you may add sugar or fresh ginger on top. the spit can also be enjoyed with butter.

title: Einen Fischbrahten zu machen.
text: to prepare it in a similar color to the freshly boiled herring, take a pike, prepare it nicely, remove the ridge, and simmer it with seasoning. retain the broth, and pound the pike in a mortar with cranberries, honey, seasoning, salt, and a little flour. temper it well with butter, mix it around on a platter like the herring, and place it near the fire. take the head, the ridge, and the tail, chop them into small pieces with the sweatings, and simmer them thoroughly with wine. rub gingerbread in, finish with seasoning and salt, or with fish broth taste it well. if you do not want to boil the pike beforehand, chop it very finely, pound it well in a mortar, and prepare it with the spices as mentioned before.

title: Würst von Fischen.
text: prepare and finely chop the sausages. grind them in a mortar. add spices and salt. stuff the casings and simmer them, as with wine. add a pinch of pepper.

title: Küchlin von Fischen.
text: prepare them nicely, wipe off the sweat, and remove the gills. retain the head, tail, and entrails, discarding the gall. then take the fish, chop them finely, both raw and cooked. grind them well in a mortar. add flour, wineberries, and good spices, salt, and butter. mix well, place it in a pastry crust with gingerbread, and it is ready. the other from the fish head, gills, and entrails make a fine broth, cooked in wine, and prepared as another fish, grilled and spiced. test it with salt these are two refined fish dishes.

title:
Dreierley essen von einem Fisch/ das doch der Fisch nach beduncken
gantz bleib.
text: cut a pike, or another fish, into four pieces. roast the first piece on a spit. simmer the second piece with wine and seasonings. fill the third piece. bake the fourth piece, the tail end, and assemble the fish so that each piece appears whole. sprinkle generously with parsley and serve. accompany with good sauce or vinegar in small bowls, so that each person may take what they desire this is unusual.

title:
Ein meisterliche Gallrad vber Fisch/ als da sein Salmen/ vnd
ander grosse Fisch.
text: cut the fish into good-sized pieces serve two or three per person. place the pieces in a wooden platter. pour over wine and vinegar, salt and spices, retaining the broth as described. add bread and proceed as before. if the sauce is too thin, add bay leaves or orange peel, or half the amount of bay leaves. grind them with the beaten bread and fish broth, strain it, and season it. taste to ensure it is properly spiced and salted, then add the fish pieces and pour the sauce over them. let it stand. if desired, sprinkle with ginger, cinnamon, or mace, and then glaze it.

title:
Gesültzt Fisch im Sommer zu bereiten/ so sie doch nicht
gern gestehen.
text: when you prepare the fish, keep the sweat and scales, and the trimmings, and put it in a pot, simmer it with wine, skim it well, pour it into a mortar, pound it well, and strain it through a cloth with its own broth, in which it was boiled. add a bay leaf, pounded and grated, and let it stand. lay in the fish, as much as you want dishes for. take then the fish broth, add the scale broth with spices and everything, taste to see what is lacking, vinegar, salt, or spices. let it simmer in a pan until it forms a froth, then pour it over the fish, let it cool in the air, and salt it once. if you want to sprinkle almonds or wine berries on top, do so at the right time, before they are half-way set, so they remain clean and good.

title: Fisch behalten/ das sie lang frisch bleiben.
text: lay them in a small vessel or an earthen pot, and sprinkle good vinegar over them, add parsley. bury them in fresh earth. and when you take the fish and vinegar out, pour fresh vinegar over them each time, and cover them again with good cloths, so they will remain fresh for a long time and will not become foul, but will always be fresh. you can cook them with water, vinegar, and plenty of salt, and let them simmer until the foam rises over twice or three times. crab shells, burned to ashes, soaked in honey and gentian, cure the bite of a mad dog.

title:
Gesültzt Krebs/ gar ein höflich vnd dewiges Essen/
on schaden.
text: prepare the crabs with wine and shell the claws, legs and bodies, keeping the other parts aside for seasoning. next, make the broth as follows take the smallest parsley, boil it in wine and vinegar as much as you desire or need, strain it, and add the crab butter from the heads. then take the insides, claws and legs, pound them well in a mortar, grind them with the broth in which they were boiled, and strain through a cloth. afterwards, take fresh crabs, only the shelled claws and legs, place them in the strained crab mixture in a pan, stir them gently, remove them from the seasonings and salt, taste them to see what they need, and let them cool.

title: Gallrad zu den eingemachten Krebsen.
text: peel as many crabs as you wish, and put them in wine and vinegar. remove the bitterness from the heads, peel the gills and belly. put them in a mortar with almonds and a little white bread. grind well with good wine, strain it through a cloth, put it in a pan, and add butter. season with spices and salt, taste it. if it's too strong, temper it with water, so that the vinegar, wine, and spices are properly balanced. serve it hot or cold, sprinkle it with welch grapes or fresh ginger if you serve it warm. if you want it cold, once it has stood well, garnish it with almonds.

title: Gefüllte Krebs.
text: boil the crabs and shell them well, setting aside the large claws separately. take the other shelled small crabs, legs, gills, and bodies, and chop them very finely. beat in fresh eggs, according to the quantity of crab, and season with spices and salt. fry them lightly, add chopped parsley, and mix well with a raw egg to bind them together. then take the shells or backs, fill them well, and cover with another shell so that the heads are nestled together and the bodies facing each other. if you want to bake them, put two or three on a spit and place them on a grill, not too hot, until the filling has set and is cooked through. serve them warm in this way. alternatively, you can roast them in butter until the filling is done. afterwards, take the remaining crab, finely shelled and cleaned, and pound it with fresh breadcrumbs in a mortar. press it through a cloth. add the largest crab claws and trimmings,

title: Pasteten von Krebsen.
text: prepare crabs with salt, shelling them well, and place them together. finely chop parsley. take fresh eggs, beat them thoroughly, and pour them into the pie crust. cut good beer into long strips, press them into the filling, add figs and raisins. crush the crab shells, and the head and tail, all according to the length. then make a good wine with spices and salt, taste it to see what it needs, and pour it over the filling in the pie crust. brush the edges with a beaten egg or two, so they don't become soggy. put butter between the pie crust and the edges. place in an oven, let it simmer or bake. look at it frequently if it smokes, it's burning, so baste it with butter.

title: Ein Torten von Krebsen.
text: make a pastry crust in a greased pan and prepare a filling of eggs and grated cheese, or gingerbread. temper it well, but not too thin, and pour it into the pastry pan. if it's too thin, mix in milk until it reaches the right consistency, season with spices and salt, saffron, and beretine. you may add sage, parsley, or other spices finely chopped, temper the filling with them, and crush some crabs. if you want to add beer, figs, or sweet apples, thinly sliced and crushed with the crabs, that is good. cover the pastry pan with a lid, put butter on top, place it over a low fire, and alternately roast coals around it, or turn the pan and wait for the smoke, then cover with butter. when the lid is browned, it is done. remove the pastry dough entirely from the pan into a wide bowl, and shape it into pieces for a formal presentation.

title: Ein Gebackens von Krebsen.
text: prepare the crabs nicely, make a yellow dough from eggs, seasoned and salted, not too thin or too thick. work the crabs into the dough, each piece separately, and bake them. but the small shells and crumbs, make them into small cakes or twists, and bake them. if you don't have nice eggs, take a little saffron to add. serve the baked goods warm. if you want, sprinkle with honey and sugar, that is good.

title: Ein Müslin von Krebsen.
text: to prepare a dish of delicate colors, proceed as follows take good milk and cornflower juice, beat them together, and temper them. add fine flour and temper again. prepare the crabs very well, removing only the gall from the heads. you may pound them with wine, or with shells and all. add stale bread, press it through a cloth, season it with spices and salt, and place it in a muslin bag. moisten it well with flour and honey, temper it with a spoonful. if it lacks seasoning and salt, season it. if it is too thick, thin it with milk to the right consistency. place it in a small pan and let it simmer like a child's porridge. if you wish to serve it warm, the more pounded crab in the muslin, the better for a good thickness, and sprinkle butter and ginger on top. set it aside like this it will keep well. if you wish to serve it cold, make the muslin with wine or

title: Krebs zu sieden.
text: simmer the fish in a covered pot with plenty of wine, vinegar, or water, and salt and pepper. add a layer of leeks underneath, and when they turn red, they are done. serve hot in covered dishes. plum sauce goes well with fish and crab. those who eat fish and crab should avoid drinking milk or water.

title: Küchlin von Krebsen.
text: prepare crabs by washing them with water and salt, then shell them nicely. take the head, scissors, and sweetbreads, flour, salt, and spices. chop them finely. spread the crab inside with honey and fold the fabric together. grease a small dish and form the pastries. bake them until brown, then dry them or place them in a strainer. if you dry them, sprinkle them with sugar. fish, crabs, and sweetbreads are much better cooked with wine than with water, beer, or vinegar alone. all fatty foods are harmful to humans, and fatty fish even more so. dry bread eaten is also harmful. but if someone wants to eat cheese and bread, they shouldn't eat them unwashed. eight years may be a lifetime six days without water.

title: Wie man äl kochen sol.
text: skin the animal completely down to the tail, cut it up. remove the innards and the gall. finely chop parsley, salt, bay leaf, and marjoram, or other good herbs, and mix with vinegar and good wine until it is well moistened. then add ginger, nutmeg, and salt, and rub it into the chopped meat all over the inside and outside. skin the animal again down to the tail. place it on a hot grill and let it brown, or cut it into pieces and thread them onto a wide wooden spit. turn it over the fire until it is cooked through. it will roast in its own fat, so nothing else needs to be added to it. season with salt or ground ginger.

title: Vom Biber.
text: the beaver is an animal, like a sea dog, long and pregnant, with very long toes. it does not live long. it keeps its tail in the water, and it is half flesh, and the other part of the tail is fish. the tail is about the length of an ell and has much fat in it. it has hind feet like a goose, which propel it as a dog does. nature has given it this ability to swim in the water like a fish with its hind feet and to walk on land like another animal. the beaver s testicles, when cut off and hung up in a dark place, are kept for medicine, called castoreum. this is the beaver s testicles, which are good against the falling sickness of the head, against the paralysis of the tongue. when powdered and placed under the tongue, it dissolves and drives it away. it also alleviates piercing stomach cramps when drunk with vinegar and expels humors from the body, brings

title: Stockfisch oder Rheinfisch zu kochen.
text: one must soak and steep the dried cod in wine or water, and season it with spices. rhine fish and bollocks boiled in water, with herbs or sauces. these and all smoked fish can be served on fast days alongside soups or herbs.

title: Gute Suppen zu machen.
text: simmer dried plums, straining them well through a cloth into a pan. add a little honey, season with salt and spices. you may use it to improve pea soup, and add it to all soups with stale bread and ginger. add sugar if you wish to improve it, and serve with hot dried fish.

title: Gut Kirschenmus.
text: grind the stems with a mortar, kernels and all. take figs, resin, for a serving, soft white bread slices in wine. temper it thoroughly through a cloth with more wine don t make it too thick, nor too thin. add a pinch of flour and butter, grind well in a pan. adjust it as soon as it simmers like another compote. add clarified fat and spices on top carry it that way. thus you may make apricot, plum, and strawberry muses. red wine suits it better than white, and the pinch of flour should be well mixed with the wine beforehand before adding it, then stir well until it simmers it will thicken and stand well.

title: Gerennet Milch.
text: make the rice small, pass it through a sieve, then add milk from ground almonds. strain the best almonds, set the others to the fire so they don't burn or boil over. add the rice flour to the milk before it gets hot, and make a thick muslin from it. afterwards, shape it into a moist bowl, let it cool, cut it into pieces, like white wafers, and place them in another bowl. then pour the thick almond milk over it, garnish with almonds, gilded or colored.

title: Vergülden
text: make a small amount of honey water, spread the almonds with it, and sprinkle with gold or silver as desired. press it with cotton to where it does not immediately lie. you may use gingerbread or something else to gild. otherwise, no other confection is suitable for eating. make a wooden skewer so that you can lift the gold do not touch it with your bare hand, or else it will spoil everything.

title: Ein blaw Mus von Mandeln vnd Reis.
text: boil cornflowers well in water, strain them through a cloth. grind almonds with the same water, strain it through as well, and you will have a blue milk. make a paste from rice or a wheat muslin with this. you may sprinkle it with small raisins. do not salt it, and do not let it burn. the muslin stands well in white dishes.

title: Ein schwartz gemüß.
text: combine wine, apples, beer, and sugar. add a little flour, and stir well together in a pan.

title: Ein gut Gemüß von Fischen vnd Mandeln.
text: clean the innards of the fish thoroughly and chop them finely, being careful with the gall. remove the scales from the fish with water and strain them. add the broth. grind the fish very well with almond milk and white bread soaked in almond milk. work it out with softly cooked rice. heat it over a fire in a pan, stirring well. if it's too thick, add more almond milk. finish with sugar.

title: Von Obs.
text: sweep the refuse up into a dry cellar, onto a heap, or onto straw, as far as possible.

title: Von Nüssen.
text: hazelnuts from your dry worm bring hawthorn kindle the stomach. ground and moistened with honey water they soothe old coughs.

title: Nüs frisch behalten.
text: lay them in fresh sand or in a dry, square cellar, not in harbors.

title: Weinbeer frisch behalten.
text: make a thin paste with spring water in a wide dish. crush the grape stems into it, so they don't move. store it in a cellar. if you need more, fill a tub with spring water and soak the stems in it until the paste softens, then drain it off. afterwards, rinse it clean with fresh water.

title: Korn oder Weitzen lang frisch zubehalten.
text: take them in a green place, either in an oven or in the sun, keep them up in a house, airy in a basket, as one keeps cherries. when you want them, lay them in fresh well water, so they return to their strength. with young chickens, or dress them with a little bacon and salt, or butter. wild birds are good and tasty, so cooked.

title: Holdermus zu machen.
text: break the holderblüt into boiling milk, a good portion. let it simmer, strain it through a cloth, and make a firm dough with eggs. roll it into thin sheets, cut the dough small into worm-like pieces, put them into the boiling milk, salt, and finish with butter.

title: Ein Holdermus von Beern.
text: wash the capers well, pound them with warm white wine. add grated bread and chicken broth or good wine. add gingerbread or honey, season it, and strain it through a cloth into a bowl or pan. let it simmer, sprinkle with spices.

title: Ein Mus von Biern.
text: cut them into small pieces, peel onions, add wine, salt, and rendered fat. cover and place in a hot oven until they are cooked through and have reduced in size. season to taste, sprinkle with ginger.

title: Ein Apffelmuß ohne Zwiblen.
text: cut small cutlets into a little milk or wine. season with salt and fat. simmer covered over a low heat.

title: Brombeer oder Weigselmüß.
text: grind them in a mortar. add bread to it, spread it through a cloth, then flour and milk very well. put it together in a pan over the fire, stir well and don't forget to salt it. this will become a brown mush, sprinkle ginger on top. the pan should be greasy so it doesn't burn. if it's too thick, add more milk. mulberry mush is made in the same way. cherries or plums are also made in this way, but the kernels and everything is ground, pressed with wine, water, or meat broth.

title: Von Bieren.
text: barley roots, leaves, and fruits have great power. boiled barley leaves heal wounds. the kernel, crushed and used on an empty stomach, alleviates liver pain. one makes beer from grains like apples, plums, peaches, and quinces. fine flour beer, eschenbach wine, water beer, cask beer, or lard beer, well rendered in an oven, and they are preserved for years. when one wishes to cook them, one cleans and places them neatly in warm water, and lets them soak. whoever steeps them in wine and lays them with figs in a dish, they protect like figs.

title: Küchlin von dürren Biern.
text: grind them finely in a mortar. flour and gingerbread, yellow wine or milk, add to it as needed until it forms a dough. knead it out, beat in a fresh egg, and spread it inside the hand, which will hold the little cakes together well. draw them through a small yellow cloth, lift them out with a spoon into the pan, and bake them well. simmer wine and honey in a pan, and sprinkle them with this. serve it thus, it is a noble, festive dish. whoever wants enough of the thin beer, they serve with figs, and are very pleasing to simple folk. such beer eaten with a bread spice is a good, poor man s meal. rock candy stirred in tastes well and strengthens the weak stomach, seasoned with salt and plenty of ginger, only with wine and vinegar.

title: Gesültzt Morchen.
text: to make a salted fish broth is good, or do it this way take a little vinegar and wine mixed together, simmer four small onions in it, or mace or bay leaf, or the leaves. strain it through a cloth, let it settle, skim it, salt it, and season it. afterwards, pour it over the same onions. if you want the broth yellow, add saffron to it. let it stand until it thickens, then prepare peeled almond kernels, decorated nicely this is very good. one could also make such a filling for crab shells.

title: Mandelmilch/ grün/ blaw oder gelb.
text: to make a dish with mallows, date kernels, or other greens if they don t taste good, otherwise the almonds will lose their flavor. add no color to it, for tasteless herbs dull the almonds as it should be. mix with fish broth where parsley has been boiled. you can make it yellow with saffron, blue with cornflowers, or red with red wine. if you want to serve it, break it into a bowl like milk, mix in sugar and salt, sprinkle a little on top, and gild it nicely. then crush almond kernels into it.

title: Ein höflicher Ziger von Mandeln.
text: chop the almonds finely and pass them through a cloth dampened with water. warm the milk in a pot and stir it well. take a clarified broth made from fish and birch bark, or from calves' or sheep's feet, well-strained, salted, and mixed with almond milk. let it cool and stand.

title: Kes von Mandelmilch.
text: heat eggs and almond milk, salt, and boil well. season or add saffron when the eggs are cooked. when they are hard, stir them well with a spoon. place a fine cloth in a pepper sieve, spreading it widely. pour the curd onto it, letting the whey drain. make as many bowls as you like, and sprinkle them with sugar.

title: Gebackens von Oblaten.
text: finely chop the dried figs and season them with spices, saffron, salt, and pepper. place an oblate wafer on a surface, spread the figs over it, then cover with another oblate wafer. roll the layered wafers through a small bowl of white flour and bake until golden brown.

title: Gebackens von Mandeln vnd Reiß.
text: grind the almond with water and grind the rice dry. strain it through a sieve, letting a thick milk settle. sprinkle the flour into it, stir it well, make a thick mush. and a thinner one with warm wine, stir it well. pour the mush onto a clean, damp board and let it cool. then cut it into shapes as you like, pull it through a roller, and bake it.

title: Ein gut gezogen Gebackens.
text: grind almonds and pine nuts in wine using a mortar. mix flour and spices into this mixture, and form small pastries. roll them out thinly through a rolling pin and bake them well. make the müslein with warm wine and white flour, color it, and serve it dry.

title: Ein höflich Essen von Erbsen.
text: boil and soak the peas well with water, strain the soup. keep the broth for seasoned soups, seasoned with spices, tasted, and clarified. take the peas into a clean bowl, mash them well with a large spoon. take a portion for eating, put it into a pepper pan, push it through with your hand into a wide bowl. lift the pan high, so the peas are separated like earthworms, large and small. keep them whole, so they fall into the bowl evenly and do not overflow. let them stand. from the other portion of the peas, make little cakes as follows put flour in your hand and, kneading the cakes together, make a dough with clarified wine. dip the cakes in this, lift them with a spoon into the pan, and bake as many as you wish. make an pea broth over it, seasoned with spices and salt, add butter and rosin. serve covered. one can also bake pea cakes gently in a pepper pot, from clarified wheat

title: Ein Mehlpfefferlin.
text: brown flour in butter, not too much, temper with wine, and season it. bake erbsküchlein before jelly, put pepper on top.

title: Ein höflich Essen in Fastagen.
text: make a small meat pie and good herbs, peeled and prepared, and place them in a pastry crust. add pear brandy and a little honey, sprinkle with nutmeg or pepper over the pie, then add beer, ginger, and butter. if you have no beer, use quartered baked apples or bake it in a small dish with butter.

title:
Fleisch das man stossen mus/ als alten Krancken Leuten/ die
nicht kewen mögen.
text: boiled meat, either veal or other fresh meat, without salt, skim it, and strain the broth, keeping it aside. grind the meat well in a mortar with a little breadcrumb. strain this mixture through a cloth with the reserved broth, and mix it with wine and vinegar. if you want it thick, beat egg yolk with the broth. if you want it thin, leave out the egg, but add spices, salt, and butter. if you want it very thin, serve with bread as a soup.

title: Ein Gallrad/ warüber du wilt.
text: slice thin white bread and place it on a rack to dry. toast it well and clean it. soak it in warm wine, soften it thoroughly, and press it through a cloth. take figs, resin, and grated gingerbread, and press them through with chicken or meat broth. mix this with the bread pulp, stir in resin in wine, stirring constantly while simmering so it doesn t burn. remove from heat and season with spices, ginger, pepper, and saffron. stir constantly until it cools, and then sweeten it as you desire. it will set quickly. you may add grated ginger or sprinkle with bacon on top. if serving cold, you won't need the bacon. chicken meat strengthens the stomach and relieves the chest, brightens the complexion, and warms the body.

title: Ein gut Essen von Hünern.
text: simmer them well and properly, then divide them into four parts the head, the neck, and all the entrails, chop and pound in a mortar. take eggs, parsley, and about two spoonfuls of wheat flour sprinkle this over with wine or water, seasoned with saffron. once everything is pounded, take it out take the other parts of the chickens, coat them with the pounded dough all around, each piece like a cake, dip the hands in wine, spread it well around and around, and place them in the old chicken broth, so that it covers them, in a wide dish. let it also simmer thus. when it is cooked, season the broth with spices and salt, and sprinkle chopped parsley over it. if you want it better, take figs and raisins, check them into the chopped mixture, and although the pieces are small, each should still be coated and added. such a chopped mixture with flour can be made into good chicken fillings. if you want

title: Ein gut Hun sieden/ brahten oder füllen.
text: prepare the hare, skin it well, and sharpen it. take the head, neck, liver, stomach, and all the entrails, and simmer them in a pot or pan. chop finely with parsley, beat in raw eggs, season with spices and salt. add chopped bacon underneath, a little rosin or beer. mix everything well together. fill the hare with this mixture and stew it in water, with wine and vinegar added, until it sets and the filling hardens. secure it in place and baste it frequently. if you wish to boil it, you don't need to boil the hare first, chop it raw and prepare the filling as before. simmer one with the other in plain water, generously seasoned with salt. the pot should be wide enough to prevent burning, skim it well, and cover it tightly. add mustard to the basting liquid this will give the broth a good flavor. if you want to garnish it, you can use saffron, if you

title: Gestossen Hüner.
text: simmer the old, fat hens well, make the broth clear, and dilute it as much as water broth, no more than that. salt it, do not sour it. take the hens out and keep the broth. strain the clearest part into another bowl, and the leaner broth into another leave it as it is. then, take the large bones out of the hens, chop them very finely. soak a good amount of white bread crumbs in the leaner broth. afterwards, take the bread and the hens, pound them very well in a mortar, force them through a pepper cloth with the old hen soup, pound once more, and force through. if it's too thin, add more white bread crumbs, force through. if it's too thick, force it through without bread. fry it in a pan. finish it with spices and salt. when it s done, these are pounded hens. add plenty of butter on top. you can pound and prepare all birds in

title: Geprester Schweinskopff.
text: boil the head in a clean pot until the bones come loose. clean it nicely, pluck the legs from it, and chop the black bits. take the ears, cheeks, and tongue, pound them well in a mortar with a little broth, season with spices and grated gingerbread as much as you need. lay the black bits on a damp pepper cloth, put the cheeks in a mortar to make the tongue, temper it, and not too thin. you may add rosin, shape it with your hands on the cloth, round and round, fold the cloth evenly, secure it well with a thread, put everything in a press between two boards wide enough, or weigh it down with stones, let it dry for a day and night, cut pieces from it into a pepper.

title: Von geprestem Schweinßkopff gebrahtens.
text: cut a piece of meat, either one or two portions, long and thick. skewer it all around with a needle, making small round marks. make a slender wooden spit, pierce it, and place it near the fire. at first, turn it gently towards the fire, gradually closer, until it is cooked through. it is seasoned from its nature, so do not salt it. if you don't have bacon, baste it lightly with hot butter or meat broth. this is how venison, loin, game, and poultry are roasted.

title: Ein füll in Brahten/ oder Geuögel zu machen.
text: beat peterlin, rosin, cooked apples, or beer with two hard eggs, whisking with one raw egg, seasoning, and a little saffron. if the mixture is well-blended and incorporated using a finger, wood, or knife, secure it with skewers or sew it closed with thread to prevent it from bursting. you may also add chopped bacon or butter to the broth, if desired.

title: Ein Sultzbrüh.
text: take young pig's ears and feet, three or four. place small onions in a clean pot with salt. afterward, bone the meat and grind the onions in a mortar with bread and its own broth, dried. press it through a pepper cloth into another pot, let it stand, and skim off the broth carefully, letting the sediment settle at the bottom. heat the salted broth in a pan, season with salt, spices, and saffron. use it hot over overnight birds, chickens, or cold meat. let it stand in the open air, in summer in the cellar. when you want to serve it, garnish with blanched white almonds.

title: Ein gut Lebersultz.
text: prepare a good, clear broth and strain it, retaining the clear parts. do not salt it yet. then, soften bread in wine with honey. grind the liver finely and rub it separately into a bowl, setting it aside. if you want the jelly to set firmly, simmer pig s feet in the initial broth, along with four small cabbages and two bay leaves. rub white bread through with the broth first the two broths previously made, and now the bread rubbed through. combine them, stir well, add spices and salt. if you wish, color it gently, but only to make it look nice, and season it well before straining. test it, sprinkle it over, and let it stand in the open air.

title: Lungen Küchlin.
text: finely chop veal lungs, spleen, and heart, omitting the gall. prepare small cakes as one makes dumplings, with spices, all well-boiled and dried, and packed with other meat. whatever meat it is, these lung cakes go well with it.

title: Lungen küchlin zweierley.
text: first, make them yourself with eggs well chopped and pounded, also parsley, salt, and spices added. knead with a raw egg and form them into flat cakes thus, they are of yourself. second, chop the heart and spleen, pound in a mortar with hard-boiled eggs, gingerbread, and a little salt. then knead with raw eggs, make cakes from them, and treat them as chicken. lay them in the liver sausage, with the other fish. for the lung cakes, you can chop everything that remains of the chicken heads, necks, and intestines and eat it in a broth, finished with butter and spices, beautifully yellowed.

title: Gebackens von Kelberlungen.
text: make a small pastry using eybert leaves, seasoned and salted. also, make small cakes from it, enclose them in a puff pastry, and bake them well in butter.

title: Knöpfflin von Fleisch.
text: finely chop some parsley, season with salt and pepper, and add a little bacon. beat in two raw eggs, form into small cakes, and simmer them in chicken or your own broth. fry them well and serve. they can be served with liver sausages.

title: Holbrahten von Kalbfleisch.
text: grind finely chopped meat in a mortar, adding egg yolks one by one. add a little flour and season with spices, grinding everything together in the mortar. add salt, mixing well, maintaining the egg's pale color. beat the mixture until it is halved, then shape it into a thick, smoky patty. remove the meat from the mortar, brush the patty with egg white, and press the meat around it, layering it thickly and tightly. compact it well with wet hands, as long as the sausage is. place it in an oven, turning it frequently away from the heat, the longer it bakes, the more it will char. sprinkle it with bacon fat, lard, or butter. if you wish to fill it with bacon or butter, do so while browning. avoid turning it too much, so it will char. cut it into long slices, sprinkle with ground ginger, and prick it with a wooden skewer. glaze with meat broth, add butter, and

title: Pasteten auff Welsche art zu machen.
text: grind wheat finely and make a crust. place it in a well-glazed earthenware dish. add warm butter and knead it well into a dough. add eggs, chicken broth, milk, or wine, seasoning with salt and chopped parsley. add cooked chicken and game birds, as well as meat, pears, or sausages all cooked or boiled. bake the crust over low heat, without smoke, for as long as possible. occasionally brush the earthenware dish with butter to prevent the dough from burning. as the filling bakes, turn the dish frequently to ensure even heat, adding a half spoonful of butter at a time to keep it moist. prick the crust with a small stick all the way to the bottom so that the hot butter reaches the base this will make the filling firm. once the butter has sunk in, remove from the heat. lift the crust out of the dish and set it aside, covered. when you place the dish back on the heat, cover it with a

title: Hirschen Lummelbrahten.
text: grind the sweat and rub gingerbread into it, pressing it through a cloth into a bowl. add a little vinegar. if the sweat doesn't pass through easily, add wine or meat broth. press the gingerbread and sweat through, along with well-washed kidneys and calf's shanks. add diced herbs, let it simmer, and season with salt and black pepper.

title: Ein Rehe Muß.
text: take a piece of shoulder meat from the back, where it is tender, and bone it. wash it in warm wine, then add grated gingerbread, and spread it in a cloth. also, cut the meat into cubes, then pass it through a sieve. when it is nearly drained, season it with good spices, or grate more gingerbread into it, and salt it to taste, and finish with black pepper.

title: Küchlin von Fleisch/ Wildbret/ Hünern oder Vögeln.
text: grind it finely, chop it small, with spices and salt, pound it in a mortar, beat in eggs, not too thin, so that it can be made into cakes, bake it brown. it can be eaten with pepper or otherwise, for cooked dishes.

title: Ein Wachtelbrüh.
text: prepare the quail nicely, ready in a meat broth. grind them in a mortar, rub gingerbread and cheese, and white bread underneath. moisten it with wine and quail broth. heat it in a pan, remove it with spices and salt, and sprinkle ginger on top when serving.

title: Kuglechte Eyer.
text: beat together grated breadcrumbs, mace, and salt. mix well and fill eggshells with this mixture. place a small piece of another eggshell inside an egg white-lined cavity over the opening of the filled eggs. fry in butter, brown, or broil them. these fillings can also be put in crab shells, chop parsley and other good herbs into them, season with spices and salt. serve in a broth or dry.

title: Ein gestrichen Gebackens.
text: make a dough of eggs and fine flour, rub gingerbread into it, bind it with warm honeyed wine, roll out the dough with a rolling pin, cut it into strips, and bake it like that.

title: Gros Eyer.
text: beat the eggs nicely and add spices and salt, cinnamon blossom, and muscat. stir well with a small stick, and cover the top with egg white. you may cook them in butter or hot ashes.

title: Ein höflich Essen von Eyern.
text: make a pleasant dough of eggs and flour, colored with cornflowers, as follows, and with herbs, give each a special color. beat the dough with a wooden roller, and bake it thinly on both sides. the dough that comes out, make into patties, like fritters. chop game, birds, chickens, or whatever cooked meat you have, boiled or stewed. mix it with a raw egg, seasoned, salted, and peppered. spread this meat on the patties, which have been cut into strips. spread the meat as thinly as the patties are thick. place another patty on top, salt around and around, like flatbreads. bake them in a pan. you can bake these fritters in two or three different ways. sprinkle sugar on top. make scrambled eggs with seasoning and salt, and a little saffron, and enclose them in the patties, whether colored or uncolored, and bake them. alternatively, boil eggs hard, chop them finely, add parsley and seasoning

title: Geschachtzabels backen mit fünff farben.
text: roll out a sheet of baked puff pastry, brushed with a little saffron. place the pastry on a dish or two, squeezing parsley juice through a cloth. temper it well, so it turns green. make a delicate dough, cut it into sheets, and do not bake them too brown. if you want them brown, squeeze cornflower juice into them, ground well with water in a mortar. the first squeezing will be a dark blue, the second paler, the third even paler. thus are all the colors of flowers, including roses, which have no more than their flavor dry them and temper them. you may also take many other flavorful herbs and flowers, ground and squeezed through a cloth, and keep them in a small glass, covered, until you need them. bake apples brown in butter, seasoning them delicately. spread them on the first yellow sheet, not too thickly, and place the green sheet on top. next, make a yellow filling with seasoned egg yolks, and place

title: Ein angestrichen gebackens.
text: make a strong dough of grated cheese flour and milk. roll it thinly on a board, cut it into strips like little fingers, bake them in butter, and arrange them in a shallow dish for fastenzeit.

title: Ein ander Form.
text: cut the dough into diamond shapes, clover leaves, or roses, and bake them. if you want to brown them, let them be quite cold.

title:
Mit demselbigen Teig ein höfliches Essen in ein schwartzes
Pfefferlin.
text: make patties from hard-boiled eggs, fried apples, or pears. chop them together, add a little saffron in wine or milk, and mix well, ensuring it thickens. form flat cakes from the dough, place the chopped mixture on top, fold over, and shape into balls as desired. bake them in butter, serve hot or cold with pepper, and sprinkle with a little ginger. alternatively, use the whites of hard-boiled eggs, cut into cubes, and sprinkle them on top, finishing with a little butter. with the same dough, you can also make filled eggs or filled crab in broth, wine soup, or pepper.

title: Ein frembd Gebackens/ heist Schnabel.
text: make white bread, slice off the bark, cut thinly. place on a board, cut the bark into plates, cut apples into halves and quarters, then toast them. chop, salt, and season them with whatever spices you have pepper or ginger. mix in saffron, chopped finely. beat well-whipped eggs into the mixture and combine thoroughly. spread the filling on a slice of bread, covering it with another slice so the top layer nearly reaches the bottom. seal it with egg white so it stays together. bake until golden brown. if you want such slices with many colors, draw the bread through a juice beforehand, as taught. but without color, you can serve it in wine soup or pepper, or in goulash, liver jelly, or cheese broth, as you wish. good apples or pears baked in butter, white bread stirred in, hard-boiled eggs chopped in, with wine and milk to make a dough, and then made into small cakes.

title: Braun Küchlin die vergüldt scheinen.
text: beat the beaten gold well on a stone, with water or burnt wine. rub it again with a raw egg yolk, form into small balls. sugar, rose, violet, or muscat, finely ground like a fingertip. shape them into rounds with wet hands, coat the small cakes with gold leaf, attach them to a knife so you may spread them everywhere. place them one after another on a board, bake them one by one in melted butter, do not stir them apart. lift them out with a skimmer and let them dry for serving.

title: Gute Streublin.
text: grind a handful of parsley with water and stale white bread crumbs. force it through a cloth, then make a small dough with egg and flour do not salt it. spread the resulting mixture thinly into a pan.

title: Gute Krapffen von Opffeln vnd Biern.
text: beat them before with egg strike one or two eggs into them salt and seasoning grind well in a mortar fill into the fritters. make other fritters from eggs parsley or other good herbs chopped into them kneaded with a raw egg seasoned salted and filled.

title: Lappen Küchlin.
text: make a strong dough with eggs and one-third milk. knead it on a board with a rolling pin and wheat flour, shaping it as you desire. if you want it brown, bake it well or if you want it yellow, mix the dough with saffron, ground in wine or milk. green with parsley juice, or the like. blue with cornflowers. some make it with salsify. with this dough, make filled fritters with apples, pears, calf s brains, or the game of small forest birds, seasoned and lightly salted. you can fill fritters with the filling as you would stuff eggs, apples, and chicken. however, every meat or fish filling must be properly and well boiled, then ground well in a mortar, with parsley or other flavorful herbs, tempered with raw eggs for taste, thoroughly mixed together, filled, and well baked.

title: Ein Krapffenteig.
text: make honeyed wine as much as you like, and take a wide bowl. mix the wine with white flour, as fine as muslin, and beat egg yolks in another bowl, and a little saffron, grinding them very well with the honeyed wine. add this to the mixed dough, temper it, and sprinkle in a little flour at a time into the bowl until a light dough is formed. then roll it out with a rolling pin on a cloth, cut it large or small, depending on how you want the fritters. dough made with yeast, beer, or hops must be left to rise, then kneaded in warm water or a boiled honeyed wine. small fritters for gentlemen should be filled only with fish livers, finely ground with a little grated gingerbread, so they have enough spice. also, bird livers and chicken livers, finely chopped and ground, with an egg yolk and grated gingerbread added, and use this as filling. all the fish innards ground with an egg yolk

title: Krapffen backen von vberbliebenen Hünern.
