text: combine wild game, either roasted or boiled, finely chopped, with beaten eggs in a bowl. add chopped parsley and season with spices and salt. mix well, ensuring it's not too thin. stir in grated cooked honey, wine, and gingerbread until well combined and easily moldable. the fritters cook quickly check for doneness by their brown color when you remove them. sprinkle all fritters with sugar.

title: Ein gut Gebackens von Eyern.
text: break eggs as much as you like, beat them well, and chop them white. crumble bread under them, grate muscat over it, don't salt it, make large or small wafers with a rolling pin, not too thin, and bake them.

title: Ein ander Gebackens.
text: to make a fine sauce, or spiced dough, like one makes salsas, white bread, or grated gingerbread, mix it well. strain it through a cloth with good wine, add tempered eggs and flour, and make a strong dough. use a spoon to spread it into butter molds or small pastries, like hazelnut shapes, and bake them.

title: Gute Turten zu machen.
text: make a strong dough with milk and eggs, roll it out thinly with a rolling pin. mix it in a pan so that it hangs around and over the pan, about a small finger's width. make a dough crust for a tart in an earthenware pan. for the filling, make a mixture of eggs, butter, and spices, beating it well together. put it into the tart crusts, top with a sheet of dough, and seal it like a flatbread, using the remaining dough to hang over the pan. grease with butter so the pan doesn't burn, rub it often. let the tart bake. a wide, moist pan is needed. in such a filling, you can add shelled crabs, firm fish like pike, perch, etc. soft fish should not be added they must be pre-boiled and seasoned. when the tart is browned, it is done. remove it from the coals, and set it on a plate.

title: Fleisch Turten.
text: make the dough as previously described, or as a simple dough. do not make the filling too strong use eggs and wine, milk, or chicken broth, or good meat broth, but not too much. beat the eggs and butter in, along with salt and spices. place the dough-lined pan in a pan with butter, as before. add the filling, and any meat you have for the filling. cover with a layer of dough, crimp the edges, and brush with butter. bake as you would a pie, as previously taught and described.

title: Gebackens von Erbsen.
text: beat the eggs and yolks well, add wine, temper with hot water, a little flour, stir and let it cool, so it thickens. cut pieces from it and press them through a yellow cloth, seasoned with spices. dip the pieces in it, lift them out with a spoon, bake them, and sprinkle with sweetened wine. serve in this way.

title: Ein gut Gebackens von Reiß.
text: boil the dough quickly in water, then gently strain it. let it dry in the sun or in a room. grind in a mortar, then sprinkle into a pan. add eggs, but don't make it too thin. set butter over the fire and let it sit. pour the dough onto this, and bake small cakes.

title: Ein gut Essen von öpffeln.
text: peel the apples nicely and divide them into two halves. hollow out each half, and make a filling of cooked apples, hard breadcrumbs, and finely chopped parsley, with one raw egg well tempered. fill both halves of the apples and place them on top of each other. insert a stick through them, not too soft, until they are baked. if you wish to brown them, prick them three or four times with a skewer, place them on a gridiron, baste them with butter, and turn them until browned. sprinkle them with boiled honey wine.

title: Ein anders.
text: cut apples round in two halves, fill both halves with used apples or quinces, or beer. grate white bread with sugar underneath you may season them or not. fill the apple halves with this. make a dough of honey and wine, boiled. brush the apples with it, cover them, and bake in butter. remove the topping or thread, and sprinkle sugar or honey on top.

title: Gefüllte Brahtbiern an einem Spis zu brahten.
text: peel and chop the apples, remove the cores. roast them in butter, chop finely, and add honey and spices. season with salt and saffron. don't add too much beer, fill the two halves with the mixture, cover, and bake as previously instructed. sprinkle with spices and serve warm.

title: Gebackens von Salbey.
text: grind soft rye bread into a mortar. toast it in honey and wine until moist, add spices, salt, and spread with sage leaves. cover with another leaf and press firmly together so they adhere well. make a paste with honey and wine, coat it thoroughly, and bake. sprinkle with sugar and serve warm.

title: Ein ander gefüllt Gebackens von Salbey.
text: make a filling of used apples, as previously learned, with yellow and salt. spread a layer of salt on a pastry sheet and cover it with the filling, then press another sheet on top. make a dough as before, and draw one layer through the other, lifting them carefully into the frying pan.

title: Gebackens von Regelsbiern.
text: shell the beers nicely, discard the cores, and make a green filling of eggs and parsley, saltwort, or other flavorful herbs. strip off the stems and stalks, chop only the leaves finely, beat in raw eggs, and stir in a little stale breadcrumbs. season with spices, and mix everything together very well. make a dough with sweetened boiled wine, not too thick, nor too thin, and work it well with a rolling pin. make cakes or fritters with this, and bake them well. during lent, you can add figs and raisins nicely underneath. if you don't use the green herbs, mix raw eggs with apples and spices, saffron, and salt, prepared in this way so that they blend well into pastries or fritters. if you don't have apples or beer, take good grated cheese, yellowed with a little flour, and knead well together with salt and spices, if you wish. into this baked good, you can add dried hazelnuts

title: Morchen mit Eyern füllen.
text: make the filling as one makes apple filling, or stewed. eggs, and the two parsnips laid one over the other, both parts filled and fastened with a raw egg on a spit, sprinkle it with butter, and roast it nicely on a rack.

title: Milchküchlin für Krancke vnd Kindbetterin.
text: make a thin pancake batter with milk, stirring it well. you may enhance it with saffron. beat some milk with eggs in one bowl and water in another, making it thick. sweeten the milk with spice from the apothecary. make a thin pancake batter, either with eggs, or with a honey-water and a little salt, and incorporate the milk as well. bake in small cakes or fritters until browned, and sprinkle with a little sugar. you may also serve it with almond milk.

title: Ein Kuch in einem Mörser.
text: eggs, sausage, white bread, cut into cubes, seasoned. mix well together, chop parsley and add. put it in a pan with a little butter, set it over coals, the longer the better, and add butter. eggs, freshly laid, beaten into warm milk, and drunk warm, will dispel coughs and all ailments.

title: Gut grün Salsen von Kreutern.
text: prepare the horse-radish, angelica, lovage, and marsh marigold, stripping the stems. then, soften white bread, vinegar, or wine, and grate gingerbread. grind everything well with the herbs, and season with vinegar and wine. soak the bread in a cloth, remove it, and season with spices. keep it in a glass jar with a lid. some sauces are made with crab apples, and to those add borage, parsley, mint, and burnet, but use more crab apple than herbs. the unripe grape is called crab apple, and it has a very pleasant sourness grind it with wine, vinegar, and grated gingerbread, and white bread. some sauces are made with meadowsweet, garden horse-radish, and sour wine apples, with bread soaked, ground together with vinegar, and rubbed through a glass sieve. if you wish to boil or bake the wine apples, they will be clearer that way test them well and cover them

title: Weichsel oder Amerellen Salsen.
text: grind them in a mortar with caraway and everything, rub gingerbread underneath, press them through a cloth with good wine, pour it into a glazed jar. grind lovage and all sorts of strong spices, and add a little salt to it. heat it over the fire, then pour it into a moist bowl and let it stand well. make little cakes or tarts from it. whoever prefers wine, salt, or herbs, take some chopped parsley, celery, or salad burnet, chop it well, and eat it. what herbs are taken from the meadow, such as salad burnet, parsley, balm, meylander, celery, and the like, grind and powder them well in an oven. you can keep them this way throughout the year and use them for any meal. garlic salt requires a little bread crumbs soaked in vinegar and ground with lean meat broth, seasoned with salt and a little vinegar, keep it in a gutter. if you want it yellow,

title: Gute Salsen von Eschlauch.
text: soft bread in wine, press the bladder in the same bread and wine, salt, and push it through finish it with ginger. this sauce is good for beef broth or game broth. sage sauce pound sage with wine and bread. radish sauce pound radishes with vinegar and bread. boile sauce pound boile with wine and bread mixed in finish it at the table like other sauces. orange sauce press oranges from them, add well-flavored sour wine, then add cinnamon blossoms. it is a princely sauce, and cannot be kept, as the oranges must always be freshly pressed. this sauce is good for all birds, chickens, and game. mustard warms the stomach and liver, struggles with the spleen, brings thirst and uncertainty. mustard is dried and hot at the fourth degree. afterwards, it requires good tempering, as it helps a sluggish stomach and can harm good eyesight from excessive consumption.

title: Senff zu machen.
text: grind the mustard well. then put it in a pan over a fire, stir it with a little salt, keep it warm, and add more of the spices that were boiled with it, working it well. if you want to serve it, make a good honey wine and temper the mustard with it, salt it, and spice it. taste it, and it will be good.

title: Ein ander behende weiß.
text: to temper honey, mix it well with vinegar, wine, or meat broth, and stir in the mustard. rose hips and figs boiled with wine or water, to temper the mustard, or rosewater, and finely ground cinnamon bark, are suitable for refined palates. a very potent cough lozenge, considered the best of all lung ailments lozenges, is made from fox lungs. it alleviates rising of the lungs, coughing, and difficult breathing, and similar ailments of the chest and lungs. wash the fox lungs with white wine, making them clean and very fresh. cut the small veins full of blood. put them in a new dish in a baking oven, then place them with wormwood leaves so they are safe from worms. when you need them, you must take them in the morning, on an empty stomach, crushed in unsalted pea broth, and then fast for an hour or three. and every evening, take half a pound of the lozenge

title: Quitten Latwergen.
text: grind or pound them well in a mortar and rub them. work the gingerbread through with good wine, season it, and add it to the szalau of the weichsel, as written above, unless more gingerbread is needed.

title: Gute Latwergen von Leutsbiern/ vnd andern guten Wein.
text: make a dough in a harbor, then work it well with a spoon. place it in a small kettle on a tripod over a small fire. let it heat up, stir it, then add honey and spice. stir it again, nutmeg, ginger, and mace, roughly ground. stir it again, and extinguish the fire until the spices are well heated, then pour it down. spread it out on a wide plate or board, treat it like a pancake batter. let it cool completely, then cut small pieces from it and set them aside.

title: Ein gut Latwergen zum Magen/ vnd für alle böse Nebel.
text: slice the angelica root thinly, or bite it. cover it and let it steep in red wine for eight to ten days in a glass. melt a measure of honey in a pan add the angelica to it. then, pound well four lots of ginger, one lot of nutmeg, one lot of mace, two lots of cinnamon sticks, and half a lot of long pepper. let it simmer for a good while until it becomes very thick, a kind of conserve. stir it constantly so it doesn't burn.

title: Zu der Brust ein Latwerge.
text: grate white radish, horseradish, asphodel, dittany, and ginger together. grind into a powder, then sweeten with honey to create a lozenge. if you desire a stronger flavor, add cubebs, cinnamon stick, and muscat flower, or other fine spices. you may also use gentian, venice lemons, long pepper, calamus, wormwood, and stonecrop, tempering them individually as described to form a lozenge.

title: Von Kappeskraut.
text: to quickly make a flavorful cold sauerkraut in autumn, use raw cabbage heads. take a clean barrel a large tub or container and sprinkle wood shavings inside. pour in good red wine to the level of the shavings, but not too much. then take the cabbage, thoroughly cleaned, and quarter it down to the core, being careful to keep it whole. place a layer of shredded cabbage on top to hold it down, and gently press the head of cabbage onto the shavings, ensuring it s level. set it on a tripod stand, build a moderate fire underneath, and let it stand as long as cabbage usually needs to simmer. afterward, remove it and let it cool. in a small pan, heat the red wine from the barrel, add caraway seeds, rowan berries, and juniper berries, pour it over the cabbage, distributing it evenly around, let it settle, then chop it finely. add vinegar or mustard to taste, and serve. some people also take the tougher outer

title: II. Propositio.
text: to make a fine custard, take good milk, and boil it gently. then add sugar and yolks of eggs, stirring constantly until it thickens. strain it through a cloth, and let it cool.

title: IV. Peroratio.
text: my dearest listeners, for a long time i hesitated, wondering whether i should maintain my former custom of urging you with a lengthy speech on this anniversary of renewing our studies, and of reminding you of your duties or whether i should completely pass those matters by, or address them with little or no preface, regarding those things about which i had resolved to explain throughout the year. for the labor of commenting on, composing, correcting, and committing to memory a speech a task light for others, but very weighty for me and also the expenditure of time that would be necessary for these matters, occupied my mind and spirit indeed, i was strongly deterred from this kind of speaking. but when i recalled how my speeches have sometimes aided you, both in forming good character and in making progress in learning, my hope of your benefit invited me more strongly to speak. therefore, in this silent deliberation of my mind, my labor was overcome by your benefit, hope overcame fear, and to say briefly,

title: C) De disputatione
text: if the time allotted for speaking should fail me, i will certainly speak about the practice of debating. this single thing, if i can persuade you through speaking what i wish, will bring you benefits in a single hour that diligent study, both public and private, would achieve over a long period. therefore, i will first explain how useful it is to debate theology, then about what topics theologians ought to debate, and finally, in what way each argument should be made. i ask you all who are present, again and again, as the best of listeners, that you believe the things i am about to say are spoken with the intention of teaching you, not as if i wished to give the rules and laws of debate to those who argue in academies and other places, from whom i myself can and ought to learn, and indeed greatly desire to. i am not so bold as to reproach the most learned theologians, nor so arrogant as to think that i can teach others besides you, my listeners

title: I cibi, che hanno, & che vsano.
text: they sow a grain that resembles millet, some white, others red, and others black, and reddish. it grows into a stalk as tall as a half-lance, and produces two or three ears, where the grain is like panic grass. the way they make bread is to place a large pot over the fire, which holds four or five cantara of water, and light a fire beneath it until the water boils. then they remove the fire and throw in the grain, which they call tayul, and sprinkle a little lime on top to loosen the skin that covers it. the next day, or within three or four hot days, when it has cooled, they wash it very well in the river or at home with plenty of water, so that it is very clean of the lime, and then they grind it with certain stones made for that purpose. as they grind it, they add water, and it forms a dough. thus, by grinding and kneading it, they make the bread

text: here's the translation of the recipe into modern english endive salad with oil and vinegar, and salt. 2. finely chopped white endive salad. 3. white cabbage lettuce. 4. white cabbage lettuce soaked in water, then drained, dressed with vinegar, oil, and salt, and sprinkled with finely ground sugar. a little broth poured over is also good. 5. green cabbage lettuce, partially raw and partially soaked, is good in both ways, whether sweet or sour. 6. green field salad dressed with oil and sprinkled with poppy seeds, is nice and decorative. 7. young, tender green salad with finely chopped red beet, tossed over when the salad is dressed, and the red beet cooked and chilled. 8. a head of white lettuce, finely chopped, partly soaked in boiled water and partly raw. add capers to the soaked portion. 9. spring cress salad, which grows in a garden or thrives near flowing streams

Speiß vnd Trachten zu machen.
text: i. roast it well-browned with a poppet or dried, or leave it cold, for it is a good dish when cold. 2. pastries, cold or warm. 3. peel the indian hen, flesh and skin, each piece separately and when it is peeled, set it to, and let it simmer over the fire. lay it on a spit, brown it, and make a broth for it let it be sour or sweet, it is good in both ways. 4. you can also preserve such peeled flesh with parsley root, good nutmeg, and beef broth, also with green, well-tasting herbs. you may make it yellow, or leave it white, so it is good in both ways. 5. you can also preserve such peeled flesh and skin in a pepper. 6. or you can preserve it green with parsley, which is well-

title: Wie man guten Essig machen sol.
text: to make vinegar, you should use seven, eight, or nine, even more, loads, which comes from the art of philosophy. you should also take an oak barrel, or another vessel, of about half a tun size, and put in a quarter of good vinegar. seal the barrel in the summer and place it on a path where people walk the most, so that they can trample it back and forth with their feet. this should be done for seven weeks. afterward, unseal it and place it in a dry place in the loft, so that it doesn't get rain on it. then, whatever you want to fill it with, whether wine or beer, it should foam when boiled. afterward, pour it in as much as you judge is needed so that the vinegar is still sour enough to work on the material that has been poured in. if you pour too much in, it will spoil let it work like this, and it will remain good. it is

title: Ein ander Kunst/ wie man guten Essig sol machen.
text: press unripe grapes and strain them well, then add other vinegar. after three days, strain it from the dregs repeatedly, and you will have good vinegar at all times.

title: Wie man Essig auß Bier sol machen.
text: to make a sour wort, take beer and seut, and if it gets cold, add sour dough and roasted or burnt peas, and a good vinegar. also, throw into the vats as needed, 13 grains of wheat and crusts of rye bread, and a little myrrh, made from beer vinegar. take 4 measures of water and a quarter of a measure of honey, and 1 measure of wine, and boil it well, and put it into a small barrel, and it will soon become sour.

title: Ein ander Kunst Essig zu machen.
text: take a large walnut root and put it in the wine, and you will get very good vinegar from it. boil the wine in a copper or pewter dish, and skim it before it settles, and you will get very good vinegar from it. take barley, roast it in a pan until it turns black, and put it in wine you will have good vinegar in two days. or take a crust of stale rye bread, toasted in a pewter pan, and do not let it become completely cooked, and put it in a jug with wine you will have good vinegar in three or four days.

title: Essig zu machen/ daß einer jn bey sich kan tragen.
text: to prepare horseradish root, place it in good vinegar for nine or ten days. after you have taken it out, dry it in the sun. when it is well dried, place it again in good vinegar for seven days. then drain it, and grind it into a powder. put a little into a glass full of wine, and you will have good vinegar. if you put powdered dried horseradish root into vinegar, it will quickly become sharp.

title: Ein ander Kunst guten Essig zu machen.
text: first, prepare a dry barrel and let it bind well. then, take half a measure of good burnt wine and pour it into the barrel. seal the barrel and stir it well back and forth until the burnt wine has gone in. let it sit in the sun for one or two days. then pour in a measure of vinegar that has also been sitting for one or two days. next, take the vinegar that has settled, boil it in a copper pot, skim off the foam, and pour it into the barrel while still warm. take a quarter of a pound of parsnip and crush the root. tie it to a string and hang it halfway into the barrel. drill a hole about the size of a thumb in the bottom of the front of the barrel, and leave this hole open, as well as the bung hole at the top, covered only with a wooden tile, so that the vinegar has air. do not be fooled if you see small gnats sitting at the

title: Guten Essig zu machen.
text: take sour wine and bake it in an oven, and place it in warm wine, and you will have good vinegar for all things.

title: Essig starck zu machen.
text: to make sour hen or capon, take it in vinegar. it will become strong, and place it behind the oven, or near the warmth, wherever you wish.

title: Roten Essig zu machen.
text: let the vinegar stand for a night or three over rose petals or meadow flowers. strain off the vinegar it will be beautifully red. you may make a flavorful vinegar with cornflowers, lavender, rosemary, and the like.

title:
Vom Hasen Wildpret seind zwentzigerley
Speiß vnd Trachten zu machen.
text: rabbit recipes 1. rabbit stew with brains how to make it from calf s brains. 2. whole, peeled parts of the rabbit, darkened with onions. take b the peeled parts cut them into pieces. take b water and vinegar, wash out the sweat strain it again onto it. cut onions and apples into it and a little bread let it simmer together drain it off and strain the sweat through a hair cloth, so that it becomes fairly thick sweat onions in lard season with pepper and cloves put them into the sweat and let it simmer clean the rabbit put it into the sweat and let it simmer until cooked make it finely seasoned and not sweet for rabbits are not very good when they are sweet you can put an apple or almond glaze over it or sprinkle with verjuice. if you want to cook a rabbit in another way

title:
Von einem Ku:eniglein seind eilfferley Speiß
vnd Trachten zu machen. [Abb]
text: roast pheasant, whether cold or warm, is good in either way. prepared in its own juices, or in black stock, whether sweet or sour, as hares are prepared in pepper and juices. prepared in its own broth with parsley. quail in pies, whether cold or warm. prepared in a yellow sauce, whether of almonds or apples, chopped with onions and sweated, made with butter, yellow and finely sour, with small black currants and good beef broth that does not salt, take some burnt flour and let it simmer. and when the quail is roasted, cut it into the sauce, let it simmer with it, and it will be tasty and good. and such quail can be roasted and cut into apples, or into an almond sauce, and cooked with it. or prepared with onions, finely sweet, it is good and tasty. smoked or salted quail, cold or warm, is good in either way, also to cook it with green herbs

title: Von einem Caninichen. [Abb]
text: from a dog's carcass, you can make all dishes that you would prepare for a king, for they are not very different.

title: Von einem Eichhorn. [Abb]
text: take an entire squirrel for roasting or making into a pie. enclose it in pastry and let it cool it will be good and flavorful.

title: Von allerley Turten.
text: i. finely chop figs mix with small black rose petals that have been thoroughly washed place in a tart shell. add a little butter and bake either in an oven or in a tart pan. and if you wish to make a tart take egg yolks and butter mix them into the flour and make a dough from it roll it out thinly and cut it into fine rounds and salt it. and such a dough can be used for all sorts of tarts. 2. remove the kernels from cherries when making cherry tarts. 3. overripe hungarian plums are also a good filling with pounded cinnamon underneath you may serve them cold or warm either way is good. 4. take hungarian plums green or dried remove the kernels they are good for preserving. 5. take black wineberries crush them and add a few egg yolks underneath and a little sugar stir them with it and it is a

title: Aber Pasteten vom taig.
text: make a dough of wheat flour, beat it into a pastry. add two eggs to it, some people use the yolks, which is good that makes it lighter. add water to it. fry it in lard, and add salt to the flour as well. make a good, firm dough that can be formed into a single mass. it shouldn't be too hard, but not crumbly either. press it together with your hands, like a spot, but leave a hole in the middle. then take a strong rolling pin, and roll it outwards and outwards, about half a finger thick. then press the top with the right hand, with your fist, spreading it outwards. with your left hand, lift the outer dough away from the center. don't make the base too thin. roll it out properly it will become shaped like a small hoop that you set on the base. place the cutlets inside, as many as you like. make a lid of the pastry dough

title: Von Pirn mach in aller maß/ wie oben steht.
text: then it must be cooked for as long as necessary, and the shank should be seasoned with spices. it is important to note that the pastry for the pies, into which one must place the meat or other fillings, should not be made too light, as it must be strengthened afterward. only a strong person can do this if it needs to be strong, you can also use a rich broth for the water and fat beef or mutton, if available so that it holds together and is strong.

title: Torten von Kütten vnd Birn.
text: to begin, you must nicely peel the chickens and cut them into quarters. take a dough as described previously for the pastry, and spread it out, folding it around the edges. raise it to the height of two fingers, ensuring it doesn't collapse. place the split chickens inside, and from the dough make a layer as thick as a wide mouth, and place it above. add spices and plenty of sugar you may also add candied citron. the dough for the tarts should not be as firm as for the pastry, but use the same technique. then, with the pears, split them and pour a syrup over them first, and place them in the tarts, with sugar and mild spices. serve hot, and sprinkle finely chopped comfits on top, then cover with a crust. do not bake the crust as long as the chickens.

title: Torten von Weichseln vnd Amerellen.
text: grind the almonds and sugar finely. put the mixture into the pastry shells, and cover with a lid. pour warm cream over the top.

title: Schwartz Torten.
text: roast pears, one or ten, and brown them, and season. simmer them in a dark, cooked wine, then strain through a sieve. take the yolks of fifteen eggs, and a pound of ground almonds, strained through a sieve. take milk as much as the yolks weigh. take half a pound of comfits, mace, nutmeg, and a small bunch of muscatel. mix all together, then take a pan with some lard, pastry dough, give it heat, sometimes less, sometimes more, cover the top and bottom with a hot, moist cloth.

title: Torten von o:epffeln.
text: take apples, chop them small, and press the juice out of them. add a good quantity of ginger and much sugar. spread this on a well-kneaded dough, as for the previous tarts. beat it finely, as one makes a flatbread, and lay a thin sheet of pastry on top, cut into strips, criss-cross. bake for a while, not too long, and let it cool. add pieces of cinnamon.

title: Reindel von o:epffeln.
text: first, take apples, slice them into a bowl, and add a little sweet wine. strain it through a sieve, then beat it. add as much sugar as you like. melt some lard in a pan, fry the apples in it, and add coal underneath and on top until they are cooked through. serve dry or in a small dish.

title: Schwartz koch von o:epffeln vnd Birn zumachen.
text: slice the apples very thinly. fry them in hot rendered fat until quite brown, and chop them very finely. put them into a deep dish or pan, add sweet wine, and honest sugar. simmer for a while, then sprinkle with gentle spices. bake anise seeds in sugar on top of that. you can prepare pears in the same way.

title: Gefu:ellt o:epffel zumachen.
text: to make a good apple dumpling take apples, not too large, that are not quite sour, peels, not cut, at the bottom a little leaf, hollow. take out the core of the apple, but let the peel remain around it. take honestly ground almonds, pound, put into chopped apples, then wine from berlin, cinnamon, stem, a sugar, and beat in an egg. fill the apples with this mixture, put the leaf on top. make small skewers, stick them in so that the leaf remains on the filling. take then some lard in a wide pan, let it get hot, put in a lid also with some embers on top. so it bakes nicely. as it begins to soften, and immediately add primroses, take it out onto a dish. if you like, make a little sweet syrup and put it on top, then put sugar on it last it is a good meal.

title:
Pirn magst gleich also machen/ sihe das
sie nicht steinig werden.
text: then, you must cook apples and pears until they are not raw, but browned in the fat, as mentioned above.

title: Dinst Pirn mach also:
text: peel the pears, leave the stems on, and bake them in hot rendered fat until they are deeply browned. then place them in a pot. add a little sweet wine, a bit of vinegar, and a few cloves. let it simmer until finely reduced. add some sugar, and a cooked must is almost as good for it. it yields a thick, sweet dish.

title: Oepffel gescherb zumachen.
text: peel apples and roast them in fat until they are honestly cooked. then add a sweet wine. take a little bit of wild boar or unseasoned meat, slice it, and put in wineberries.

title: Ein eingehackts.
text: to make a chopped dish, chop the apples and roots. and proceed as above. you can also make it with quince in the same way, taking apples and quince together. serve it over wilted greens, or wherever you like you may have it as you wish.

title: Bachen Kütten zumachen.
text: cut the chicken into thin slices. remove the core and stones. place in warm fat, not hot, and let it stand on a warm spot for an hour, until softened. then take a thin dough made with wine and sugar, press it through, and bake in the fat until the dough turns yellow.

title: Oepffel zubachen.
text: to make a kind of pastry, some use a dough made with beer, others with wine. mix it with yeast in flour, and bake in hot fat they will be light. also, if you make tarts from the black cooked, you must roll out a pastry crust, spread the black on it, and bake it like any other tart, filling it with citron or red cherries they will be very good.

title: Ein fast gu:ots mu:oß/ das schwartz ist.
text: cut apples into wedges and add a portion of red currants or sloes, also a good portion of soft breadcrumbs, and sprinkle with wine. let it simmer well until it becomes finely soft, then strain it through a sieve or cloth. add sugar and good spices, let it reduce in a pan, serve cold or warm.

title: Von Ayrtorten zumachen.
text: to make white cakes, take a quarter of a pound of butter, beat it with a little salt, and add as much milk as the butter was. grind half a pound of almonds, either crushed or ground, and strain them through a sieve. then mix all together. add half a pound of sugar and mix well. put it into a pan with a small amount of clarified butter, ensuring the butter is very thin. bake it from underneath and above with a hot lid that is very hot.

title: Torten von Reiß.
text: beat the rice and pass it through a sieve, as much as almonds. take also egg whites and sugar as above, and it will be white like white tortes.

title: Zumachen die obgeschribnen Torten.
text: first, as mentioned above, take fine sugar when it is boiled. then take ambergris, almond essence, strained through a sieve, mixed with sugar, and fine sugar with rosewater, and subtly glaze the tarts with it. heat the iron lid and place it over the tarts, creating a crust like marzipan. for good tarts, take a little bit of bergamot, a little bit of coral, a little bit of amber, and place them in the prepared tarts they will be wonderfully good.

title: Torten von gruenem kraut.
text: first, take bird s tongue, which must be well dried. take some good parsley, bertram, marjoram, and a little borage, finely chopped. press the juice from the chopped herbs, until the herbs are quite dry. then take the bird s tongue and put it in a mortar. grind well, and beat it against the bird s tongue. add a little sweet wine, a little grated semolina, and sugar. add the chopped herbs to it. mix everything together and press down firmly.

title: Gemueß Pasteten/ Dotter muoß.
text: first, take half a measure of wine and four slices of a fine, baked loaf of bread. submerge them in the wine. let it stand as long as it takes to walk across the room. stir it all together and let it cool slightly. then, take forty egg yolks, stir them together with everything. add a little saffron, two handfuls of white sugar, and a piece of fresh butter the size of an egg yolk. place it over a gentle heat that won't burn. stir with a spoon, and when it's thick enough, pour it into a bowl. let it cool, and add a few raisins. stir it together, let it set, and you can serve it warm in a bowl.

title: Torten von Ayer gemueß.
text: to make a tart take good, skimmed milk. then, with either lard or butter, set over a fire. in a pan, and when it begins to simmer, take fourteen egg yolks and a spoonful of breadcrumbs, stirring them into the mixture. add a whole grated loaf of bread. when the milk begins to simmer, set it over a gentle heat, stirring the egg mixture into it. let it simmer a little until it is sufficiently thick. take a handful of sugar and wineberries, place them in a pastry crust, and on a tart. bake for half an hour.

title: Ayer Kuechlein.
text: make a dough with two pounds of flour, a little grated semolina, and a measure of semolina flour. add a generous amount of fresh, rendered lard, about a large cupful, seasoned with salt. add a handful of water, enough to make the dough slightly thicker than strudel dough. the oven must be almost completely hot, and previously cleaned. then, grease the baking pans in which the cookies will be baked, and place them on the bare hearth of the oven. bake for about fifteen minutes. when you take them out of the oven, cut them apart along their width, and brush them with fresh lard or butter, then drizzle with a little sugar on top and inside. serve hot on a table.

title: Mehr ein Torten.
text: to make a good milk dish take milk, as much as half a measure, and beat four or five eggs underneath it. take parsley, and also the green tops of four or five small cabbage heads. chop these and stir them in one at a time, alternately. take a bowl, crumble bread or crumbs into it, into the milk, so that it appears green, and according to the cabbage s taste it must be as thick as armful. sweeten it well, and do not salt it too much, nor make it too sweet. make the dough like a herb tart, let it rest half-baked, cut it when it s baked, stir in a little fresh lard underneath, and sugar on top serve it hot.

title: Gebratne milch zumachen.
text: first, take saffron and put it in a small bowl. then, place it in simmering water in a kettle, ensuring the water doesn't spill over. let it simmer until thickened, then stir in salt. sweeten it with honey until it resembles a cheese. then, make it smooth like a udder. skewer it and roast it on a spit. season with spices and baste with melted fat. serve.

title: Heydnische Kuochen zumachen.
text: make a dough of flour as best you can. roll it out thinly into sheets like a pancake. fry in fat, then take good wine, half souil honey, and mix them together. moisten the pancakes with this mixture when you want to serve them.

title: Torten von gruenem Kraut.
text: to make a savory tart, take some sauerkraut, bertram's, and whatever else you think is good, chop it very finely, and roast it in lard. grate a mild loaf of bread underneath, one that isn't too strong, and sprinkle yeast on the cabbage and a raisin. add crumbs that's just the husks. then take an egg or two, depending on how large you want it to be, and beat them well. take the pan and put a little lard in it, so that the pan is completely coated with lard. melt the lard until it s smooth, and then pour the beaten egg into the pan, letting it run around and around so the pan is completely covered with the egg. then add the prepared filling to the pan and place it on a rack. put a small amount of embers underneath, and cover with a lid. bake it gently it will come out of the pan easily if you don

title: Ein Torten von Vogelspeiß.
text: make a bird pie to look quite dry. then take and pound well in a mortar five or four eggs, add a quarter pound of melted lard underneath. add wineberries and honest sugar underneath. also grease the pan with a beaten egg, as stated above, and bake it like any other, quite cool. then place it on a plate, put some preserve on top, and you may well garnish with cinnamon sticks. serve warm on the table.

title: Pasteten von Ayren.
text: make a high pastry dough as instructed. bake it in an oven, only until it is firm, not pale. then, spread about six ounces on a table and crush it. mix in as much spice as there are ounces, then take one loaf of good bread, plenty of sugar, and candied citron. place this mixture over the baked pastry, cover again and bake until it rises nicely. it will become a beautiful rugel. do not bake it too long, serve it warm. it is a lovely dish place it on a plate and sprinkle sugar over it.

title: Ein Ayrmuoß (?) zumachen.
text: first, take the clear cream from the feet of the cows or sheep, clean it. then, take a sweet milk jug, place it in a beautiful pan. let it simmer, and skim the cream from the surface, do not let it simmer too long. this will become a sweet. add honest sugar to it, and serve it warm. if you let it cool on a thin bowl, and pour it over, you have sweetened milk, which is often enjoyed at weddings or other celebrations.

title: Schüssel muoß zu machen.
text: first, set out five measures of flour, beaten and taken. take two souls of good, sweet milk, add sugar, and salt to taste. then, take a bowl and melt some lard in it. add the cold flour and milk to the bowl. place the bowl covered on the hearth, and let it bake until it is finely set on the sides of the hearth, like salt. then it is well done and a good, simple dish. to make the bowl-cakes, form the dough into bowls, then take flour and milk and mix them together. pour into the bowls, set on a trivet or grate, and place a lid on top with a pleasant bit of glowing embers. bake until it is finely done if the bowl is not too hot, it will be well-risen.

title: Auffgangens Reindel.
text: make a dough with water and much more than water, enough to form a good space. add a little salt, then a spoonful of wheat flour. take a pan that is often used for schmaltz, one that is not light, and heat some schmaltz in it. take quite a lot, and add water and space. place it on a grate and put a lid with glowing embers on top. bake it in this way until it burns on the sides and on top. when you want to serve it, remove the lid so that it separates from the pan. then tip the pan into a bowl, and the fritters will fall out. sprinkle sugar on top and serve in this way.

title: Ein gehacks [!] koch zumachen.
text: make a dough with eggs, and knead it well. then chop the meat finely, adding a little flour as you chop, so that you chop it as small as a grain of rice do this until it separates. cook it in boiling milk, and if you wish, until it thickens slightly. serve it then.

title: Haesmbs koch zumachen.
text: set out some water on a table, beat it, and add a little milk underneath. then take some flour, not too much, and set a little milk over it in a pan. let it cook, and then pour the batter onto it. let it rest for a moment, until the heat has passed. if you wish, sprinkle a bit of sugar or spice on top.

title: Ein Troesetztkoch zumachen.
text: make a dough with three or four eggs and set a good ring of milk in a pan. melt a knob of lard in the milk. when the milk boils, add the dough little by little. knead until it becomes thick. add sugar to it as well. if you want it sweet, add sugar to it.

title: Scherbelkoch mach also.
text: take water, good milk, and flour, stir them together. then put some lard into a pan, and sprinkle into the hot lard. lift it over a sieve until it becomes quite thick, then set it on a pot. then put a lid on the pot with a pot underneath, so it simmers finely. when the lard has rendered out, it is done. grind good oats, put them in a pan.

title: Zottenmuoß zumachen.
text: to make a thin pastry, roll out the dough very thinly. cut it into small pieces, like herbs, and scatter them evenly. then, bake them in a dish with warm milk, butter, and sugar, as you would herbs or moss.

title: Buotter muoß mach also.
text: make a bird pie from ten eggs, put it in a shallow pan or rider's dish, finely dried. then take half a pound of good butter, pound it, and add bird pie to it, forcing it through a shallow pan, well-stirred up onto the height, with plenty of sugar put it on last for a dish.

title: Ein durchtribne milch zuomachen.
text: make a good linseed porridge take good milk. set it over, and take of the water as much as you will boil it very gently. when the milk boils, add the water as well as you desire add the whey to it. let it simmer finely together, let it boil out, and strain it through a pepper sieve finely carved. take then very good milk, which is well sweetened add it to the strained whey mixture. serve it cold for a supper.

title: Ein gesottens koch zumachen.
text: to make a fine pastry, take four or five eggs, very well beaten, and add a little milk, honest sugar, wine berries, and schmaltz. add a clarified piece of ham to the beaten eggs. combine this with a clean little bowl, set it in simmering water, and let it simmer until it becomes as fine as a strudel. often stir it. first, adjust the seasoning so that the eggs are broken up. strain it through a sieve. when the bird is added, it is called a broken dish. for the milk, one must add a little meat broth or beef broth.

title: Ein Ayer gemueß zumachen.
text: to make butter, beat it well. take a little schmaltz in a pan, then add the beaten butter. season with salt first, then place on a hot hearth. stir it with a spoon in the pan, but don t make it too thick. pour it into a bowl and form into pats.

title: Ein guots haertel zumachen.
text: take about four or five eggs and break them into a dish. add two yolks or just one good milk, salt, and cut very thin slices, as thin as possible, into the eggs and milk. take a pan that is not easily scorched, grease it, set and stir in a clove of garlic and a little butter on top, so that it is fine. see that it doesn't burn. when it is firm, pour it into a bowl. it is a fine scramble put some sugar on top.

title: Ein anders.
text: heat a little rendered fat in a pan. add sugar and stir until it melts and blends together like a jam. serve on a dish do not cook it too long, as it should be a good, mild dish.

title: Ein guots haertel mit wein.
text: prepare a table for six or eight people, and a measure of sweet wine. mix them together, add salt and good breadcrumbs. cut bacon into it and put it in a pan where a little fat is. set it on a gentle heat it will become finely thick. then, it must be well simmered even a midwife or bloodletter can eat it.

title: Schnee milch.
text: to make a delightful dish, prepare a harbor or a bowl. mix it with a little yeast. lift the same yeast out onto a sieve or a clean cloth. if you have a lot of yeast, take three or four pieces of sweet bread. spread the crumbs on top, then add currants. pour the yeast on top, so it forms a high mound it won't melt. if it stands for eight days, serve it like this. if you dip into the yeast with a spoon and nothing rises, it's a dish for adventurers, but it s good on the bread slices. you must sweeten the milk well.

title: Dockenmilch zumachen.
text: to make a good curd take milk that has been skimmed, and set it where it is warm. then, with a bite that is, a piece as large as a quarter of the milk, or as desired make a bite that is good. once it has stood, you must take it out with a fine cloth on a straw-covered surface. press the cloth finely together and heavily, so that the water is pressed out of it, and then turn it onto a sheet. cut it into even, square pieces with a knife, like small tiles, and sprinkle sugar on top.

title: Gesultzte milch.
text: to make a sweet milk dish heat milk in a pan. then pour it into a beautiful bowl and take the clear part of ten eggs, beat them well and pour into the boiling milk. stir constantly, but do not boil for long. when it has settled, add sugar and a little salt, and adjust the flavor. pour it into a bowl. from the yolks, make a custard and place it in a mold so that it looks good. place it in the center, sprinkle salt over it. also, make a custard and place it in a separate mold. this dish is very good with almonds and sweet milk poured over it it's a good dish for the evening.

title: Tauffte milch.
text: to make snow, take as much as you like, twice its volume in water. stir it in a copper pan until it comes together. place it in boiling water until it is fully combined. you can lift it out with a spoon and place it in a bowl, serve it warm, and sprinkle with sugar.

title: Geschnitten flecken von ayren.
text: to make pancakes, take a wide pan, the hot fat, and add the cooked apples until they cover the bottom. let them simmer until they separate nicely from the pan if you have leaves, turn them occasionally. chop some onions finely, roast them in the fat, and add a little vinegar to the pan with the onions. let them simmer in the vinegar for a long time. then add them to the chopped apples, and add some herbs for a meat broth. season with salt, pepper. if you like, sprinkle some flour into the pan to thicken it. let it simmer for a while. serve this as a dish on a friday or saturday, so it looks as neat as possible.

title: Ein guoten Torten von ayren.
text: first, place eight eggs on a table, beat them very well. then take a vessel much larger than the eggs, let it simmer. pour the eggs underneath and fry some flour in the fat until about a good spoonful is burned. pour the eggs and the liquid into the pan where you are frying the flour, stir it well or twice, and add salt. add some sugar. then take a pan in which there is a little fat, heat it so that the pan is greasy everywhere. remove six spoonfuls of fat and sprinkle the hot, greasy pan with groats. then add the eggs and milk as described above. set it over a good heat and make a lid hot. place hot ashes on top and a good heat underneath, and let it bake in this way, so that it is brown on the bottom and top, and it comes easily out of the pan. sprinkle sugar on top.

title: Ein guot ayer gemueß oder Torten.
text: first, take some groats or flour and mix them together. fry them well in lard. then take some groats, and on a table, spread out eight eggs, beating them well. then take a sweet milk measure underneath, and mix it with the fried groats or flour until it forms a thick mass. then add some raisins. heat some lard in a pan. add the cooked mixture as described. place on a gentle heat and cover with a lid. place also a warming plate on the lid, so it browns on all sides. let it bake slowly in this way. as you prepare it, tilt the pan so it comes out fine and whole. add sugar it must be thick, spread it out, and it will be like a thick lard cake. by master hans schatzmeister, servant.

title: Von Vischen.
text: to make a roasted dish for lent, take a wooden mold split in two like a capon. form a capon shape within it, then press dough into each side. take fish, finely chop it and the skins, and season it well. pack it into the mold, adding broth until it holds together. then roast it, basting with good butter.

title: Ein Raechbraten zu machen in der Fasten.
text: take a large fish, whatever kind it may be, and gut it. crumble the bread very finely, grate some bread, and season well with spices. mix these together with salt. form the mixture on a dish into the shape of a roast. place it in a pan, and wrap it. skewer it on a spit and prick it all over with green sprigs and chopped bacon it will then resemble a roast.

title: Ein weisse Sultz von Vischen zumachen.
text: first, take a fish, a large one, or whatever kind of fish you have. clean it with wine and water, season it with salt to taste. take almond kernels, grate them very finely in a shard. then beat them with hot, clear wine. place the fish in a pan, remove the skin. don't make the broth too thick, it should be a fine white color. add a little ginger and sugar. let it simmer until cooked through. skim off the foam until slightly over. place the fish on a dish, drizzle the broth over it. spoon the remaining broth over the top. if you want gold leaf or lettering on it, you can do that as well.

title: Pasteten von Vischen.
text: to make pies, do so as the others. pies, with wild meat, take some ginger and pepper. a little wineberry, let it simmer for an hour. braised pies. make also so, or the fried fish, or the carp, which are whole.

title: Von schwartzen Karpffen.
text: 85. cut the pies into pieces, one after the other, seasoned and salted, and steeped with the same spices as the other fish. add a little of various spices, a little sugar, berries, lemons, a little fish fat, and also the carp's sweat, a little reduced with wine and vinegar. pour over it, cover, and let bake for two hours. make all the pies in this way. some use wine for the vinegar and a quince for the lemon, also berries, and let them bake as long as the others.

title: Ein Pasteten von gebachnen Hoechten.
text: to make a lemon cake, grind almonds and rice. when you have the dough ready, grind all of it together, and the peeled almonds separately. then grind everything together and mix with good, thick milk don't make it too thin, so that it remains a bit moist. add a measure of sugar, saffron, and salt to taste. make a dough like for a pie. put the mixture into the pie crust and bake it in an oven, being careful not to burn it.

title: Wie man ein Hoechten füllen soll.
text: to prepare a head, skin it completely down to the tail, but do not tear or slash the skin. soak the skin in water, then with a knife, pare the meat evenly and chop it finely. add some rock salt, two onions, and beat them together. season the meat with salt again. then, carefully pull the bladder over it, all the way to the head. afterwards, place it in a well-seasoned broth with wine and vinegar, and simmer until it is done.

title: Von heiß gesotten Vischen.
text: to cook fish well and properly, do not leave the fish standing for long. place it in a pan or pot over water, and pour good vinegar over the fish. salt it generously, so that the water boils. then pour the fish with the vinegar into the pan. let it simmer until the fish is done, then when the boiling subsides and the hunger knows it, and the color fades, they are sufficiently cooked. the noble folk need more salt and longer cooking than the commoners. it is also to be known that whatever fish it may be, it must be prepared. take a live lime and throw it into a pan so that it boils well. if you wish to cook carp well, do not pour the vinegar in immediately, and let it simmer in it. rather, when you want to place them, quickly remove the vinegar from the fish into the pan, so that they retain their shape. place the head pieces in first and let them simmer, then add

title: Die Kappen.
text: simmer the caps, seasoned with vinegar, until they detach entirely in the vinegar, salt, and water. proceed thus place them in boiling water until they open up at the edges or the back becomes firm then they are done.

title: Pfrillen.
text: to prepare the parsnips, salt them well and add vinegar at the appropriate time do not boil them for too long. some people like them this way. when the parsnips are boiled, arrange them on a clean dish or platter. take a little vinegar and let it simmer, then pour it over the boiled parsnips. add some grated ginger on top and drizzle with melted fat. if you wish to boil fish well, after it is thoroughly cooked and drained, let a good, strong vinegar simmer, pour it over the boiled fish, add some salt, and let it steep briefly it will become firm.

title: Pfrillen im butter.
text: take some pike fillets and salt them, not too much, and one measure of wine. put one measure of fillets in a pan, and add butter to the wine, as much as a hen's egg. let it simmer, then add the fillets, not for too long, and serve.

title: Grundel.
text: boil the sausages as well as the vinegar to them, so they become finely blue.

title: Rutten/ ist ein Visch.
text: boil the meat in a pan in cold water, and not too heavily salted, until it is quite tender. when it is done, drain it with vinegar, or wine is better. it shouldn't be too dry. you can serve it hot, or in a light yellow sauce.

title: Huochen.
text: heat the mixture in a small yellow or black pot, as you will hear. the juices should be almost simmering, and require salt.

title: Salmbling/ Schlein.
text: to prepare the shleins, one must put them in hot water before they are thawed, and take them out of the water. then, take a broom handle, and draw them off so well, that a frothy scum comes down. such shleins can be boiled just as well as calf s flesh they are prepared like a poor fish. prepare the prachsen as the carp.

title: Schwartze süpplin an die Karpffen zumachen.
text: to make a dark carp soup first, drain the carp and collect the sweat from the fish. then take a piece of rye bread, slice it, and let it become dark, crumble it, and add wine to it. let it simmer until soft, then strain it like pepper and mix it with wine. add a little nutmeg to it. from the strained slices, you get a fine, thick mixture otherwise, use grated stale bread. but the slices are more pleasant and wholesome. let the soup simmer honestly, and boil the fish in salt as one usually boils fish. when the fish is boiled, pick out the pieces finely into a wide bowl, pour the soup over the pieces everywhere, and sprinkle with ginger or cinnamon. the sweat from the fish, which you collect, must be heated in wine beforehand this gives the soup color. if you don t have the sweat, make it dark as described above, using rye bread slices.

title:
Schwartz vnd gelben suepplein an die Visch
zumachen.
text: first, finely prepare the fish, salt it, then drain it. after that, put it in the broth. take a good ten wines, color them well with saffron and spices. if you want it sharp, don't add nail ginger, it will only make it black, but add muscat grapes, cinnamon, ginger, muscat, and a little peppercorn. mix all of this together. when you have strained the fish, add the broth to it, and let it sit in the broth so that the fish takes on the spices. you can also do this with the black soup, but the soup will be sharper from the salt, as if you had not cooked the fish in the broth.

title:
Den grad von einem Huochen/ oder sonst 
ein grossen Visch einzumachen.
text: to make a good wine, take wine, half sweet, or if you don't have sweet wine, take sugar. there is no sugar in wine, but you can chop a few peeled apples very small and put them in. let it simmer for a while, then add muscat. add spices as desired. when the fish is almost cooked, put a bit of butter in the pot.

title:
Auff ein andere form Visch einzumachen/ 
wie die Koech pflegen zuthuon.
text: to prepare fish, use embers or hot ashes, taking the pieces of fish and salting them well. if the fish is large, leave it in the salt for a longer time then, take a piece at a time, wiping off most of the salt with your finger. place in a cauldron or pan, and add good sweet wine to the fish, seasoned, and buttered, along with chopped onions. let everything simmer together. if the fish is a large head, it needs to simmer longer ashes, embers, and heights shouldn't simmer as long. you may well cook the yellow apples with lemon in the fish broth they are almost deliciously eaten. slice the lemons and simmer them in the soup. when you serve the fish in the soup, place lemon slices and ginger over the pieces of fish. you can also cook the fish in a dark soup, salting it, the fish, and everything together, but use more embers, spices, and sugar.

title: Visch oder Pfrillen im Butter zu kochen.
text: season the fish with salt, letting a little remain in the salt. then sprinkle salt over the fish, take wine and a sweet butter, as a hen is cooked in wine, seasoned with spices for the fish, and let the fish simmer alongside. when it is cooked through, adjust with the broth, and parsley tastes good if it is boiled with it.

title: Pfrillen im Butter.
text: boil them also in wine, with butter, and seasoned. sprinkle the prunes with salt at first, not too much, and put them into the boiled wine do not let them simmer too long. groundles are also good, cooked in butter.

title: Pollische suepplin.
text: to make fish in a polish style take a good portion of parsley root and let it simmer gently in wine. once it is very tender, strain the cooked parsley root along with the wine. add more wine, butter, and peppercorns, and let it simmer again. when the fish is cooked, pour the previously prepared broth over the cooked fish and let it simmer in the broth until fully done. it will have a very good flavor. if you do not have parsley root, celery root is also good peel it, do not cut it, grate it into a fine sieve, add wine, and let it cook until tender, then strain it as you did the parsley root.

title: Gesultzte Visch zumachen.
text: take a fish, be it herring, perch, or carp, which has open gills. open them, and salt it as you salt other hot-boiled fish. let it boil in this way, but not quite done. if you then wish to strain it, take the salted fish from the pan into a different dish, or wash it. then add the salt mentioned later and let it simmer in the salt, but you must add salt to the fish as well, if the broth becomes watery.

title: Die Sultz mach also.
text: to make a good sauce it is very good, half a measure whoever then can have boiled must, is exceedingly good take up on a table well three measures. and it tastes good. if you make it for good people, you must not spare the saffron. take house leaves, on a table almost a quintal, if it is cold weather or winter times, then the soles like it well you do not need many house leaves. but in summer you must have on a table well a half pound, before the salted fish that do not skin. those may also have much house leaves. then take a wine, with together with the house leaves, and sweet it well. the spice take not from standing three only when you want to prepare it. ginger stump is not good make it dry, but to small pieces, cut the ginger, and so boiled. muscat stump, muscat flowers, also cut

title: Auff ein andere art vnd formb.
text: prepare the salt fish as the cook needs. take the fish, soak it, cut it into pieces, salt it, and let it lie in the salt for a while. then wash the pieces and rinse them off. pour in a good sweet wine, as mentioned before, and color it well with saffron. you can cook it well in a pot or in a pan over a fire, just very carefully, so that the foam and impurities are properly removed together. then skim off the pan with a ladle. if it has genuinely lost all its moisture, add the spices. carp fish don't need bay leaves when cooked in salt, but for other fish, you must take a bay leaf. it is also good to cook white horseradish, to taste, until the soup is finely sweet. you can also add such soups to the salt, but not too much, so it doesn't become watery. also, tie the trimmings from the fish

title: Visch im Kaschanat.
text: you eat it cold, if you have fish, like herrings, mackerel, salmon, or whatever fish it is, take the boiled fish, place it in a bowl or on a platter so it can cool. then sprinkle vinegar over the pieces everywhere and chop an onion very finely, sprinkle the pieces with it. also take parsley and other good herbs and put them on the fish, so it will look nice and hard, almost good to eat. if some fish remains at mealtime, you can do this too, or if you have fish that you don t want to keep, salt it well and put it in a glass jar, like often a layer of fish, then often a layer of thinly sliced onion and finely chopped green herbs. if you can get it, sprinkle vinegar on top of it. such fish can be kept for eight or ten days, it will be nice, hard and pleasant to eat, you can always take some, and keep the rest in a cellar.

title: Kalt Hoechten macht man also.
text: take a large fish and salt it, letting it lie in the salt for a while. then place it on a roasting rack, having made cabbage underneath. do not make the heat too high. baste the fish with a little melted fat until it is finely and lightly browned, being careful not to scorch it. afterward, drain the fat from the fish and add some sour wine, as one drinks from the table, and as much vinegar as you like. pour this over the fish to baste it. for a fish of a pound, use a small measure of broth, and take a spoonful of ginger, mace, and nutmeg, if you desire. let the fish simmer in this way until the wine has boiled down well it will then be very good. do not add any pepper.

title: Die Hoechten mit dem Speck.
text: to prepare a dish, set the hearth to the stove and take small cubes of bacon, letting it cook in a pan over a gentle heat. add wine and vinegar together, then add the cooked bacon to it. include some ginger. let it simmer, and when you prepare the fish, heat the bacon and fry it with the parsnips on the hearth it will then be ready.

title: Knoedel/ auch Wuerst von Vischen.
text: prepare a small amount of ground meat. take one or two fresh apples, then add the ground meat to them. beat well. add a little wine and marjoram, with good linden spice. and if you have a large fish, like a noble fish, or otherwise a large fish, then take the flesh out and add the chopped ground meat to it. mix well, don't let it be too thick. put a little ground meat into a sausage casing, binding it firmly at both ends so the casing doesn't tear. then take a clear barley broth and place the sausage in it. let it simmer well. also add some of the kernels from this broth to the sausage, or especially if they have been simmering in the barley broth for a while, add a yellow soup stock as you would for fish. let the sausage and the kernels simmer very gently, like the fish. whether it's a pike or another fish, cooked in soup, then take and slice the

title: Auff ein andere weiß Würst zumachen.
text: first, chop the bread finely, taking about a mole of semolina. chop some of the semolina as well, but not half as much as the bread. once it is finely chopped, take some wine berries, and chop those in as well. season with cinnamon, nutmeg, and mace, salt to taste. then take small sticks, about a thumb's length long, and dip the ends in lukewarm water, and form them into sausages, not too long, like a sausage. if they don t hold, join them at both ends to form a single, neat sausage against a hot glow. turn it gently. when it has become firm, place the sausage on a board, press down on it with one hand, and with the other, pull the stick towards you. the sausage will resemble a real sausage and sprinkle it with pea flour as described. then place it in a small apple pot, set it near the hearth, and place it with the other preserved fish

title:
Jtem ein gespickten Braten von 
Vischen mach also.
text: take a fish and split it open, and cut the brown skin down, as you think it may taste good. then take and cut the piece where the other part is attached, and let the brown skin cook on it. take then the two brown pieces and chop them together. take saffron and pepper, and a little grated semolina underneath. and two eggs to a bowl, so that it is firm and strong. take the brown meat and make a patty from it, as it pleases you, and let the patty fall from a brown bread crumb into simmering water, or better yet, into a fruit broth, which has room in the pan. when it has simmered well, prick it on a skewer and brush it with red egg yolk on the skewer against the fire. take a white heart s eye, cut it to the length of the fish pieces, and stuff the patty.

title: Jtem der ein gefülten Visch machen will.
text: take a fish, peeled, about the length of a small finger, and remove the tail. also, take some fat from it. strain the fat well. simmer it, chop the liver, and fry it with spices and wine berries. take a little of the fat, beat it around the liver, spread the skin over it. when the liver is filled, make small dumplings, place them on a rack, and put the fish on top. let it fry slowly until it is ready.

title: Ein gemueß von Vischen.
text: take the seasoned herbs out and clean them well. hull the gall and drain. take the fillet of fish, scrape it clean and chop the fish very finely. grind it with almond milk and white bread soaked in almond milk. strain it through a cooked rice. put it into a pan, let it heat up, stir well, and do not salt it. if it is too thick, add more almond milk. add honest sugar.

title: Ein Raechbraten in der Fasten zuomachen.
text: to make fish patties take fish, as much as you like, large in size. grind it finely, and the peel as well, very small. rub some breadcrumbs underneath. mix it together with a wet knife onto a dish, in the shape of a roast. skewer it onto a spit it is now ready.

title:
Ein Pasteten zumachen von bachen 
Hoechten Mandel.
text: to make almond and ground rice cakes, if you desire a rich result, place them on a dish and spread them evenly. grind the blanched almond kernels separately. once ground, combine everything together the rich ingredient, rice, and almonds. add enough milk to make a batter, but not too much that it s thin, it should be like a mush. add a generous amount of sugar, make it yellow, and add salt to taste. make a dough from a sack of wheat flour, boil it in hot water until it's well-cooked and hard, and shape it tall, like a pie crust. place the filling described above inside. put it in an oven if you don t have an oven, it s also good in a pie pan. just watch it so it doesn t burn then it s ready.

title: Ein bachens in der Fasten.
text: take a few fish livers, and chopped rye, or pound them in a mortar. take also fish fat and small currants, and chop them together. make a thin pastry crust, beat an egg on top, and bake it in a pan. serve warm.

title: Ein gestossens von Vischen.
text: to prepare the fish and bread each should be nearly good enough on its own. if they are fried, put them in a mortar with grated bread crust and beat them with slices of white bread. then, force them through with a bean purée, but don t add too much of the purée instead, use a non-sour wine, no more than the bean purée. add sugar and spices, and serve on white bread, like another purée.

title: Hausen.
text: boil various white turnips, salted. then wash them and sprinkle with black pepper, or serve them in a dish with stewed apples, chopped, and currants, and butter. if they are still green, cook them in a small yellow apple, finely chopped. similarly, salted house turnips, like a roast, being salted, take a piece water enough put it in a pot, steam it a little, sweeten with wine and water, roast it in fat, and in a small amount of wine, burn it off so that a fine sauce is produced serve it like a steamed roast.

title: Pasteten von Vischen.
text: take a large fish, not too large, and place it on a dish. remove the gall and let it soak in the rinsing water. season the fish thoroughly, as one does with trout, and place it on its sides. if it is a carp or a flat fish, scrape it. add fine salt, letting some remain in it, then sprinkle it well with vinegar and season it inside and out with good spices and a few cloves. add a bit of nutmeg, but leave a good amount in it to soak and flavor. then take a fine, sifted, well-kneaded flour and mix a dough with hot water, adding a good amount so it becomes smooth. add a little salt. take the dough and roll it out into a wide sheet, about half a finger's thickness. place the whole fish directly on the sheet and fold the other half over the fish. cut the dough around the fish, leaving enough dough to form a border by hand. then take one or

title: Stockfisch zukochen.
text: to prepare a cod, one must leave it whole and cut it into pieces. then bind the pieces with a thread so they do not come apart, and wash it. after it has been left for a night and a day, it can be cooked.

title: Jn raum mach jn also.
text: simmer a piece of dried cod as long as it takes to cook a fish. boil the fish, take it out, and place it in cold water, removing any gray matter and impurities. put it in a pot, slice it in half, roast it in fat, and add a little milk to sweeten it. simmer it with the halves and add stockfish. let it cook as long as it takes to cook a fish, then drain it and sprinkle with honest verjus, and arrange it in slices.

title: Geroest Stockfisch.
text: cook a piece of beef, chop it finely, and fry it in the drippings. grind a clove of garlic and add it to the cod. then, add the cod to the drippings as well, and fry everything together with pepper. season to taste and serve with sauerkraut or as you desire.

title: Auff ein andere formb.
text: take a piece of salted cod and some water, and a bit of rendered fat mix them together. then take the cod and work it with your hands, preparing it as you would for frying. season with salt and pepper, add some berries, and bind it together. place it in boiling water and rendered fat. add two honest eggs, and let it stand as it is. when it's done, it will have a fine, thick sauce serve with greens.

title: Braten Stockfisch.
text: send for the sow's head, taking a good, weighty piece. let only the wallow remain, not more, take nothing sheerly out before it over-wall, and pluck also the grease from it, and chop two finely. roast them coolly in the fat, and put into the sow's head stump, wineberry, a few fullens with pounded kernels, or with pounded almonds, and bind the sow's head finely again. lay sparingly on a roasting rack, put it on there, roast it coolly, salt it at first before you bind it. then take it between two cooking ladles, greet it with hot fat, let it not lie too long on the rack, adjust it on a plate, add a ladleful of hot fat to it, and it is good.

title: Von Krepsen zu kochen.
text: boil the cabbage in a pot or pan. add wine or water, salt, and pepper. season with mustard, but not too much. when it has cooked sufficiently, it is ready. if it is already red, it will be pleasing it burns easily in the pot, so one must be careful and ensure it tastes good in the pot.

title: Krepsen eyterlen zumachen.
text: to make small crab patties, take a hind quarter of a crab and the shells, leaving the gall behind. break off the middle part of the body. take as many crabs as you like, pound them roughly in a mortar, and add a good measure of milk. beat it well and put it into a pan, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon so it doesn't stick. cook it like birdseed, letting it simmer gently. add a little vinegar so it thickens, then strain the mixture through a fine sieve or pepper pan. it will be heavy, but that makes it lovely. cut it into pieces. make a yellow apple sauce with slivered almonds or sprinkle with pepper it is a very pleasant, mild dish to eat.

title: Gefuellt Krepsen.
text: to prepare crayfish, boil them until they are cooked. then peel them, take the shells and chop them very finely. add a little good spice and salt. beat an egg in and mix it with the shells, either into the shells or the bodies. add another egg to it, alternating between them. attach them to a wooden spit and roast them over a grill. fry a few slices of bacon in fat, but don't fry or bake them for long.

title: Gestossens von Krepsen.
text: boil the crayfish as usual, shell them, and keep some of the shells and husks. grind the remaining shells well in a mortar, chop a piece of stale bread, grind it with a good sweet wine, add some sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and muscat raisins. stew it a while, then sprinkle over the bread slices. insert the large, shelled crayfish tails into the slices, and also arrange some crayfish roe on top. alternatively, for the large crayfish, shell them nicely, then take a piece of bread, which must be prepared finely first take a loaf of bread and core it out. crumble this into a bowl, and place the crayfish tails in it, sprinkling soup over the top.

title: Ein suppen mit geschelten Vischen.
text: to prepare a good and clear fruit sauce, first put the fruit in a clean pot, and add parsley and root vegetables. let it simmer until the vegetables are soft, then season with ground pepper and whole muscat flowers. add some rendered fat, and then add peeled fish, simmering until it is cooked through. color the sauce slightly, as with capon. test the seasoning on a piece of bread, and if desired, pound some greens with almonds and sprinkle them over the fish, as one would over a roast.

title: Die [<Vie] Karpffen so mans Selchen will.
text: take sheep's head and salt, put it in, let it lie in salt. then take it out, cut it into pieces, and take a large needle with a skewer, fasten the pieces on, always a hand's breadth apart, hang them up thus, and dry them in the smoke until they are almost good.

title: Huochen Selch auch dermassen.
text: roast as above, but not open. forhen and salmon are also good seasoned.

title: I.
text: first, blanch the almonds, wash them when peeled. put them in cold water, so they become nice, hard, and grainy. then, use a stone to grind the almonds, as often as necessary, adding a little water on top. grind until they are as thick as a room. if you don't have an almond mill, you must grind them for a long time with a mortar. however, a lot will remain in the pan. also, add a slice of bread and grind it in salted water, and add it to the almonds, grinding slowly and adding a little water until they are completely doughy. then take the ground almonds, add water to them, press them out, and strain them. after that, heat it over the fire and let it simmer like milk soup. if you want it sweet, add sugar and spread it on toasted bread. add currants on top do not add salt until you are ready to serve, or it will spoil

title: Weinbeer zu Mandel.
text: mix a thick almond milk and add a few wine berries to it. let it simmer in that. add honest sugar as you like. serve it cold or warm.

title: Mandelmu:oß.
text: grind almonds finely. grind rice and chop it in. if you want to cook rice in almond milk, it must be boiled first. but if you cook unground rice in almond milk, boil the rice in water first, and wash it. then add the almond milk to the rice, and let it simmer as one usually simmers rice. add sugar generously, serve warm, sprinkle with sugar, and garnish with raisins.

title: [B1b||1b] Gerendte Milch.
text: take rice and pound it small, then pass it through a sieve. add almond milk and let it simmer in a glass pot over low heat. cook the pounded rice in the simmering milk until it thickens. spread it on a wet bowl and let it cool. cut it into pieces and place it on a dish. season with cold almond milk and garnish with cinnamon. additionally, you may color the milk with saffron or any other dye you desire, and arrange it in a fine pattern on the dish.

title: Ein Jgel von Mandel.
text: take almonds, as many as you wish, grind or pound them, and pass them through a sieve. put them into a bowl, mix them with wood until they are well combined. pour cold milk over them, then add sugar. what remains in the sieve, form into a shape like a small cake. let it sit in the dish until it is level. it will resemble a small cake. decorate with almonds on top. these are the powdered almonds you can color them, or gild the almonds. add honest sugar to them.

title: Mandelka:eß.
text: to make it also take almond milk, which is already very fine. you must have about four lots of mace for every pound of almonds. first, boil the mace in water, and then strain the almond milk through that same water. some people take the almond pulp, well beaten, which passes through a sieve, but it is reluctant to pass through, or through a pepper pan that is not copper, reinforced with mace. add honest sugar to it, sweetening it for as long as two hours. then, once sweetened, place it into a mold where you have poured the egg custard. once it is cold, let it stand. when it has stood, you must place the almond and the mold into hot water. it will then come out readily. drain it onto a bowl, and pour cold almond milk over it. it should not be reinforced with mace. pour in as much milk as will not go over the cake. then you can see the shape of the

title: Ein roten Krebsen von Mandel.
text: if you want to make it red like a crab, add sorrel. the water must also be infused with borage leaves. with this, you must press the almonds through a mold, shaped like a crab place it in there and let it stand, just like cheese. then, transfer it to a bowl, adding almond milk. don't be stingy with the sugar. once you've shaped it over the infused almonds, let it cool don't put it in while hot, or it won't set properly.

title: Ein Reindel von Mandel.
text: take a good, thick milk from almonds and pour it into a mold. or a bowl underneath, grated semolina, as much as will make it thick. mix it with saffron and good linden spice, and sugar. set it over a heat, let it simmer until it thickens. when it has thickened to your liking, set the bowl on a platter. it is now ready.

title: Gegossen Stern von Mandel.
text: then add sweet, white almond milk that has been boiled and infused with borage leaves, once it has cooled, into a pewter bowl. let it stand, and when it has stood, add butter, sweetened and shaped into stars, over red, blue, or yellow.

title: Pfifferling von Mandel.
text: grind almonds into a powder using a piece of quartz. mix with sugar and rosewater until nearly white and thick. shape the ground almonds into small mushrooms, leaving a small portion protruding at the top as a stem. place the finely shaped almonds in a bowl and add almond milk.

title: [B2b||2b] Gesultzt Mandel.
