text: first, truss and partially boil them until very white. then, place them in a small pot with sweet herbs, mace, and pieces of cinnamon. chop a bit of parsley coarsely, and strain the yolks of four or five eggs with a little verjuice, which should be added when they are about to be removed from the heat. garnish your dish.

title: To boyle Chickins in a soope.
text: boil them until they are tender, boil artichokes very well, and blanch them. then put your chickens into a small pot with rich broth. cut your artichokes, and put them into a small pot with a few sliced dates. wash a few raisins and a few currants clean, and put them into a small pot. then take columbine, and wash it clean, and parboil it very well. when you take them from the heat, and blanch them very clean, and put them into a small pot. then take some of your artichokes left, and a little white bread soaked in a bit of broth and verjuice, half a dozen yolks of hard-boiled eggs, and a little rich broth and verjuice, a quarter of a pound of sugar, put it into the small pot, and stir it all together, with a good quantity of butter. then mince the flowers of marigolds, and boil them with the rest. skim the

title: To boyle the common way.
text: first, truss and partially boil them, then place them in a small pot with rich broth. next, take parsley, endive, spinach, and a bundle of sweet herbs. crush the parsley and endive, and add them to the pot along with two or three mutton ribs. if you have potatoes or skirrets, add them in with marigold flowers, and let them boil well together. then slice one carrot and add it, serving with a few large maces and a little sorrel. take the yolks of half a dozen eggs, mince them finely separately, and the partially boiled parsley as well. mix them with a few barberries, and cast all these ingredients on top of the chickens after you have placed them in a dish. you may do the same with a veal knuckle.

title:
To boyle Chickins with Lettice, the
best way.
text: cut each chicken into four pieces. after parboiling them, put them into a small pot with two or three loaves of ale bread. or, if you cannot easily obtain so many, take the udder of an ale, and parboil it thoroughly. cut it into pieces and put it into the pot, along with a sliced lemon. then take lettuce cut it, wash it clean, and bruise it with the back of a ladle, and put it into the pot. next, take about half a pound of sweet butter, half a pint of sack, a quarter of a pint of white wine, mace, a sliced date, and a nutmeg. you may add three or four sliced dates if you have them. let all of these boil together over the fire with marigold flowers and sweet herbs.

title: To boyle a Rabbet.
text: boil your rabbit well and cut it into pieces. then take strong broth and a bundle of herbs, a little parsley, sweet marjoram, three or four yolks of eggs, strained with a little white bread, and put all in a small pot with mace, cloves, and a little nutmeg to give it flavor.

title:
To boyle a Rabbet with Grapes
or Gooseberryes.
text: roast your rabbit whole, and boil it in rich broth until it is cooked through. then take a pint of white wine, a generous handful of spinach, chopped into pieces, the yolks of eggs, cut into quarters, and a little ground mace. let all simmer together with a bundle of sweet herbs, and a generous knob of butter.

title:
To boyle a Rabbet with Claret
Wine.
text: as before, slice onions and a carrot, a few currants, and a bundle of herbs, mainly parsley, picked barberries, mace, nutmeg, and ginger. put them all into a small pot. boil with half a pound of butter.

title: To boyle a wilde Ducke.
text: truss and partially boil it, then half roast it, then carve it, and save the gravy. take plenty of onions, parsley, sliced ginger, and pepper. put the gravy into a small pot with washed currants, large mace, barberries, a quart of claret wine. let it all boil well together, skim it clean, and add butter and sugar.

title:
To boyle a tame Ducke, or
Widgin.
text: boil your fowl well, then take strong mutton broth, a handful of parsley, chopped finely with an onion and barberries, picked and rinsed. throw all into a small pot with a turnip cut into pieces and partially boiled, until the bitterness is gone. then add a little white wine or verjuice, half a pound of butter. boil all together, stirring, and serve it with the turnips, ground mace, pepper, and a little sugar.

title: To boyle Pigeons.
text: boil your pigeons with parsley in their bellies and butter. place them in a small pot with four cups of rich broth, a large piece of mutton, plenty of mace, a little coarse pepper, ground cinnamon, a bit of ginger, and sugar. add a few raisins, currants, and bunches of barberries, along with half a pint of white wine. boil everything together with a little bread soaked in broth, to add color. strain it with some of the broth and return it to the pot. let them boil until cooked through, and then serve. this broth can also be used to cook woodcocks or partridges, with this difference remove some of the broth from the pigeon preparation and add a minced onion. let it boil until it is done.

title:
To boyle Pidgeons with Capers
or Sampyre.
text: place them in a small pot with a pint or more of white wine, a little strong broth, and a few pieces of veal. rinse the salt from your capers or gherkins. blanch half a pound of almonds, placing them in cold water and cutting them lengthwise, then add them to the pot along with raisins. add a generous amount of mace, a little sliced ginger, and a sliced nutmeg. let these ingredients simmer together with a bundle of herbs. stir in three or four egg yolks and a piece of butter, then add the capers or gherkins. this simmering dish will serve well with rabbits.

title: To boyle Sawceges.
text: place them in a quart of claret wine. add mace and barberries. include cinnamon and a handful of sweet herbs. garnish this dish with cinnamon, ginger, and fine sugar.

title:
To boyle Goose-giblets, or 
Swannes-giblets.
text: pick and parboil them clean, and add some strong broth with onions, raisins, and parsley. let everything boil together with plenty of mace and pepper. boil well with a bundle of sweet herbs, then add verjuice and butter.

title: Giblets with Hearbes, and Rootes.
text: pick and parboil them, and put them into a quart of claret wine in a small pot. add half an ounce of sugar, a generous amount of barberries, spinach, and a bundle of sweet herbs, boiled turnips, and sliced carrots. add these to the pot and boil well together. then, take strong broth, verjuice, and the yolks of two or three fresh eggs. strain them and add them to the pot.

title:
To smoore a Racke, or ribbes of
Mutton.
text: cut your mutton into pieces and split them with the back of a cleaver. place them in a dish, adding a piece of sweet butter to the bottom. then take a bundle of sweet herbs and coarse pepper, stew them in a covered dish with a little salt, turning them occasionally. when they are cooked, place them in a clean dish with toasted bread. this dish is best garnished with barberries and pepper.

title:
For the fillets of a Veale, smoored in a
Frying-panne.
text: cut them as you would olives chop them roughly. cut lard finely and use it to coat the chopped pieces. then, place them in a frying pan with strong beer or ale and fry until lightly browned. next, add them to a pint of claret wine and simmer with a little cinnamon, sugar, and ginger.

title:
A Dish of Steakes of Mutton, smoorde
in a Frying-panne.
text: take a leg of mutton, cut into steaks, and put it into a frying pan with a pint of white wine, browning it slightly. then transfer the steaks to a small pot. cut a lemon into slices and add them to the pot. add a generous amount of butter and heat it over the fire. when the butter is about to sizzle, add a handful of parsley, and once it s fried, put it into the pot and boil everything together. this dish would be garnished with cinnamon, sugar, and lemon slices.

title: To smoore a Chickin.
text: cut it into small pieces and fry it with sweet butter. for the batter, take sack or white wine, parsley, a chopped onion, a piece of whole mace, and a little coarse pepper. add a little sugar, verjuice, and butter. then take a good handful of clary, and pick off the stalks. make a fine batter with the yolks of two or three freshly laid eggs, and fine flour, two or three spoonfuls of sweet cream, and a little nutmeg. then fry it in a frying pan with sweet butter, and serve it with your chickens, with the fried clary on top. garnish your dish with barberries.

title:
To frye Mussels, Perywinckels, or
Oysters, to serue with a Ducke,
or single by themselues.
text: boil these shellfish, then flour and fry them. then put them into a small pot, with a pint of claret wine, cinnamon, sugar, and pepper. take your duck, boiled or roasted, and put them into two separate small pots, if one is boiled and the other roasted, and add a little sugar, ground mace, and fried toast, arranged around it with butter.

title:
To marble Smelts, Soales, 
Flounders, Plaice, &c.
text: fry fish in oil in a frying pan until it is cooked through, adding more oil as needed. fry bay leaves in the same oil. pour claret wine into an earthenware pan, placing some of the fried leaves at the bottom and a few on top. add an ounce or two of nutmeg, ginger, mace, and cloves, along with wine vinegar. place the fish into the liquid, ensuring the bay leaves and spices cover it completely. serve with the bay leaves and spices from the liquid.

title:
To congar Eeles, in collars, like
Brawne.
text: cut them open with the skin on, and remove the bone cleanly. mix large mace, coarse pepper, and some finely chopped sweet herbs. then stuff the herbs and spices all along the inside of your eel, and roll it like a collar of brawn. you can do the same with tench, boiled in clear water, white wine, and a quantity of salt, adding some sliced ginger, nutmeg, and peppercorns. when it is well boiled, put it into an earthenware pan, covered with its own liquid and a little white wine vinegar.

title: To sowce a Pigge in collors.
text: prepare your pig in two pieces. remove all the bones, soak it in a bowl of water overnight. the next day, scrape off all the impurities from the back and dry it very well. then sprinkle it with pepper, a little mace, and ginger, along with a bay leaf or two, as you would season a collar of head cheese. let your pot boil before you add it. skim off any scum until it is half-cooked. then remove a ladleful or two and place it in a separate pan. add some rhine wine or claret, sliced nutmeg, coarsely ground pepper, and sliced ginger to the boiling liquid. let it stand until it is almost cold, and then serve it with bay leaves.

title: To sowce a breast of Veale.
text: bone your breast and place it in cold water until the blood is gone. then take it, dry it, and combine all kinds of sweet herbs, grated nutmeg, grated cinnamon, and grated ginger but not too finely ground with lemon peel, thinly sliced. mix all together, spread it over the breast, and roll it into a shape like a brawn collar, binding it tightly. bring your broth to a boil and add the breast. you may use racks and breasts that are untied. skim it very clean, then add a bundle of sweet herbs and keep it covered, as this will make it white. when it is nearly cooked, add sliced nutmeg, large mace, and a little ginger, along with a lemon or two, sliced.

title:
To hash a shoulder of Mutton, or
a Legge of Lambe.
text: take your meat off the spit and chop it into a pewter dish. add retsina wine, raisins, sliced lemon, and raw oysters. combine all ingredients in a small pot and stir. if you desire oysters and raisins, add two whole onions. if you want wine, use strong broth, verjuice, and sugar. sprinkle a few barberries into the dish and serve it on toasted bread or small pieces of toasted bread.

title:
A Legge of Lambe fearst with
Hearbes.
text: prepare it as previously described, with sweet herbs and grated bread. add biscuit crumbs, a few coriander seeds, lemon peel, finely ground nutmeg, sliced dates, and a little coarsely ground pepper. incorporate clean, washed capers. combine all ingredients with six or seven yolks from freshly laid eggs, which should be hard-boiled and whole. mix these with sugar, rosewater, and verjuice, along with the marrow from one or two bones, salt, and pepper. put everything into the pastry crust. caraway seeds and orange zest are the most suitable garnishes for your dish.

title: To smoore Calues feet.
text: boil and blanch them, and place them in fresh water and salt. when they are cold, cut them in half and remove the dark bits. put them in a dish with sweet butter. finely chop parsley, onions, and sprigs of thyme. add mace, pepper, and a little wine vinegar. let everything simmer together until ready. stir in a few barberries, finely chopped parsley, two or three hard-boiled egg yolks, and rosewater and sugar, mixing them separately. when serving, sprinkle with parsley and hard-boiled eggs.

title: Another way.
text: prepare them as before, place them in a dish with fresh water and butter, chopped lettuce, and spinach. put them in a dish and let them simmer with plenty of mace, lemon slices, a few grapes, or a stewed cucumber, sliced. let everything boil well together with pepper. strain the yolks of eggs, cream, and sugar into a dish. strain these ingredients together just before serving. this boiling sauce will serve for calves' feet, sheep's trotters, or pigs' feet serve them hot at supper.

title: To hash Neates-Tongues.
text: boil them and blanch them, then slice them into pieces. put them into a small pot with raisins, ground mace, sliced dates, a few blanched almonds, and claret wine. boil everything together with half a pound of sweet butter, verjuice, and sugar. strain a ladleful of the liquid with the yolks of about half a dozen eggs.

title: The same vvith Chestnuts.
text: prepare your tongue as before put it in a small pot with blanched chestnuts, strong broth, a bundle of herbs, ground nutmeg, rinsed ginger, a little pepper, a few cloves, and whole cinnamon. boil all together with butter, season with salt, and garnish your dish as you please.

title:
TROISIÈME PARTIE
-------
DES SIMPLES COSES
QU'IL CONVIENT A OUME USER
text: to make a fine tart of apples. take good apples, and pare them well and core them. then bake them in a dish with a little butter and a little saffron. when they are baked, take them out and set them aside. then take good spice, ginger, cinnamon, and grains of paradise, and a little salt. grind them together and add sugar. then moisten with rosewater. lay the apples in a pastry crust, and sprinkle them with the spice. cover with a good pastry and bake well.

title:
CHI APRIÈS DIST IL LES QUELES VIANDES
ET LI QUEL BEVRAGE SONT MILLEUR
text: the first chapter will be about all kinds of wheat, and bread made from it. the second about all kinds of beverages. the third about all meats. the fourth about all legumes. the fifth about all fruits. the sixth about all fish. the seventh about all herbs. the eighth about all spices.

title: DEL FORMENT
text: make cheeses from wheat that is agreeable to all wheats in nature. however, it holds one part of heat and varies depending on its age, whether new or old, and the soil in which it grows, and for other reasons as well. one should choose to eat cheese that has grown in good soil, that is pure of all other things, and that is between old and new, and has a color between red and white, and is kept cleanly, not in a pit or a damp place, but should be in houses where the wind can enter. such wheat is suitable for a man, for the person who is made of such wheat, as we have said, is more tempered than anyone made of any other wheat. and know that the bread made from such wheat, as we have said, is hotter than cheese, and takes such heat in the oven when it is cooked, and no bread is so good or so quickly cooked on the fire as this one, but it should be

title: CAPITELES DE L'ORGE <ET DU SOILE>
text: barley is cold and of the first degree and is almost tempered, but it tends more towards coldness. and the soil is of this same nature, as avicenne says, meaning that it is not so tempered, and for this reason we will tell you about barley, so that you may understand about the soil. know that barley nourishes and swells the bowels more than wheat, but it cools more, and therefore those who are afflicted with windiness and pain in the flanks, and swelling of the groin should not use it but those who are hot and who want to eat it can use it well. and know that the humour that is engendered from it is melancholic, and therefore, it is better to use it according to the way of medicine than for maintaining health, that is to say, to use it in fevers, as to make barley water and other things that the author of physic teaches.

title: CAPITELES DE MILLOS ET DE PENIS
text: a thousand and leeks are cold or first degree and dried or second, and i will tell you about these two together, because they have one nature. i say that leeks are good for nourishing, because the juice which is born in them is heavy and bad, and therefore, those who wish to fatten and have abundance of good juice should not use them often, because they restrain the belly and make the spleen swell. but to those who use mustard, they may use it with milk, and with almond oil, and with fatty meat, because fatty things make them lose their malice. for a thousand and leeks are better for removing illnesses than for keeping health, and it is fitting, if one wants to use them, to roast and boil them, for distortions and other pains that are caused by wind, and in other several illnesses.

title: CAPITELES DU RIS
text: rice is the first course, or the second, and when it is heated, it is tempered. but it is of a heavy nature, and remains very long in the stomach, and constricts the belly, and therefore, those who suffer from flatulence and who have a weak stomach for cooking meat should not use it. however, those who use stewed fruit, to remove malice, to give sufficient nourishment, and to engender a great abundance of blood, should mix it with almond milk, and with sugar, and with all things thick.

title: CAPITELES DE L'AVAINNE <ET DE L'ESPIAUTRE>
text: barley and spelt are cold and dry, and are in nature like barley, and have similar properties in all workings on the body and they are more useful for those with a hot constitution than for those with a cold one, and are better for removing illnesses than for maintaining health. for they, by their nature, warm and swell, but they have the property of drawing out swellings that come from windiness, if they are put warm on top. and they are better to use for those who are lean and prone to wasting away, in this manner take flour of barley and spelt, and mix it with the color of burnt wheat bran, with warm water, and with honey, and with pennyroyal, and with four ounces of eggs, and cook it like a porridge, and use it for those who are wasting away and who are weakened by hot illnesses. this is a wholesome meat that fattens above all things.

title: CAPITELES DE SEGINE
text: seitan is a manner of wheat, cold and dry, and it grows in lombardy in the manner of canvas, which is not good to use for health. it should be avoided, because it gives great nourishment and makes the blood melancholy, and swells the belly, and restrains the fortitude. it is said that it weighs down the feet because it is heavy, so it makes meat difficult to swallow. and bread is made from this wheat, and all other bread holds the nature of the grain from which it is made, but it is one degree less warm, and this heat comes from the fire in which it is cooked, as isaac says.

title: CAPITELES DU FAR
text: here is one way to make wheat bread, but it is thicker, and colder, and has a drier temper, and the virtue of giving great nourishment to the body when it is well cooked. but it inflates the stomach with wind, and is more useful for wasting away illnesses than for maintaining health, especially hot illnesses.

title: CAPITELES DE BRENS
text: wheat bran is a cause and sustenance, and it is small and unpleasant, but it has the virtue of cleansing the limbs. when it is put into hot water and steeped, and afterwards cooked like a porridge, it has the virtue of purging the bladder of thick humors and bad ones it does not cause the stomach to swell and it remains light, and for this reason, it can be given in fevers and in all hot diseases, with sugar, in such a manner. but barley bran is better, for when it is of wheat, it cools and furthermore, boil wheat bran in water or wine and make a poultice to apply hot to the breasts that are swollen and hard from abundance of milk, to unswell them and set them right and this same poultice is good for bites of vipers and of all other venomous beasts.

title: CAPITELES D'EWE
text: the sheep, as the philosophers say, is naturally cold and moist, and does not give nourishment, but it has the virtue of lessening nourishment, so that it passes more easily through all the limbs, and it has the virtue of aiding and cooling all those who are of a hot constitution more than wine does. and the sheep that is lighter should be chosen, and which easily warms and cools, and which holds a small measure of a sweet flavor. such sheep should be drunk. of turbid ones, and of salty ones, and of other manners, one should be wary, unless it is to remove illnesses and if one uses the stews, they will be amended according to the instructions we gave in the first part, for we will pass over those instructions briefly there.

title: CAPITELES DE VIN
text: wines differ in many ways, according to their substance, and whether they are new or old and it is said that all kinds of wine, by their nature, warm, some more and others less wines red and clear and white do not suffer water easily, this is less cause, but they have the nature to make one drunk, and they should be used by those who have fever and the forceful heat, and are better for all people in summer when it makes great heat. clear and well red wines, and which are somewhat bitter, and which suffer enough water, so are more cause the one that is black, and thick, and has a sharp flavor, is not so cause, but it makes it bad to use because it swells and thickens the forceful heat and blocks the passages of the body, but it restrains the belly and therefore, makes it

title: CAPITELES DE CIERVOISE
text: here's a recipe for making beer, using barley, wheat, and rye. but the beer made with wheat and rye is best, because it doesn t cause bloating or produce so much wind. however, whether it is made with barley, rye, or wheat, it harms the head and strengthens the body, causing bad humors and bad teeth, and fills the spleen with bad fumes. therefore, those who drink it with wine become easily intoxicated, but it has the property of promoting good urination and making the flesh white and soft. and beer made from soil or sourdough bread is better than any other beer.

title: CAPITELES DE VIN DE PUME
text: wines that are made from sour plums are of a watery and moist temperament, but they are not healthy to use, because they swell and thicken the spleen and block the passages of the liver and lungs. but they have the nature of making dirty and giving sufficient nourishment, and are especially good for those who have a bitter and dry constitution, and who cannot easily break wind. and such wines are made from sour plums, so they have the nature of a sour wine, and are better for those who have a bitter spleen and who have a feverish liver and all people could use such wine when there is a great heat.

title: CAPITELES DE VERJUS
text: to make a syrup, use fresh rosehips, sorrel, and verjuice, and other tart ingredients of a similar nature, to cool the heat, soothe the burning in the stomach that comes from it, quench thirst that arises from great heat, settle the belly, and ease and restrain vomiting. this is made with old and new ingredients, but the old is more effective due to the nature of salt.

title: CAPITELES DE VIN AIGRE.
text: to make sour wine, which by nature is cool and causes mixing, as avicenne says, but it holds more coldness, and has a nature to dry, to disperse, and to pass. it is more useful for treating illnesses than for maintaining health. and you can make it in this way take good wine and put it in a vessel, but not filled to the brim, and leave it uncovered, and it will become sour, and then place it in the sun for three or four days. and if you wish to make it sooner, take a hot ember or a stone from a river heated, and put it inside, and it will become sour. and if you wish to know if it is good, cast it upon the ground, and if it bubbles and foams, know that it is good, and if it does not bubble, it is bad. such wines are good for restraining the belly and for inducing vomiting, and are good for all hot diseases especially when

title: Dei cauli.
text: to prepare cauliflower well-cooked. remove the stalks of the cauliflower and clean them thoroughly, ensuring no leaves remain trim the tender tops. when the pot is boiling with oil and water, add the stalks or the cauliflower florets, and include some fennel bulb, cooking them until they are tender. if desired, you can add oil, meat broth, or capon broth, pepper, spice powder, beaten eggs, and saffron for coloring and give thanks to the lord. to prepare green cauliflower with meat. remove the healthy florets of the cauliflower and add them to the boiling pot with the meat, cooking them until tender. drain them and place them in cold water. transfer them to another pot with broth, and when it is time to eat, place the cauliflower with the broth in the aforementioned pot. simmer briefly, and you can add meat broth or oil. of the above. remove the cauliflower and cook it with castrated boar meat, pork, or

title: De le foglie minute, et dei finocchi.
text: remove spinach, swiss chard, and beet greens clean them well and boil. then drain them and chop them forcefully with a knife. next, remove parsley, fennel, anise, and onions, and chop and mince them with a knife, then sauté with oil. add other finely chopped herbs and sauté them together, then add a little water and let it simmer, adding pepper and spices and serve. in this way, you can add beaten eggs, fish pulp without bones, castrated boar and pork meat or salad meat, and vary it according to the discretion of a good cook and use marjoram, wild thyme, parsley with good fish or pounded meat, to make mortadellas, sausages, and many other things in this way you can use domestic herbs, or even wild ones, if you cannot have them from the garden. serve with borage. remove

title: Salsa di finocchio.
text: remove the fennel flowers and pound them in a mortar. add saffron, nutmeg, cloves, cardamom, egg yolk, and blend with the saffron. this is a good sauce in september, with eggs.

title: De' senacioni; cioè in più modi.
text: remove the stalks, and finely chop them, washing them thoroughly in warm water and pressing out the excess moisture then cook them in water with pork or other meats and plenty of salt. once the stalks are boiled, finely chop them with a knife, and fry them with a little onion. then add them to another pot with oil and salt. this dish is beneficial for those who have difficulty urinating due to kidney stones. alternatively, in the style of the nobility remove the flower buds of cauliflower, or the tender buds of turnips, and cook them. when cooked, fry them with oil, with leeks or onions, or without either. they can be served separately or combined together.

title: De la senape.
text: drain the mustard seeds and boil them in water then discard the water. fry in a pan with oil and salt, or add them with meat to cook.

title: De li sparaci.
text: remove the stems and boil them. when boiled, cook them with oil, onions, salt, and saffron, and chopped spices, or without.

title: De le lattuche.
text: wash lettuce with fresh goat's milk, from april, with spices, egg yolks, fresh lard, and pork. this dish is called lettuce eating, because it is made with lettuce marrow.

title: De le zucche.
text: peel, wash, and thoroughly squeeze young squashes, then cook them with fresh pork, pepper, and saffron. alternatively, peel, wash, and thoroughly squeeze young squashes. combine them with hard-boiled eggs, onions, and finely grated cheese, then add to boiling water with pepper, saffron, enough oil, and salt. these can be used to make ravioli filled with ground mixed meat, or fried pastries. alternatively, soak dried squashes in warm water overnight. when softened, chop them finely and arrange on a platter with onions, oil, pepper, and saffron. sauté and serve in a sauce made with vinegar and breadcrumbs. this can also be prepared with almond milk, pepper, parsley, salt, and oil, or with walnut milk.

title: De le pere.
text: peel fresh pears and soak them in water. drain the water and boil the pears in fresh water with salt and oil, along with a little onion. simmer with spices and saffron in a little water, and let them cook. when they are cooked, serve a little of the spiced mixture in bowls. alternatively, you can prepare them in a little almond milk, without oil and without onions, adding a touch of sugar and a pinch of salt.

title: Di cipolle.
text: remove the onions, washed and well-cleaned, and cook them with meat and cheese, pepper, and saffron. then add beaten eggs, pepper, and saffron, if desired, along with spices in individual bowls.

title: De' porri.
text: remove white leeks, prepared in the tuscan style, finely chopped or sliced, wash them with warm water, and cook them with a piece of fresh meat, then chop the meat with the aforementioned leeks, pepper, and saffron, and beaten eggs then add pork or other meat, and serve. place spices in small bowls. alternatively, during fasting. remove chopped leeks, well washed and squeezed, and cook them with oil and breadcrumbs, or grated bread, tempered with eggs, pepper, and saffron add poached eggs and cheese, and serve. alternatively. leeks can also be cut into four pieces, well boiled and drained, then fried with oil, salt, and pepper, over the small bowls during lent. alternatively with meat. remove white leeks, finely chopped and well washed, and cook them with castrated boar meat when cooked, serve with spices. alternatively. remove leeks, well washed and boiled

title: De' naponi, ovvero navoni.
text: remove the ends of the artichokes, blanch them briefly then drain them. next, cook them in the chicken fat. if you want them to be colored, add saffron, or beaten eggs thinned with the broth. you can also add eggs, diced or ground meat, and goat s milk, as desired.

title: De' raponcelli.
text: drain the rapini, which have been well boiled in water, and sauté them with olive oil, onion, and salt. when they are cooked and served, place spices in small bowls alongside. alternatively, drain the rapini or cardoons with olive oil and salt, and add grated cheese and beaten eggs. add more cheese and eggs lost during cooking, on saturdays.

title: De le rape.
text: remove turnips, boiled with their leaves, and cook them with beef, pepper, and saffron. when cooked, place them in bowls for the family to share. alternatively. remove the tops of the turnips, without leaves, chop them, and boil them in water. discard that water, cook them with a capon or other meat, and color them with saffron and pepper. add in them eggs, grated cheese, and boiled eggs, add goat's milk, and serve. alternatively. remove turnips without leaves, peeled, boiled, and drained, and cook them with salt and walnut milk, and add pepper and saffron. alternatively. remove turnips without leaves, boiled discard the water, remove bread soaked in the meat broth and from the said turnips, and grated cheese, and meat fat, make a soup, which is called soldier's soup.

title: De' ceci.
text: use red or white chickpeas soak them, then cook with pepper and saffron, and fragrant herbs. when these ingredients are cooked, place some in a mortar and pestle until thick, then add flavorful broth. next, add roasted whole chestnuts and parsnip root, and meat broth or, if you prefer, you can cook them with meat this way. alternatively, for saturday. use broken chickpeas and chicken, cooking them with pepper, saffron, and diced cheese, and lost or beaten eggs. alternatively. use boiled broken chickpeas, discarding the cooking water, and add sautéed onions, well-candied with oil or lard, as the season or day requires. alternatively. use boiled broken chickpeas, discarding the water, and cook them with almond milk, spices, and saffron or you can make them without spices with ginger, and the chickpeas will be white. alternatively. use whole chickpeas and cook them with any salted meat, washed and well-

title: De' peselli.
text: remove the beans and place them in a large pot of boiling water, reserving the water you can use it to make soup in the french style. in a pan, sauté onions with oil when softened, add the reserved water to the pan. then, add bread, cut into roughly medium-sized pieces, to the water along with spices, and let it soften. next, remove the beans and cook them in fresh water with oil, salt, and onion, and serve. alternatively, remove the well-boiled beans and, discarding the water, cook them with ricotta, oil, and scattered eggs you can add parsley. alternatively, cook fresh beans with oil, salt, spices, saffron, and beaten eggs, and serve.

title: Peselli con carne.
text: cook the peas with meat, well drained of salt and once the meat is cooked, chop it finely and place it in bowls. alternatively, boil the peas and discard the water, then cook them in fresh water with salted pork meat and a little saffron. you can also add fresh veal or other meat as you like.

title: De le fave sane.
text: boil fresh broad beans drain the water and cook them in goat s milk, sheep s milk, or almond milk, or with meat, well purged of salt. add beaten eggs and lardons in small bowls, if desired. alternatively, when the broad beans are tender, boil them, drain the water, and cook them in fresh water with pork or ricotta serve. alternatively, boil fresh broad beans drain the water and cook them with sautéed onions and pounded fragrant herbs, adding pepper and saffron. alternatively, remove the broad bean blossoms and cook them with fresh pork when they are almost cooked, add beaten eggs, milk, and spices, saffron, and salt, and stir frequently, as when making mortadella. alternatively, cook the broad bean blossoms with a whole cockerel at the end of the cooking time, add almond milk and beaten eggs, pepper, saffron, and salt cook in a suitable dish.

title: De le fave infrante.
text: shell the broad beans, crush them well, clean and sort them, and boil them once. drain the water, rinse them thoroughly, and place them in another pot with just enough water and salt to cover them. stir frequently. when they are cooked and thick, mash them vigorously with the stirring spoon. then, loosen them with a little added water, and form into bowls. add apples, or fried oil with onions, or fried pork fat. alternatively, crush and wash the broad beans with hot water. boil them, and when cooked, rinse them well again. return them to boil in enough water to cover them and protect them from the steam. when they are very well cooked, mash them with a pestle. then, loosen them with cold water or white wine, until well blended. make soup with them, and top with fried oil and onions. serve. if you wish, you can loosen them with hot water, and add pepper, saffron, apples, and sugar. you

title: De le lenti.
text: remove the lentils, well washed and cleaned, from their pods, and cook them with fragrant herbs, oil, salt, and saffron. when they are cooked, mash them well then add beaten eggs and grated cheese to serve. alternatively, cook the lentils with fresh pork or bacon, and serve them as they are, without eggs and cheese.

title: De' fasoli.
text: well-washed and boiled beans, cook with oil and onions, with the aforementioned spices, grated cheese, and beaten eggs. alternatively, in the treviso style. place boiled, peeled beans to cook with salted meat, pepper, and saffron. they can also be sautéed with oil, adding a little vinegar, starch, and salt. alternatively. drain the boiled beans, discarding the water, and cook them with castrated boar meat, pork, beef, or whatever you prefer, pound it well, add a little saffron and salt, and serve.

title: De' fungi.
text: gather wild mushrooms, boil them, and sauté onions with pork fat. then add spices and fragrant herbs, and beaten eggs serve. alternatively, gather wild mushrooms and boil them drain the water, then fry them with finely chopped onion or white leek, spices, and salt. serve. alternatively, gather dried mushrooms and soak them overnight drain the water, finely chop them with a little white leek or onion, and fry them with oil or pork fat and spices, chestnuts, vinegar, a little water, and salt. then add mustard with cooked grape must and pork, if you like.

title: De la composta.
text: prepare carrots, thoroughly washed and boiled, then cooled. in the water from the carrots, cook turnips cut into quarters, but not overcooked. similarly, cool them. then, remove parsley roots, horseradish, leeks, fennel, pears, capers, and cauliflower florets, and boil each ingredient separately, cooling them as before. according to lombard custom, you can add gherkins. next, add good mustard made with strong vinegar and fennel seeds, anise seeds especially the horseradish. place finely chopped horseradish in each layer of the aforementioned herbs, then add mustard and then the herbs, as appropriate. arrange these ingredients in a jar, cover with a large cloth, and let it stand for eight days. alternatively, chop horseradish very finely, anise, and fennel seeds, and cook them in must. cook until the must reduces to half. use this must to thin the mustard. then, take small turnips, rutabagas, quince, apples cut into quarters, and pears halved

title: De' brodi: e primo, de brodo granato.
text: remove the chicken pieces and fry them with onions and pork fat. add enough water when they are almost cooked, remove the fragrant herbs. finely chop them with saffron, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, and ginger, then thin with the aforementioned broth, and mix everything together. then, add beaten eggs and a little cold water, and stir in some of the broth, mixing well, and place over heat. when it begins to boil, remove from the heat and serve. alternatively. remove capons or hens and boil them. add spices and herbs inside. remove the egg yolks with the broth, and mix in a bowl then boil together until the broth becomes grainy. do this with all the birds, with or without pork fat. alternatively. remove large pieces of chicken, cut, disjointed, or whole, and fry in pork fat with fragrant herbs, spices, whole lemon, and proceed as above but make a little

title: De la gelatina di pesce.
text: drain the wine, removing a little vinegar, and once it boils, skim off the foam and add the fish. once cooked, remove the fish and let the wine boil until it reduces to about a third of its original volume. then add saffron and other spices, along with bay leaves. after straining the wine, add a sprig of herbs and allow it to cool. finally, place the fish in a serving dish.

title: Del brodo del pesce.
text: clean the fish thoroughly, as much as you like fry it generously in oil. then let it cool. next, prepare onions sliced thinly. fry them in the remaining fish oil. then take blanched almonds, dried currants, dried raisins, and prunes, and fry them with the onions together. remove any excess oil, and take out the pepper and saffron, and other fine spices, along with wine and vinegar. temper it strongly and bring it to a boil. then remove it from the heat and place it in another vessel. arrange the fish neatly on a platter. if you prefer it sweeter, add cooked wine or sugar to taste. alternatively, take good wine and a little vinegar and bring them to a boil, skimming off any foam. then add the fish to cook. once cooked, remove the fish. let the wine boil until it reduces to a third of its original volume. then add bay leaves, saffron, and fine spices, and warm the

title: Del paparo.
text: slit the throat of the goose or duck, pluck it well and singe it cut the skin, hollow out the inside, and wash it thoroughly. then remove any sorrel and garlic, and if you don't have those, use fragrant herbs soaked in vinegar. roast it again, put it on a spit, and roast it. if it isn't fatty enough, add some lard. put a little water in a bowl and remove the fat that comes out. when it's cooked through, remove it from the heat and serve it with orange, lemon, or mandarin juice. if you wish, you can make a pepper stew with a millstone of toasted bread and the toasted liver, ground with the same millstone. and all the ingredients, tempered with vinegar, boil and add pepper, saffron, cloves, and other good spices. from the head, feet, ventricles, and liver, you can make sorrel, adding beaten eggs, saffron, and spices

title: De la grua.
text: clean a goose well and partially boil it in a large pot. place it on a spit and roast it, but not thoroughly. prepare onions, cut into small dice, and fry them well with lard, coloring them with saffron. have some bread slices, slightly toasted, and good wine, cooked and mixed with the aforementioned onions. simmer the goose, shredded, with these ingredients in the wine for a brief boil. in the lean broth of this flavor, soak the aforementioned bread. on a large platter, arrange the flavorings, spices, and meat in layers, as appropriate. at the end of the cooking, add some fat of the same flavor. this can also be done with a castrated bull s head or veal, well peeled and blanched but do not overcook them. when prepared as described above, place it on a warming dish and then serve.

title: Del brodo saracenico.
text: remove roasted capons and their livers with the spices, and toasted bread grind them in a mortar, and mix with white wine and lemon juice. then, shred the capons and put them to boil in a pot with the aforementioned ingredients. add dates, raisins, whole blanched almonds, and enough lard. serve. use a similar method for fish. pears and apples can be added to the broth.

title: Del brodo dei capponi.
text: remove the capons and boil them when cooked with the spices you desire, break them up in a bowl with eggs and their broth, and sprinkle with flour, mixing well. then add all of this to the broth and let it simmer briefly. this is called apollonio broth. alternatively, prepare it provençal style. remove livers, gizzards, and giblets from well-washed and finely chopped capons place them in a pot with a little water, and cook with spices and beaten eggs, coloring as you like. you can also sauté these ingredients and add sweet and sour juices. similarly, you can prepare it with the heads and feet of capons, or similar parts. alternatively, prepare a green broth in the spanish style. remove birds, livers, or any meat you choose boil them well with good spices and crushed green herbs then add beaten eggs and pollenta to the broth, and simmer. the broth should not be thick.

title: De le starne.
text: remove the boiled giblets and disjointed chicken with fragrant herbs, salt, and finely ground spices in a mortar. sauté the meat with lard, then cook the chicken in a little water in a pot. add almond milk. at the end of cooking, stir in saffron, thinning it with the broth. if desired, create a deep red broth. this method can also be used with peacocks, pheasants, young chickens, and small birds.

title: De la gratonia.
text: remove the sheep's milk and whisk it vigorously with eggs, then place lard in a pan over heat until it's well warmed. pour the egg and milk mixture into the pan, spreading it evenly, and cook thoroughly. once cooked, remove from heat and add sugar, then serve. alternatively, add tightly beaten egg whites, cut into dice, to the broth this is called spanish gratonia, and you can color it as you wish.

title: De' crispelli, ovvero frittelle ubaldine.
text: take fine, white flour and mix it with eggs, allowing it to rise slightly. add saffron, then cook it with rendered lard. afterwards, add sugar or apples and serve. alternatively, take white flour with a little yeast and mix it with warm water, allowing it to rise, that is, to ferment. then, take roe of pike, trout, dace, or another fish, and combine it strongly with the prepared dough. add saffron, and cook as described above. alternatively, you can do the same with chopped onions, mint, and herbs fry them with garlic or lard. then, take flour and mix everything together with egg white. add elderflower blossoms and other flowers as you like diversify the colors as you please, and place them in boiling lard, distributing the mixture evenly.

title: De' guanti, cioè ravioli.
text: drain the soaked white chickpeas cook them thoroughly, then drain and mash them well. mix the mashed chickpeas with a little of the cooking water, and strain the mixture. dilute the strained mixture with flour to your desired consistency. fry over low heat in lard or olive oil, and top with grated cheese. alternatively, mix the flour with eggs, then shape into small patties or other desired forms. cook thoroughly in a pan with hot lard or olive oil.

title: Di salsiccie, o vuo' tortelli di pesce.
text: put the fish in boiling water so that you can easily remove the bones, and add fragrant herbs, finely chopped together with the fish pulp, and spices. then place everything in a large, clean linen cloth and squeeze it firmly. next, put it in a pan with hot oil and shape it into long or rectangular patties, as you prefer.

title: De' crispelli di carne, o vero tortelli e ravioli.
text: take pork belly, skin removed, and boil it. then chop it finely with a knife. remove fragrant herbs in a generous quantity and pound them well in a mortar. add fresh ricotta to them along with a little flour, and mix with egg white until it forms a stiff paste. take fresh pork fat in a generous quantity and put it in a pan, allowing it to sizzle. fry crispies until cooked, then remove them and sprinkle with sugar. alternatively, omit the ricotta. chop the fresh cheese finely, add a little flour, and mix with egg white until it forms a thick paste. cook it with lard as described above, and sprinkle with sugar as in the other version.

title: De le gualdaffe di ventri et caldumi.
text: trim the veal sweetbreads, and wash them with cold or warm water, scraping and cleaning them as much as possible. then place the sweetbreads in a pan without any liquid over the fire, turning and flipping them frequently until they are well cleaned and smooth. then wash them with water, as before. next, simmer them briefly in water, adding whole mint and salt. then fry them with lard in the pan, as you desire, and remove the broth, which is called gualdaffa. alternatively, stuff them. remove sweetbreads from young veal wash them well, and stuff them with the cooked gualdaffa, finely chopped, mixed with beaten eggs and grated cheese, spices, and salt. once this is done, place them to simmer, and you can then roast them serve. you can also place these gualdaffa in broths or in pastries. and so you can make gualdaffa from other animals.

title: Dei detti gualdaffi e caldumi.
text: you can make broth from the called gualdaffi and raw cow intestines, if you wash them well. cut the said intestines and fry them in lard with finely chopped onion. boil some poultry and add egg yolks with breadcrumbs and spices make a thick broth, if you wish, and color it as you like. this broth is called caldume.

title: De la corata e ventre di porco in caldume.
text: prepare the pork belly and offal wash it well. finely chop it and fry it with lard and onions, as described above.

title: De li savori.
text: remove the ginger, bread crusts, and salt, and pound well in a mortar. then, dilute with good wine, a little broth, and bring to a simmer. this flavor is called cenamata and is suitable for all roasted venison and rabbit. note that venison can be roasted with or without bones. the same applies to rabbit and other meats, such as roe deer and deer, to which this flavor, and a sauce of blackcurrants with spices, are well-suited.

title: De la peverada.
text: remove toasted bread, a little saffron that doesn't color, spices, and ground liver pounded in a mortar, and loosen with vinegar or wine and the aforementioned broth, making it sweet or sour as you desire. this peppered dish can be made with domestic, wild, and fish meat.

title: De' civeri di lepore e altre carni.
text: dismember the hare completely and, after a quick wash, cook it in water. then, remove the cooked liver and lungs, pound them well in a mortar, and once the hare is cooked, remove the spices, pepper, and onion, and sauté them in lard with the aforementioned lungs and toasted bread. once all ingredients are combined, serve. you should finely chop and pound the cooked liver and lungs in a mortar with spices and burnt bread, and mix them with good wine and a little vinegar. once the hare is cooked and sautéed with the onion, pour the mixture over the hare and let it cool until lukewarm, then serve. this method can also be used for partridges, that is, quail. alternatively, use cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, mace, bird livers, egg yolks, and small birds, whole or halved, and fry them in lard. then cook them in the aforementioned broth, and proceed as described above.

title: Di sommacchia di polli o di uccelli.
text: remove the chicken pieces and fry them in lard. add almonds and sumac. simmer them with water, ensuring the broth is frequent, and serve. you can prepare fish in a similar way fry the pieces like chicken, or use them for capons, guinea fowl, or small birds, as well as capon giblets. you can add starch to this dish it is particularly helpful for those with digestive issues. you can also prepare fish pieces that have been beaten, using oil instead of lard.

title: Di limonia di polli.
text: fry the chicken with lard and onions, and pound the unrefined starch. mix it with the pork broth, salt, and cook with the chicken and spices. if you don t have starch, thicken the broth with egg yolks and when the time to serve approaches, add lemon, lime, or caper juice.

title: Di gratomea di polli, uccelli et pesci.
text: dress the chickens and remove the livers. combine the livers with breadcrumbs, spices, and egg yolks. moisten with broth, frequently adding more, and cook until well done. sprinkle with finely chopped sugar and serve. prepare capons in a similar manner, seasoning and flavoring them as described. prepare fish similarly, adding oil instead of lard.

title: Di romania di polli.
text: fry the chickens with lard and onions, and pound the unpeeled starch. mix it with the juice of strong or sweet crab apples press firmly and beat well, then add it to the chickens and let it simmer briefly, stirring with a spoon or whisk. add spices. if crab apples are unavailable, make a broth with herbs.

title: Di agliata bianca con li capponi.
text: remove the cooked capons and, with the broth, temper spices, garlic, and almonds, simmering until the sauce is thick. this is called a white garlic sauce it loses its name if colored any other way. it can also be made with roasted and larded capons.

title: De' blanmangieri.
text: remove chicken breasts, cooked and place them on a table, slicing them as thinly as you can. meanwhile, wash the rice and dry it, grinding it into flour. sift the flour through a sieve or fine cloth then mix it with goat's milk, sheep's milk, or almond milk, and bring to a boil in a well-washed and clean pot. when it begins to boil, add the sliced chicken breasts, along with white sugar and fried lard watch it carefully, avoiding smoke, and simmer gently, without a strong fire, so that it becomes thick, as rice usually is. when it s ready, add chopped or crushed sugar and fried lard. if you wish, you can prepare it with whole rice, arranged and presented with goat s milk, in the foreign style and when you serve it, top it with fried almonds and sliced white ginger. alternatively, for lent. remove almonds, peeled and blanched with

title: De la festiggia.
text: remove whole fried chickens, fry them in lard then simmer them in water with sugar and ginger and thicken the sauce.

title: A empiere un pavone.
text: pluck the peacock, leaving the head with its feathers. then remove lean pork and pound some of the peacock meat, or another meat, and grind and pound them together. also pound spices, cinnamon, and nutmeg, whichever you prefer grind these finely and pound them with egg whites, mix them well with the spices and meat, and set the yolks aside. then stuff the peacock with the ground and pounded meat and spices. wrap the peacock in a pork casing, securing it with wooden skewers. place it in a pot of warm water and simmer gently. when it has shrunk from simmering, roast it on a spit or grill, and color it with the beaten egg yolks that you set aside. don't use all the yolks, but make small apples from the rest, as follows remove raw pork loin and grind it very finely with a knife, then beat it well. mix the meat with the reserved egg yolks and spices, and form it into thick patties that fit between your palms

title: A empiere una gallina.
text: pluck the chicken, remove the skin, and combine its meat with ground pork, spices, eggs, and clear lard. fill the chicken skin with this mixture, then simmer in boiling water in a large pot. roast on a spit, being careful not to let it dry out. this method can be used with other birds as well. alternatively, skin the chicken as described, seasoning the meat with spices. take an earthenware pot shaped like a pumpkin, that is, a molded or flask-shaped one. place the skin inside the pot, keeping the chicken s neck protruding from the rim. fill the skin with the prepared filling, then tie off the neck and add a little water. cover and cook until done. when cooked, break the pot and serve.

title: A empire uno vitello.
text: remove the young veal, skinned or peeled, and roast it. stuff it as you wish you can put in it pigeons, chickens, and capons, and the stuffing mentioned above, and any other good ingredients. however, put a lot of pounded lard in its belly. then, remove the fat that falls off when it s roasted and combine it with toasted bread and saffron let the sauce simmer briefly on its own and serve.

title: A empire uno castrone.
text: you can prepare a whole castrated pig as described for the chicken dish, and for its stuffing, you can use whole cooked chickens or partridges, or any other good ingredients you desire be sure to prevent it from bursting. you can prepare a young, peeled goat in a similar way.

title: A empiere una spalla, o altro membro.
text: remove the shoulder of castrated boar and remove the meat from the bone, and remove the pork belly, and grind them all together, pounding them with a knife on the table. then take fragrant herbs in abundance, pepper, with spices and saffron, and mix them with the meat and pork belly. add fresh cheese, well ground with eggs, in a good quantity temper it so that it is not too thick nor too soft. then take a sheet of pork or castrated boar skin and spread it on the table, and spread half of the meat over it. next, take the bone from the shoulder and place it on the meat then take the other half of the meat and place it over the bone on the other side, so that the bone is in the middle, and cover everything with the said skin. then place it on a grill and roast it until done, and serve. you can do the same with the other cuts.

title: A empiere un ventre.
text: clean a pig's belly or castrated boar, washing and trimming it well. then remove the fat and some of the meat, cooking it slightly. mix this with spices, eggs, and stuff the belly with this mixture, then cook it in water, covering the opening and pricking it with a skewer while it cooks. alternatively, you can roast it on a grill, coloring and flavoring it to your liking. you can also fill it with good pork belly, along with whole ravioli. similarly, you can fill any fowl you desire.

title: A empiere budelle.
text: you can stuff pork or veal sweetbreads with pork fat and other meats, along with spices and fragrant herbs, and proceed as described for the tripe, binding and skewering them then serve.

title: De la suppa.
text: remove round-cut bread, like small boards fry it in a pan with fresh lard and sprinkle with good spices, then remove the toasted bread and mix it with the fat that has dripped from peacock or other birds, and sprinkle it over the fried bread in the pan then sprinkle with sugar or acidic juices and eat. alternatively, remove round-cut bread as mentioned above, and dip it in beaten egg yolks and fry it in the pan. then arrange it neatly on plates, one piece next to the other and, if you wish, you can add sugar or spices, and serve with peacock or other birds.

title: Del pastello romano.
text: take chicken pieces, spices, and saffron, and fragrant herbs mix them together and fry them lightly. then add beaten eggs and verjuice in abundance. meanwhile, prepare the pastry crust. assemble the pie, making two or three layers, and place spices on each layer. on top, add lard and cover the pie, then make a hole around the center. form birds or other animals of dough and fill them place lard inside. bake in the oven and serve. a similar method can be used with fresh ricotta and ground meat.

title: Del pastello dei capretti.
text: cut the kid goat and seps well and fry with lard. also, add a generous amount of fragrant herbs and saffron, and pound vigorously, along with fresh ricotta, finely chopped, and mix it with the meat. place in a dish over the embers, making it somewhat thick. then make the dough in the pan thinly, and spread some fried lard between the dough and the pan. add pepper sufficiently and the meat with the eggs mentioned, place in the pan, and make another layer of dough, then cover with it. place embers above and below. alternatively, take minced kid goat or small chickens, chopped, and fry them with fresh lard and chopped onions, fragrant herbs chopped with saffron and egg yolks, and mix vigorously. bind with eggs, and place everything in a dish over the embers, turning it frequently until it is thick.

title: Del pastello di uccelli vivi.
text: make a pastry and fill it with semolina, and bake it in the oven and when it is cooked, pour out the semolina through a hole underneath or from the side, and enclose inside as many live birds as you wish and make windows in the pastry, like the windows of a cage and once this is done, place it in the tree that will be indicated. otherwise, a good pastry. if you want to make a pastry of wild animals, roast the meat and lard it as you wish soak it with wine with a greater abundance of spices. otherwise. you can make the pastry with beef, castrated bull, and pork, finely chopped with garlic, onions, shallots, chicory, or with herbs, as you wish.

title: De la torta parmesana.
text: remove the disjointed chicken pieces and cut them, then fry them with finely chopped onions, using a generous amount of lard. once the chicken is cooked, season with plenty of spices and salt. remove the fragrant herbs, add a generous amount of saffron, and grind strongly... a generous amount, and place the marrow on top of the fat, pounding it vigorously with a knife. then, combine it with the aforementioned herbs and a little grated cheese, making it thick and rich. next, remove another quantity and make ravioli. also, remove fresh cheese and make white ravioli. remove parsley and other fragrant herbs, fresh cheese, and make green ravioli, combining all the above with eggs. remove blanched almonds, pound them strongly, and divide them into two parts in one, add plenty of spices, and in the other, sugar. make ravioli, alternating between the two parts. then, add eggs and fill them. also, remove well-fattened

title: De la torta di capponi, fagiani, uccelli, coratelle e pesci.
text: you can also make a cake with capons, pheasants, guinea fowl, wild and domestic birds, small and large, with coral paste and with sea fish and river fish, and with apples, and similar things on fasting days, and with fish pounded with spices, with almond milk and eggs and flavor and color it as you wish.

title: De la casciata.
text: drain the fresh ricotta, wash it thoroughly, and press it well. then crumble it finely with your hands into a bowl. add the eggs and beat them well with the ricotta and ground lard, and a little pepper if you like. season with salt and bake. if mint or catnip is added, it s called erbata. it can also be made with scallions and squash, and it s possible to make this dish without a crust on top.

title: Del coppo di polli o d'altri uccelli.
text: disassemble the chickens or birds. mix the flour with warm water and make a very stiff dough. then shape the dough into a large, flat pastry shell. place the poultry inside with uncrushed sorrel, saffron, and spices, and a little cold water. cover with more of the dough and bake in the oven or between hot plates. top the pastry shell with a large piece of lard.

title: Del coppo d'altre cose, e da ciascun giorno.
text: you can make a similar dish with beef or pork, as mentioned above. if you lack sour ingredients, you can use juice from lemons, oranges, and rosewater. you can also make coppo with venison and other meats, and with kid goat sweetbreads, fragrant herbs, spices, and saffron, diversifying and coloring them as you wish and with chickpeas, beans, pumpkins, and other mixtures that are used in pastries.

title: Del pastello di anguilla.
text: skin, wash, and clean the eels, then cut them into pieces. prepare a hard crust and place it inside. season generously with spices, then drizzle with a little oil and orange juice, citron or lemon juice. cook between two hot surfaces and serve hot, as it is best.

title: Del coppo di lampreda.
text: remove the lamprey, washing it well, and pound it with salt do not cut or fillet it. insert a clove into each hole in the head. once the hard pastry crust is made, place the lamprey inside in a circular fashion with spices and saffron. add a little pink-tinged water, color the top as desired, and cover it. a similar method can be used for smaller lampreys without cloves, with pink-tinged water and juice from lemons, oranges, or limes. alternatively, the lampreys can be roasted and eaten with sauce.

title: Del pastello de le trote e d'altri pesci.
text: shape the pastry dough into a long, trout-like form, or round if you prefer. remove the trout and prepare it well, scaling, washing, and salting it. for the filling place it inside the dough. add spices, finely chopped, with saffron and oil, and seal the dough according to the trout shape, forming horns at each end like small boats. make two holes in the dough, one near the head and the other near the tail, or make one hole in the middle. bake in an oven or on a griddle. once well cooked, insert rosewater through the holes, or orange or lemon juice. when serving with meat, use crumbled lard instead of oil. similarly, you can make it with pastry shells or pies filled with other fish, such as sardines, anchovies, mullet, and others, using the same method.

title: Del polpo.
text: a large octopus can be boiled and eaten with salt and cumin, or other fish similar to octopus, which are called moscatelli.

title: De la seppia.
text: remove the cuttlefish, open it, and extract the ink, reserving it. then, finely chop the cuttlefish and fry it in oil with spices. once fried, add a little water and simmer it. dilute the reserved ink, known as cuttlefish ink, with good wine and add it to the broth along with fragrant herbs and spices. serve.

title: Del nero e de la seppia.
text: to prevent the squid ink from scattering, bind it tightly at the top. smoke it, so that when you wish to make sauce, flavouring, broth, or another black dish, you can use it. note, as mentioned, in each sauce, flavouring, or broth, you can add precious things gold, precious stones, select spices, or cardamom, fragrant or common herbs, onions, leeks, as you desire, for the healthy and the sick.

title: Del pesce calamaro.
text: to roast squid, hollow out the insides through the ears. season the inside of the ears with salt, or through the mouth, leaving space as if it were a sword, and cook it briefly near the fire. then lard it thinly and carefully, as if it were a pheasant, and roast it again until done, serving it with orange juice, bergamot, pink grapefruit, or lemons.

title: De l'interiori e budelli di pesci.
text: fry the fish innards, washed and coarsely chopped, in olive oil with thinly sliced onions. add spices, saffron, and chopped marjoram. moisten with a little boiling water and remove a piece of stale bread, finely chopped and moistened with a bit of water, and simmer briefly. if you prefer, you can use cumin instead of marjoram. if you wish to make this broth frequently, use unblanched and ground almonds, mixed with wine. strain the mixture, omitting the saffron, and sprinkle with coriander seeds and meat, finely chopped with sugar.

title: De la gratonata di polli.
text: disassemble the chickens, fry them with lard and onions and while they are frying, add a little water so that they cook well in the pot, turning them often with a wooden spoon. add spices, saffron, and verjuice, and bring to a boil. for each chicken, remove four egg yolks and whisk them with the verjuice, then bring to a boil. whisk everything together in a bowl, and cook everything together with the chickens. once cooked, remove from the heat and serve.

title: De sardamone di carne.
text: remove the castrated boar meat, from the breast chop finely and bring to a vigorous boil. when cooked, to remove any gamey taste, drain the water and fry the meat with lard. then add enough of that water until only a little broth remains when cooked, add finely chopped coriander and carrots, with spices and saffron to taste. if you don t have coriander, use cumin, and serve.

title: De la fromentiera col pollo.
text: start with good wheat, or other good grain, and pesto. grind them together in a mortar, well-washed. in the evening, set it to simmer and when it begins to crackle, add a plump hen or a good, warm castrated boar breast to the pot. cover it well and serve it like this until morning. in the morning, remove the hen or the meat, and set it aside on a cutting board, and serve it. cook the wheat with goat s or sheep s milk, adding rendered lard or fat. then remove the meat and strip it from the bones, and make soups. top with fried lard. this is good food, and if you don't have milk, make it with eggs and cheese.

title: Del farro di spelta.
text: remove the hulled and cracked spelt and boil it briefly. drain the water and rinse the spelt thoroughly, then return it to the pot and cook with goat's milk, sheep's milk, or almond milk until tender. chop fresh ricotta and mix it with egg whites, then add it to the simmering spelt and cook for a short time. you can add chicken or poultry meat, prepared like blancmange. top with pork fat if you wish to make it yellow, color it with saffron and egg yolks, and sprinkle with sugar.

title: De la zeunia di colombi, polli e altri uccelli.
text: when you slaughter chickens, pigeons, or other fowl, reserve the blood and livers. then, butcher them and fry them with onions and pork fat. add dried oregano, finely ground and mixed with wine. remove the blood and livers from the aforementioned fowl with a little toasted bread, then pound them well and mix with vinegar and wine, coloring it thinly. bring to a boil with the fowl, adding pepper as needed. for pigeons especially, add a head of garlic. serve and enjoy.

title: De le ova piene.
text: peel, boil, and shell the eggs, then cut each in half and remove the yolks. in a bowl, combine a generous amount of saffron and cloves, then whisk them with the yolks until smooth. add grated cheese to the mixture, and for every eight eggs, incorporate one raw egg. once this is done, fill the egg whites with the savory mixture and fry them in good lard. serve with french verjuice. fried, roasted, and beaten eggs are so well-known that they require no further description.

title: Dei tomacelli, ovvero mortadelle.
text: remove the pork liver and boil it. then, remove it and chop it finely on the table with a knife, or grate it with a coarse grater. add marjoram and other fragrant herbs, generously seasoned with pepper, to the chopped liver. in a mortar, mix the liver with eggs until it is thick. then, take strips of pork belly and cover them in small, rounded mounds of the liver mixture, frying them separately in a pan with lard. once cooked, remove them and place them in a clean pot. add spices with saffron and pepper, diluted with good wine, and simmer everything together in the pot. serve hot.

title: De li fegatelli.
text: remove the liver, cut it into pieces, and roast it on a spit. when it's not quite cooked, wrap it in pork netting and continue cooking. once cooked, place it in a new pot and season it, as mentioned previously wrapping each piece of liver separately in the pork netting improves the flavor.

title: Del coppo di latte caprino, o pecorino.
text: remove white flour, work it into a dough like a cap, and place it in molds so that it is firm. then, take milk with beaten eggs, along with saffron, and pour it into the molds, carefully sprinkling it over. you can break fresh eggs into it as well, since they will cook in the milk.

title: De la gelatina di pesci senza oglio.
text: bring wine and vinegar to a boil, then add the well-cleaned fish to cook. once cooked, remove and set aside. in the same wine and vinegar, add sliced onions and boil until the liquid reduces to a third of its original volume. then stir in saffron, cumin, and pepper, and pour everything over the cooked fish. allow to cool. this is a tavern dish.

title: Del giardino.
text: for grand feasts and holidays, create a tree, a vine, or a garden from pasta. decorate the tree with apples, pears, birds, grapes, or whatever you desire, all made from pasta dough mixed with eggs. fill them with the aforementioned fillings and color them with various colors, such as yellow, green, white, and black. to honor the tree, place a small pastry or a cage filled with birds in the center. you can adorn the tree with any fruits that are in season. when bringing it into the courtyard, build a large wood fire beneath the tree and add fragrant sprigs display them lavishly.

title: Del dulcamine, cioè frittelle non quaresimali.
text: roll out a dough made with flour, eggs, and water until very thin. cut it into leaf shapes or fig shapes, or however you like, and fry it in plenty of lard or oil. once cooked, serve with boiled apples and enjoy.

title: De li erbati.
text: you can make a savory dish with cheese, eggs, and spices, using any of the flowers and herbs mentioned, and bake it in the oven or between heated plates. the crust will be called erbata.

title: De le lasagne.
text: take good, white flour mix it with warm water until it's thick. then roll it out thinly and let it dry. cook in capon broth or another rich meat broth, and then place it on a dish with grated, fatty cheese, as much as you like.

title: Del mele bullito co le noci, detto nucato.
text: remove the simmered and skimmed apples, along with walnuts and spices, cooked together moisten your hand with water and spread the mixture out. let it cool and serve. you can add almonds and hazelnuts instead of walnuts.

title: De li tortelli.
text: you can make any shape you like from pasta, such as horses, buckles, rings, letters, and any animal you desire. you can also fill it, if you wish, and cook it in a pan with lard and oil, and with fish, coloring it as you please.

title: De la ioncada.
text: remove pure, clear, strained milk and add a piece of kid or lamb. when it has thickened, wash it well and simmer it between green branches, offering it to the lord. alternatively, place it in cold water until serving time.

title: De la paniccia col latte.
text: remove any stones and sand from the legumes and wash them well. bring them to a boil with a little water, then add enough milk, along with some rendered lard or fried pork fat, and color it as you like. you can eat this dish with roast kid.

title: Dei savori: e prima del savore per l'arrosto.
text: pound basil in a mortar and pestle, adding pepper and working it into a paste with verjuice. this flavor is good with every roast and boiled egg if verjuice is unavailable, use oranges, mandarins, or lemons.

title: Dei savori con li pippioni
text: roast the young pigeon livers and gently simmer them. then, pound them in a mortar with pepper and toasted bread soaked in wine or vinegar, and blend to a paste. if you wish to boil it, you may otherwise, serve it raw.

title: Del savore con la grua.
text: remove the crane's liver and roast it over the embers then take bones, spices, marjoram, saffron, and the said liver, and pound everything well together. add two egg yolks to this mixture, and thin it with good wine and a little vinegar then add a little cooked must, so that it is tart and sweet.

title: Savori per papari e per porchetta.
text: do as stated above, except for the cooked wine. and the fat that drips from the duck, put it in the seasoning. do similarly with roast pork and if you don t want to make that seasoning, make green sauce.

title: Savore per malardi et anatre.
text: follow the instructions above regarding the flavor of the crane however, do not add saffron for any birds found near rivers. with these things said, the discerning cook will be able to be informed in all matters, according to the diversity of the realms and he will be able to vary and color the dishes as he sees fit.

title: De la pastringa.
text: remove the fat from the ricotta and chop it finely, and take out the pork skin. mix these ingredients with flour and eggs, and blend well. add saffron, then place in pastry crusts to bake, and make it white. or, color it as you desire.

title: Del solcio dei piedi d'uccelli et di capo di porco.
text: boil the feet and heads vigorously. add vinegar in a generous amount, along with sage leaves, and serve. it can be preserved for fifteen days, during the winter. similarly, prepare these ingredients as described above, and when the meat is almost cooked, add vinegar to the water, enough so that it is neither too strong nor too weak. bring it to a boil until it reduces to a third of its original volume, in time for summer. then place the meat in another vessel. add bay leaves, and remove the spices and saffron. moisten with the aforementioned broth. pour the broth over the meat, and add finely chopped chives. season with salt to taste, and serve. if you don't have chives, use cumin instead. you can prepare aspic with pork, chickens, or other birds as you desire.

title: Del cascio arrostito.
text: remove the rind, whether from a goat, buffalo, or other tender and fatty animal. clean it thoroughly and, if very fresh, wash it. then, pierce it with a split stick or place it on a skewer, and cook over the fire until it begins to melt or slide off with the heat. serve it on thinly sliced bread or on a platter, and bring it to the table.

title: Dei cauli per li 'nfermi.
text: simmer the cauliflower briefly in plain water, and cook the castrated boar separately. then remove the cauliflower and the boar meat, and place everything in a pot. simmer well, adding parsley, and cook as desired for the sick.

title: De l'erbe minute.
text: boil spinach, borage, parsley, chard, dill, and similar greens. drain the water, then pound them very finely on a board. cook with almond milk, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.

title: Per li costipati, stitici, e che non orinano.
text: remove the spinach, along with a few fennel bulbs, parsley, and borage. also, mallow, thoroughly washed bring to a boil, then chop and cook with castrated boar meat. cabbage is also a purgative for the sick. remove cauliflower florets from young cauliflower plants and add them to the broth in which the capon was cooked, and simmer well, adding a little salt. even on days of fasting, remove cauliflower florets with fennel, and simmer with oil, milk, and saffron.

title: De le zucche.
text: remove young pumpkins, wash them well with hot water, and squeeze them firmly. then, cook them with almond milk. note that delicate foods made from herbs and leaves for the sick can be cooked in the broth given to them.

title: Dei ceci per l'infermi.
text: use red or white chickpeas cook them with oil, salt, and pepper. add saffron and a little rue pound in a mortar and eat. alternatively, use broken chickpeas and boil them. drain the water and place them in fresh water to cook with oil, lard, salt, saffron, spices, beaten egg yolks, and a little cheese. combine all ingredients and serve.

title: De le lattuche.
text: halve the lettuce leaves and cook them without salt then, place them on a cutting board and serve with green sauce or seasoning.

title: Dei peselli freschi per li 'nfermi.
text: remove the young peas, thick milk, and almonds, and add a little salt. then, make a well-composed pastry crust. add sugar if you like, and bake. serve warm.

title: De l'amandolato et del farro per li 'nfermi.
text: remove the almonds and blanch them grind them and dilute with boiled water, then place milk in a saucepan to heat with breadcrumbs or farro. add egg yolks and continue to grind or mix, then incorporate saffron, sugar, and a pinch of salt.

title: De la tria genovese per li 'nfermi.
text: put the pasta in boiled almond milk, and a little salt, and serve.

title: Riso per li 'nfermi.
text: cook the rice in the water used to boil the kid's trotters, then add almond milk and sugar.

title: De la farina per infreddati.
text: bring water to a boil with four ounces of marshmallow root and two ounces of sugar while it boils, gradually add white flour, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon, and let it cook well, then cool. you can also cook it for the sick, with fowl, fish, according to their health, simply boiled or in broths, as mentioned above, and administer with scrambled eggs and many other things.

title: De le triglie per li 'nfermi.
text: pan-fry the triggerfish with parsley and saffron, and serve.

title: De' pomi lessi per li 'nfermi.
text: peel the apples, then slice them. let them cool and give them to the sick person.

title: De' pomi arrostiti.
text: wrap the apples in their skins and place them over low heat let them cook, then slice them put them in wine and give them to the sick person. alternatively, from the aforementioned cut the apples in half and remove the seeds inside, and fill those empty spaces with pounded sugar. then cover the apples and roast them on a spit so they appear whole and when they are well roasted, give them to the sick person. roasted meat is more flavorful than boiled, because it is cooked in its own juices, while the latter is cooked in another's.

title: A cocere prestamente e bene uno arrosto.
text: remove the embers and cook with them when they are well lit, pour wine over them, and they will last longer and burn more fiercely. also, remove oil and lard, mix pesto and chopped herbs together, and grease the meat with it.

title: De la insalseggiata di cipolle.
