text: peel onions, cook them over low heat, and then peel them. slice them lengthwise into thin strips. add a little vinegar, salt, oil, and spices, and serve.

title: A trarre il sale de la pentola.
text: place a loaf of bread wrapped in white linen cloth or some say flour into the pot. alternatively, if you suspend it near the broth, it will absorb the salt.

title: A cavare il fumo del mangiare.
text: place a perforated walnut in the pot, and it will draw the smoke to itself.

title: Frittelle nuove.
text: grate some breadcrumbs and prepare a fine herb sauce with mint and parsley. whisk the eggs and combine with the sauce, then fry in fresh lard or pork fat in a pan. drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: A chi non avesse levame.
text: crumble a piece of bread and grate it, then mix it with flour this won't make good bread, but it will produce good yeast.

title: A fare agresto.
text: remove the lees, that is, sediment from white wine pound it well. cook it with wine or water, and it will be sour.

title:
¶ A Proper
newe Booke of Cokerye,
declarynge what maner of
meates be beste in season,
for al times in the yere,
and how they ought
to be dressed, and
serued at the table,
bothe for
fleshe dayes,
and fyshe 
dayes.
text: to make a tart of quinces. take a pound of quinces, peel them and core them, and saw them in slices. then take a quarter of a pound of fine sugar, and a dram of saffron, and a spooneful of rosewater. set the quinces in a pot with a little water, and let them simmer till they be tender. then straine them, and put them into a pewter pot, and lay the sugar to them, and the saffron, and the rosewater. stirre them well together, and set them in a bain-marie, and stirre them often till the sugar be dissolved. then put them in a tart pan, and bake it in a moderate oven till it be through.

title: ¶. THE BOOKE OF COKERYE.
text: brawn is best from forty days before michaelmas until lent. beef and bacon are good all times in the year. mutton is good at all times, but from easter to midsummer it is worst. a fat pig is ever in season. a goose is worst in midsummer moon and best in stubble time, but when they are young green geese, then they are best. veal is best in january and february, and all other times good. lamb and young kid are best between christmas and lent, and good from easter to whit-tide. kid is ever good. hens are good at all times but best from november to lent. fat capons are ever in season. peacocks are ever good, but when they are young and of a good stature, they are as good as pheasants, and so are young grouse. snipes are best between all hallows day and lent. a mallard is good after a frost, until candlemas, so is

title: ¶. The fyrste course.
text: potage or stewed broth. bold meat or stewed meat. chickens and bacon. dried beef. pies. goose. pig. roasted beef. roasted veal. custard.

title: ¶. The seconde course.
text: roast lamb. roast capons. roast geese. chickens. fowls. baked venison. pie.

title: ¶. The fyrste service at supper.
text: a salad. a pig's head. dried beef, sliced. a mutton shoulder or a breast. veal. lamb. custard.

title: ¶. The seconde coorse.
text: roast capons. roast conies. roast chickens. roast pigeons. roast larks. a pie of pigeons or chickens. baked venison. tart.

title: ¶. The seruice at dyner.
text: braised fowl or poultry in white broth. a venison forcemeat on toast. a beef joint and a breast of mutton boiled. small pies filled with fine mutton. three young geese in a dish, with sorrel sauce for a goose, mustard and vinegar. after all hallows' day, a swan sauce with shredded cabbage. a pig. a double rib of beef roasted, with pepper and vinegar sauce. a loin of veal or a breast, with sauce. half a lamb or a kid, with oranges. two roasted capons, with wine and salt sauce, or ale and salt sauce, unless served with bread. two pastries filled with venison in a dish. a custard. a dish of blancmange.

title: ¶. The seconde course.
text: jelly. peacock sauce with wine and salt. two rabbits or half a dozen hares sauce with mustard and sugar. half a dozen chickens on sorrel leaves. half a dozen pigeons. mallard. tail quail stork heron s show crane curlew bittern. bustard. pheasant sauce with water and salt, and sliced onions. half a dozen woodcocks, sauce with mustard and sugar. half a dozen partridges, half a dozen tails, sauced as the pheasants. a dozen quail. a dish of larks. two pasties of red deer in a dish. tart. gingerbread. fritters.

title: ¶. Service for fyshe dayes.
text: butter. a salad with hard eggs. soup of sand eels and lampreys. red herring, green and broiled, scattered upon. white herring. lunge. haberdine with mustard. salted salmon, minced. sauce of mustard, verjuice, and a little sugar. powdered conger. shad with vinegar sauce. mackerel. whitefish with sauce made with the liver and mustard. plaice, sauce of sorrel, or wine and salt, or mustard, or verjuice. thorneback with liver and mustard sauce, pepper and salt scattered upon, after it is bruised. fresh cod with green sauce. bass. mullet. eels on toast. rockfish on toast. perch. pike in pike sauce. trout on toast. tenche in jelly or in caper sauce. custard.

title: The seconde course.
text: flounders or flounders in pike sauce. fresh salmon. fresh conger. brete. turbot. sauce, vinegar. halibut. bream on toast. carp on toast. soles or any other fried fish. roasted eels. sauce, dripping. roasted lampreys. roasted perch. sauce, galantine. fresh sturgeon. creves. crab. sauce, vinegar. shrimps. baked lamprey. tart. cheese. figs. raisins. apples. pears. blanched almonds.

title: ¶. To dresse a Crabe.
text: first, remove all the legs and heads, then take all the fish out of the shell and make the shell as clean as you can. put the meat into a dish and butter it on a warming dish of coals. add cinnamon and sugar and a little vinegar. when you have warmed and seasoned it, put the meat back in the shell again. crush the heads and place them on the dish alongside it, and serve.

title:
¶. To make a stewed broath for 
Capons, mutton, beyfe, or any other
hoate meate, and also a
broathe for all maner
of fresh fyshe.
text: take half a handful of rosemary and as much of thyme, and bind it on a bundle with thread after it is washed, and put it in the pot after that the pot is cleanly skimmed, and let it boil a while, then cut slices of white bread and put them in a large platter and put it on the same scalding broth, and when it is soaked enough, strain it through a strainer with a quantity of wine or good ale, so that it is not tart and when it is strained, pour it in a pot and then put in your raisins and prunes, and so let them boil until the meat is enough. if the broth is too sweet, put in more wine or else a little vinegar.

title: ¶. To make Pyes
text: fine minced mutton or beef, seasoned with pepper and salt, and a little saffron for color. add a good quantity of suet or marrow, a little vinegar, prunes, large raisins, and dates. use the fattiest part of powdered beef broth. if you desire royal pastry, combine butter and egg yolks, and temper the flour to make the pastry.

title: ¶. To bake Veneson.
text: do not use anything but pepper and salt, but let it have enough. and if the venison is lean, lard it through with bacon.

title: ¶. To Rooste Veneson.
text: roast venison must have vinegar, sugar and cinnamon, and butter boiled in a warm dish with embers, but the sauce should not be too tart, and then place the venison upon the sauce.

title: ¶. Chekins upon Soppes.
text: take a generous amount of sorrel sauce and add cinnamon and sugar. let it boil, then pour it over the croutons, and then arrange the chicken pieces on top.

title:
¶. A Pyke sauce for a Pyke, Breme,
Perche, Roche, Carpe, Eles, Floykes and al
maner of brouke fyshe.
text: take a bunch of rosemary and thyme and bind them together, adding a quantity of parsley that is not bound. put these herbs into a pot with water, salt, and yeast, and let them boil for a while. then add the fish and a generous amount of butter, and let them boil for a good time, and you will have good pike sauce. for all the fish mentioned above, if they must be broiled, make a sauce of butter, pepper, and vinegar and boil it in a chafing dish. then place the broiled fish on the dish. but for eels and fresh salmon, use only pepper and vinegar over boiled fish. and if you wish to fry them, take a generous quantity of parsley after the fish is fried, and put it into the frying pan to fry in the butter. take it up and place it on the fried fish, along with plaice, whitings, and other fish, except eels, fresh salmon, and conger, which are

title: ¶. To make a Custarde.
text: to make a custard, the mold must first be hardened in the oven, and then take a quart of cream and five or six yolks of eggs, and beat them well together. put them into the cream, and add sugar, small raisins, and sliced dates. line the mold with butter or marrow, but for the dates, use butter.

title: ¶. To make cleare Jellye.
text: take two calf's feet and a shoulder of veal, and set it over the fire in a clean pot with a gallon of water and a gallon of claret wine. let it boil until it becomes jelly, then remove it and drain the liquid. add cinnamon, ginger, and sugar, and a little turnsole to color it to your liking.

title:
To make a dyschefull of
Snowe.
text: take a pint of sweet, thick cream. beat the whites of eight eggs with a spoon, then add them to your cream along with a small bowl of rosewater and a dish full of sugar. take a stick and clean it, then cut the end into a four-sided shape, and use it to beat all the ingredients together. as the mixture rises, remove it and place it in a sieve. once this is done, take one apple and place it in the center, along with a thick sprig of rosemary. set this in the middle of the platter, then spoon the mixture over the rosemary, filling the platter with it. if you have wafers, scatter some among the mixture and serve.

title: To frye Beanes.
text: take your beans and boil them, and put them into a frying pan with a dish of butter and one or two onions, and let them fry until they are brown altogether, then sprinkle a little salt upon them, and then serve them forth.

title: To make Panne puffe.
text: to make the dough for stock fritters, take some ale and a little yeast and sugar, mace, and saffron. heat it in a chafing dish and add it to your flour with the yolk of a raw egg, and then in this manner make your dough.

title: To make Blewe manger.
text: take a capon and remove the breast meat. partially boil the breast meat until the flesh comes from the bone, then dry it as thoroughly as you can in a clean cloth. next, use a pair of cards to shred the meat as finely as possible. then take one pint of milk and one pint of cream, and half a pound of rye flour, along with the shredded capon meat, and put all into a pan. stir it all together and set it over the fire. when it begins to boil, add half a pound of powdered sugar and a spoonful of rose water, and continue to boil until it is very thick. then transfer it to a serving dish and let it cool. you may then slice it as you would a pie and serve it.

title: ¶. To make pyes of grene apples.
text: take your apples and peel them cleanly, then core them as you would a quince. next, make your pastry in this way take a little warm water and half a dish of butter, and a little saffron, and set all of this in a warming dish until it is hot. then mix your flour with this liquid, and the whites of two eggs, and also make your pastry. season your apples with cinnamon, ginger, and enough sugar. then put them into your pastry and lay half a dish of butter on top, and seal your pastry. bake them.

title: ¶. To bake chekins in lyke paest.
text: take your chickens and season them with a little ginger and salt, and then put them into a baking dish. add barberries, grapes, or gooseberries, and half a dish of butter. cover the dish and set it in the oven. when the chickens are baked, take the yolks of six eggs and a dishful of verjuice and strain them. place the strained mixture on a warming dish, then add the baked chickens to it. serve them hot.

title:
¶. To bake pygeons in short paest as you
make to your baken
apples.
text: season your pigeons with pepper, saffron, cloves, and mace, along with parsley and salt. then put them into pastry, and seal them up. bake them they will bake in half an hour. afterward, take them out, and if you think them dry, add a little parsley and butter and serve them.

title: To make vautes.
text: take the veal kidney and boil it until it is tender, then chop it finely with the yolks of three or four eggs. season it with chopped dates, small raisins, ginger, sugar, cinnamon, saffron, and a little salt. for the pastry, take a dozen eggs, both whites and yolks, and beat them well together. then take butter and put it into a frying pan, and fry them as thin as pancakes. lay your filling within, and fry them together in a pan, and sprinkle sugar and ginger on top. serve it forth.

title: ¶. To make pescoddes.
text: take marrowbones and remove the marrow. cut it in two pieces, then season it with sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and a little salt. make your paste as fine as you can, and as short and thin as you can. then fry them in sweet butter and sprinkle with a little cinnamon and ginger, and serve them at the table.

title: To make stock frytures.
text: use the same ingredients you would for a pâté, and you can either fry them or bake them.

title: To Stewe Trypes.
text: take a pint of claret wine and set it upon the fire, and cut your tripe into small pieces. add a good quantity of cinnamon and ginger, and also a sliced onion or two. let them boil for half an hour, and then serve them on toast.

title: To make a pye of alowes.
text: take a leg of mutton and cut it into thin slices, and for the stuffing, take parsley, thyme, and savory and chop them small. then mix in with them three or four yolks of hard-boiled eggs, chopped small, and small raisins, dates cut with mace, and a little salt. lay all these in the steaks and then roll them together. once this is done, make your pie and place all of this inside. season them with a little sugar and cinnamon, saffron, and salt. then sprinkle over them the yolks of three or four hard-boiled eggs and chopped dates, with small raisins. close your pie and bake it. for a syrup to serve with it, take roasted bread and a little claret wine and strain them together. add a little sugar, cinnamon, and ginger, and put it into your pie, then serve it forth.

title: To make short paest for tarte.
text: take fine flour and a handful of fair water and a dish of sweet butter and a little saffron, and the yolks of two eggs and make it thin and as tender as you may.

title: To make a tarte of beanes.
text: take beans and boil them until tender in clear water, then remove them and mash them in a mortar and strain them with the yolks of four eggs, curd made from milk. season it with sugar and half a dish of butter and a little cinnamon, and bake it.

title: To make a tarte of goseberies.
text: take gooseberries and partially cook them in white wine, claret, or ale, and boil with a little white bread. then, take them out and press them through a strainer as thickly as you can with the yolks of six eggs. season with sugar, half a dish of butter, and bake it.

title: To make a tarte of medlers.
text: take medlars when they are overripe, and mash them with the yolks of four eggs, then season with sugar and cinnamon and sweet butter, and bake it.

title: To make a tarte of damsons.
text: take damsons and boil them in wine, either red or claret, and add a dozen pears, or else white bread, to make them stiff all through. then thicken it with the yolks of six eggs and sweet butter and bake it.

title:
¶. To make a tarte of borage
floures.
text: take borage flowers and boil them gently, then strain them with the yolks of three or four eggs and sweetened curds, or else take three or four apples, and boil them with wine and strain them with sweet butter and a little mace, and then bake it.

title:
¶. To make a tarte of marigoldes
prymroses or couslips.
text: use the same ingredients and seasoning for each as you would for a borage tart.

title: To make a tarte of strawberyes.
text: take and strain them with the yolks of four eggs, and a little white bread grated, then season it up with sugar and sweet butter and so bake it.

title: To make a tarte of Cheryes.
text: to make the tart, use only damsons, without any pears.

title: ¶. To make a tarte of spinage.
text: take spinach and boil it until tender. then take it up and squeeze out the water cleanly, and chop it very finely, and set it upon the fire with sweet butter in a frying pan and season it, and set it in a platter to cool, then fill your tart and so bake it.

title: ¶. To make a tarte of Chese.
text: take hard cheese and cut it into slices, and pare it, then lay it in fair water or in sweet milk for the space of three hours. then take it up and break it in a mortar until it is small, then draw it up through a strainer with the yolks of six eggs, and season it with sugar and sweet butter, and so bake it.

title:
¶. To make a stewe after the guyse
of beyonde the sea.
text: take a potful of fair water, and as much wine, and a breast of mutton chopped into pieces. then set it on the fire and skim it clean. next, add a dishful of sliced onions and a quantity of cinnamon, ginger, cloves, and mace, with salt. stew them all together, and then serve them with bread for dipping.

title: ¶. To make egges in moneshyne.
text: take a bowl of rosewater and a dish full of sugar, and set them upon a warming dish, and let them boil. then take the yolks of eight or nine freshly laid eggs and put them thereto one by one, letting each harden a little. after this manner, serve them forth and sprinkle with a little cinnamon and sugar.

title: ¶. To make Applemoyse.
text: take a dozen apples and either roast or boil them, then push them through a sieve. mix in the yolks of three or four eggs, and as you sieve them, stir in three or four spoonfuls of orange flower water. if you wish, season with sugar and half a dish of sweet butter, and boil over low heat in a shallow dish, set on a platter. sprinkle with biscuits, cinnamon, and ginger, and serve.

title: ¶. To frye Trypes.
text: take your tripe and cut it into small pieces and put them into a pan. add one or two onions and a dish of sweet butter, and let them fry until they are browned. then take them out and set them upon a chafing dish and add a little parsley and ginger, and serve it.

title: To make a tarte of Prunes.
text: take prunes and place them in a slow cooker. add a little red wine and put in a muffin. let them simmer together, then press them through a sieve with the yolks of four eggs and sweeten with sugar. then bake.

title:
¶. To make a couer tarte after the 
frenche fashyan.
text: take a pint of cream and the yolks of ten eggs, and beat them all together, and add half a pound of sweet butter, and sugar, and boil them until they are thick. then take them up and cool them in a platter, and make two cakes of fine pastry, and place your filling in one of them and cover it with the other, and cut the top open, and then bake it.

title: ¶. To stewe capons in whyte brothe.
text: to make your broth, take four or five beef bones, then remove them when they are cooked and strain the broth into another pot. put in your capons whole with rosemary and let them stew. after they have boiled a while, add whole mace wrapped in a white cloth, a handful or two of whole parsley and whole prunes, and let them boil well. when serving, add a little vinegar and salt, and sprinkle them upon toasted bread and the marrow bones around, with the marrow laid whole above them, and serve.

title:
¶. For Gusset that may be another
potage.
text: take the broth of the capons and put it in a fine pan. then take a dozen or sixteen eggs and beat them all together, whites and all. grate a quarter loaf of white bread as finely as you can, and chop it with the eggs together. add salt and a generous amount of saffron. before adding the eggs, put into the broth thyme, savory, marjoram, and parsley, finely chopped. when you are ready for dinner, set the pan over the fire with the broth, let it simmer a little, and add the eggs. stir it well to prevent lumps. the less it boils, the more tender it will be, and then serve it with two or three slices on a dish.

title: ¶. To make a whyte broathe.
text: take a neck of mutton and fresh water, and set it over the fire, skimming it clean. let it boil until the liquid has reduced by half. then, remove two ladlefuls of broth and place them in a dish. chop two generous handfuls of parsley, not too finely, and let it boil with the mutton. next, take twelve eggs and the aforementioned two ladlefuls of broth, and strain them together until the mixture has a tart flavor from the strained ingredients. season the broth with salt, and just before serving, add all of these ingredients to the mutton, stirring well to combine. serve with bread for dipping.

title:
¶. Another broathe with
longwortes.
text: take mutton and clear water, and let them boil over the fire. then add lettuce or spinach, and if you wish to boil with it two or three chickens, add salt and vinegar to your liking, and serve it forth, the meat below, the herbs above.

title: ¶. To make a Frasye at nyght.
text: take chicken heads, livers, giblets, wings, and feet, and chop them into pieces about half an inch long. boil them all together, and when the broth is nearly gone, chop a little parsley and add it along with verjuice and half a dish of butter. let them boil, and make it tart enough, and then serve.

title: ¶. To make Shoes.
text: take a piece of beef and let it boil for an hour or two, and add a large quantity of kale and let them boil together for three hours. then add a couple of woodcocks or teals, pheasant, or other wild fowl, and let them boil all together. season them with salt, and serve.

title: ¶. To make Porraye.
text: take a capon or a hen and beef or mutton to flavor the broth, and boil them together until very tender. then remove the capon or hen from the pot, and take out all its bones, grinding it in a mortar with two pounds of blanched almonds. strain the broth from the capon or hen, making it quite thick, then put it into a small pot. season it with a little sugar, sandalwood, cloves, mace, and small raisins, and boil it. serve with toasted bread.

title: ¶. To stewe bones or gristels of biefe.
text: take beef tendons and stew them until they are very tender, about six hours, until there is no broth left. then place a generous bundle of rosemary in a clean linen cloth, and a good amount of mace in another cloth, and boil them all together. after that, squeeze the juice from the rosemary and mace over the meat, and season it with salt, and serve.

title: ¶. For to stewe mutton.
text: take a neck of mutton and a breast to make the broth strong, and skim it clean. when it has boiled a while, take some of the broth and put it into another pot and add a pound of raisins. let them boil until they are tender, then strain bread with the raisins and the broth all together. chop thyme, savory, and parsley with other small herbs, and put into the mutton. then add the strained raisins with whole prunes, cloves, and mace, pepper, saffron, and a little salt. if you wish, you may stew a chicken with it, or else sparrows or other small birds.

title: To stewe stekes of mutton.
text: take a leg of mutton and cut it into small slices, and put it in a sauté pan. add a pint of ale and simmer until clear. then add seven or eight onions, thinly sliced, and after they have boiled for an hour, add a dish of sweet butter, and let them simmer until tender. finally, add a little pepper and salt.

title: ¶. For to make wardens in Conserue.
text: first, make the syrup in this way take a quarter of good quince and put in a pint of clarified honey, and a pound or half a pound of sugar, and mix all those together over the fire until they boil, and then set it to low heat. and this is a good syrup for many things, and will be kept a year or two. then take your quinces and scrape cleanly away the bark, but pare them not, and boil them in good red wine so that they are well soaked and tender, that the wine be nearly absorbed into them. then take and strain them through a cloth or through a strainer into a vessel, then add to them of this syrup aforesaid until it is almost filled, and then add the powders, such as fine cinnamon, cinnamon, powder of ginger, and such other spices, and put it in a box and keep it if you wish, and make your syrup as you wish to work with, as if you wish to work with twenty

title: CAPITOL PRIMER PER FER CONFEGIR PONSEMPS
text: take the quince and grate them, and make them into patties. wash the peel and the pulp, and put them to soak for eight or nine days, changing the water every day. after eight or nine days, put them to boil until they are a pale white. then take them off the fire and plunge them into cold water, either in a bowl or a pot, and after three or four days, boil them again until they are very white. then plunge the quince into cold water. afterwards, drain them in a strainer and let them sit for two or three days until they are well drained of water. then take the said quince and put them in a pot or bowl or some other earthenware vessel. make the said vinegar, and when it is made, pour it over the quince. this vinegar is to be made in this way you will take honey as much as you need and add half a bowl of water to it. then put the quince on the fire and boil it for

title:
CAPITOL SEGON PER CONFEGIR CARABASAT
O SINDRIAT
text: take the squashes and cut them into slices, and when you have made them, make them wide and good slices. and then remove from them the crust from above and below, all the pulp inside until the flesh is white. and, after making your slices, put them in a pot or saucepan with a wide mouth. in this way, make a layer of salt, another of squashes until it is high or until there are no more. and then put a good stone on top, and, two weeks before you want to prepare it, or during lent, take it out of the salt and put it in water for 8 or 9 days, changing the water every day. and then taste it to see if the squash is very sweet and not salty at all, and then give it a boil with water until it is a little white. and then take it off the fire and pour cold water over it in some bowl or saucepan and after 3 or 4 days return it

title: CAPITOL TERCER PER CONFEGIR AMETLLES
text: take the almonds and put them in a pot with spring water, and place them over the fire to boil them for 4 or 5 boils until they are soft. then remove them from the heat and, with a cloth, peel them and rinse them in cold water. once all are peeled, drain them in a sieve and prick them with an awl. then take the said almonds and put them in a pot or saucepan and add the syrup, pouring it over the said almonds. as is said, for 8 days, let them rest and remove the syrup, giving them one boil, and as soon as it boils, pour the syrup over them again. do this as many times until you know they are ready, and then cook everything with the said almonds until you see the syrup boil and bubble. you will need 1 lb of almonds and ½ lb of honey.

title:
CAPITOL QUART PER CONFEGIR TERONGETES
E LIMONS
text: take the oranges and lemons and prick them with a skewer in a cross shape, and put them in water. for eight days, change the water every day. after eight days, put them to boil with water and boil them until they are slightly soft. remove them from the heat and throw them into cold water, letting them sit for two or three days, changing the water every day. then, return them to boil with water and boil them until you can insert your nail and they are well soaked. then, remove them from the heat and throw them into cold water. afterwards, take them out of the cold water and place them on a drying rack, letting them sit for three or four days until they are well dried. then, take ginger and cloves and soak them in red wine, inserting them through the holes. once done, put them in an earthenware pot or pan. add the previously mentioned syrup and pour it over the oranges, and check them every eight days. remove the syrup

title: CAPITOL .V. PER CONFIGIR CODONYS ENTREGUES
text: take the walnuts that are delivered and pound them, and remove the kernels. boil them in water. once boiled, spread them out on a table and season them with cloves, ginger, and soaked cinnamon, as has been said, with rosewater. once done, place them in an earthenware pot or pan. then, add the previously mentioned aserop and sprinkle its juice over the walnuts. for eight to eight days, recognize them. remove the aserop and give them a sprinkling of boiled pearls without the walnuts. then, take it off the heat, and when it is warm, sprinkle the walnuts over it again. do this as many times as you need until you know they are ready. then, take the aserop and the walnuts, all together, and cook everything until you see the aserop begin to sprout. you will need 1 pound of walnuts and 3 pounds of honey.

title:
CAPITOL .VJ.e PER CONFEGIR CODONYAT O CRAN
DE CODONY
text: take the plums and dry them in the oven, and after they are well cooked, peel them, and once peeled, remove all the flesh around, leaving only the stone. then take all the flesh and pound it in a stone or earthenware mortar, and after it is pounded, take all the pounded flesh and strain it through a cheesecloth. then weigh it and see how much it weighs, and for every pound add as much honey. then cook it until it thickens, and when you want to take it off the heat, sprinkle it with a little rosewater, as you do with all other preserves. in every pound of plums, use a pound of honey.

title: CAPITOL .VIJ.e PER CONFEGIR PONSEM RAS
text: take the mushrooms and grate them with a grater that the grocer will lend you, and once it is grated, put it in a cloth bag and soak it in water for seven or eight days, changing the water every day, ensuring no water remains. and so it stays for eight or nine days, and after those eight or nine days, boil it in a pot of water and then strain it over the grated mushrooms. in this way, take the cloth bag with the grated mushrooms and wring it out very firmly, so that no cold water remains. then, let the water boil and pour it over, and after having done that, wring it out firmly and spread it on a rush mat for two hours. and after you have it well-boiled, add the honey to it and let it sit for that day and night, and then cook it until it thickens. you will need 3 pounds of mushrooms and 3 pounds of honey.

title: CAPITOL .VIIJ.e PER CONFEGIR LO RAVE GUALESCH
text: take the large parsnips and peel them well with water. then grate them finely and place them in a pot with water, and add a good handful of salt and boil until very soft. then remove the parsnip and place it in cold water for eight or nine days, changing the water every day. and when it is well drained, boil your honey, and, well skimmed as said, place it with the honey or syrup and boil strongly until the syrup thickens and forms threads. you need one pound of large parsnips, five pounds of honey.

title:
CAPITOL .VIIIJ.o PER CONFEGIR LA REYLL
DEL PENICALT
text: take the artichoke and clean it well with water. once clean, cut it into pieces and remove the choke, and once the choke is removed, soak it in cold water for eight or nine days. afterwards, bring it to a boil with water until it is tender, and then remove it and place it in cold water, and then spread it out on a dry, heated mat for a whole day. once that is done, take the said artichoke and place it in an earthenware pot or pan with iron, and sprinkle the prepared vinegar over the said artichoke, as has been said, for eight or nine days. then remove the artichoke and add a sprig of boiling sage, and once it is warm, sprinkle the vinegar over it again, and do this as many times as needed until you know it is done. then cover everything, the artichoke and the vinegar, until you see the artichoke sprout shoots. you will need one pound of artichoke for half a pound

title: CAPITOL .X. PER CONFEGIR BESTONAGUES
text: take the mussels and scrub them very well. once clean, put a pot of water on the fire and, when it boils, add the mussels. when they open, remove them and, with a cloth, rub them well until they are cool. then, make them into chopped pieces and, once chopped, take the said mussels and put them in an earthenware pot. prepare the vinegar as follows. you will need honey, and in two pounds of honey, put a small cup of water, and let it boil for three or four times. when it is lukewarm, pour it over the said mussels, and for three or four days, leave the vinegar and the mussels. then, put them over the fire and cook until you know the vinegar has thickened, but be careful that the mussels with the honey are left standing for two days before adding the vinegar. you will need one pound of mussels for six pounds of honey.

title: CAPITOL .XJ. PER CONFEGIR PRESECHS
text: take the plums and pierce them with a skewer, and when they are pierced, boil them with water. when they are boiled, remove them and place them on a rush mat so that the water drains well for two or three hours. afterwards, put them in a clay pot and sprinkle over them the aforementioned aserop. after two or three days, you will have everything the plums and the aserop, and boil two or three bulbs. and once that is done, if the aserop is not tight enough, remove it from the pot and boil it until it bursts, and then sprinkle it over the plums. you need one pound of plums and one pound of honey.

title: CAPITOL .XIJ. PER CONFEGIR POMES
text: take the apples and prick them with a knife, and once pricked, place them in a clay pot or pan. then, add a handful of your sorrel on top and sprinkle salt over it, because the apples do not boil, but for eight days it all remains together until the sorrel forms shoots as mentioned. you will need three handfuls of apples and three handfuls of honey.

title: CAPITOL .XIIJ.e PER COMFAGIR PERES
text: take pears and pear them, and when they are pearled, boil them with the aforementioned vinegar, two or three measures. afterwards, for eight days, let them soak and remove them from the vinegar, giving them one measure of pear juice, and when it is tepid, return the pears to it. do this as many times as you know it is done. afterwards, cook everything together until you see the vinegar start to bubble. you will need one pound of pears and one pound of honey.

title: CAPITOL .XIIIJ.e PER COMFAGIR NOUS VERDES
text: take walnuts and shell them, and once shelled, line them with a cross-shaped skewer. put them in water for eight or more days, changing the water fresh every day. after eight or more days, put them to boil with water and boil them until they are slightly soft. remove the walnuts from the heat and throw them into cold water, and let them sit for two or three days, changing the water every day. then, return the walnuts to boil with water and boil them until you can insert a fingernail and they are very soft. then, remove them from the heat and throw them into cold water. after that, remove them from the cold water and place them on a mat spread out and let them dry for three or four days until they are thoroughly dried. then, take ginger and cloves and soak them in rosewater, piercing the walnuts through the holes. when that is done, put them in an earthenware pot. prepare the syrup as described below, for the

title: CAPITOL .XV.e PER CONFEGIR DATILLS
text: take the dates and, at the thinner end, insert a twig or straw, and at the thicker end, remove the stem. then, have ginger and cloves and steep them in warm water, and put the ginger inside the date at the thicker end, and at the thinner hole, insert the clove. once done, place them in an earthenware pot or bowl and cover with syrup made as dried fruits and apples are. and you should sprinkle a little on top. after 2 or 3 days, cover everything together, the syrup and the dates, until you see the syrup begin to bubble. you will need 1 pound of dates and 1 pound of honey.

title: CAPITOL .XVJ.e PER CONFEGIR SIRERES GENOVINES
text: take genoese lemons, neither too green nor too ripe, and place them in a pot or earthenware dish. add honey in equal measure. to all the honey you use, add a ladleful of water and two or three spoonfuls of broth. once this is done, let it sit for a month. at the end of the month, add a spoonful containing the lemons and the zest. you will need one pound of lemons and one pound of honey.

title:
CAPITOL .XVIJ.e PER FER LA RASEPTA DE LA COMPOSTA 
DE L AXEROP E DELS CONFITS
text: to make candied fruit for approximately 17 pounds of preserved fruit, proceed as follows 3 pounds of dried plums and 3 pounds of orange peel, 3 pounds of raisins, and a half pound of welsh turnip. then, for all the other preserved fruits, follow these steps. first, take 2 ounces of finely ground mustard and dilute it with a little vinegar and a small amount of olive oil, just enough to dilute the vinegar, and let it sit for 2 or 3 days like this. next, take the preserved fruits and place them in a jar or pot. add 11 ounces of finely chopped and weighed cinnamon first, put a little cinnamon in the jar, then a layer of the preserved fruits, and another layer of cinnamon until all the fruits are combined with the cinnamon. let it sit like this for 2 or 3 days. after that, take all the juice from the said fruits and put it all in a large pot, adding

title: CAPITOL .XVIIJ. PER CONFAGIR PONSEMPS EN SUCRE
text: to make quince paste, do it in the form and manner in which it is to be made and boiled. and after they have been spread and drained from the water for two or three days, take the said quince and put them in a pot or other vessel and add the aserop, and when it is made, pour it over them. this aserop is to be made in this way you will take as much quince as you want to make, and, as it is weighed, you will see how much sugar you must take, equal to the weight. and when you have the sugar, put it in a pot, and in one and a half pounds of sugar, put a quarter of a pound of fountain water, along with a third of a pound of rosewater. and when all the ingredients are there, put it over the fire and cook until you see it beginning to bubble. have a hen's egg shelled and take the white and put it

title: CAPITOL .XVIIIJ.o PER FER PINYONAT
text: to make pine nut brittle, take as many cups of pine nuts as you wish, ensuring they are clean, free of shells, stones, or any impurities. you will also need half a cup of pine nuts and two cups of sugar. combine all the sugar with a small amount of rosewater and bring to a boil. once boiling, add the pine nuts and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until well combined. spread the mixture evenly on a clean surface. allow it to cool and then cut into squares or round shapes as desired.

title:
CAPITOL .XX.e PER CONFEGIR CARABASSAT O SINDRIAT
EN SUCRE
text: to make candied or dried pumpkin, proceed as follows boil and drain it from the water for two or three days. once drained, place it in a pot or other vessel and add the sugar mentioned previously. when this is done, remove the foam that forms on top and pour it over the candied or dried pumpkin, simmering until it is candied. then, remove everything that is, the candied or dried pumpkin and the syrup and boil it further until it thickens.

title:
CAPITOL .XXJ.e PER CONFEGIR TERONGETES O LIMONS
O PONSEMPMETS EN SUCRE
text: to prepare courgettes, lemons, or preserved plums, do it as follows, as i have already told you when making the honey syrup for the aforementioned courgettes or lemons, in the way they are to be made and boiled and drained, and laid out on a rack for three or four days until they are dried. take the courgettes, lemons, or preserved plums and place them in a pot, and make them with the aforementioned syrup from the preserved plum sugar, and when it is made, pour the syrup over them, letting it soak until it is absorbed. then, cook them until they are candied. afterwards, take everything together, that is, the syrup and the courgettes or lemons or preserved plums, and boil them until they thicken. and you will need in one pound of preserved plums or lemons, two pounds of sugar.

title:
CAPITOL .XXIJ.e PER CONFEGIR CODOYNS ENTREGUES
EN SUCRE
text: to make candied citrons, do as follows first, prepare the honey syrup as described when making the honey syrup for those citrons, in a way that it is to be boiled. once the citrons are drained and dried on a cloth, place them in a pot and cover them with the aforementioned honey syrup. once the syrup is made, pour it over the citrons and simmer until they are candied. afterward, remove everything that is, the syrup and the citrons and boil until it thickens.

title: CAPITOL .XXIIJ.e PER CONFEGIR PRESECHS EN SUCRE.
text: to make candied fruit, do it as i have already told you in the making of the honey syrup for the aforementioned candied fruit in the following manner boil them, and spread them on a table for two or three hours. afterwards, place them in a pot and pour the aforementioned syrup over them, after the sugar has been added. once it is made, sprinkle the lemon zest over the candied fruit. and to know when they are candied, take everything out that is, the syrup and the candied fruit and boil it until it forms a thread.

title: CAPITOL .XXIIIJ.e PER CONFEGIR POMES EN SUCRE
text: to make apples, you must pare them with a knife. once they are pared, put them in a pot and add the water behind the amount of sugar. when this is done, pour the syrup over the apples. and you will know they are candied when you take everything out that is, the syrup and the apples and boil it until the syrup makes a thread.

title: CAPITOL .XXV. PER CONFEGIR PERES EN SUCRE
text: to prepare pears, you will take them and pare them with a knife. once pared, place them in a pot and make a syrup with water and sugar. when it is made, pour the syrup over the pears. then, in the morning, give them a boil with the syrup and pears all together. afterwards, when you see they are candied, return them to the heat and boil until the syrup thickens.

title: CAPITOL .XXVJ.e PER CONFAGIR DATILLS EN SUCRE
text: to make dates, you must prepare them as described below in the making of the honey syrup for the said dates. proceed in this way first, make the syrup as you would for the honey syrup for the dates, and place them in the pot. after making the syrup, add the sugar to it, and once it s done, pour the syrup over the dried dates. you will know they are candied when, taking everything together that is, the syrup and the dates you boil it until the syrup thickens.

title: CAPITOL .XXVIJ.e PER FER ALOSSES
text: to make almond candies, determine how much you want to make. for 4 or 5 pounds, in one pound of sugar, take half a pound of water, a mix of rosewater and spring water, equally. heat it until it begins to thicken. then, have two pans of middlings ready, soaked in a little rosewater. once soaked and dampened, add it to the boiling sugar, stirring gently, and cook it until it s as thick as tallow. for a pound and a half of sugar, you ll have marzipan that is already made from almond flour. divide it in half, placing one half in one container and the other half in another. in this way, make as many as you wish, multiplying the quantities as needed. if, by chance, you need it for chest ailments or another condition, add one denier of sweet olive oil per pound.

title: CAPITOL .XXVIIJ.e PER FER MERSEPA
text: to make mersepa, you will take almonds and blanch them. after blanching, wash the almonds. then, spread them on a cloth over a bowl and place them in the air in a well-ventilated area for three or four days until they are completely dry. afterwards, take them little by little with a mortar and pestle and grind the almonds. moisten the mixture with a little rosewater so that it doesn't form oil. when everything is well ground, add one level tablespoon of sugar for every level tablespoon of almonds. return to the mortar and continue grinding and mixing. when ground, melt some sugar and drizzle it over the paste, forming little mounds. cover the mounds with the paste, shaping them into cubes about half an inch thick. then, sprinkle with plenty of sugar and salt on top. afterwards, take some clean and scrubbed lemon or orange rinds and place them inside, and take them to the oven and bake for a short while.

title: CAPITOLL .XXVIIIJ.o PER CONFEGIR GINGEBRE VERT
text: to make candied ginger, you will need as much ginger as you desire, ensuring it is good, and add the juice of lemons or limes until it is covered. preserve it in this way for an entire year. when the time comes to make it again, take it out, blanch it in water, and keep it there until it is no longer sour. afterwards, remove the water and place it in a pot, adding the sugar mentioned above. then, periodically remove the ginger and add a handful of boiling water, pouring it over and over until you know it is candied. when it is candied, drain both the ginger and the syrup until it forms a thick consistency. then, remove the ginger with a skimmer and you will see how much syrup remains, to your liking. in 12 ounces of syrup, add a white of egg with a clove, and take all the whites with the cloves and a little spring water. beat it well, and when it is well beaten

title:
CAPITOL .XXX. PER FER UN PERFUM MOLT
MERAVELLOS
text: to make a very wonderful perfume, you will take mastic gum 2 ounces. and it should be soaked for two days with rosewater and good juice of lemon and almonds. one dram of amber and storax 2 ounces. and it should be very fine, and then you will take a little musk, and when all that is ready, you will pound it all together. when it is pounded well, with a reed or with whatever you wish to perfume it, you will fill it, smoothing it, smoothing it, until you know it remains with a good fragrance. and when you have filled it, you will have a knife and make it into small tablets, and when you have made the tablets, round them into shapes like small loaves, thus made as half-baked. and as you wish to perfume, take from the loaves and make them into small pieces and so throw them onto the brazier and perfume them with whatever you wish. and if you wish

title: CAPITOL .XXXJ. PER FER PINYONADA DE MEL
text: to make pine nut paste with honey and use it for fillings, you will need pine nuts, as many as you want to make six. clean them well. once clean, take a little sago and, with a small bowl, put the pine nuts in little by little and toast them. when toasted, put them on a brazier with the sago and everything, and cover them well with a piece of wool and let them steep covered for a little while. afterwards, take them and remove them from the sago and crush them a little. take honey as much as you can handle, that is, about a spoonful per pine nut, and put it in a pot over a low fire and cook it well. then, take it from the fire and stir it in as the honey thickens and work it for a long time. afterwards, quickly return it to the fire and cook it until it is done, always with

title: CAPITOL .XXXIJ. PER FER TORONS DE AVALANES
text: to make torrons from toasted pine nuts and honey, and form them into tablets, you will take the pine nuts and toast them, and when they are toasted, you will clean them thoroughly with a piece of glass and ensure they are very clean. then, you will take honey in the amount you need, that is, about a pound of honey per pound of pine nuts, and put it over low heat and bring it to a boil, and then remove it from the heat. then, for every pound of honey, add one egg white and whisk it in as the honey is still warm, and keep stirring it for a long time. and after that, return it quickly to the heat and cook it until it is done, maintaining a low heat at all times. the consistency of the honey when it s cooked is explained in the chapter on nougat. once the honey is cooked, remove it from the heat, and take the pine

title: CAPITOL .XXXIIJ. PER FER CASQUETES
text: to make hazelnut, almond, and pine nut sweets, you will need as much fruit as you require, that is, as much hazelnut as almonds and as many dried pine nuts, and toast them. once everything is toasted, clean it well with a piece of glass. and once it is all well cleaned, crush it all into a sandy texture. afterwards, add spices, that is, 6 pounds of fruit, 3 ounces of cinnamon and 2 ounces of ginger, 2 grated nutmegs, 3 pinches of marjoram, and 3 pinches of cloves. all of this should be crushed and ground into a powder, and then incorporate it into the crushed fruit. after that, take honey, that is, for every 6 pounds of fruit, 3 pounds of honey. take the honey and melt it with a small bowl of rosewater, and as it starts to bubble, remove it from the heat and add the fruit to it, and

title: I. Amidono d' amido.
text: to make almond pudding for twelve people, you will need two pounds of almonds and one pound of starch, half a pound of sugar, half a cup of ground pine nuts, and half a quarter pound of cloves. peel the almonds well and grind them finely, then mix them with clear, boiled water. heat three parts milk to boiling point of the remaining raw mixture, add to the milk and bring to a boil. taste, then mix in the starch and a little more milk, stirring frequently and lifting it up to thicken. add sugar to taste, and sprinkle sugar, cloves, and ground pine nuts on top of the dishes. if you want to make it for more or fewer people, use the same proportions it s a perfect dessert.

title: II. Ambroyno.
text: to make ambrosia, take chicken pieces and finely chopped onions and fry them in rendered lard. add sweet and strong spices, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, and mace, all finely chopped with a knife, and lemon zest. add slivered almonds, marzipan, verjuice, and saffron, all together. when cooked, place the chicken pieces on top. for three chicken pieces, you will need about a pound of almonds.

title: III. Agliata.
text: season the meat with garlic and parsley. cook it under the grill, then crush it well and add raw garlic, a handful of breadcrumbs, sweet spices, and broth. mix everything together and let it simmer a little, then remove from the heat.

title: IV. Ambrosino bono e perfecto et cetera.
text: to make ambrosia for twelve people, take six plump capons and two pounds of almonds, and one pound of raisins, one date, and one pound of broad beans, and one and a half pounds of finely ground ginger, and half an ounce of nutmeg and cloves. and saffron threads, and half a pound of fine sweet spices, and take the capons and break them down, making seven pieces each, and put them to fry in clarified lard in a pot. and when they are well fried, the first thing you add should be the grated ginger and the nutmeg, finely chopped, cinnamon in good pieces, whole cloves, whole peeled almonds, and dates, well washed, and put in sweet spices abundance, and let it cook a little and when it is cooked, take it back when it is cooked, add the first almonds with the husks, grind them, and temper them with a little vinegar, and when the dish is cooked,

title: V. Bramagere.
text: to make bramagere for twelve people, you will need four pounds of almonds, one pound of rice, four chickens, two pounds of fresh butter, one and a half pounds of sugar, and half a quarter of cloves. use the almonds, blanch them, and use a generous amount of almonds. grind the rest, and mash them with a little clear water, straining them well through a sieve. take the rice, well-blanched and washed with hot water, and thoroughly scrubbed, that is, wiped with a cloth, and grind the spice, or pound it, and strain it. take the breasts of the chickens and poach them briefly, then shred them finely and fry them in butter over a gentle heat in a pan. put the almond milk on the fire, using two bowls. when the milk boils, temper the rice flour with some of the raw milk, and bring it to a boil, stirring constantly over the fire. immediately add the chicken pulp and shredded

title: VI. Brodo de polastri.
text: to make chicken broth, pluck the chickens and blanch them. then, add almonds, pounded and steeped in chicken broth, along with rosewater and verjuice, and combine everything well. next, add cinnamon, ginger, and cloves half whole, half finely chopped and put them into the broth. let everything simmer continuously. when it's time to serve, place the chickens in the broth and ensure they are very hot. when you serve, sprinkle sugar over the bowls, and it will be a delicious dish.

title: VII. Bon savore da polastri.
text: to make a flavorful dish with chicken, apple granates and wine, to taste, and add spices generously, put them into the wine. if it seems too strong, soften with a little pesto, otherwise rose water. others use apple and pomegranate wine, and sweet grape wine, and put these two wines together with spices very sweet. if you don t have grapes, add a little honey, and bring to a boil. the spices should be raw they shouldn't be cooked, as they spoil.

title: VIII. Brodeto de starne bon.
text: fish stew boil late and almonds, and eggs yolks, saffron, parsley, and sweet spices, until cooked through, and it will be good.

title: IX. Brodeto camelino a caponi.
text: to make camelina broth for twelve people using chickens, you will need six plump chickens and three pounds of almonds. also, two ounces of fine spices, long pepper, and grated nutmeg, well combined. salt the chickens and, when they are plucked, let them cool. take the almonds with their skins and wash them well, then grind them. temper them with the chicken broth, bring to a boil, and add a little sour wine and unripe grapes. remove the spices once they are well boiled, set aside for service, and do not put the chickens in the broth. instead, place the finest spices you can find on top.

title: X. Butiro de chaxi freschi, etc.
text: if you want to make butter from fresh cream, use as much fresh cream as you can, and when it is well whipped and tempered with clear cold water, the cream will separate skim off the fat and place it on the cutting board, and use it to season whatever you like, and in pies it will be fine.

title: XI. Butiro de grasso de mandole.
text: to make butter from almond paste for lenten or friday dishes, take three pounds of almond paste to make a cake or any dish for twelve people, and this butter can be used for tarts and other cakes. on days when meat is not eaten, soak the almonds, peeled and washed, and finely ground, and temper them with clear water, ensuring they are very well mixed. then, bring this almond milk to a boil. when it has boiled well, pour it onto a clean cloth. when the water has drained well from underneath, take a beautiful knife and remove it from the cloth, place it on a plate, and put it in the dish you want.

title: XII. Brodeto de ovi schieto, bon e perfetto.
text: if you want to make a clear broth, here's how beat the eggs and add them to chicory, cold water, and enough salt. take some broth from what you cook, whether it s meat or fish, and put it in a pot as much as you need, and place it over a low heat. add the eggs and stir often so they don t stick, and then add soup and sprinkle with good spices.

title: XIII. Brodeto de pessi.
text: cook the fish and let it cool, then add parsley and walnuts, and a little bread and pasta together. add sweet and strong spices and boil together, then place the fish on top, and it is perfectly delicious.

title: XIV. Ciuiro overo sauore negro a cengiaro.
text: to make a flavorful black sauce for pork, save, take the meat well-cooked and well-beaten and well-ground in a mortar, and breadcrumbs well-burnt that are well-soaked in vinegar and well-ground, so that they are well-drained and mixed with the ground meat. add long pepper, mace, and nutmeg, and grind these three spices very finely, and add them to the sauce with vinegar and lean broth from the meat. bring this sauce to a boil in a pot. this sauce should be black and potent with spices and tart from vinegar.

title: XV. Ciuiro over sauore a ceruo, etc.
text: if you want to make roast venison, make the flavor of the meat similar to the previous one and it is good.

title:
XVI. Ciuiro a carne de cavriolo o de livore
alesso o rosto per lo megliore che tu voy, etc.
text: proceed similarly as described above for the wild pork, and if this salad is warm, add it to the flavor if it is cold, add it as is.

title: XVII. Caponi ouer polastri impliti.
text: to cook chickens for twelve people, use fresh chickens and twelve eggs, and eleven measures of fine sweet spices, half a pound of fresh lard, and wash and clean the chickens well, then simmer them. when they are well cooked, pluck them all, remove the bones, and serve them. then beat the meat with some parsley, mint, celery, the aforementioned spices, hard cheese that you have finely ground, and enough eggs to suffice. from these ingredients, make a good, fine, soft, and well-seasoned paste. remove the bones and stuff each chicken with some of this paste, then bake them in small pork casings and fry them in lard. when they are fried, sprinkle with the aforementioned spices, then add egg yolks and spices, saffron tempered with a little liquid, and a sauce of red grape juice or gooseberries, or broth from the chickens. from these ingredients, make a good broth and bring it to a boil. when it's ready, add the

title: XVIII. Ciuiro de lepore, over de altra carne.
text: if you have good venison, hare, or other meat, wash it and cut it into pieces and set it to roast, and take bread and burn it until it is black, and put it to soak in vinegar. then take the onion and grate it well like cheese then take the meat and the onion and fry them well in rendered lard. take its liver and mash the bread well and mix it with vinegar and honey, or with a broth, and add the spices, and boil everything together. when it has boiled well, let it cool and it will be good and perfect.

title: XIX. Coradella d' agnello, etc.
text: to make lamb coratella, take the lamb coratella and roast it whole then cut it into thin slices, ensuring that one slice doesn't separate from another. next, add good herbs and red egg yolks, beaten together, and fry in rendered lard. once fried, add sweet and strong spices, and sprinkle chopped chives inside. then, place some herbs between one slice and another, and roll them up in a net or string. place them in a split cane basket and bake, and it will be good to eat.

title: XX. Coradella di chapreto, etc.
text: if you want to make a whole kid's roe, take the roe and let it rise, then beat it with a mallet, then add good herbs and blood sausage, fried in lard. stuff it inside the roe, and pound everything together, and add some fresh cheese, and add fine spices, and add three eggs, and mix everything together. then wrap it in its own membrane, then place it in a pan, and it will be delicious.

title: XXI. Composta bona e perfetta.
text: to make good compote, take sour cherries or pressed grapes and anise, and fennel, and coriander, and nutmeg and a little mustard, and vinegar, and mix everything together, and add saffron to taste then add turnips or pears and herbs and gentle pastry, and boil a little, then remove that scum from the top.

title: XXII. Cime de vitte.
text: to make fried borage blossoms, take the twisted blossoms and blanch them briefly when they are slightly cooked, drain them well and fry them with plenty of fat. then add verjuice, parsley, and water, along with spices and salt mix well and pour over the blossoms, letting them simmer. next, add a little sage, diluted with water, and pour over, and it will be delicious.

title: XXIII. Cisame de pesse quale tu voy.
text: to cook and fry fish, to boil eggs and prepare them a little, then cut them into small pieces and fry well. then remove vinegar and water, and blanched almonds. mix in raisins, strong spices, and a little honey, and bring everything to a boil together, then place over the fish.

title: XXIV. Formentra bona e utille perfetta.
text: if you want to make polenta, take the cornmeal, and grind it well until the husk rises then wash it well, then put it to boil, not too much, then throw away the water, then put it into the fat from the meat that you roast, and let it be often, not too much, and add spices, both sweet and strong, and saffron, and if you don't have cornmeal, use flour it will be good.

title: XXV. Fongi.
text: if you want to make fritters, take dried fongi beans and soak them in warm water, washing them well. then boil them and cook them as you like and season them. next, add onions and herbs and season with sweet and strong spices. then put the beans inside and fry everything together. add unpeeled and finely chopped almonds, and then place them on top of the fritters. some people like them with verjuice and served hot.

title: XXVI. Fritelle da Imperadore magnifici.
text: to make fritters like an emperor, you will need egg whites and pieces of fresh cheese, and beat them with egg white. add a little flour and pine nuts. heat a pan with oil, let it boil, and make the fritters. when they are cooked, sprinkle them generously with sugar and keep them warm.

title: XXVII. Fritelle de fiore de sambugho, etc.
text: grind the elderflower and milk together. let it soak well, then strain it. grind it well and add a little flour and temper with egg and some of the milk. then, have the pan with plenty of butter and fry. when they are cooked, cover with sugar and good cream.

title: XXVIII. Fritelle bianche.
text: to make white fritters, with almond paste and semolina flour, mixed together. let them rest, then make the fritters. when cooked, sprinkle with sugar and they are delicious.

title: XXIX. Fritelle de pome per quaressima.
text: peel and core the apples, then slice them thinly, like wafers. make a batter with flour and butter, and add raisins. dip the apple slices into this batter then fry them individually in oil. sprinkle with sugar while they are still hot.

title:
XXX. Gelatina de polastri,
overo de pesse. chiamase peverada e bona.
text: to make chicken or fish jelly, cook the chicken until it s halved and browned, then shred it. crumble bread crusts and soak them in vinegar. add raisins and blanched almonds, and grind everything together. moisten with ripe wine and oil, and add all the best spices you can find, ground. boil together with the fat from frying the chicken. once it has boiled, pour it over the chilled chicken.

title: XXXI. Gelatina de zaschuna carne.
text: to make good jelly from any meat use wild boar meat, ears and feet, and every part, capons, chickens, thrushes, hares, deer, and pheasants remove these parts and put them in a pot with water and vinegar. when it boils and is well skimmed, add spices, pepper, cinnamon, and grated ginger, together with as much mace as there is meat. as the meat cooks, remove it as it s done, leaving behind ears or feet if there s not much substance. when everything is taken out, grind all the spiced meat into a powder, and put the jelly back on the fire and let it rest, then add saffron and mix it with the jelly. place the meat in a vessel and surround it with bay leaves, then pour this jelly mixture over it, along with the saffron and stamens. once it s layered over the meat, add sweet spices and temper them with the same jelly, and sprinkle

title: XXXII. Gelatina per un altro modo.
text: to make jelly, you ll need ginger, long pepper, mace, cloves, raisins, and musk almonds. grind these ingredients together with saffron. then, take bread and remove the crust, add large hazelnuts and toast them in live embers. combine all these ingredients and thin with fine white wine. bring this mixture to a boil. it is good with eels and lampreys, and with every kind of saltwater fish. if it s for meat, it s good with capons and chickens, etc.

title: XXXIII. Gellatina communa e bona de pesse.
text: to make fish jelly for twelve people, take three large conger eels, two sprats, of strong and sweet spices together, and half a quarter of saffron for that and the fish well washed and left in the sun a little, cook it in part water and vinegar, and bring it to a boil. and when it is well boiled, the first thing you add, add some of the said spices and saffron, and everything, and let it simmer gently, and strain it well. when it is cooked, take it out and let it cool have as many laurel leaves as possible, well washed and ground with the said spices, and then the fish and preserve it in the vessel, and let it rest. others boil the saffron, others do not. when the jelly is a little cooled, pour it over the fish, and add spices to taste, and it is done, etc.

title: XXXIV. Herbe battute perfecte e bone, etc.
text: to make perfect herb patties, take peeled and ground almonds and strain them, and then add eleven ounces of rice flour and then remove the breasts from the capons and shred them finely, and then put the almond milk to simmer, thinned with the rice flour, and add the capons and the shredded meat within, and let it boil well and when you have cooked it, sprinkle it with sugar and other powdered spices. and if you don't have rice flour, add almonds powdered as much as needed to make it thick, and so on.

title: XXXV. Herbetella, etc.
text: to make cooked herb sauce in a pan, take mint and sage, and parsley and marjoram, and any good herb you can have, pound everything together in a mortar, and mix with egg yolk and lard, and then cook in the pan with some fat.

title: XXXVI. Herbetella de quaressima.
text: to make herbette for lent, with oil, that is, herbs spinach, chard, parsley, mint, and a little marjoram well cleaned and washed, and let them wilt. when they are cooked, drain the water and squeeze them well by hand, then chop them with a knife, then crush them with a pestle. put them in a pot and sauté them with oil and enough salt to taste then add that cooking water on top, and let it thicken until it s well combined, then lift it up and let it rest. when serving, sprinkle with spices.

title: XXXVII. Lenolata over Enolata.
text: peel and finely chop the potatoes, then mash them with raw pork belly, fresh ricotta cheese, and eggs. form a crust, place it in a frying pan, add melted butter, and cook.

title: XXXVIII. Lasagne.
text: to make lasagna for lent, cook the lasagna sheets and grate some cheese, and add walnuts, peeled and finely ground, and mix them in with the lasagna, and protect them from the smoke and when they are brought to the table, add broth and a sprinkling of spices and sugar.

title: XXXIX. Manzare de pomo bono e perfetto.
text: peel, core, and quarter the apples, and let them soften. when they are almost cooked, drain the water, then place them in the fat from the roasted meat, and cook them in the same way you cook squash. sweeten with spices to your liking and add whipped egg as you desire.

title: XL. Migliaciti bianchi e vantagiati, etc.
text: to make white migliaciti, the best way to do it, if you can, for twelve people, is to use a starter that s quite risen, about a loaf and a half. use a little warm water, not too much, until it forms a stream. then use four fresh eggs that are very fatty and use two pounds of fresh butter, finely ground with a little heat, well strained. when the starter is well worked, add in a small bowlful of flour, and a little water, and add three finely chopped onions, and add the eggs you have. make this mixture long and soft, and place it in a warm, well-buttered baking dish. sprinkle the two finely chopped onions on top, and the other half of the fat, very hot, and let it cook. if you are making it for more or fewer people, use the ingredients in that way.

title: XLI. Mandolata cocta e perfetta.
text: to make candied almonds for twelve people, you will need three pounds of almonds and half a pound of sugar. peel the almonds well, wash them thoroughly, and dry them completely. sprinkle them with a little clear water and drain well. bring to a boil in a pot until they thicken, and add the sugar little by little. if you are making it for more or fewer people, use the same proportions.

title: XLII. Mostarda e mostarda bona.
text: to make mustard, use the fat that comes off roasted chickens or other meats, along with mustard seeds and grind them well. when ground, mix them with boiling water, then add cooked wine and continue grinding everything together, letting it simmer slightly. alternatively, to make a delicate mustard, chop and wash the turnips thoroughly, rinsing them well with hot water and mixing them with a cooked broth. add sugar and a pinch of ground cloves.

title: XLIII. Manzare de rape.
text: boil the turnips with the small greens, and cook them. when they appear nearly cooked, drain the water and add plenty of grated cheese, and let it boil well together. when they are cooked to your liking, add more of that cheese on top of the plates.

title: XLIV. Malmoma, etc.
text: if you are making a large quantity for twelve people, prepare the ingredients in the same way as they are prepared for a branda, except that you want it to be very sharp and citrusy with orange or lemon zest, and with all those ingredients that go into a branda, similarly for so many people.

title: XLV. Mortarolo per XII persone.
text: to make a pounded dish for twelve people, you will need six chickens and four fresh leeks, chopped. also, sixteen eggs, half a pound of ground almonds, one date, half an ounce of ginger, finely grated, half a quarter pound of cloves, and three ounces of pine nuts. prepare half a pound of fine sweet spices. stuff the belly of a pork loin and simmer it, cooking it well. take the leeks you have and a portion of the spices, along with a quantity of parsley, mint, and sage. make a good pounding with these ingredients. when the pounding is done, make half tortelli, ravioli, and fried pasta in fresh, rendered lard. when they are fried, sprinkle with the aforementioned spices. add the chickens, shred them, and fry them in the pan. add some of the spices and, when they are fried, add the ground almonds and grated ginger, frying them briefly. add a little water so that they cook through completely.

title: XLVI. Mortadelle bone e perfette, etc.
text: to make mortadella, take the pork liver and its reticulum, or honeycomb, along with the liver itself. sauté them and when cooked, remove them. then take fresh herbs, pepper, wine, nutmeg, mace, and salt, as needed, along with the liver and these ingredients. grind them well in a mortar and make a paste, moistening it with egg and a little of the liver's juices. then take the reticulum and form the mortadella. when they are ready, fry them in good melted butter when fried, serve hot.

title: XLVII. Ove plene.
text: if you want to make omelets, take eggs and bring them to a boil and make them quite hard. when they are cooked, take them out and put them in cold water, peel them, and cut them in half, removing the yolks. then take some cheese, the best you can find, with sweet and good herbs that you have well cleaned and washed, and pound them in a mortar. when they are well ground, add the egg yolks, cheese, and spices, and put them in the mortar with the good herbs together and pound well, making a paste. mix with raw eggs until it s smooth, and put it in a pan over the fire. take the egg whites you have and fill them with this paste and cook. when they are cooked, take them out and sprinkle with sugar and serve hot. and if you want to give them flavor, remove

title: XLVIII. Pastero de quaye boni e vantagiati.
text: peel the squash and cut it in half, then hollow it out. fill it with pine nuts and walnuts, powdered mace, and lard slices. cover it and when cooked, add moscato wine and bring to a boil.

title: XLIX. Pastero de polastri.
text: roast chicken pastry disassemble the chickens. make a pastry crust and place it inside the chicken pieces. add spices and raisins, then pieces of pork fat. once cooked, beat eggs and mix them together, then pour them into the pastry. let it simmer for a while.

title: L. Pastero de pipioni.
text: roast the pigeons and let them simmer, then pluck them. next, make a crust of pastry and place the pigeons inside with sweet spices and pine nuts, slices of fatback, and verjuice. if you have time, bake it, and once it s cooked, add verjuice and it will be perfectly delicious.

title: LI. Pastero de carne de porcho optimo.
text: cut the meat finely and pound it. make a crust and stuff the meat with it, adding finely chopped onion and a little grated ginger. once cooked, add vinegar, sugar, and a little water, and bring to a boil.

title: LII. Pastero de capreto bono.
text: to make goat meat stew, cut the meat into small pieces and lightly brown it. add the meat with cinnamon powder and slices of pork fat then, when it's cooked, add broth and rosewater and let it simmer together.

title: LIII. Polastri a sumacho boni e perfecti, etc.
text: to make chicken with sorrel for twelve people, you will need twelve chickens and two pounds of almonds, and one ounce of cinnamon and ginger, and half a quarter of cloves, half a pound of nutmeg, and one pound of sorrel. put the chickens in to fry whole in rendered lard, and when they are well fried, add sweet spices and cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves, and fry well. then add a little water and the sorrel, well cleaned, and add it to soak in vinegar. remove the almonds washed with the juice and grind them well and thin with water. then add the sorrel and thin it with the vinegar that has been soaking. when the chickens are cooked with the other ingredients, add prunes well washed, strain the sorrel and the almonds separately, discarding the pulp, and add the remaining ingredients to the chickens and bring to a boil with sweet spices and enough water and salt. this dish will be of sorrel and spices and saffron, and sour

title: LIV. Polastri in brodo bianco.
text: to make chicken in white broth for twelve people, use chicken pieces sufficient for eight. take two and a half pounds of almonds, one and a half ounces of grated white ginger, one and a half pounds of sugar, and one and a half pounds of fresh beans. cook the chicken and when it is cooked, take some fresh lard and sauté it. when sautéed, add grated ginger, sugar, cinnamon, cloves, and a little lemon juice and enough water to flavor it. bring to a boil for a short time and then return it to the pot to serve as a soup. place the chicken in the broth, and when serving, portion the chicken with a serving spoon. the dish should be both tart and sweet.

title: LV. Panicata con agresta.
text: to make panichata with sorrel, take pounded bread, well-washed zest, and well-cleaned two pounds of almonds well-cleaned and finely ground, and tempered with clear water, and three geese and marrows roasted, and soften over the fire the almond milk, two parts and the breadcrumbs well-cleaned, and let it cook, and when it is well cooked, add the fat of the goose and marrow inside the breadcrumbs and more fresh fat from a pig, and a quantity of sugar and salt as needed. this dish should be as white as possible, and garnish with sugar and geese, sliced with another flavor, and should be made as described. whoever takes the goose liver and boiled egg yolks, boil them together and when they are cooked, pound them in a mortar with fine spices and temper with lemon juice and sorrel and let it cook at this flavor it should be camelina

title: LVI. Paniera cum carne bono e perfetto.
text: to make a meat pie for twenty people, you will need eight pounds of pork loin that is good and suitable for boiling. when it's cooked, beat it well and place it in a pot, then add thirty-six egg yolks and four fresh cheeses, along with some broth from parsley and spices, sweet and strong enough to flavor saffron. combine these ingredients and add them to the pot with the pastry and the ground pork to cook together. this dish should be served hot, ladled out in bowls, and sprinkled with spices. if you're making it for fewer or more people, use these proportions.

title: LVII. Polastri pini e boni.
text: to make stuffed capons for twelve people, first skewer the capons and then skin them well, and then remove everything from inside. then add one pound of almonds, well-skinned and ground, and drained. add eight ounces of candied fruit, and twelve eggs. add parsley, mint, and other good herbs, wash them well, and pound them thoroughly with cheese. add three ounces of spices, not saffron, and add the herbs and eggs together, making a paste, and thin it with almond milk until it has the consistency of fritter batter. then add the capons, well-washed and skinned, and stuff them inside the skin and flesh. then sew them up tightly so that the paste doesn't leak out, and it will be good.

title: LVIII. Pane de noxe maravigliosso e bone.
text: to make walnut bread, gather the walnuts and peel and crush them. then add some good herbs, a little grated onion, sweet and strong spices, and a bit of sugar. mix all this in a mortar with the walnuts until it forms a paste. next, add flour and make a large, wide, and thin sheet of dough, like lasagna. spread this crushed mixture on top, moisten everything together, and shape it like a loaf of bread. then, fill it so it s thin, like a flatbread. bake it in the oven and, when it s cooked, take it out and let it cool.

title: LIX. Peverada scleda zoè schutelini.
text: to make a pepper sauce, suitable for meat or fish, combine white flour and apple vinegar with enough water to make it thin. add meat broth or fish broth, ensuring it s lean and gentle. simmer with plenty of spices as needed. if the sauce is yellow, add saffron if it s white, do not add it.

title: LX. Quinquinelli zoè rafioli boni molti.
text: if you re going to make quinquinelli with almonds, peel and grind them well, and add sugar. if it's meat season, add lard and mix well with the almonds, then shape them like small ravioli and fry them in good fat when they are fried, keep them warm.

title: LXI. Rixo in bona manera.
text: to make rice pudding in the best way, use two pounds of rice and two of almonds, half a pound of sugar use good quality rice and wash it well, and the almonds, peeled and blanched, soaked and drained in a colander. put the rice in a pot with clear water when it has come to a boil and is well skimmed, drain the water into a container and add the almonds. cook over low heat, stirring frequently to prevent sticking when it begins to thicken, it will be firm on top of the almonds, and when it is cooked, add some sugar. this dish should be white and very thick, and when ready, sprinkle with powdered sugar.

title: LXII. Rafioli friti, etc.
text: to make fried ravioli for twelve people, you will need three pounds of pork loin and a bunch of fresh basil, eight eggs, and twelve ounces of raisins. also, some parsley sprigs and two pounds of fresh spinach, and four ounces of sugar. take the pork loin, cook it well, and pound it finely. wash the basil and chop it finely, and wash the raisins. combine all these ingredients and make a paste. form small, thin, and delicate ravioli and fry them in oil. when they are fried, sprinkle them with sugar and add the remaining ingredients on top.

title: LXIII. Rafioli commun de herbe vantazati.
