text: remove the pork liver and other livers and cook them in boiling water, but not too long then grate them as you would cheese. remove pork belly according to the quantity of livers and pound it very well. add a little aged cheese, a little fresh cheese, a pinch of marjoram and parsley, some raisins, spices, and two or three eggs, depending on the quantity, and grind all these ingredients together with the livers. then form large balls, the size of a walnut or an egg, and wrap each one with the pork casing. cook them in a pan with good lard and let them cook gently they should not be overcooked.

title: Per fare bon cervellate de carne de porco o de vitello giovine.
text: take lean meat, free from sinew, such as from the thigh, and some good pork or veal fat. beat it very finely with a knife as much as possible. then take some aged ricotta and a little rich ricotta, along with good spices and two or three eggs, and salt according to the quantity. mix all these ingredients thoroughly and make them a slightly yellow color with saffron. remove the large casings from the pork, clean them very well so they are thin and free from any fat, and stuff them with this mixture. tie them securely in the casings, making them long or short as you prefer they should be cooked in boiling water and will last no more than two days at best. however, if properly managed, they can be preserved for fifteen or twenty days, or even longer.

title:
Se tu vorrai fare bone salzicchie di carne di porcho o d'altra
carne.
text: remove lean and fatty meat together, ensuring there are no sinews, and chop it finely. if the meat is ten pounds, add one pound of salt, two ounces of finely ground fennel, and two ounces of coarsely ground black pepper mix these ingredients well and let them sit for a day. then, remove clean and well-prepared casings and stuff them with this meat, and hang them to dry over smoke.

title: Per fare dui piattelli di gelatina.
text: remove forty calf's feet and skin them, taking out the bones. soak the feet in fresh water for three or four hours. then wash them very well and add a jug of white vinegar, a jug of white wine, and two jugs of water. bring the feet to a simmer, adding salt as needed, and boil gently, skimming off any scum carefully. when they are half-cooked, remove one-quarter black pepper, one-quarter long pepper, one-quarter grains of paradise, one-quarter whole cinnamon, and half a quarter of nutmeg. crush all these spices coarsely, so that any that are not crushed are left whole, and add them to the feet to simmer. let them simmer until a third of the liquid has evaporated. when the feet are well-cooked, remove them and return the broth to the heat as it begins to boil, stir in ten beaten egg whites until they foam. stir once with a ladle and then strain the broth through a wool cloth

title: [Capretto arrosto in sapore.]
text: take a quarter of kid goat and prepare it well as you would roast it, lard it, and place inside a generous amount of garlic cloves. prepare wild herbs as you wish to stuff or lard them. then, remove from the fire a handful of wild herbs, two yolks, two cloves of garlic well pounded, a pinch of saffron, a pinch of pepper, and a little rich broth, and mix all these ingredients together. place them in a dish beneath the kid goat while it roasts, and baste it occasionally with this sauce. when cooked, place the quarter of kid goat on a plate and pour the same sauce over it, along with a little chopped parsley. this quarter of kid goat should be well cooked and eaten hot, hot.

title: Per far brasciole de carne de vitello.
text: trim the lean meat from the leg and slice it thinly, but not too thinly, then pound it well with the back of a knife. season with salt and fennel and place them on each corner of the slices. then, cover them and let them sit for about half an hour if you have the time. afterwards, roast them on a grill, turning them as needed, and keeping a slice of fat on top to keep them moist. these meatballs should not be overcooked and are best eaten immediately while still hot, providing a delightful taste and stimulating the appetite for drinking.

title:
Per fare figatelli de ucello, o di pollastri, o di porcho,

o d'altro animale.
text: cut veal into walnut-sized pieces and season with salt, fennel seeds, and sweet spices. wrap them in a casing of pork, veal, or preferably goat, and roast on a spit, being careful not to overcook them.

title: Per fare carbonata
text: remove the salted meat, ensuring a balance of fat and lean, and slice it thinly. cook the slices in a frying pan, being careful not to overcook them. transfer them to a serving dish and sprinkle with a little sugar, a pinch of cinnamon, and finely chopped parsley. repeat the process with cooked ham or prosciutto, adding a splash of orange or lemon juice as desired this will enhance the flavor.

title: Per cocer li turdi et farli el sapore.
text: roast blackbirds are best served with this sauce. then, take blanched and ground almonds and combine them with a generous amount of saffron to give the flavor a red hue. temper it with a little grape must and a little broth, adding plenty of ginger and cinnamon. then, pass this sauce through a sieve into a serving dish. simmer it for about fifteen minutes. when the blackbirds are cooked, place them in a small dish and pour the sauce over them. alternatively, top the blackbirds with orange or lemon juice, salt, and sweet spices.

title: Per cocer una testa de vitello o bove.
text: once the veal or beef is slaughtered, remove the head and peel it with warm water, cleaning it very thoroughly, and then cook it. to enhance the flavor, remove the offal. if you wish to roast it, roast it in the oven and stud it with garlic and good herbs, and other suitable spices to fill it out. and in this way, it is very good.

title: Per conciar el cervello d'un vitello.
text: once the head is boiled, remove the brain and crush it very finely. then remove two egg yolks, a little mustard, a little verjuice, and a little salt mix everything together with the brain. fry it in a pan with a little lard. as it begins to brown, remove it to a dish and sprinkle with sweet spices. this dish should be eaten immediately.

title: [Beccafichi arrosto.]
text: take the woodcocks and clean them very well, without removing or disturbing any of the innards. then, remove vine leaves and stuff them with salt, fennel, and a little lard. wrap the woodcocks in these leaves and cook them over hot embers for about half an hour, or less, as they cook quickly. if you want to roast them, secure four together around the spit by the head and feet. this is done so as not to damage the spit.

title: Per conciar starne al modo catalano.
text: remove the plover and roast it, and when it's cooked, take it out. then, separate the wings and the breast meat from the body of the plover. next, put a little salt into the cavity, a little sweet spice, a little pounded cloves mixed together, and a little juice of oranges, or lemons, or gooseberries. and this should be done while the plover is hot, and not overcooked, but still pink, almost bloody, that is, not very well done, and hot. turn it quickly and not slowly.

title: Per far structo de porco.
text: take fresh pork fatback, or fresh lard, and cut it into chestnut-sized pieces, adding a generous amount of salt. then, pound it very well and let it sit, pounded, for a day. afterward, place it over a low heat in a large pot. if you were to put a hundred pounds, add ten or twelve large jugs of water and let it simmer gently until it is completely melted. strain this rendered fat through a cloth. then, carefully ladle it off from the top, being careful not to scoop up any of the water that will remain underneath, and pour it into a clean jar. keep this jar in a cool place, and in this way, the rendered fat will last for a year.

title: Per far una ventresca di vitello piena.
text: take the veal belly and make an opening in the end large enough to fill it with the following ingredients aged parmesan cheese, four eggs, a pinch of cracked black pepper, a pinch of saffron, raisins, and a little chopped parsley, marjoram, and steeped mint mix all these together. then stuff them into the belly and cook it in simmering water until thoroughly cooked.

title: [Prosciutto cotto.]
text: insert the knife into the middle of the ham and hold it to your nose if the knife has a good smell, the ham is good, and conversely. if you want to cook it and make it last longer, remove some white wine, or vinegar, and the same amount of water, but it s better without the water then boil the ham in this wine until it s about halfway cooked. then remove it from the heat and let the ham remain in the broth until it is cold. afterwards, take it out, and in this way it will be good and will last a long time.

title: [Sinnata e lingua cotta.]
text: primarily, the sausage shouldn't be too fatty, and should be well-red and cooked in the same manner as the prosciutto and likewise the tongues and the fatter the tongue, the better it is. they should be cooked a little more than the prosciutto. and so, every other cured meat should be cooked in this way.

title: Per far un pastello de creste, ficatelli et testiculi di galli.
text: cut each crest into three pieces and the livers into four. leave the testicles intact and remove a little lard, finely chopping it but not pounding it. remove two or three ounces of good beef fat and beat it very well even better if you use bone marrow from a cow or the beef itself. have thirty or forty dried figs, cinnamon, and ginger, plenty of sugar, and a few raisins. mix all these ingredients together, form a pastry, and bake it in the oven or in a pan. when it s half-cooked, remove a yolk, saffron, and verjuice, beat them together, and add them to the pastry. let it stand until it is cooked through.

title: Per cocer un pipione et farlo senza osse.
text: prepare the pig's head and clean it thoroughly. soak it in strong vinegar for twenty-four hours, then wash it very well. stuff it with good ingredients and spices. boil or roast it as you prefer you will find it free of bones.

title: Per far che un pipione para due.
text: take a capon and pluck it very thoroughly, without water, being careful not to tear the skin. then remove the insides and turn the skin inside out so it remains intact, and set it aside. clean it, and stuff it full of good things, and it will look like a whole capon. next, prepare the body of the capon, and cook both capons boiled or roasted as you prefer. if you roast it, remove a little grated bread and salt. and when the capon is half-cooked, sprinkle the aforementioned bread on top then take an egg yolk and brush each capon with it, so as to create a crust, and give it a little fire to color it. in this way, it will appear as if it hasn't been plucked and so it will seem.

title: Et primo : per far bianco mangiare sopra caponi.
text: to make twelve portions take two pounds of almonds, and grind them very finely. to make them whiter, soak them in fresh water for a day and a night. then grind them very finely, and when ground, add a little fresh water so they don't release oil. next, take a breast of capon and grind it with the said almonds, and take the crumb from a white loaf of bread and soak it in a thin broth of capon grind it with these ingredients, and add a little sorrel, half an ounce of well-cleaned ginger so that it is white, and half a pound or more of sugar mix all these ingredients with thin capon broth, and strain them through a sieve into a clean bowl, and place the bowl over low heat, stirring it frequently with a wooden spoon, and let it cook for about half an hour. when cooked, add three ounces of good rosewater. then make the portions, either covering the capon or

title: Per far XII menestre de bianco mangiare a la catelana.
text: take two jugs of goat s milk and eight ounces of finely ground rice flour, and put them to boil in the milk. then take the breast of a chicken that has died that very day, and is half-cooked, and thinly slice the entire breast like hair. then put it in the mortar and do not press it more than two times with the pestle. when the milk has boiled for half an hour, add the sliced breast along with one pound of sugar, and let it simmer for about four hours this mixture must be stirred continuously with a wooden spoon from beginning to end. to tell when it is cooked, dip the spoon and it will appear viscous. then add rosewater as mentioned above and make the portions, placing a little sugar on top, and then serve.

title:
Per far un brodo consumato de capponi, o de fasiani, o starne,

o caprioli, o pipioni, o columbi salvatichi.
text: take these ingredients and clean them very well. if you wish to consume a rooster and make two broths, take a pot that holds four jugs of water and put the rooster inside, which should have all its bones broken, and place it over the fire. then add an ounce of lean salted meat, thirty or forty grains of cracked pepper, a pinch of crushed cinnamon, three or four cloves, five or six leaves of crushed sage in three pieces, and two bay leaves. let this pot simmer for seven hours until only two measures of broth remain, or less, if you want it to be flavorful. be careful not to add salt. if this broth is made for the sick, do not add salted meat, and use very few spices in this way it will be good for both healthy and sick people.

title: [Per fare dece menestre di brodecto.]
text: to make ten servings of broth-based pasta, take thirty egg yolks and good cream, and good meat broth, or capon broth which will be better, and a little saffron, and a pinch of sweet spices, and mix them together, then pass them through a sieve and place them in a bowl. put the bowl over low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. as you see the spoon begin to coat, remove it from the heat however, continue stirring with the spoon until you've said two hail marys. then, form the pasta and sprinkle with a pinch of sweet spices and season it sweet or sour according to common taste.

title: Per fare dece menestre di brodetto biancho.
text: remove half a pound of almonds, peel and grind them well, then add a little cold water to prevent oil from forming. next, add twenty egg whites, a little softened white bread, a pinch of verjuice, a little meat or capon broth, and a little white ginger, and grind all these ingredients together with the almonds through a sieve. cook it as described above in the other broth.

title: Per far brodetto verde.
text: remove everything from the initial broth, except for the saffron, and take out some chard, and a little parsley and some wheatgrass leaves if you can find them strain everything and pass it through a sieve as described above.

title: Per far zanzarelli.
text: to make ten portions remove eight eggs and half a pound of grated cheese, and one grated breadcrumb, and mix everything together. then take a bowl with a yellow saffron broth and place it over the fire as soon as it begins to boil, pour in that mixture, and stir it once with a spoon. when it seems cooked, remove it from the fire, form the portions, and sprinkle spices on top.

title: Zanzarelli verdi.
text: do as said above, and don't add saffron or those herbs from the green broth.

title: [Zazzarelli in bocchoncelli o bianchi, o verdi, o gialli.]
text: to make zazzarelli, either white, green, or yellow, prepare the dough to resemble the color you desire, and make it slightly firmer. remove a small spoonful. and when the broth begins to boil, shape the bocconcelli like fava beans, and drop them one by one into the broth.

title: [Per fare zanzarelli bianchi.]
text: to make white zanzarelli, take a little almond milk and grated white bread, and some egg white. add good meat broth, preferably from fatty chicken, to a small bowl with a little almond milk. then cook as described above.

title: Farro con brodo de caponi o altra carne.
text: to make ten portions first, clean and wash it very thoroughly. simmer it with good broth made from capon or another large chicken, and let it boil well. when it is cooked, add some good spices and remove three egg yolks and a little of the broth, slightly cooled, and blend them well together. then add them to the broth and mix thoroughly. it should be yellow with saffron.

title: Riso con brodo de carne.
text: do as it's said to do. but many don t want eggs with the rice. so, adjust this to the patron s taste.

title: Miglio con brodo de carne.
text: cook the millet with meat broth, and let it simmer gently, stirring frequently and watching it carefully to prevent it from sticking. it should become a vibrant yellow, like saffron. initially, ensure it is very clean and washed with warm water, like rice.

title: Per far brodetto de pane, ova et caso.
text: simmer the grated bread in meat broth for fifteen minutes. remove a little of the grated cheese and beat it with eggs, allowing the boiled bread to cool slightly. then, add the eggs and cheese, mixing well. this soup should be yellow with saffron and somewhat thick.

title: Per far una menestra de verzuso.
text: take four fresh egg yolks, half an ounce of cinnamon, four ounces of sugar, two ounces of rosewater, and four ounces of dried orange peel, and beat all these ingredients together very well. simmer them like broth, and it should be a little yellow. this dish is best enjoyed in summer.

title: Fava menata.
text: shell the beans, remove any damaged ones, and rinse them thoroughly. place them in a pot. once they begin to boil, drain the water and add fresh water to cover the beans by about an inch. add salt to taste. simmer over low heat, covered, until the beans are cooked and dried. then, mash them very well in a mortar. return the mashed beans to a pot to warm them. sauté finely chopped onion in a pan with a little good oil until it s cooked through but not burned. add a few sage leaves and chopped figs or apples to the oil with the onion, and let them warm. then, make the fava bean soup, drizzle it with the oil and the ingredients in it, and sprinkle with good spices.

title: Piselli fricti in carne salata.
text: take the peas with their rinds as they are, and blanch them. remove salted, cured pork and slice it thinly, about half a finger s length. fry it briefly. then add the peas to cook with the pork. add a little sorrel, a splash of must, or sugar, and a pinch of cinnamon. similarly, fava beans are fried.

title: Friger la fava.
text: remove the fava beans, sage, onion, figs, and apples as described above, and also add other good herbs, mixing everything together. fry it in a pan with oil, make it into a frittata, and once cooked, take it out and sprinkle with good spices.

title: Menestra de carne.
text: take lean veal cooked in broth and pound it finely. set it to simmer in rich broth, adding grated breadcrumbs, a little pepper, and saffron, and let it boil for about half an hour. then let it cool slightly and add egg yolk, grated cheese, parsley, marjoram, and mint, finely chopped with a little lemon juice, and beat these ingredients together. mix them with the meat, stirring gently with a spoon. this soup should be as thick as the broth. it can also be made with lamb sweetbreads.

title: Menestra de trippe.
text: first, ensure the tripe is thoroughly cleaned and washed until white. cook it well with a piece of salted meat to give it a good flavor, and without salt to keep it whiter. once cooked, cut it into small pieces and add a little mint, sage, and salt. simmer briefly. then, prepare the soup and add spices and grated cheese to taste.

title: Menestra de trippe de trute.
text: roast them very well and ensure they are fully cooked. when they are about halfway done, add finely chopped parsley and mint, and a little pepper. once cooked, make a sauce and place sweet spices on top.

title: Menestra d'ova di trute che para piselli.
text: simmer the eggs slightly. then remove them from the broth and separate them. to prevent the broth from being too clear, remove a piece of bread and process it through a sieve, or alternatively, add some broth from peas which would be much better if you have it. with whichever broth you choose, return the eggs to simmer with a pinch of spices and finely chopped parsley and mint.

title: Menestra de roselli.
text: simmer the dumplings in meat broth. when they are nearly cooked, add a little chopped parsley and mint. if the broth is too clear, strain it through a sieve as described above. when the dumplings are cooked, season with spices.

title: Menestra le lactuche che para zucche.
text: take the whitest part of the lettuce, that is, the middle part, and boil it like pumpkins with eggs and sorrel.

title: [Minestra di semola.]
text: cook the semolina with rich meat or large chicken broth, adding it little by little to the broth while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon. let it boil for half an hour over low heat, away from the fire, so it doesn't smoke. then, make it into a porridge, and add whatever you like in terms of seasonings and spices. for lent, cook it in almond milk with sugar and rosewater.

title: [Minestra di rape.]
text: peel and roughly chop the turnips, then cook them well in a good meat broth. pass them through a large perforated sieve, or a ricer, and then return them to simmer in a rich broth with a little salted meat, pepper, and saffron.

title: [Minestra di finocchi.]
text: fennel is cooked like snails, except it should be smaller and cooked with a little pepper and salted meat, or oil.

title: Maccaroni romaneschi.
text: use good quality flour and work it into a dough slightly thicker than that for lasagna. roll it around a stick, then remove the stick and cut the dough into strips about a centimeter wide, creating noodles or strands. cook them in broth or water until tender. they should boil as soon as they are added. if cooking in water, add fresh butter and a little salt. once cooked, serve in bowls with care, butter, and sweet spices.

title: Maccaroni in altro modo.
text: make the pasta as described above. similarly, cook it, adding the ingredients listed, making the pasta slightly thicker and cutting it very finely and thinly these are called triti or formentine.

title: Menestra de radici de petrosimolo.
text: take the roots of parsnip, and remove the woody core, then clean them well and cook thoroughly in meat broth. afterward, pound them very finely and return them to another rich meat broth with a little pepper and saffron.

title: [Funghi fritti.]
text: clean the mushrooms very well, and boil them in water with two or three cloves of garlic, and pieces of bread. this is done because they are naturally poisonous. drain them well, allowing the water to drain completely so they are dry, and then fry them in good olive oil or lard. when they are cooked, sprinkle them with spices.

title: [Altri modi di cucinare i funghi.]
text: another way to prepare the mushrooms is to clean them thoroughly first, then grill them. top with a mixture of chopped pancetta and garlic, and pepper. alternatively, you can season them with oil. you can also cook them in a pan like a cake.

title: Zucche fritte.
text: peel the squashes well and then slice them thinly, like the edge of a knife. briefly blanch them in water, drain, and dry them. sprinkle with a little salt and coat in fine flour, then fry in oil. remove and drain. grind a little fennel seed, garlic, and breadcrumbs together. mix with verjuice until it s quite thin, then strain it. pour this flavorful mixture over the squashes. they are also good simply with verjuice and fennel seed. if you want the flavor to be yellow, add a pinch of saffron.

title: Menestra de pome cotogne.
text: cook the quince in a broth made with lean meat. then grind them and temper them with almond milk made with meat broth or good chicken broth, if the season requires it and pass them through a tammy, and place them in a bowl with sugar, ginger, and cinnamon, and a pinch of saffron and set them to simmer away from the fire, over a low brazier that doesn t produce smoke, and stir them often with a wooden spoon. adding a little fresh butter or lard would be better. then, when they seem cooked, make them into a compote, and sprinkle with sweet spices and sugar.

title: Fave piene.
text: soak the broad beans when they are well soaked, split them slightly on the side that isn't dark. carefully remove the beans, taking care not to break the skins. then, take white, clean almonds and grind them very finely with a little rosewater so they don't release oil. add plenty of sugar. use this mixture to fill the bean skins, then press them together so they resemble half-cooked beans. place them to warm in a bowl, frying pan, or other vessel where there is no water or other liquid, watching carefully that they don't burn. add the beans to small bowls, topping with a little hot meat broth, some finely chopped parsley, and a few finely chopped fried onions. if you don t like onions, omit them.

title: Menestra di seme di canepa.
text: to make twelve portions, take one pound of hemp seeds. grind them and boil them in a pot until they begin to open. then, remove one pound of blanched almonds, finely ground, and add them to the seeds, grinding everything very well. add a piece of bread to the mixture. moisten these ingredients with meat or lean chicken broth and strain through a cloth. place it to simmer in a pot over low heat, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon. then add half a pound of sugar and half an ounce of ginger, along with a pinch of saffron and rosewater. once the portions are ready, sprinkle them with sweet spices.

title: Ravioli in tempo di carne.
text: to make ten portions take half a pound of aged cheese, and a little of another fatty cheese, and a pound of fatty pork belly or a veal shank, and simmer until well broken down. then beat it well and add a generous amount of finely chopped herbs, pepper, cloves, and ginger adding the breast of a pigeon pounded the night before will make it even better. combine all these ingredients. next, make the pasta very thinly, and mix this filling into the pasta as you desire. these ravioli should not be larger than half a chestnut, and cook them in a capon or meat broth, colored yellow with saffron when boiling. let them simmer for the length of two our fathers. then serve as soup, and sprinkle them with grated cheese and a mixture of sweet spices. similar ravioli can be made with pheasant, guinea fowl, and other fowl.

title: Maccaroni siciliani.
text: take the finest flour and knead it with egg whites and rosewater, or ordinary water. if you wish to make two portions, add no more than one or two egg whites. make this dough very firm then roll it into long, hand-sized strips, as thin as a playing card. take a long iron wire, a palm s length or more, and as thin as a piece of twine, and lay it over the dough. roll the dough once with both hands on a table then remove the wire and stretch the perforated pasta in half. these pasta shapes will keep for two or three years, especially if made during the month of august cook them in water or meat broth. serve in bowls with plenty of grated cheese, fresh butter, and sweet spices. these pasta shapes require boiling for about two hours.

title: Vermicelli.
text: prepare the pasta as described above, and roll it out thinly, breaking it into small pieces with your fingers like vermicelli. set them aside to dry in the sun, allowing them to last for two or three years. when you want to cook them, simmer in meat broth or a rich chicken broth for about an hour. then, prepare the stews and add them, grated, along with spices. if it is not meat season, cook them with almond milk and sugar, or with goat s milk. and because this milk does not boil as much as the vermicelli require, boil them first with a little water, as you would rice. similarly, cook the lasagna, the tritte, or the fermentine. all these pasta dishes should be yellow with saffron, except when cooked in milk.

title: Menestra d'herbette.
text: remove the violet leaves and a little borage, and blanch them in boiling clear water then drain and chop them finely with a knife. pick a little parsley and fresh mint, and chop them in the same way. grind them well in a mortar and add them to a bowl with rich broth, and simmer briefly. if desired, add a pinch of pepper.

title: Riso con lacte de mandole.
text: to make ten portions, take one pound of almonds and peel them well until they are white. take half a pound of rice and wash it two or three times with warm water, then place it over the fire with clear water and cook it thoroughly. remove it from the heat and let it dry. then grind the said almonds very well, moistening them and skimming off the foam frequently with a little fresh water, so they do not release oil mix them with fresh water and pass them through a sieve. add this mixture to a pot and bring the milk to a boil, adding half a pound of sugar. when it begins to boil, add the rice and place the pot over low heat, turning it frequently with a spoon so it doesn't stick, and let it boil for half an hour. you can also cook the rice with goat s milk or another kind of milk. because this dish tends to foam, if it does, here s how to remove it take the

title: Mandolata.
text: to make eight portions remove one pound of peeled and blanched almonds and grind them very finely, moistening them frequently with fresh water as described above, so they don t release oil. add a piece of soft white bread. mix everything well with fresh water and pass it through a sieve, then place it in a pot to simmer over low heat. let it simmer for about eight hours. also, add half a pound of fine sugar to simmer with the almonds. this almond mixture should be slightly liquid. adding a little rosewater would improve it.

title: Lasagne de pelle de cappone.
text: remove the skin from the boiled capon and cut it into pieces. place it in a rich capon broth and bring to a boil for about half an hour with a little saffron. then, prepare the soup and top it with some broth and spices.

title: Brodo de ciceri rosci.
text: to make eight portions, take one and a half pounds of chickpeas and wash them with warm water, placing them in the pot where you intend to cook them. ensure they are loose and add half an ounce of flour, preferably fine flour, a little good olive oil, a pinch of salt, about twenty grains of cracked black pepper, and a pinch of ground cinnamon. mix all these ingredients thoroughly with your hands. then add three cups of water, a little sage, rosemary, and parsley root, and bring to a boil until the chickpeas have reduced to the quantity of eight portions. when they are almost cooked, add a little olive oil. if the broth is for the sick, omit the olive oil and spices.

title: Manfrigo in menestre.
text: to make ten portions remove three loaves of bread and discard the crust. shred the bread very finely with a knife and place it on a board. add a pound and a half of fine flour around it, and incorporate four or five eggs with the bread, beating well together with the knife, continuously scraping the bread with the flour. when the mixture resembles small sugared almonds, place everything on a kneading trough and work in the flour, setting aside the remaining bread to dry. when you want to cook it, simmer in meat broth or good chicken broth. add a touch of saffron to give it a slightly yellow hue, and boil gently for about half an hour. add a little cheese and spices to the soup.

title: Cocer zucche.
text: prepare the squash however you like, then dice it and simmer in meat broth, or water, adding onion to your liking. when it appears cooked, remove it and pass everything through a sieve or grind it very finely. return it to the pot and cook with rich broth and a little lemon juice. color it slightly yellow with saffron when cooked, remove from the heat and let it cool slightly. then, remove the yolks from eggs in the desired quantity and beat them with a little aged cheese, and add them to the squash, stirring constantly with a spoon so they don't curdle. serve with sweet spices on top.

title: Zucche con lacte d'amandole.
text: roast the pumpkins with water, then drain as much water as possible and pass them through a straining cloth or a perforated spoon. return them to the pot to boil with milk and sugar, and a little dried lemon juice to taste.

title: Carabaze a la catalana.
text: take the pumpkins, also known as carabazze, and clean them very well. place them in a dry earthenware pot with good, finely chopped lard. set the pot over a low heat and simmer continuously with a wooden spoon. they need to simmer for about four hours. then, you ll have a rich, yellow broth, made flavorful with a little saffron. add sugar and sweet spices, along with a touch of sourness to taste, according to your lord s preference, or that of others. as we mentioned earlier in the chapter about pumpkins, you can also add some beaten egg yolks with a little aged cheese.

title: Fave fresche con brodo di carne.
text: shell the broad beans with hot water, as you would almonds, and then simmer them in good broth. when they appear cooked, add a little chopped parsley and mint, and also boil some salted meat along with them. this soup should be slightly green, which makes it more attractive. similarly, prepare peas, and any other fresh vegetables, but note that they should not be shelled with hot water, but left as they are with their thin skin.

title: Verzuso in Quadragesima.
text: to make ten portions take a pound and a half of almonds. blanch them in lukewarm water, and grind them very well as mentioned above. add a little fresh water so they don't release oil. then take a handful of white bread and soak it in good wine. next, take the almonds and the bread, along with orange juice and rosewater, and combine all these ingredients. add an ounce of cinnamon and a pound of fine sugar. pass everything together through a sieve, creating a yellow mixture with a touch of saffron. then bring it to a boil in a pan away from the heat. stir frequently with a wooden spoon to prevent sticking. let it simmer for about an eighth of an hour.

title: Bianco mangiare in Quadragesima.
text: to make ten servings you will need a pound and a half of almonds, blanched and ground very finely as mentioned above, and a softening of white bread soaked in white pea broth. if peas are not available, supplement with another broth, boiling a very white bread for half an hour, adding the said softening to this broth. then, take some good saltwater fish, or good freshwater pike, cooked by boiling. from their firmer, whiter flesh, you will take half a pound, and grind it very finely with the almonds and softening, along with a little broth, and some orange zest. if orange zest is unavailable, supplement with a little lemon juice, adding some rosewater, and half a pound of grated ginger, with eight ounces of sugar. all these ingredients, well combined, passed through a sieve, you will cook in a saucepan over a low heat, away from the fire so it doesn't smoke and stir constantly.

title: Piselli in Quadragesima.
text: you can also make small fritters with almond milk during the lenten season, as mentioned earlier in this chapter about white foods.

title: Herbe con lacte d'amandole.
text: first, steep the herbs and bring them to a simmer in water. the water should be boiling when you add them. then, remove them and place them on a board and finely chop them with a knife. grind them very finely in a mortar. finally, simmer them in almond milk, adding enough sugar to taste.

title: Herbe senza lacte.
text: gather the herbs and first boil them as previously mentioned. then you can make thick or thin soups with them, as you prefer and desire.

title: [Sementa di canipa.]
text: take the canapa seeds and let them soak for a day and one night, discarding the granules that float on the water as they are bitter. then, take some well-peeled almonds and grind them. grind them together with the seeds, ensuring they are finely ground. blend with fresh water and good pea broth, adding some fine sugar and a little rosewater. then, cook all these ingredients for about eight minutes, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.

title: Cavoli a la romanesca.
text: break the curled cabbage leaves by hand, as is customary, and add them to boiling water. when they are about half-cooked, discard all the water. then, add a generous amount of pounded lard, and stir it well into the cabbage. next, add good, rich broth and simmer over a low heat for a short time.

title: Menestra de vivanda gialla.
text: to make twelve portions, you will need one pound of almonds, unskinned, and pound them very well with the breast of a rooster or other fowl that you like cooked boiled or roasted, as you prefer, along with four egg yolks, pounding them well with the almonds. then add half a pound of sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and a little saffron. next, with chicken broth or another good broth and a little lemon juice, temper the aforementioned mixture, passing it through a sieve. then place it over a low heat, far from the flame so it doesn t smoke stir constantly and let it simmer for about an hour. when it s about halfway cooked, add two ounces of good lard or fresh butter then form the portions and add sweet spices.

title: Menestra de fior de sambuco.
text: to make twelve servings for lent, you will need a pound and a half of peeled and finely ground almonds, as mentioned above. you will also need three ounces of dried elderflower. first, soak them well in cold water for about an hour, squeezing and pressing out the water. from these flowers, grind half with the almonds, adding the softness of a white bread crumb and half a pound of sugar, with a little ginger. if you want it to be yellow, add a pinch of saffron, and then pass the mixture through a sieve. cook it as described in the previous chapter. once cooked, place the remaining half of the flowers on top. when it is sufficiently cooked, form the servings and top them with good sweet spices. if you want to make this dish during meat season, add three egg yolks to it and thin it with rich chicken broth or another good broth, passing it through a sieve, and adding the sugar and other spices with the whole flowers as described above

title: Zanzarelli bianchi.
text: to make ten servings first, you will take one pound of almonds, peeled and ground as mentioned above, grinding them with a little elderflower. then, thin them with fresh water, passing them through a sieve. when you have obtained the quantity of eight servings, put this liquid matter to cook in a pot, first using a common cupful of the raw mixture. then, take two breadcrumbs of white bread, finely grated, and take ten egg whites. and that cup of milk mentioned above, along with the grated bread and all these ingredients, beat together, adding half a pound of sugar. when the aforementioned milk begins to boil, add this other mixture on top, and do not stir it or move anything with a spoon. then, when you see it coming together, make the servings, sprinkling them with sweet spices.

title: Bianco mangiare al modo catalano.
text: to make ten portions, take one pound of almonds, well peeled and finely ground. moisten them with rich chicken broth, or another good broth, and pass them through a sieve. bring to a boil in a clean pot, adding two ounces of rice flour, tempered and strained with almond milk. simmer for about an hour, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, adding half a pound and a chicken breast, very finely chopped and ground, which has been cooked from the beginning in the almond milk. when this mixture is fully cooked, add a little rosewater, and when serving, sprinkle with sweet spices.

title: Sapor bianco.
text: take almonds according to the quantity you desire, ensuring they are well peeled and ground. to prevent them from releasing oil, as i have mentioned several times, add a little cold water while grinding. then, take a small amount of softened white bread that has been soaked in vinegar, and grind it with the almonds, adding as much white ginger as needed. this mixture should be thinned and blended with good vinegar, or juice of oranges or lemons, sweetened with sugar and made sharper with vinegar and oranges, more or less, according to the taste of your lord or others. this flavor can be served with any meat dish, or during lent.

title: Sapor camellino.
text: finely chop the raisins and pistachios. then, take two or three slices of toasted bread and soak them in red wine, adding as much as you need. grind these ingredients together. next, combine a little red wine, grape must, and verjuice. if you don t like verjuice, substitute it with vinegar, sweetening or souring it to your preference. strain the mixture through a sieve, then add good cinnamon, cloves, and finely ground walnuts.

title: Salsa de pavo.
text: have ready hard-boiled red beetroots and boiled chicken livers. also, toasted almonds, in the quantity you desire. grind all these ingredients together very well with good vinegar or verjuice, then pass them through a sieve, adding cinnamon and a little ginger, and sugar. note that this flavor should be slightly cooked and made yellow with saffron.

title: Sapor de progna secche.
text: take pigeons and send them to the wife in red wine, and pluck them. remove the bones and grind them very finely with a few unblanched almonds and a little toasted or grilled bread. add all these ingredients with a little verjuice, some of the aforementioned wine, and a touch of treacle, or sugar, which would be much better. strain the mixture through a sieve, adding good spices, especially cinnamon. to make the peppercorn dish, refer to the chapter above which discusses it, and follow the instructions therein.

title: Salsa verde.
text: take parsley and celery, and a little leek, with some other good herbs, a pinch of pepper, and ginger, and salt. grind all these ingredients together very well, mixing in good strong vinegar, and pass it through a sieve. if you wish it to have the flavor of garlic, you can grind a few garlic shoots with the above ingredients, according to your taste.

title: Sapor fior de persico.
text: blanch and grind almonds with a little white bread, a pinch of ginger and cinnamon, and a touch of verjuice and red wine, adding a few sandalwood shavings. then blend this mixture, adjusting the sweetness and tartness with red wine to your liking.

title: Sapor fior de ginestra.
text: take almonds, saffron, and egg yolks, ensuring the almonds are ground as desired, and blend them well, adding some powdered ginger.

title: Sapor de uva.
text: take good black grapes and crush them thoroughly in a bowl. crush with them a piece of bread, or half a loaf depending on the quantity you wish to make, and add a little good lemon zest or vinegar, so that the grapes are not too sweet. boil these ingredients over the fire for about half an hour, adding cinnamon, ginger, and other fine spices.

title: Sapor de moroni.
text: prepare blanched and finely ground almonds with a little breadcrumbs. then, take the almonds and grind them carefully with all the other ingredients, avoiding any forceful grinding or crushing to preserve the small granules within. add cinnamon, ginger, and a pinch of nutmeg. pass everything through a sieve.

title: Sapor de cerase negre o viscioli.
text: to achieve similar flavors, follow the order given and described above in the chapter on flavoring grapes. however, you can vary the color, adding more or less according to your preference.

title: Sapor de crognali roscio.
text: follow the same method described above for the flavor of cherries and grapes.

title: Mostarda.
text: take the salsify and blanch it for two days, changing the water frequently so that it becomes whiter. then, with almonds, peeled and ground as desired. and when it is well ground, mix it with the salsify and grind them together very well. then add good country wine or vinegar, and also a little white bread mix it well and pass it through a sieve. make it sweet or strong as you like.

title: Mostarda roscia o pavonaza.
text: take mustard seeds and grind them very well, then take dried grapes and grind them just as well as you can. have a little toasted bread and a few almonds, and cinnamon, and with a little sorrel or vinegar, and grape must, temper this mixture and pass it through a sieve.

title: Mostarda da portar in pezi cavalcando.
text: grind the horseradish and mustard as described above, and have grapes ready. grind the ingredients very well, and add a little cinnamon and a few cloves. then, you can form them into round balls, like those made with a mold, or square pieces of the size you prefer. place them in a single layer on a board to dry, and you can move them from place to place as you wish. when you want to use them, you can dilute them with a little verjuice, vinegar, or cooked wine.

title: Sapor celeste de estate.
text: gather wild purslane, and a few ground almonds, with a little ginger. combine these ingredients with sorrel and process them through a sieve.

title: Peperata gialla da pesce.
text: slice the bread and cut it into pieces, then lightly toast them. take some red wine, with a little vinegar and reduced wine, and bring it to a boil with the slices of bread. then, pass the bread through a sieve, adding sweet and strong spices. color it yellow with a pinch of saffron.

title: Agliata bianca.
text: grind blanched almonds very finely and when they are half-ground, add as much garlic as you like. grind them together well, adding a little fresh water to prevent oil from forming. then take a piece of white bread and soak it in a clear meat or fish broth. this garlic paste can then be served and adapted to suit all rich or lean seasons as you desire.

title: Agliata pavonaza.
text: follow the order of the chapter above, except you shouldn't add broth. instead, take some black grapes and crush them well with your hands in a bowl or other vessel then simmer them for half an hour. after that, use this must to temper the garlic sauce. a similar thing can be done with cherries. this garlic sauce can be served with meat or fish, as desired.

title: Agresto verde.
text: you will take some sour herb called usiglie or agrette, and pound it very well with a little salt. you will then have a little old sourness with which you will temper it, passing it through a sieve.

title: Salsa.
text: prepare the purslane and walnuts very well, and if it pleases you, you can add some parsley, a little breadcrumb, and salt. mix these ingredients with vinegar or sorrel, and process them through a strainer.

title: Agresto con finacchio.
text: use garlic to your liking, and the finest, sweetest fennel flowers you can find, grinding them very well together. add fresh sorrel and use it to blend this mixture, passing it through a tamis. season it lightly with salt, as needed.

title: Sapor [di roselli].
text: the roselles should be slightly green, not overripe, and well-picked. you will then pound them with a clove of garlic, if you like, otherwise leave it out. next, temper them with a little sorrel and pass them through a sieve.

title: A servar el suco de crognali per lo inverno.
text: pick ripe plums and crush them by hand in a bowl or other large vessel as much as possible. to this, add a generous amount of fresh sorrel, pepper, and a good deal of salt. boil for two hours or more, then strain through a sieve with large holes, setting the resulting liquid aside in a jar or another container where you can store it. note that it should be very salty, and this liquid will be excellent for adding color and flavor to other dishes as you prefer.

title: Torta biancha.
text: take a pound and a half of good fresh cheese, and chop it finely. grind it very well, and take twelve or fifteen egg whites, and grind them very well with this cheese, adding half a pound of sugar and half an ounce of the whitest ginger you can find, similarly half a pound of good, white pork lard, or in place of lard, an equal amount of good fresh butter, and also milk, enough as needed, which will be about a third of a jug. then you will make the dough or crust in the pan, as thin as you like, and put it to bake, giving it a gentle heat from below and above and you will make it slightly colored on top from the heat. when it seems cooked, take it out of the pan, and on top you will put fine sugar and a little rosewater. bolognese cake. you will take as much cheese as is said in the previous chapter about the white cake,

title: Herbolata de maio.
text: take as much fresh cheese as mentioned above and pound it very well, and have fifteen or sixteen egg whites with a quarter, or about, of good milk and take a good quantity of borage, that is, for the most part, and a little marjoram, plenty of sage, a little mint, and plenty of parsley. and all these herbs you will pound together very well, pressing out the juice, and passing it through a sieve. this juice you will put together with the things mentioned above, adding half a pound of good lard or fresh butter and you will take a few leaves of parsley, and very few leaves of marjoram, and with a knife you will cut them and beat them as finely as possible, and grind them very well in a mortar, incorporating them with the things mentioned above, adding half an ounce of white ginger and eight ounces of sugar. and make sure that this entire composition is well mixed in a bowl, which you will place over the

title: [Torta di zucche.]
text: peel the pumpkins thoroughly and grate them as you would cheese. simmer them gently in a good broth or milk. add as much fresh cheese as indicated previously, combining it with a little aged cheese that is flavorful. also, use one pound of good pork belly or a very well-cooked and finely chopped veal chop. if you prefer, instead of these two ingredients, you can use butter or lard, adding half a pound of sugar, a little ginger and cinnamon, a glass of milk, and six eggs. when you think the pumpkins are cooked, remove them from the water and pass them through a sieve. color this mixture yellow with sesame seeds. then place it in a pan with a thin pastry base, but not a top crust. cook over gentle heat from below and above. when it seems about half-cooked, sprinkle it with finely chopped lasagna sheets. when it is cooked through, top it with good sugar and rosewater.

title: [Altre torte.]
text: you can also make tarts using turnips, and even pears that have been cooked and seasoned very well under the cover. similarly, you can make them with quince, cutting them first into quarters or pieces, peeling and coring them well and you can simmer them in good broth. if you prefer, you can also bake them under the cover, which might be better, always passing them through a sieve and adding the other ingredients as mentioned with the pumpkin.

title: [Migliaccio.]
text: to make a migliaccio for four or five people, beat very well one pound of ricotta, the freshest you can find, until it appears to have returned to milk. then, have three or four ounces of flour and eight or ten egg whites, and half a pound of sugar, mixing all these ingredients thoroughly and incorporating them well together. if you don t have flour, use a handful of grated white bread, finely grated, substituting it for the flour. have a pan without pastry or crust, and on the bottom inside, spread a generous layer of good lard, making it about an inch thick. place the pan over the embers until the lard is very hot, and pour in this mixture, applying moderate heat from below and above as described for other tarts. when it s cooked, remove it and sprinkle the top with good sugar and rosewater.

title: [Torta di fiori.]
text: pick the flowers, carefully removing them from their stems, and gently incorporate them into the dough for the white cake, as described in the previous chapter. note that this mixture, when combined with the flowers, should be either quite firm or quite thick. this is to ensure the flowers are evenly distributed throughout the cake, from bottom to center, top, and all around.

title: [Torta di caprioli.]
text: remove the venison and rose hips, bruising them. finely chop them with a knife do the same with the dried figs. you will have a good fresh cheese and a piece of veal, well-seasoned, pounding everything together thoroughly. if you prefer, you can use lard or butter with the veal, adding enough ginger, cinnamon, and sugar. place this mixture in a pan, covering it with a crust both below and above. when it s nearly cooked, prick the top crust in many places, almost entirely. once it's baked, sprinkle sugar and a generous amount of rosewater over it.

title: [Torta di riso.]
text: wash the rice and rinse it very well, then cook it in milk or a rich broth until it is well cooked and then you will take it out onto a cutting board and let it dry. you will take a bit of good fresh ricotta, finely strained, and combine it with ten egg yolks, sugar, and rosewater. you can also add a little milk, about a small cupful. once everything is well mixed together, you will cook it in a pan, observing the same order and method as described for the white cake. note that this requires a smaller amount of ricotta than the other cakes mentioned above.

title: [Torta di farro.]
text: clean and boil the pork loin well, and let it cook in a rich broth. then, prepare horse meat to dry it as has been said for rice. and you will take one pound of fresh cheese and half a pound of good aged cheese, grinding one and grating the other as is customary. you will also need a pork belly or a veal breast, cooked so much that it is almost falling apart and well beaten with a knife, adding good spices and sugar if you like, and fifteen eggs with a little saffron. mix all these ingredients well together only the crust will be placed in the pan to cook. when it seems almost cooked, add well-dried lasagna sheets on top, thickly. let it cook a little longer, and when it is fully cooked, sprinkle sugar and rosewater on top.

title: Torta di carne de vitello, o capretto, o capone giovine.
text: you may choose any meat you like from those listed above. first, boil it, ensuring a mix of lean and fatty cuts. remove any sinew and pound the meat well with a knife. then, grind it slightly in a mortar. add some fresh ricotta and a little aged ricotta, along with some parsley and marjoram, finely pounding them together. incorporate ten to fifteen eggs, along with a piece of pork belly or a veal breast, well-seasoned and thoroughly beaten. add a little pepper, ginger, cinnamon, and saffron. cook it in the same way you would cook a white pie.

title: [Torta di castagne]
text: boil the chestnuts, then mash them slightly. combine them in a bowl with a little good milk, adding all the other ingredients and components of the farro cake as described above, and make it yellow with saffron.

title: Torta commune.
text: have on hand eight eggs and good pork or veal fat, or butter, raisins, ginger, cinnamon, and a little grated bread, with a little rich broth that is yellow with saffron, and prepare it as above for the white cake.

title: [Crema di miglio fritta.]
text: wash the millet very thoroughly, ensuring it is white and clean. cook it in good goat s milk or cow s milk, and make sure it cooks until quite thick and is well done. then take a little flour and two egg whites, and mix them together in the flour. for those who do not like eggs, you can mix the flour with milk instead, and once mixed, add it to the millet, stirring well with a wooden spoon. then let it simmer for a little while, adding good sugar, stirring again and mixing very well. next, pour this mixture onto a large cutting board, spreading it out as you would prepare a pie crust, and let it cool. when you want to cut it at the table, slice it into large or small pieces as you like, and fry them in a pan with good lard, turning them occasionally, cooking them until they are slightly colored on both sides. remove them piece by piece and place them on a plate,

title: [Torta di ciliege.]
text: find the darkest cherries you can and pit them. grind the pits very finely in a mortar. then, take some red rose petals and chop them very finely with a knife, along with a little fresh ricotta and a little good aged ricotta. add spices cinnamon, ginger, and a pinch of pepper and sugar. mix everything together thoroughly, adding three or four eggs depending on the quantity you wish to make. place the mixture in a crust and bake it gently in a pan. when cooked, sprinkle with sugar and rosewater.

title: [Torta di erbe varie.]
text: simmer the quince and let it soften, then extract everything good from it and grind it very finely in a mortar. make a good almond milk, straining the almonds or milk through a sieve with a little rosewater if you don't have rosewater, pea broth or crushed white chickpeas will do instead. with these ingredients, grind a few raisins and four or five figs, adding another few healthy raisins, a little parsley, marjoram, and savory, fried briefly in good oil and finely chopped with a knife. add ginger and cinnamon, and sugar. this mixture should be ground very well in the mortar. to ensure it sets like other cakes, incorporate a little powdered amaretto, mixing it thoroughly with the other ingredients, or a little pike roe, ground and passed through a sieve, which helps it set better. make crusts for the top and bottom as you would for other cakes. when cooked, sprinkle with sugar and rosewater.

title: [Torta di anguille.]
text: you will split the eel and cut it into strips about two inches wide, parboiling it slightly, but not overcooking it. prepare a beautiful, white almond milk by grinding the almonds with a good quince and rosewater, ensuring the milk is quite thick, almost strained. grind a small amount of raisins very finely with three or four dried figs. then, take spinach, breaking it finely with your hands and frying it briefly in oil, adding a little chopped parsley, about an ounce of whole raisins, and an ounce of shelled pine nuts, along with ginger, cinnamon, pepper, and saffron, discreetly, according to the quantity you wish to make. mix all of this composition well with your hands and place a pastry crust at the bottom of the pan. then, layer this composition on top of the crust, filling it completely, first with a layer of the composition and then with a layer of eel repeating in layers as you like, until the composition is complete. cover with another

title: Torta de dattali, d'amandole et altre chose.
text: take a pound of blanched almonds and grind them very finely, and with good, rich fish broth, and a little rosewater, pass them through a fine sieve you will need half a pound of good, clean dates, with a few raisins and four or five dried figs, ground very finely. also, two ounces of well-cooked rice then grind all these ingredients together in a mortar. take a little spinach, parsley, and marjoram, and fry them in good oil, chopping them with a knife adding some chicken liver or fat from a good fish would be good, beating it together with them. then have one and a half ounces of whole, clean pine nuts, to be used for sprinkling on top when you have spread the filling of the tart and take another ounce of raisins and half a pound of sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and a little saffron mixing all these ingredients together, incorporate them very well. to help it set, you will need half

title: Torta de riso bianco.
text: have one pound of blanched and finely ground almonds, and a little rosewater, and a little rice broth when it's nearly cooked. with this, temper the almonds then pass them through a sieve. take eight ounces of rice and, once cooked, grind it very finely with the almonds, adding two ounces of white yeast, a quarter of almond flour, or a little finely sieved pike roe as mentioned above, and half a pound of sugar, also half an ounce of blanched pine nuts, lightly crushed in a mortar but not ground. mix all these ingredients together, and place them in a dish to bake covered with a crust. when it s half-baked, top with thinly dried lasagna sheets. as it finishes baking, sprinkle with sugar and rosewater. note that this cake should not be overbaked.

title: [Torta di ceci.]
text: make a pound of red chickpeas cook them very well, and with their broth and a little rosewater, pass them through a fine sieve. you will need a pound of almonds, well peeled and white, ground very finely, so they pass through the sieve. with these, grind two ounces of raisins and three or four dried figs, also a half ounce of roughly broken pine nuts and not ground, adding sugar, rosewater, cinnamon, and ginger, mixing all these ingredients well together. to help it set, incorporate some almond flour or roe of the pike as mentioned above, and cook it with a crust underneath. when it seems almost cooked, sprinkle it with sugar and rosewater, and give it another warm baking. note that this cake should be low.

title: Torta di pesce, fecatelli et lacte di pesce.
text: simmer the fish with these innards, and have a pound of cooked and very finely ground peas, then pass them through a sieve. similarly, grind the fish, the faggotini sausages, and the milk, carefully removing all the bones. if you have trout or bream roe, they will be good to add and grind with these other ingredients. then have parsley and marjoram, finely chopped, and add them to grind together in a mortar, adding sugar, ginger, and cinnamon as needed. with a little rosewater, mix and incorporate all these ingredients well and bake this tart in the oven until it is well cooked, observing the order mentioned several times in the previous chapters. note that you can make all the tarts described above in various and different colors in the same pan, according to the timing, and also with different fillings, and of different materials, adapting some very thin pastry shells which you will place to divide them in half, or

title: Torta in brodo.
text: make a thick pasta, as is used for pastries, of a size that suits you. have some chicken and pigeons, partially boiled and cut into quarters, dividing each quarter into two or three pieces. you will also need finely ground almonds, a little egg yolk, saffron, and rich broth with a touch of verjuice. first, dry the pasta as you would for pastry dough. to ensure the edges stand straight, fill it generously with flour, covering it with a pasta lid, and let it cook until it appears firm. then, cut away the lid and remove the flour, and place the aforementioned pieces of meat inside, seasoning them as you would for a pie. over the meat, pour the mixture of broth and the other ingredients mentioned above. ensure it is well seasoned with ginger and a little pepper. bake this pie in the oven, or in a pan, as you would other pies.

title: Marzapane.
text: peel the almonds very well, and grind them as finely as possible so they don't pass through the sieve. to make the almonds whiter, more flavorful, and sweeter, soak them in cold water for a day and night, or longer, pressing them gently to clean them. when grinding, moisten them with a little rosewater so they don't release oil. to make a good cake, use an equal weight of sugar and almonds, that is, one pound of each, or more or less as you like, and add an ounce or two of good rosewater incorporate all these ingredients very well together. then take wafers or meringue made with sugar, and first moisten them with rosewater arrange them on the bottom of the pan, and cover them completely with this mixture. once spread and leveled, moisten it slightly again with rosewater, and sprinkle generously with powdered sugar. after leveling it well with sugar, bake it in the oven or over the fire

title: Per far caliscioni.
text: you will prepare a similar filling or composition as the aforementioned marzipan, and knead its dough with sugar and rosewater. roll out the dough as if making ravioli, fill it with this mixture, forming pieces large, medium, or small as you prefer. having a well-crafted wooden mold, shape and press them gently to make them more beautiful. then, bake them in a pan like marzipan, being careful not to burn them.

title: Per far ofella.
text: you will need good quality parmigiano cheese that isn't too aged, and a little fresh ricotta, and have them grated. add egg yolks, raisins, cinnamon, ginger, and a pinch of saffron. mix and combine all these ingredients very well, ensuring the filling is quite dense. then, have a thin pasta, like that used for lasagna, and spread the filling onto the pasta, making large, medium, or small shapes as you prefer. brush the tops with a yellow saffron color, or any other color you like and bake them in the oven, being careful not to use too high a heat, as they shouldn't be overcooked.

title: [Pasticcio d'anguilla]
text: prepare skinned and cleaned eel, or other fish if desired, similarly cleaned and cut into pieces about two inches wide. have also good butter and fish broth, finely chopped, and mix it with the aforementioned pieces. take a little mint and parsley, finely chopped. also, one ounce of raisins, cinnamon, ginger, pepper, and cloves, ground together. mix all these ingredients thoroughly and combine them. then, have the pasta well made and rested, and place this mixture inside. add a little good butter on top and cook it. when it's almost cooked, have two ounces of blanched almonds, peeled and finely ground, diluted with verjuice and passed through a sieve. add this mixture inside, and sprinkle more saffron on top. then, let it boil and cook a little longer, until everything is very well cooked, as it should be. note that when serving, you can add eggs and dilute them with verjuice, together with the other ingredients mentioned above two egg yolks

title: Pastelli secchi facti con pesce sano.
text: clean and fillet the fish, scoring it slightly along the spine. season it thoroughly inside and out with a mixture of salt and good spices. then, prepare a rather coarse dough and enclose the fish within it, binding it well. bake in the oven until fully cooked.

title: Pastelli de poma cotogne.
text: prepare the pastry as described for the other pastries, and you will need quince, peeled, cleaned, and polished, and hollow them out, removing the cores and all the hard parts inside. make a large and suitably wide hole in each quince, and inside those holes, fill them with good beef or veal marrow, along with plenty of sugar and cinnamon. arrange the quince neatly in the pastry, adding more of the marrow both inside and out. brush the entire pastry with sugar and cinnamon, and salt it generously on all sides. then, top it with a pastry crust or lid, and bake it according to the order and method described above.

title: Gioncata d'amandole in Quadragesima.
text: blanch and finely grind the almonds with a little rosewater to prevent oiling. then add two ounces of sugar and two ounces of rosewater, and a quarter jug of good fish broth, ideally made from pike or perch, as other fish, both saltwater and freshwater, are not as good. be careful not to make the broth too salty, but ensure it has good substance and the fish is very fresh. mix all these ingredients thoroughly and pass them through a fine sieve, reducing this mixture until no trace of the almonds remains. let this mixture sit overnight in a dish or other vessel, and in the morning you will find it curdled and thickened like a cream of fresh milk. if you like, you can set it with leaves or herbs as other creams are set, or leave it in dishes, topping it with sugar or anise candies.

title: Ricotta contrafacta in Quadragesima.
text: take one pound of blanched and finely ground almonds, as described in the previous chapter, and combine with four ounces of sugar, one ounce of rosewater, and half a cup of fish broth of the quality noted above. mix all these ingredients together and pass them through a fine sieve. place this mixture into molds and let it set in a cool place overnight. in the morning, turn the molds out onto plates or cutting boards and serve this ricotta, adding sugar or anise seeds, which will enhance the dish.

title: Butiro contrafacto in Quadragesima.
text: take similarly as said above one pound of almonds. clean and grind very finely with half a cup of rosewater. pass them through a very fine sieve to ensure they are well compacted, add a little bit of cornflour, or, which will be better, half a cup of pike broth with four ounces of sugar and a pinch of saffron to make it yellow, passing everything as i have said as finely as possible. then give them the shape of a butter roll place them to set overnight in the coolest place.

title: Suppa de lacte de seme de canape.
text: bring the ground almonds to a boil until they begin to split their skins, then pound them very finely in a mortar. mix with a little fresh water and strain through a sieve. return to the pot and simmer briefly, adding salt and sugar to taste, and a little pepper if desired. simmer again for about as long as it takes to say a miserere. prepare slices of bread, lightly toasted. arrange these slices in a dish or bowl and gradually pour the almond milk over them, adding it as needed to soak the bread. finally, pour out all the milk, being careful not to disturb the bread. repeat this process once or twice more. top with good, sweet spices and serve.

title: Diriola.
text: prepare the pasta in the shape of a cake and dust it well with flour so that it stands upright while cooking in a pan until it is slightly dry. once this is done, remove the flour and take some egg yolks, milk, sugar, and cinnamon. make a mixture with these ingredients and place it in the pasta, baking it like a cake, stirring and turning it frequently with a wooden spoon. when you see it starting to set, add a little rosewater and stir well with the spoon. when it is cooked through, it will be ready. note that it shouldn't be overcooked and should tremble like a flan.

title: Per farne una in Quadragesima.
text: combine almond milk, sugar, and rosewater with cinnamon. to help it set, add a little amaretto flour, following the instructions in the previous chapter.

title: Caso in patellecte.
text: use good quality lard, not too old or too salty, and cut it into strips or squares, as you prefer. have ready some small frying pans made in that style put a little butter or fresh lard in the bottom and heat them over the embers. then place the pieces of lard in the pans. cook them once, until tender, and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon. serve immediately, as it is best eaten after a meal and while still hot. alternatively, you can prepare the lard by first toasting slices of bread over the fire until they begin to brown on each side, arranging the slices in order in a tart pan. then place some thinner slices of lard on top of the bread. cover the pan with a hot lid so that the lard begins to melt or soften. once this is done, sprinkle with sugar, a little cinnamon, and ginger.

title: Rape armate.
text: roast the turnips under the embers, either whole and healthy, and slice them thickly, as wide as a knife blade. have some fatty cheese, sliced as wide as the turnip slices, but thinner. have sugar, pepper, and sweet spices mixed together and in a cake pan, layer by layer, you will arrange cheese slices as you would make a crust base, and on top of them, pile the turnip slices, sprinkling them with the aforementioned spices and a generous amount of fresh butter. and so, layer upon layer, you will arrange the turnips and cheese until the pan is full, cooking them for a quarter of an hour or more, like a pie. this dish should be presented as superior to the others.

title: Suppa dorata.
text: you ll need slices of white bread, peeled and without crust, cut into squares. lightly toast them until they are golden brown on all sides. then, beat together eggs with plenty of sugar and a little rosewater soak the bread slices in this mixture, then carefully remove them and fry briefly in a pan with a little butter or lard, turning them frequently so they don't burn. drain them on a plate and sprinkle generously with rosewater tinted yellow with a pinch of saffron, and plenty of sugar.

title: Frictelle de fior de sambuco.
text: have good fresh curd and a little aged curd, and make sure they are very well mashed, and with them, add a little flour, and egg whites according to the amount you want to make, also a bit of milk and sugar and grind all these ingredients very well together. remove them from the mortar, and you will find enough elderflower blossoms according to your discretion and these flowers should not be mashed or broken, making the mixture neither too clear, that is, liquid, so that you can make round fritters by hand or in whatever shape you like, frying them in good lard or butter, or good oil and send them to the table while still hot.

title: Frictelle de bianco de ovo, fior de farina et caso fresco.
text: follow the order and method described previously, except that in these fritters you do not add milk or elderflower blossoms.

title: Frictelle de gioncata, et lacte quagliato.
text: take the salted cod and, with garlic, place it in a terracotta pot so that the brine or water has drained from it. once this is done, take what remains in the pot and, with a little flour, egg white according to the quantity you want to make, sugar, and rosewater, mix these ingredients well together. this mixture shouldn't be too stiff make the fritters with a spoon, little by little, large or small as you like, and fry them in good lard or butter that is well seasoned.

title: Frictelle de riso.
text: cook the rice very well in milk, and when taking it out to make fritters, follow the order and method written above, except that you should not add any cheese or other milk.

title: Frictelle de salvia.
text: take a little flour and combine it with eggs and sugar, and a pinch of cinnamon and saffron to give it a yellow color. have whole sage leaves, and one by one, dip them or wrap them in this mixture, frying them in lard or good oil.

title: Frictelle de poma.
text: peel the apples and slice them thinly, removing the cores. fry the slices lightly in lard or oil, then remove them to drain on a cutting board. next, wrap them in a similar batter as described in the previous chapter, and fry them again in hot fat. if it is lent, you can fry them in oil without adding fat or egg.

title: Frictelle con fronde de lauro.
text: fry the bay leaves in some good fat or lard. then, scoop out the marrow and let it dry and with a similar preparation as with sage, you will make these fritters.

title: Frictelle d'amandole.
text: grind the blanched almonds very finely with rosewater and a little milk. pass through a sieve. separately, grind the cooked chicken breast. combine the almond mixture, chicken, a little flour, two or three egg whites, and sugar to taste. mix well. shape the batter into small fritters and fry in hot lard or butter until golden, being careful not to overcook them.

title: Frictelle de fior de sambuco.
text: grind almonds or pine nuts very finely, whichever you prefer, and process them through a sieve with a little rosewater or pea broth. then, add a bit of good, white yeast and elderflower blossoms to your liking, and mix all these ingredients together with a little flour. note that this mixture should be prepared the evening before so that the fritters will be lighter in the morning. in the morning, add a little sugar, shape the fritters into whatever form you like round or otherwise and fry them in good oil.

title: Frictelle con herbe amare.
text: combine flour and a little yeast with finely chopped herbs, preparing the mixture the evening before so it will be light and airy. in the morning, add finely chopped dried figs and raisins. this mixture shouldn't be too soft. then make the fritters and fry them in good oil, topping them with sugar and grated apple.

title: [Altre frittelle di riso.]
text: cook the rice very well, and once cooked, drain it thoroughly on a cutting board. if you wish to grind it, proceed to do so, otherwise leave it whole. have almonds in the quantity you prefer, and grind them very finely with a little rosewater or a bit of the broth used to cook the rice. ensure this almond milk is quite thick. then, have a little flour and sugar. mix these ingredients well, and form the fritters in the shape you like, and fry them in good oil.

title: [Altre frittelle di pomi.]
text: peel and core the apples very well, and cook them in water or under a roasting pan, removing the hard core. then, mix them thoroughly with a little yeast, a little flour, and sugar. fry into fritters in good oil.

title: Frictelle de fichi piene.
text: take a few almonds and pine nuts, according to the quantity you want to make, and grind them very well, ensuring they are white and fine. add two dried figs and a little raisins while grinding. then, have a little finely chopped parsley and a few whole raisins with good flavor. if this mixture is too thick, add a little rosewater. have the dried figs opened and scooped out from the bottom, that is, from the flower end and fill them well with this mixture, frying them over a high heat in good oil, then lightly flour the top.

title: [Frittelle di pesce.]
text: lightly cook the fish, and grind very finely its whitest flesh. have a little almond milk well strained, and a little flour mixed with sugar combine these ingredients with a little rosewater or plain water. then shape the fritters as you like, and fry them in good oil.

title: Frictelle in forma de pesce.
text: peel the almonds and grind them until smooth. then, take some good fish pulp and grind it very finely with the almonds. grind some raisins with a little sugar as well. next, add a little finely chopped parsley and marjoram, along with a pinch of saffron. you will then have prepared a thin dough, similar to that used for lasagna. incorporate larger or smaller pieces of this mixture into the dough, as you prefer. after this, prepare wooden molds shaped like fish of various kinds and designs, as you like. use these molds to shape the dough with its filling. these fritters are to be fried in good oil, or alternatively, baked dry in a pan like a cake. when cooked, they will resemble fish.

title: Altre frictelle in forma de pesce.
text: make a paste of almonds and thin it with rosewater and sugar. prepare a batter with flour, plain water, and sugar mix everything together and form the fritters into the fish shapes mentioned above. note that these should be cooked directly in a frying pan like a cake.

title: Frictelle in forma di raffioli.
text: make a mixture of almonds, flour, and sugar, and with it, make fritters. to make another type of similar fritters, use shelled almonds or pine nuts or walnuts, and grind them well with a few raisins and dried figs. add fish broth or sausage broth, along with finely chopped parsley and marjoram, and a pinch of good spices. color this mixture yellow with saffron. then, make the fritters and fry them in good oil.

title: Frictelle in forma de pastelli piccoli.
text: cook the rice very well in water and grind a few almonds. pass them through a fine sieve with a little rosewater for the dough. incorporate the rice with the almond milk, then add sugar and a pinch of amaretto flour. fry these fritters in the shape of small pastries in oil.

title: Frictelle piene di vento.
