text: melt sugar with rosewater to your liking, and let it boil until it becomes like syrup. while boiling, add two beaten egg yolks to make the sugar whiter, then strain the melted sugar through a cloth to remove the egg whites. return the sugar to the heat and continue to boil, stirring constantly with a spatula. when you see it form clumps like snow, it is cooked enough. remove it from the heat and continue stirring with the spatula until it becomes small grains and tiny bubbles. then, drop it into molds shaped like fruit or figures, as desired.

title: Pour la couleur de succre.
text: for the red rosette of paris, use red dye. for the green, use green bladder dye. for the yellow color, use saffron. for brown, use brown ochre.

title: Pour faire moustarde de Cremone.
text: take half a pound of candied orange peel, half a pound of candied quince or marmalade, and chop them all together very finely. then take half a pint of very thick mustard, and add melted sugar with rosewater, and include saffron to give it a deep red color. boil it until it resembles syrup, then mix in what you have chopped, and blend with the mustard. add enough syrup, and serve in small dishes, three or four spoonfuls, to accompany roasted meat.

title: Pour faire pastez d'Espaigne fueiltez.
text: make a dough with the finest flour you can find, adding two eggs, a little butter, and mix with cold water until it is slightly soft. knead it well for half an hour, then let it rest for a while. afterwards, roll out your dough on a long board and stretch it as thinly as paper, about half a foot wide. take some rendered pork fat and grease your dough well, all over. roll your dough into a log, then roll out the dough again as before, greasing and rolling onto the other log until you have a roll as thick as an arm. let it cool. once the dough is very cold, cut it into pieces about the width of three fingers. take a piece of paper the size of a hand or larger, and place a piece of dough on top. place your two thumbs in the center of the dough and stretch it into a small pastry, no thicker than half a little finger. take some minced mutton with beef fat. note

title: Pour faire pastez enragez de chair.
text: make the pastry as above, roll it out thinly, like the other pastry. instead of sage, use plenty of butter and generously enrich the pastry, then form a thick roll and make a pastry much more tender than the other. to fill the pie, take a measure of veal meat, half a measure of beef fat, and a beef foot that is well cooked, and chop everything together. then place in a measure of spanish wine, four ounces of sugar, half an ounce of cinnamon, half an ounce of nutmeg, a little salt, and add a handful of pine nuts, mixing everything well. fill your pastry, then take candied orange peel and other candied fruits cut into small strips, and place over the meat so that it is covered. if you have beef broth, add that to the pie as well, then cover the pie. when the pie has been in the oven for a good quarter of an hour, add more through a small hole melted butter with a little more spanish

title: Pour faire pastez pouplin.
text: take the pastry as described above. roll out a piece of pastry a little thicker and longer than the other. shape it continuously by rolling upwards, ensuring it's large enough to contain a pigeon. place the pigeon inside, feet pointing upwards, then add salted lemon slices, grated nutmeg, and ginger, chopped marjoram, and fresh butter. close the pastry over the top, allowing the pigeon's feet to protrude, and bake in the oven.

title: Pour faire pastez d'Angleterre.
text: take sifted wheat flour through a large sieve, then make a pastry that is well-enriched with butter, five or six yolks of eggs, and that the pastry is well-sweetened. then you will make a crust for a pie, and you will take a quarter of capon or lamb that is well-fattened, or some piece of veal that is fatty, and boil the meat, and cut the piece according to the pie. then put in a crushed nutmeg leaf, a little pepper and cinnamon, chopped dates, also chopped candied fruit, pine kernels, beef marrow, sugar that is quite sweet, and fresh butter, and cover your pie, and put it in the oven to bake. before putting it in the oven, rub the top of the crust with egg yolks, and then sprinkle with sugar all over, and put it in the oven to bake.

title: Pour faire pastez d'Huistres.
text: open the oysters and rinse them with a little white wine. place them in a pastry shell until the shell is more than half full. add a little pepper, nutmeg, chopped marjoram, a bit of fresh parsley and butter, and a pinch of salt. cover the pastry shell if you wish, you may add slices of fresh lemon.

title: Pour faire pastez d'artisseaux.
text: take artichoke bottoms that are cooked, then take the base of the artichoke cut into slices, and put them in a shallow pastry crust. then sprinkle with pepper, nutmeg, and chopped mint, and fresh butter. bake for a quarter of an hour. then pour in white wine and let it cook for another quarter of an hour.

title: Pour faire pastez de veau reuestu.
text: take a pound of raw veal and half a pound of beef fat, and chop them both finely together. add three eggs, two maces, a little pepper, and a salted lemon, all finely chopped. shape the mixture into a small roast of mutton. stud it with capers and bake it in a hot oven for half an hour, pouring in white or verjuice wine as needed, and letting it cook thoroughly.

title: Pour faire pastez d'Esturgions.
text: take a slice of sturgeon, about three inches wide, and boil it vigorously to loosen the scales. then take some cloves, and place them into the fish on all three sides. add nutmeg, pepper, whole bay leaves, and chopped marjoram, and enough butter. make a roux of white bread that is nicely browned without burning, and soak it with warmed wine, straining it through a sieve. add enough sugar and boil until the roux is smooth. when the fish is cooked, pour the roux over it.

title: Pour faire pasté de Cheze fresche.
text: take the cheese, thoroughly cleaned, and cook it until it is done. then take two or three chopped onions and sauté them in butter, a little salted lemon in pieces, nutmeg, and pepper, a little chopped mint, and add all together into the pastry, and enough butter. note that you must cut the cheese into pieces, and when the pastry is half-cooked, add a little spanish wine.

title: Pour faire pastés de caracolle.
text: take snails that are well-cooked and cleaned as they should be, and chop them coarsely with a knife. add nutmeg, pepper, and butter. after half an hour in the oven, take four egg yolks and beat them with a little spanish wine. remove the pastry from the oven and add the snails to the pastry. let it bake for another pater noster in the oven, and no more.

title: Pour faire pastez de chien de mer.
text: take a piece of monkfish, four fingers wide, and boil it for an hour, then peel it. fill it with cloves of nutmeg, and add salt pastry and mint, and chopped marjoram. when the pastry is well cooked, make a pepper on toasted bread and sprinkle it with nutmeg, cinnamon, and cloves, so that the sauce is very rich, and sprinkle it over the pastry when it is cooked.

title: Pour faire pastez enragez de poisson.
text: take half a pound of fresh salmon, half a pound of carp, and half a pound of smoked salmon, finely chopped and mixed together. add two mace nuts, one small stick of cinnamon in powder, half a stick of ginger, two ounces of pine nuts, two ounces of currants, one small glass of spanish wine, a little salt, three ounces of sugar, and mix all together with four ounces of melted butter. fill the pastry case as you did the other, with candied fruit cut into pieces.

title: Pour faire offaelle fueiltee.
text: make puff pastry as before, and create a small lid the size of your hand. then, have half a pound of ground almonds and three candied quince, also ground, combined. add half a pound of sugar, two ounces of cinnamon, one ounce of nutmeg, and two yolks of raw eggs. mix everything well with two ounces of fresh butter. then, take an egg's worth of the mixture and place it on the pastry lid, and fold the lid in half, forming a twisted shape. bake them in the oven. when cooked, sprinkle with sugar.

title: Pour faire Raphioulles.
text: make a dough of white flour with eggs and butter, and you will make small covers like the others, then take roasted veal meat, cold or other cooked veal meat for every pound of meat, half a pound of beef fat, finely chopped together, and add in 3 raw eggs, three ounces of grated parmesan, half an ounce of cinnamon, two nutmegs, and mix everything well together, and make them into a raft shape like the others, then boil them in water, and take them out of the water, and put five or six in a dish with a fatty broth, and sprinkle grated parmesan and cinnamon over them, and boil two or three broths in the dish, and serve thus if you want to make them smaller, it would be better to put a dozen in a dish.

title: Autre rafioule.
text: take a good handful of spinach, a small handful of finely chopped meat. along with the spinach, press out the excess water, then add three ounces of grated parmesan cheese, four ounces of fresh butter, three yolks of eggs, two nutmegs, and a half ounce of cinnamon. make a small, neat patty and boil it like the others. place it in a dish with water and butter, parmesan cheese, and cinnamon on top, as you would the others. serve when it has boiled twice or three times in the dish.

title: Pour faire Agnoilen.
text: make a dough with cream and butter, and boil them together. then add the flour while it s over the heat. next, take four eggs and beat them well into the dough, off the heat, until they are fully incorporated. then take two or three more eggs and beat them well, as you did the others. add a generous handful of grated parmesan, mixed into the dough, and shape into long rolls about the thickness of a thumb. then cut them into small pieces like small shells, and boil them in rich broth. place them in a dish and sprinkle with parmesan and cinnamon, as you would with ravioli.

title: Aultre sorte.
text: take a well-cooked piece of beef and finely chop it with four ounces of fat. then add three ounces of parmesan cheese, half an ounce of cinnamon, a pinch of pepper, and two ounces of cooked quince. form small, elongated patties about the length of two fingers and no wider than one finger, twisting them into rings. moisten one side with beaten egg to help them stick together, then boil them like ravioli. serve with boiled capon or mutton, and cover with rich broth and a little cinnamon on top. serve in this way.

title: Pour faire maquaron.
text: make a dough of eggs and butter, and make large covers of dough, well rested, and cut into strips the width of three fingers, and cut them like ribbons, and boil them like small pasta, and place them on a dish with melted butter, parmesan, and cinnamon on top, well mixed together and serve in this way, adding a little cinnamon on top.

title:
Pour faire Capilotade 
douce.
text: prepare cold rosti, guinea fowl, capon, or another fatty roasted dish, cut into pieces about two or three finger-widths wide, and boil with wine, butter, oranges cut into small pieces, and candied quince also cut into small pieces, currants, nutmeg, and cinnamon, and sugar. once well boiled together, make pastry covers the size of a trencher. fry them in butter. then take one of the pastry covers, place it in a dish, and add two or three pieces of meat with pieces of quince and orange. then add another fried pastry cover, and meat with quince on top, up to four layers. pour some of the cooking juices over it, and place the dish with the lid on over the heat. let it boil for three or four boils, then sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon, and serve in this way.

title:
Pour faire Capilotade de 
parmesan.
text: prepare cold roast pieces and cut them into portions. simmer them in rich broth, then take some slices of white bread. place four or five in a dish, then add three or four roast pieces. top with parmesan and cinnamon, and repeat this process three times. pour broth over the top and let it simmer for fifteen minutes. sprinkle with more parmesan and cinnamon, and serve hot.

title: Esturgion en potage.
text: prepare the sturgeon, cut into pieces. boil it vigorously to remove the scales and clean it thoroughly. then place it in wine and a little water, and add cinnamon, nutmeg, saffron, a pinch of pepper, two or three chopped onions, and sauté them in butter. add sugar, and let it simmer well. add peeled almonds, cut into long pieces, ensuring they are well cooked. serve with cinnamon sprinkled on top.

title: Esturgions rostys.
text: take a piece of sturgeon and boil it vigorously to remove the scales. then place cloves and small sprigs of rosemary on top, and roast it like this, always basting with butter. once cooked, make a sauce with wine, sugar, and cinnamon, nutmeg, a few slices of salted lemon, and a little butter. boil everything together and pour it over the sturgeon, then serve.

title: Poulpette d'esturgions.
text: cut the sturgeon into strips the length of a hand and the width of three fingers, and beat it with the flat of a knife without breaking it. then take finely chopped fresh herbs, and add nutmeg, ginger, yolks of eggs, and fresh butter, a little salt, and spread the herbs over the fish so that it is covered. roll this up and place it in skewers of wood or iron, and roast it slowly over a grill. once cooked, pour melted butter and orange juice over it, and add a fresh lemon cut into small pieces. serve in this way.

title: Saulsisse d'esturgions.
text: take three sturgeons. chop them very finely, with one and a half ounces of salt, a dash of pepper, two onions, a pinch of nutmeg, a pinch of cinnamon powder, and a measure of spanish wine. mix everything well together, and form into sausages like bolognese sausages.

title: Pour faire mortadelle d'esturgion.
text: take three pounds of sturgeon, as above, half an ounce of cinnamon, two nutmegs, a little salt, two ounces of grated parmesan, mix all together, three yolks of egg, two ounces of fresh butter, when all is well combined, make the sausages, put them to stew with a little water and wine, marjoram, a nutmeg leaf, a salted lemon in slices, butter, and boil well together. place slices of white bread underneath in the dish serve the sausages on top.

title: Esturgion en adobe.
text: take a piece of sturgeon, well cleaned, roasted, and minced in butter or olive oil. then add vinegar and wine in equal measure, and bring it to a boil. include a salted lemon in slices, saffron, pepper, bay leaves, rosemary, marjoram, crushed radish root, and a small handful of coriander. once boiled, pour it all hot over the sturgeon and keep it well covered. turbot and eel, being fish of the sea, can be seasoned in the same way.

title: Escreuice ou Crabe demer [sic] farcie.
text: prepare crayfish or crab and boil them like small crayfish. then remove all the meat, but do not break the shell. chop the meat finely and place it in a chopped mold, add nutmeg and pepper, three or four yolks, and stir it all together with butter. return the mixture to the shells and arrange the small claws around the edges, frying them in butter.

title: Les [sic] mesme Escreuice ou Crabe en potage.
text: take all the raw meat out, and cut it into small pieces, and simmer it with white wine, fresh butter, mace, a little pepper, chopped mint, or fresh lemon cut into strips. cook it well, ensuring it s rich with butter, and when it s thoroughly cooked, place it on small croutons and serve five or six in a dish.

title: Pour faire trippe de Brochet.
text: take pike and carp meat, and fresh salmon in equal amounts, and chop everything very finely. add nutmeg, salt, pepper, chopped marjoram, and mix all with three egg yolks. roll the meat into small sausages. take the roe and bladder of the pike and fill them with your meat. cook with wine, water, butter, slices of salted lemon, rosemary, and marjoram. when well cooked, serve as is.

title: Pour faire trippe de chien de mer.
text: take a pound of fresh dogfish meat, for a portion of meat four ounces of sea samphire, and finely chop them together. add two or three finely chopped onions, a small piece of cinnamon, half a piece of pepper, and salt. if you have dogfish blood, mix it in to make tripe if there s no blood, take a measure of cream, crushed and strained pike roe, and mix with the meat. then take sheep or pig intestines, the smallest ones, and clean out the fat thoroughly, fill them with your meat like tripe, and cook them with water and salt, a good handful of wild thyme. once cooked, roast them on the grill.

title: Chien de mer en adobe.
text: take a large piece of dogfish and roast it, first removing the skin. once well roasted, cut it into long pieces and prepare it like other fish.

title: Chien de mer boully.
text: take a piece of salt cod and salt it well, then put it in a pot to boil with water, and add a generous handful of sage and a handful of wild thyme. cook it well, as for serving. remove the skin. it is eaten like salted meat with mustard.

title: Chien de mer rosty.
text: boil the dogfish until the skin can be pulled off, then lard it with sage, and put cloves inside. roast it, basting constantly with butter and vinegar. when well roasted, make a pepper sauce as for venison, which should be sweet and sour, and serve in that way.

title:
Pour faire pastez en pot de chien
de mer.
text: take dogfish meat and mince it very finely, then sauté it in butter. place it in a pot with a little wine and water, prunes, and quince. add nutmeg and pepper, a little sugar that is both sour and sweet, and boil well. serve in this way.

title: Tonine boullie.
text: poach salmon with salted water and a handful of sage. once cooked, peel off the scales and skin, then let it cool. slice the salmon, sprinkle with chopped mint and oregano, drizzle with vinegar, add a little pepper, and serve.

title: Tonine en potage.
text: take the tuna when it is cooked and well cleaned, removing all scales, cut it into long pieces and lightly flour it, then fry it in olive oil or butter. next, take slices of white bread that are not burnt, and soak them in hot wine and vinegar, then strain the mixture through a sieve with three yolks. add cinnamon, nutmeg, sugar, and saffron, two chopped onions that have been fried in butter, and boil everything together with the tuna, adding a little pine nut, and serve in this way.

title: Tonine en ladobe. [?]
text: take the veal, once cooked, and stew it. prepare the sauce as described previously.

title: Tonine d'vne autre sorte.
text: take slices of tuna, about a half-inch thick, and flour them on both sides. fry them in hot butter once fried on one side, spread mustard over the slice so that it is completely covered. then, have some grated white bread and sprinkle it over the tuna. press gently with your finger so that it adheres to the mustard, then turn the bread underneath and continue frying on the bread side. finally, serve three or four pieces on a plate.

title: Autrement.
text: make a batch of white bread, adding sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger to the dough. boil the bread until it is yellow with saffron, then cut it into pieces as large as you like. place in warm sauce and serve.

title: Tartoufle boullye.
text: take truffles, well warmed, and put them to boil in water. once cooked, peel them and slice them. pour melted butter over the slices and season.

title: Tartoufle autrement.
text: slice the truffles as shown and cook them with spanish wine and fresh butter, and nutmeg.

title: Autrement.
text: slice the truffles and cook them with butter and chopped marjoram. then, take four or five yolks, beat them with a little wine, and pour them over the top while it's simmering. remove from the heat and serve immediately.

title: Autrement.
text: roast the truffle in hot ashes as you roast chestnuts, then peel it and slice it thinly. place chopped mint on top, followed by boiled crepinettes. add vinegar, a little pepper, and serve in this way.

title: Moulle de boeuf en potage.
text: take seven or eight large pieces of beef, well washed, and put them in a dish with good broth. bring to a boil, then add five or six beaten eggs and chopped parsley and marjoram. add grated nutmeg and mix well with the eggs, then pour them into the boiling beef. let it cook a little longer over the heat until the eggs are slightly set. then, have some slices of white bread and place a generous spoonful of butter on top of them. put the bread with the broth over it, and serve it all hot.

title: Vne autre sorte.
text: bring the beef broth to a boil. add a little grated white bread, having been over the fire for a quarter of an hour, then add sugar and cinnamon, six egg yolks. beat with the wine from the dish and mix with the broth, and serve in this way.

title: Animelle ou soupitte de veau en potage.
text: bring the tripe to a boil in water, then remove the small membranes and place them in a good broth. add nutmeg, chopped marjoram, butter, and a little white wine, and serve.

title: Autrement.
text: take the sweetbreads, being cooked, and fry them in butter with a fresh lemon, sliced. season with orange juice and pepper, and serve in this way.

title: Autrement.
text: make a white wine sauce with an egg and a little wine, a little sugar and pepper, then take the sweetbreads and soak them in the sauce, and sauté them in butter, and serve in that way.

title: Autrement.
text: take cooked sweetbreads and cut them into pieces about the size of an inch, and place them on small, well-bound wooden skewers. sprinkle them with chopped sage and salt. then take a pork caul and wrap the sweetbreads in it, and roast them on the grill, basting frequently with butter. serve with orange sauce.

title: Chapon en potage de Hongrie.
text: take a half-cooked capon. cut it into quarters and sauté it in a little butter, being careful not to brown it. then take sliced onions and quartered apples, and sauté them in the butter, then scatter them over the capon in a pot. add a little broth and wine, and let it simmer further. add saffron, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and mace, and stir well until it is thoroughly cooked, then serve.

title: Chapon reuestu.
text: take a capon that is well plucked, then open the capon from behind, and lift the skin up, and cut the wings from behind along with the skin, then you will take the meat of the capon, all the breast with the thighs, and leave the drumsticks whole then take the capon meat and as much veal meat, and chop together with a little beef fat and add nutmeg, ginger, chopped marjoram, a little salt, four yolks of egg, and mix everything well then replace the meat on the bones of the capon, and pull the skin over it, and tie it with string, and put it to boil in a pot when cooked, take two slices of stale bread in hot broth, four yolks of egg, and pass everything through a sieve with a little white wine, then add it to the capon broth

title: Chappon en adobe.
text: take a capon and chop it up in butter or olive oil, and put it in a stew like the egyptians do.

title: Chappon bardé & rosty.
text: roast the capon until it is half-cooked, then add small sausages and lard the capon. return the capon to the oven to finish roasting, and prepare a white cream sauce with egg yolks. add sugar and cinnamon to the sauce, ensuring it is slightly translucent. pour this cream sauce over the capon, turning it to coat evenly, until the crust is slightly firm. be careful not to add any fat. pour the cream sauce over the capon again twice, and let it simmer continuously. when the capon seems cooked through, remove it from the oven and generously brush with butter. serve on a platter, and garnish with thinly sliced peeled orange.

title:
Pour faire vn pot pourry dict en 
Espaignolle Oylla podrida.
text: take a piece of beef, about two pounds, and put it in a large pot to boil, along with a capon or chicken. after boiling for half an hour, add a small leg of mutton, then a duck as well. next, add two veal sweetbreads coated with pigeon, two partridges, two small cabbages stuffed, two purslane, two bologna sausages, and two cooked mortadellas. include half a mayence ham, also cooked separately, along with pork feet and ears, also cooked separately. then, add small sausages, salted limets cut into quarters, four andouillettes, four jerusalem artichokes, which should be stuffed with veal and covered, and four mutton cauliflowers stuffed with wild herbs and good, fatty cheese, along with a fried onion and raw eggs, as the stuffing should be prepared, and you will fry it in butter. place a handful of marjoram and mint on

title:
Pour faire heuspot de veau
en mesnage.
text: take a veal shank that is half-cooked, and add nutmeg, a salted lemon in slices, marjoram, and mint, some verjuice or white wine, and butter. let it simmer together.

title: Autrement.
text: prepare a veal breast cut into pieces and browned in butter on both sides, then place it in a pot with more butter and let it cook thoroughly. next, take some herbs of your choice, finely chopped and pounded with breadcrumbs, and crack some eggs into the mixture, beating until it is thick. add a little sugar. then, have a pan with hot butter, and take a spoonful of your beaten herb mixture, forming small cakes that are cooked on both sides. place these cakes into the pot with the veal, add some wine, a little grated nutmeg, and let it simmer together until well cooked. serve when ready.

title: Autrement.
text: take a piece of veal and boil it. once cooked, add a little broth and butter to the pot. then, take a quarter pound of peeled almonds, pound them, and pass them through a sieve with the broth. next, take a little grated radish, and add it to the pot with the broth, and boil for two or three minutes. serve it like this.

title:
Pour faire vn foye de veau farcy
en potage.
text: cut the foie gras into thick slices, about the width of a finger, then with a sharp knife, cut into it from the inside and remove what you can, without turning it over. then lightly boil the foie gras after it s been removed, and finely chop it with a little beef fat, and chop a small handful of fresh herbs with it, and one chopped onion. add a little nutmeg and ginger, some salt, three egg yolks, and mix well. then fill the foie gras, and take a piece of veal or pork netting, and tie the foie gras inside, ensuring it is well secured. then place it to cook in a pot with good broth, nutmeg, a little sherry or wine, and salted lemon slices. let it simmer well, and serve.

title: Pour faire Tomaselle de foye.
text: take a veal loin cut into slices and boil it for a pater noster. then, finely chop it. add a chopped and sautéed onion in butter, a little nutmeg, pepper, and cinnamon, a handful of rich cheese, four yolks of egg, and mix everything together well. then, using a spoonful of the veal, make a batter with egg yolks and a little flour, until it s like a small pancake batter. dip the veal in the batter and fry it in butter. serve nine or ten in a dish, sprinkled with cinnamon.

title: Chappon boully farcy.
text: take cooked chestnuts and chop them with a little beef fat, then add four yolks, nutmeg, and pepper. incorporate some chopped marjoram and fill the capon s cavity with this mixture, carefully sewing up the belly to prevent anything from escaping. boil until thoroughly cooked. next, prepare some well-cooked greens, sautéing them with wine, chopped marjoram, butter, and a little grated nutmeg and caper berries that have been thoroughly rinsed in warm water. add these to the pot to boil with the capon. once the greens are well-boiled, pour them over the capon, along with the broth.

title: Perdris en potage a la Portuguese.
text: take partridges and boil them. once cooked, cut a fresh lemon into slices, shuck some oysters, clean some chanterelle mushrooms, add butter, white wine, and a little pepper. simmer well together and serve.

title: Perdris a la Catelane.
text: roast partridges, then take halved dates, candied orange peel cut into small pieces, marmalade cut into pieces, spanish wine, fresh butter, sugar, and cinnamon, and stew them well together, then serve.

title:
Vn gigot de mouton reuestu
& boully.
text: peel the sinew from the meat, and take all the meat from the bones, and chop it very finely with a little beef fat and a salted lemon cut into pieces, well washed. then add a little mint, also chopped, along with nutmeg and pepper, a little salt, half a cup of white wine, and three raw eggs. chop everything together very well, and mix thoroughly. then return the meat to the bones, shaping it into a roast like it was before. next, take a piece of pork cloth you should have beaten egg yolks. rub the cloth with the egg yolks, then wrap the cloth around the roast so that it is well covered, and tie it tightly lengthwise and across, ensuring nothing escapes, and put it to boil until cooked. then, take half a loaf of white bread and soak it in the broth, and strain it with four ounces of blanched almonds pounded and passed through a sieve. add this to the roast in a short broth,

title: Autrement.
text: take a leg of mutton prepared as described when it is well formed like a leg, place it in a large pie dish and stud the leg with cloves. cover with a sheet of paper and bake until fully cooked. make a sauce with wine, sugar, and cinnamon, along with chopped oranges and dates, and let it simmer together. pour the sauce over the leg of mutton and serve.

title: Veau reuestu en potage.
text: take a veal shank and finely chop it with beef fat, using half as much fat as meat. season it with the same spices you would use for a roast leg. then take some meat about the size of two eggs and shape it by hand like a small ham. cook this alongside the veal with a little wine, mace, saltwort in pieces, and a few cloves. cook well, then serve four or five portions on a plate.

title: Autrement.
text: take cooked veal, roasted or boiled, and chop it finely. add sugar and cinnamon, nutmeg, a little salt, half a pint of cream, three raw eggs, and mix everything well with melted butter. place it in a pie dish and bake it over coals, both above and below, until you see it begin to crack on top. then, using a knife, cut it into eight portions within the pie dish, and serve four portions on a plate, sprinkled with sugar and cinnamon.

title:
Pour faire vne espaule de mouton
farcie & rostie.
text: remove the skin from the shoulder, lifting it about half an inch thick, then cut into the flesh down to the bone on both sides. finely chop the meat and combine it with a handful of boiled parsley, spinach, marjoram, and mint, finely chopped, along with four egg yolks, nutmeg, pepper, a little salt, and anise seed. return the meat to the cavity you ve cleared, replace the skin on top and underneath. wrap with veal cloth and secure tightly with small skewers. bake in a moderately hot oven until cooked through, turning it two or three times to ensure even browning. once cooked, discard everything from the baking dish and arrange peeled orange slices on a platter. drizzle with a little good vinegar and serve.

title:
Vn gigot de mouton rosty à la
mode d'Irlande.
text: take your leg of mutton and beat it firmly without removing the skin then soak it in vinegar for three or four hours. afterwards, take it out, dry it with a cloth, and insert cloves into it, as well as small pieces of cinnamon the length of a little finger. lard it with a little sage and marjoram, and roast it on a spit, basting it constantly with butter and spanish wine. when well cooked, cut two lemons into small slices and scatter them over with the fat from the roasting pan, along with a little vinegar, and serve in this way.

title: Foye de veau en potage.
text: take veal liver and cut it into pieces about the width of two fingers and longer than one. then lard them with three or four strips of bacon, a little isop and marjoram between each piece. put them to boil in good broth with two chopped onions, a little nutmeg, and some oregano, and butter. cook well and serve like this.

title: Autrement.
text: prepare the veal liver, cut into slices, and blanch them slightly. then, finely chop it and mix in three raw eggs, nutmeg, pepper, and cinnamon. add a little grated cheese, a little chopped mint, and blend everything well together. place the mixture in a greased pie dish and pour it in. bake in a moderate oven, with heat from above and below. once cooked, cut into slices, arrange three or four slices on a plate, sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon, and serve.

title: Foye de veau rosty.
text: take the foie gras and simmer it briefly, then lard it like veal. next, have a piece of pork cloth, and take some finely chopped fresh herbs, and spread a little pepper and salt on top. wrap the foie gras in the cloth and roast it, and make a sweet and sour sauce.

title: Autrement.
text: slice the foie gras thinly and toast it. make a sauce with toasted white bread crumbs, season with egg yolks, and blend with the bread. add sugar, cinnamon, and saffron, then boil well. pour over the foie gras and serve.

title:
Pour faire vne loigne de veau
farcie & rostie.
text: take some wild garlic herbs and chop them finely, sauté them in butter. add four yolks of egg, nutmeg, ginger, cinnamon, a little sugar, salt, and cook it slightly, not too much. then chop a salted lemon mixed with the wild garlic. next, take a veal loaf that has been partially boiled. put the wild garlic mixture under the veal loaf's skin, wrap it in a double layer of veal cloth, and fasten it with skewers so that nothing falls out. once cooked, remove the skin and chop it. add two yolks of egg, a little sugar and cinnamon, a little salt, and place the chopped veal on toasted bread slices. put it in a pie dish with butter inside, cover with more toasted bread slices, and warm them gently over low heat. arrange the toasted bread around the plate where the veal loaf is placed, and pour all the fat over the veal loaf with vinegar and orange slices on top.

title: Autrement.
text: take a piece of veal or breast and boil it. when almost cooked, add diced parsnip roots. once the roots are cooked along with the meat, add mashed radish roots and twice as much mashed mint, then stir in the veal broth. add a knob of butter or wine, ensuring the broth is rich, and serve.

title: Pour faire veau reuestu farcy.
text: take veal, with as much fat as possible, and chop it finely. add yolks of eggs, nutmeg, ginger, a little salt, a handful of mint, and marjoram. then form the meat into flat pieces, the size of a hand, the thickness of a finger. next, take peeled almonds and pound them with chopped and boiled quince, and pound them again with the almonds. add sugar and cinnamon, two or three yolks of eggs, and mix everything well together. then form a flat piece like the chopped veal, and enclose it between the two pieces of the aforementioned veal. cook it in a pie dish, and create a crust on top with boiled orange peels, cut into small, long pieces, and corellian cherries, sugar, and cinnamon. let it simmer well with red wine, and pour it over.

title: Autrement.
text: take a veal shank and cut it into slices the length of a hand and three fingers wide, pounding it with a knife without tearing it. then take finely chopped fresh herbs and add egg yolks, nutmeg, cloves, and ginger, a little salt, and chopped beef fat mixed together. spread the veal slices on a table and take of this fat-infused herb mixture, spreading it over the veal slices. then roll them up and place them on skewers of wood or iron, and boil and stew them with salt lemons, grated nutmeg, verjuice, or white wine, and butter, allowing them to stew well, and serve. if you wish, you can also roast them and serve with oranges and melted butter.

title: Autrement.
text: cut slices of veal, beaten well, and place them in a small pot with good broth. add two whole onions for flavor, then stir in chopped marjoram, nutmeg, pepper, butter, and white wine. let it simmer together well, and serve.

title: Pour faire neige.
text: take a pot of new cream, four ounces of sugar, four ounces of rosewater. take a small white ramakin like a large handful of sprigs, and beat the cream very strongly for half an hour, then let it rest, and you will see the foam rising on top like snow. then take a skimmer and lift the snow out, and put it in a dish, a trencher underneath to let the snow drip, and beat the cream again as before, until you have enough snow. then put it in small dishes, a sprig of rosemary inside, and serve in this way.

title: Pour garder gruselles & aigrets.
text: take fresh, well-cleaned snails and nearly mature them. then take verjuice and an equal amount of rainwater and let them simmer together. skim them and allow them to cool. add a little powdered alum and place the snails or hedgehogs inside, keeping them as they are.

title: Pour garder poires de coing.
text: peel the quince and remove the seeds. then boil the peelings with the seeds until the peel is very tender. add the quince, let it boil for two or three more times, then remove it and let it cool completely, along with the broth. place everything in a small barrel together with the peelings and all, and keep it stored like this.

title: Pour garder des concombres.
text: take small cucumbers and leave them on a table to sweat for three or four days. then take vinegar and boil it, skimming off any foam, and let it cool. after that, put the cucumbers in, and leave them there for fifteen days or three weeks. then discard the vinegar and take another vinegar, boiled and skimmed, and let it cool. pour it over the cucumbers and add a clove of garlic. also add some fennel seeds that are almost ripe, and put them in the jar, which should be well sealed. keep it like this.

title:
Pour donner au vin nouueau le goust
de muscadelle.
text: prepare the flowers of sahout, ensuring they are well-matured, and let them drain. then, at the time of the wine being in the barrel, add two ounces of sahout flowers to the barrel. you could also add apples and pears steeped in sahout.

title: Pour faire vn cabus farcy.
text: take a red cabbage that isn't too large, and put it to simmer whole gently, leaving it for as long as you can separate the leaves, one behind the other, until you see that the cabbage is as big as your fist. cut this off outside, and put some ground meat inside that is seasoned like other meats with eggs and spices, then wrap the cabbage with the leaves all around it should be well tied, and put it to cook with sausages, or whatever you like.

title: Pour faire racine farcie.
text: take large white or yellow root vegetables, as you prefer, and hollow them out lengthwise with a large knife. then take ground veal, as above, and stuff them well. cook them with beef broth, or whatever you like. you can also stuff cucumbers and zucchini in this way.

title:
Pour accoustrer vn canar à la 
mode d'Irlande.
text: put a good duck to boil, having taken it from the mire, new butter, and newly grated radish roots, well pressed add sugar and cinnamon to it, and boil it, then pour it over the duck, and serve in this way.

title: Autrement.
text: take a duck that is laced with small pieces of bacon and put it to boil in spanish wine. when it is almost cooked, add slices of fresh lemon, cooked and peeled chestnuts, nutmeg, cinnamon, and sugar. stir these ingredients well together, then take small sprigs of sage and soak them in a batter made with egg whites. fry the sage in unsalted butter and scatter it over the duck while it's still in the dish. serve with powdered sugar on top.

title: Pour faire Ceruelle de veau dorè.
text: take the cooked veal brain and finely chop it. mix in cinnamon, nutmeg, a little salt, and three or four egg yolks, blending everything well. then, take a piece of pork cloth and cut it into pieces, trimming away the fat with your hands. using a spoon, take some of the brain and place it on the cloth, wrapping it well inside. moisten it with beaten egg yolks and fry in butter that isn't browned, sprinkling sugar on top.

title:
Pour faire teste de veau pellee à la 
mode d'Irlande.
text: take a calf s head with the hair and salt it well, then cook it thoroughly. once cooked, remove the hair with your hands, then extract the brain and prepare it as you would another brain. have some very dry slices of bread and place the brain between two slices, then fry in butter. next, take prunes, raisins, dates cut in half, and pine nuts, and boil them with spanish wine, sugar, and cinnamon. pour this mixture over the head and serve the fried brain around the dish.

title:
Teste de veau doree à la mesme
facon.
text: take a calf's head, cut in half, leaving the brain inside. then, sauté it in butter and let it cool completely. next, make large pancakes from beaten eggs. once cooked on one side, sprinkle with grated parmesan cheese and a little cinnamon and pepper. place the calf s head on top and fold the pancakes around it, turning and frying again once or twice. sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon, and serve.

title: Pour accoustrer vne tortue.
text: take the turtle, and cut off the head, and let it die, then put it to boil as gently as you can, so that you can remove the back shell from the flesh. then remove all the skin you find, and take the flesh and the eggs if there are any, and stew it with good broth, and add a little nutmeg, a little pepper and rosemary, marjoram, mint and fresh butter, and salt, and white wine or verjuice, and a fresh lemon in slices, and let it stew well like this, and serve.

title: Autrement.
text: when the turtle is well cooked, stew it in butter, with a fresh lemon cut into slices on top, or make a sauce with toasted white bread and ground white almonds. strain everything well through a sieve, add sugar and ginger, and bring to a boil until it thickens. add the stewed turtle to the sauce and serve.

title:
Pour faire blanc manger frite
en la paelle.
text: prepare a firm, cooked egg white purée. then, add egg yolks according to the amount of egg white purée you have, and a little grated bread, mixing well. next, melt some unsalted butter in a pan. when the butter is hot, take a spoonful and drop small patties of the egg mixture into it, and cook them on both sides. sprinkle with sugar and serve.

title: Autrement.
text: make a pastry shell a little thick, and put some egg white inside the shell, the length of a sausage, and turn the shell all around, and cook well, and serve like this.

title: Autrement.
text: make small patties of dough, and put the white meat inside, then fry in butter.

title: Pour faire des oeufs farcis.
text: boil the eggs until hard, and cut them in half. then remove the yolks from both sides and finely chop them with parsley, marjoram, a little salt, and mix in with the yolks of raw eggs, also finely chopped together. fill the whites with this mixture, then brown them in butter. afterwards, make a light and tangy pepper sauce and serve.

title: Autrement.
text: take the same eggs, put them in water with melted butter, and add parmesan or another good, rich cheese, cinnamon, and pepper with butter. serve in this way.

title: Pour des oeufs de May.
text: boil eggs until they are soft. then, make a hole in each egg at both ends with a wooden skewer, large enough to hold a pea. blow out the yolk, then finely chop some parsley and mix it with the egg whites, a little salt and pepper. add another or two egg yolks, or more if you like, and fill the eggs with the mixture using the tip of a knife, pressing them tightly at the bottom with a little breadcrumb to prevent leakage. next, have a pot of boiling water and put the eggs in, letting them boil until hard. remove them, peel them, cut them in half, and top with melted butter and sorrel juice.

title: Pour faire des oeufs d'Angleterre.
text: take a dozen yolks. beat the eggs well, add a little sugar. then, in a small pot, melt some sugar. when it begins to boil, take the beaten egg yolks, place them in a sieve, and let them drain into the boiling syrup. the syrup should cover them completely. when well cooked on one side, turn them over. once thoroughly cooked, remove them and make three or four pieces like this, placing three or four on a plate.

title: Autrement.
text: beat some eggs as follows, and take a pie dish, and put the beaten eggs into the dish. let them cook like an omelet, and cut them into quarters, either ten or twelve. top with slices of white bread, then sprinkle with warmed marmalade mixed with butter, and put it over the bread and eggs. finish with cinnamon and serve.

title: Pour faire vne vote de Hongrie.
text: take a dozen beaten eggs, and mix them with white bread soaked in a little thick cream, then beat this well with the eggs, and make a cake, being well cooked on both sides, with sugar and cinnamon sprinkled on top.

title: Autrement.
text: make two patties of six eggs each. then have apples chopped and fricasseed in butter, quince poached in sugar, finely chopped and mixed with two or three egg yolks, sugar, and cinnamon, and place this between the two patties. then put it back on the heat to cook on both sides.

title: Autrement.
text: make two patties as before fry onions in butter, and add grated parmesan cheese and three or four yolks beaten together. then cut the patties into squares and place them between two, and fry them well on both sides, sprinkling with sugar and cinnamon.

title: Pour faire Marselette Romaine.
text: take three fresh eggs, half a pound of finely sifted powdered sugar, two grains of mace, and enough white flour to make a soft dough. cut the dough into pieces about the size of an egg and place them on wafers and on parchment paper. bake in an oven or a tart pan, and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title:
Pour blanchir l'huyle d'oliue pour
manger en quaresme.
text: make a small basin. beat the butter, a little at a time from underneath to draw out the water. then add cold water and olive oil that is firm, and beat as you did the butter. having beaten it for a long time, let the water drain out, and add new water two or three times until you see the oil turn white. then drain it off and serve in dishes.

title: Pour faire beurre de May.
text: warm a quarter of milk in a saucepan over heat, stirring constantly until it thickens. when it begins to boil, add a dozen beaten eggs and stir them in. cook until the eggs are set. drain the mixture through a cloth, pressing out all the excess liquid. then, pound it well in a stone mortar with half a pound of fresh butter, and strain it through a fine sieve, adding a little rosewater. once strained, beat it vigorously and add sugar to taste. serve in small dishes, raise it slightly, and sprinkle with sugar on top.

title: Pour neige seiche.
text: beat six egg yolks well. cook for a quarter of an hour, allowing a large foam to form. then, remove the foam and beat again until it is completely removed. add one pound of powdered sugar and blend with rosewater. cook until it falls from the spoon like snow. then, add two grains of mace with a little powdered ginger and mix well with the melted sugar. add all the egg yolk foam and blend well with sugar until it thickens like cream. spoon into dishes and serve. i refrain from writing many things i would, fearing to displease the readers, since knowledge is spread throughout the world, and everyone wants to be a master in such matters. praying the creator grants you a long and happy life.

title: Pour le premier seruice.
text: take a generous amount of butter, and place it on a wooden spit to roast. when it begins to warm, sprinkle it with powdered sugar and twice as much cinnamon as sugar, coating the roasting butter over the fire until it forms a thick crust then it will be ready. cut oranges into segments, and sprinkle them with sugar and cinnamon. place them on a grill over a low heat, and drizzle with melted butter until the sugar melts. then add more sugar and cinnamon, and butter, increasing the heat slightly. repeat this process until the oranges are glazed.

title:
Deuxiesme seruice. 
Pour potage.
text: make warm milk with egg yolks, candied sugar, and cinnamon, full of pine nuts, and put slices of marzipan bread into it.

title: Faisant rosty lardé d'orenges confites.
text: roasted partridges, generously basted with butter and black sauce, must be cooked well and served with brown bread called monstachalle. oysters, beef, and pistachio pastries.

title: Pour le troisiesme seruice.
text: white manchet pies, with may butter, and eat them with candied citron and sugar paste and be careful not to drink malvoisie or spanish wine without sugar.

title: Pour contrefaire maluoisie.
text: take one measure of rainwater, and heat it. then put in twenty-seven pounds of spanish honey, and put it into the water, and dissolve it well in the water, so that it is completely melted, and boil it well for an hour, and skim it well, and you will boil it with half a pound of coriander, and half a pound of grains of juniper or grains of pepper, and eight ounces of cinnamon, broken when boiled you will put it into a tub or a barrel, and leave it as it is for two days then make a hole in the barrel, or tub, three fingers from the bottom, and and draw out what is clear what remains inside the barrel must be passed through a cloth, as best you can, and put it into barrels, and keep it thus it is better after three years than the first year. note to know for

text: to make a fine tart. take good wheat flour, and egg yolks, and a little salt. mix them together with water, and make a good dough. then roll it out thinly, and line a tart pan with it. next, take good capons or hens, and cut them into pieces. season them with salt, pepper, and grains of paradise. then take onions, and cut them into slices. also, take good parsley, and cut it finely. put the meat into the tart pan, and lay the onions and parsley on top. then take good butter, and spread it over the tart. bake it in an oven until it is well cooked. serve it forth.

text: take almonds, wash them without scalding or plucking, and grind them. then have clear pea puree and large, beautiful crayfish, and cook both in two parts water and one part wine, and a pinch of vinegar, if you wish puree, and let cool. remove the feet and claws to one side and take them out of their shells. empty the bodies into a bowl, beat and grind very well like the almonds, and mix everything together with pea puree, wine, and verjuice. strain the mixture through a cloth. then take ginger, a pinch of cinnamon, a pinch of grains of paradise, and a pinch of cloves, a little less than the grains, and a pinch of long pepper. take the feet and claws of the crayfish and fry them in a little butter, until they are dry like fried eel. put to boil in a pan or a beautiful clean pot. add the spices with a little wine and verjuice, and add enough sugar. boil everything together and

title: UNG ROZÉ A CHAIR
text: take almonds without peeling and grind them very well, then take beef broth, wine, and verjuice, and after you have drained your almonds, strain them through a cloth. then take your meat, that is to say, veal breast and a whole fowl or in pieces which are cooked together with a beef shank or another good piece of meat. then fry your meat in lard until it is browned, then take fine cinnamon, not too much, white mace, and small spices such as grains of paradise, cloves, and long pepper. and to give color, you should have turmeric and orcanet and orcanet is also disabled like turmeric, which refines it, because it does not have such a vivid color as turmeric and it should be soaked in a little warm water for three or four hours, and after that, it should be thrown into its pot, and stirred very well, after the soup has boiled, and stir very well until it has a color similar to the

title: BROUET DE DAINTIERS DE CERF ET CERVOISONS
text: first, you must thoroughly scald and wash the venison haunches in boiling water, and cook them well, then cool them. afterwards, cut them into square pieces, neither too large nor too small, and fry them in lard, placing them in a paella dish. add beef broth to the dish, along with chopped parsley and a fine spice powder, ensuring it is not too strong. to give them flavor, use a little camelina oil, or take a chicken liver or two, and a little white bread, and soak them. place them in the pot in place of the camelina oil, and add a pinch of vinegar. make your spices with wine and verjuice, two parts verjuice and one-third wine, or, in place of verjuice, grapes and season properly with salt.

title: FLAONS COCHUS.
text: take cream and egg yolks well beaten, then put them into the cream. make larger dumplings than those usually made, and incorporate fine, white flour into them. then obtain large eels, about the size of a fist, and blanch and roast them very well, cutting them into pieces. place these pieces upright in the dumplings, three or four in each. sweeten them greatly when they are cooked, and let them cool.

title: DOREURES
text: a dish for a festive day or a prince s feast on the three days of the week sunday, tuesday, and thursday. for the apples and fowl for the apples, use raw pork, it matters not which, from which the fowl will be stuffed and it is fitting, after the fowl is killed, to break a skin flap from the head, and have a quill and blow into it until it is well filled with wind, and then scald them, and afterward, slit them open under the belly, and pluck them and set the ribs to one side. and it is fitting, to make the stuffing to stuff the fowl, use bread soaked, chopped with the meat, and add eggs, fine spice, pine nuts, and coriander, and stuff the skin of the fowl, but do not fill it too much lest it burst, then sew it up and it is fitting to boil it in a pan over the fire, and do not leave it too long to cook

title: COQZ HEAUMEZ
text: roast pork and poultry, such as capons and old hens. when the pork is roasted on one side and the poultry on the other, those who wish may stuff the poultry, without flaying it. it should be stuffed with beaten pastry and eggs. when it is golden, place it on top of the pork, like a rider. a paper helmet should be glued on and a lance stuck into the poultry's breast. cover them with gold or silver leaf for the lords, or with white tin leaf, vermilion, or green.

title: TOURTES PARMERIENNES
text: take mutton, veal, or pork, and chop it finely then you must have poultry, and boil it, and pluck it into quarters and you must cook the grain before it is chopped, then have fine powder and spice it very reasonably, and fry the grain in a skilled manner, and afterward, have large uncovered pastries, and let them be higher in pastry than other pastries and the size of small plates, made in a crenellated fashion, and let them be strong in pastry so that they can bear the grain and those who wish can mix pine nuts and coriander seeds with the grain, and sprinkle crushed sugar on top, and put three or four quarters of poultry in each pastry to display the banners of france and the lords who will be in the presence, and gild them with dissolved saffron to make them more beautiful. and those who do not want to spend so much on poultry need only make flat pieces of roast or boiled pork or mutton. and when they are filled with their

title: BLANC MENGER PARTY.
text: take scalded and peeled almonds, and grind them very finely, and thin them with boiled water. then, to make the binding agent to thicken them, you need beaten rice or starch. and when the milk has been boiled, it must be divided into several parts, into two pots, for those who want only two colors, and those who wish, into three or four parts. it must be very well thickened, as if it were kneaded wheat dough, so that it does not clump when it is drained or in the dish. then take orcainet, or turnesol, or asur fine, or parsley, or samandre, or a little saffron mixed with the greens, so that it holds its color better when boiled. it is also necessary to have pork blood and soak the orcainet or turnesol, and the azure likewise, in it. throw sugar into the milk as it boils, to draw it back, and salt it, and stir vigorously

title: LAYT LARDÉ
text: take milk and put it to boil over the fire, and have egg yolks beaten, then take the milk off the fire and put it on a bed of embers, and drizzle the yolks into it. if you want it to be meaty, take bacon and cut it into two or three pieces, and throw it with the boiling milk. if you want it to be fish, do not put in any bacon, but throw in wine and verjuice before it is taken off the fire, to make it curdle, then take it off the fire and put it in a white cloth, and let it drain, and wrap it in two or three folds of the cloth, and press it until it is firm like beef liver then put it on a table and slice it into strips like a palm or three fingers, and fasten them with cloves, then fry them until they are browned and arrange them, and sprinkle sugar on top.

title: TOURTES DE LAYT
text: take milk and put it to boil over a low charcoal fire, and have eggs interspersed, or all auburn, as one wishes, and when it boils, divide it into two bowls, then have parsley greens and stir with half of the eggs, and take wine and verjuice, and pour it in until it is well brushed, then let it cool until one can hold their hand in it, and have a linen cloth two feet long, then take a spoonful or two of the said milk, and wrap it two or three times within the cloth, then rub it with your hands well and firmly, and when it is taken and firm, remove it from the cloth let cool and prick two or three rows of cloves into it, and afterwards, fry them in oil until they are reddish-brown and they should be served with the milk streaked with bacon on a platter, half one way and half another.

title: BUIGNETZ ET ROYSOLLES DE MOUELLE CRESPES GRANDES ET PETITES
text: to make large crepes, use a syrup pot or a copper pan. for the smaller ones, use an iron pan prepare them with egg yolks and beaten flour, combining them together. have a hollow wooden bowl and some clarified butter, and place some of the batter in the bowl. don't make the batter too thick, and dip your hand in the pan over clarified butter, preventing them from browning too much. for small crepes, beat egg yolks and whites with flour, making the batter slightly thinner than that of the large crepes. use a low heat as long as the fire is hot, and have a wooden bowl with a pierced bottom. place batter in it, and when everything is ready, pour and shape into a small loop or a larger one, and through the loop, create a pattern with more batter. let them cook in clarified butter until they are round. if you want to make cheese-filled crepes, have good rennet cheese in large pieces

title: ALOUYAULX
text: take beef tripe or beef caul, and cut it into long, thick pieces like a man's fist, and rinse the beef tripe in hot water, just blanching and pulling. the caul should be cut more broadly. have a veal truss, and remove the meat from the bones as much as possible, and place it in thin casings, spreading the casings on a clean board. wrap the pieces of tripe in the veal casings, and add a little white salt and fine white powder. then, have a sturdy iron spit and skewer them. have some dough like that used for small crepes, and coat them with it, when they are well-cooked like those of tripe.

title: DYAPRÉ
text: proceed in the same manner as with the almonds and rosewater previously described, but do not give it such a strong color, and do not stir it as much in the pot as the rosewater. and add enough sugar properly, as much to this dish as to the other and it requires a generous amount of grain that has been fried in butter, just like the other.

title: TAILLÉ
text: take almonds, unpeeled, wash and grind very well, then take beef broth, wine, and verjuice, and once the almonds are broken, grind them very well. then add spices as for rose and diapre, except that there should be more cinnamon and cinnamomum and add a pinch of poultry and veal, and fry them in oil, and add enough sugar skillfully and let it be sweet with sugar.

title: A yours de poisson.
text: to change those potatoes for a fish day, and if one cannot find verjuice, use boiled water, and prepare the greens without peeling. then, for the potatoes themselves, have perch and small fish, and boil them until they can be plucked. then fry them in fresh butter, and use spices like saffron and rosewater, ginger, and cinnamon, and fewer spices. and if one does not have freshwater fish, take smelts, whiting, and flounders and add sugar generously, more than in the potatoes mentioned for meat days, and season them well with salt.

title: TAILLIZ DE KARESME
text: take almonds, and grind them very well in a mortar, then have boiled water and cooled to lukewarm, and after removing the almond skins, strain through a cloth, and boil your milk over a small charcoal fire. then take scalded prunes that are cooked from one or two days old, and chop them into small pieces like dice. then take figs, dates, and raisins of spain, and slice the said figs and dates, like the prunes, and then throw everything in, and let it steep like dough, and add sugar to boil with. it is necessary to put one or two onions to boil in the almond milk and to give it color, have saffron to color it like wheat, and let it be gently salted.

title: PASTEZ NOURROYS
text: take cooked meat, finely minced, pine nuts, currants, and grated cheese, and a pinch of sugar and a little salt. to make small pastries, like pastries for a white or bottom dish, and fry them, and let them not be too thick with pastry. and whoever wants to make lettuces and ears, must make pastry covers, some larger than others, and fry them in sweet pork fat until they are hard, like cooked in an oven and whoever wishes, can gild them with gold leaf or silver leaf, or with saffron.

title: HERISSONS ET POTZ D'ESPAIGNE
text: take raw meat, chop it as finely as possible, then add a bit of rhine sausage, crumbled rennet cheese, and mix all together with fine flour. then have mutton casings, scald and wash them very well, and not in too hot water so they don t shrink, and fill them with the chopped meat, and then sew them shut with a small skewer of rosemary. and whoever wants to make spanish patties, should take small clay pellets in the shape of little pieces of earth, and moisten them inside with egg yolk so that the filling holds better then fill them and boil them over the fire in a paella pan or cauldron and when they are well cooked, take them out and let them drain, and when they are cool, break the patties and do not take anything apart, then have skewers of small thorns, not too fine and make small balls, and put them on skewers in two or three rows. and then glaze them with pastry and flower.

title: ESPAULES DE MOUTON FARCIES MOTES ET MANGONNEAULX
text: put them to cook in a pan over the fire, and mutton and pork shanks, and let them not be overcooked, then let them cool. remove the meat from around the bones, and chop it finely, and the meat from the plums and turnips likewise. then have pine nuts and coriander seeds, and a large quantity of fried egg whites, then cut them into small pieces like dice, and be careful they are not burnt. then take all these ingredients and grated rennet cheese, and put everything in a clean pan or bowl, and mix very well. then you need mutton caul, and spread it over, and put fine flour with the bones inside without stuffing, then wrap the bones and stuff them, and then wrap them with the mutton caul and sew them with skewers of boythorn to hold the meat from falling around the shoulder, as those who know the manner well do. and for the turnips which are made in the form of small pies, and the plums as long as

title: CIGNES REVESTUZ DE LEUR PEAU
text: prepare the birds by singeing, skinning, and scalding them. before skinning, split them open from beneath the belly and remove the insides. then, roast the insides on a spit, browning them, turning them, and brushing them with a batter made from egg yolks, alder wood ash, and marrow mixed together. once removed from the spit and allowed to cool, they can be covered with their skin, if desired. it is fitting to have small skewers of reeds placed around the neck to keep it upright as if it were still alive this dish is suitable for a feast on the second day.

title: PAONS
text: to make them rise and swell like swans, and roast and brown them equally. they should be served as the final course. when they are dressed, one must have skewers of small rushes and kept to pass through the feathers of the tail, or a cord of bowstring to straighten the feathers as the peacock does its crest. to make the knight at the swan to his liking, one must have twelve pieces of light wood, of which the four that are straight should be stronger than the others, and assemble them all together, and nail them firmly. then, one must have lead as wide as a table three feet long and as wide, and it will require two or three tables of lead, and make it in the shape of a small chest that is about a foot deep, capable of holding two or three barrels of water, and make a small cradle of parchment glued where the image of the said knight at the swan will be placed. also, one needs the likeness of a small swan

title: UNE TOUR
text: to make a tower covered in dyed cloth, as if it were masonry, provide four windows to the four squares of the tower, and let there be something similar, like saracens and moors pretending to shoot at a wild man who would want to attack them. and to make the wild man, you need a handsome man, tall and straight, dressed in a cloth robe and stockings and soles all held together, and let the said robe be entirely covered in painted hemp. and in the tower, there must be the figure of a young gallant disguised as a wild child, and he should have balls of leather filled with stuffing or painted stones in the manner of stones to throw at the said wild man.

title: POUR FAIRE L'YMAGE SAINT GEORGE ET SA PUCELLE.
text: to make a large platform of pastry or light dough, like that used for pies, and fashion it into the likeness of a saddled and bridled horse, and the image of saint george upon that horse, and a dragon beneath the horse s feet, and the maiden who leads the said dragon bound with her sash around its neck.

title: POUR FAIRE L'YMAGE SAINCTE MARTHE
text: to make the image of saint martha, the dragon with its body turned to one side, and a golden chain tied around the dragon's neck, so that saint martha will hold it, as she conquered it. and this figure can be made by two people, if desired, or with a painting of any height and size one wishes.

title: ENTREMETZ PLUS LEGIERS
text: to make terraces of bread, shaped like a maiden seated on a terrace, which terrace should be covered with green and herbed tin foil, resembling green grass. and there should be a lion whose two front paws and the maiden's lap support it. one can make its mouth of tin, and its tongue of tin held in place, and its teeth of paper glued to said mouth, and put in camphor and a little cotton. and when one wishes to serve before the lords, put fire beneath it. and those who wish to make the likeness of a wolf, a bear, a donkey, a serpent, or some other beast, tame or wild, can be made similarly, each in its place. the pulse for a fat poulet. gather the fat of the poulet and the liver as well, and pass them through a sieve with beef broth, and soak a pinch of ginger with verjuice, and boil everything together in a pan, and bind it

title: POTAGES LYANS.
text: pork chaudin. cook in water and salt, then cut into pieces, fried in pork fat. take ginger, long pepper, saffron, and stale bread soaked in beef broth and cow's milk, strained through a cloth. take fresh juice, sour wine, and cook slightly in water, add to your soup just before serving add egg yolks and boil all together. pea cretonnée. pea purée from new peas, cooked until smooth, then mashed and fried in pork fat. add cow s milk and boil for a short time add crumbled white bread to the milk, then add ginger and saffron, dilute the milk, boil, and add cooked quail, quartered, fried in pork fat, boil, reduce, add a generous amount of eggs. new broad bean cretonnée. as with peas. poultry cretonnée. poultry purée cooked in wine

title: CHAPISTRE DE ROST.
text: porc rosty. in green broth some add onions in pastry, with green grain broth and fine powder. veau rosty. veal rosty should be boiled and larded served with cameline, in pastry, with fine powder and saffron. fraise de veau. veal fraise that one says is meat cut your veal finely, and let it be cooked, curled in the art, ground ginger, saffron and eggs well ground, strain the eggs over it while curling. mouton rosty. with fine salt, with cinnamon, or in green broth. chevreaux et aigneaulx. push in boiling water and pull them out quickly, put on the spit served with cameline. oyes. plucked geese dry, reworked in hot water, roasted without being larded served with garlic or sorrel. poules ro

title: VIANDES ET POTAGES DE CARESME.
text: to start with fish. cooked in water, in the evening, in oil refined almonds, from your broth, ginger taken, from your milk and beaten arranged over your grain when it is boiled. and for the sick, sugar is needed. green sauce. take white bread and put it to boil in sour wine, and then put it to cool. the most sovereign greenness is from wheat, the other, in default of wheat, is from sorrel or dock. and in the sauce of the meat, it is made similarly, but so that you put a little sage in it, and pass it through the sieve. and, if it is too sour, put in white wine, and put in ginger and pepper, and no other spices. oyster cive. cive of oysters, oysters scalded and washed very well, simmered and crisped in oil with onions, refined ginger, cinnamon, grains of paradise and saffron, taken pounded farl

title: POYSSONS D'EAUE DOULCE.
text: brochets, perch, barbels, carp, eels, shad, fresh all cooked in water and salt served with green sauce. salted shad, served with garlic. lamprey. lampreys cooked like lamprey in pastry and finely ground. cresme. scalded like an eel served with green sauce. sea pork. sea pork split along the back and placed on splints in water, taken wine and the fish water, refined ginger, cinnamon, grains of paradise, pepper, and a little saffron, boiled and not too yellow. gurnard and red mullet. gurnard and red mullet, cooked in water, or roasted on the grill, and split along the back served with cameline. fresh mackerel roasted on the grill, placed in fine salt or mustard. salmon. fresh salmon cooked in wine and water, served with cameline the salted with wine, and with

title: POISSON DE MER.
text: prepare sole, ray, turbot, or flounder cook in water, with wine and with green broth. serve soft-shelled clams in water, eaten with vinegar salted, with mustard or butter. fry cuttlefish and monkfish with onions, seasoned with fine powder.

title: SAULCES NON BOULLYES.
text: cameline, green sauce, and cameline herbs, white herbs, and fresh herbs of the hare. cold sauce. a cold sauce to keep with saltwater fish, ground bread, parsley, samphire, beaten with sour wine, ground ginger, cinnamon, pepper, galangal, grains of paradise, nutmeg, a little saffron, beaten with green juice, sour wine and strained, poured over your fish some add samphire to the root.

title: SAULCES BOULLYES.
text: black pepper. ground ginger, stale bread, wine dregs, sour juice, and green juice, strained and boiled some add seeds and galangal. yellow pepper. ground ginger, pepper, saffron, stale bread, wine dregs, and green juice, boiled some add seeds and galangal. poitevin sauce. poitevin sauce, ground seeds and leaves, mixed with wine and green juice, boiled, and with roast fat added, then poured over your roast in spoonfuls. jance. ground almonds, then refined with ginger, mace, and white bread, mixed with green juice and wine if desired, made with cow s milk and boiled when you wish to serve. green juice. take sorrel with all its seeds, mixed with other green juice, strained, and add a crust of bread inside so that it does not turn.

title: ESPICES APPARTENANTES A CE PRÉSENT VIANDIER.
text: ginger, cinnamon, cloves, paradise grains, pepper, mastic, galangal, nutmeg, saffron, cinnamon, sugar, ginger and fine powder. from the garland made at boys on the sea on the sixth day of june, 1455 by my lord of mayne, and my lady of chasteaubrun. first white and feathered pastries covered with violets and bouquets, amongst other pastries placed on said large pastries, a green ribbon between them, and these were silvered the wafers and gilded the tops, and, on each of them, 195 a silvered crenellated turret, and the top azure, and a banner with the arms of my said lord of mayne, and some with the other arms of my lady of villequier and my said lady of chasteaubrun and inside these pouches, cormorants, bust

title: BANCQUET DE MONSEIGNEUR DE FOYES.
text: first courses chicken with sugar, pike or rabbits in cream sauce, cold sauce, sour wine, venison in soup. second courses shoulders of goat, stuffed, sea fowl, breaded and armored, quail with sugar. third courses dolphins in cream sauce, flounders, turbots, pears, oranges, fried, jelly, pâtés of rabbit. fruit course white cream, and strawberries, strewn with, and almonds.

title: BANCQUET DE MONSEIGNEUR DE LA MARCHE
text: first. vinaigrette, creamed duck with cinnamon, venison with cloves. second course peacocks, guinea fowl, herons, snipes in a rich sauce, partridges with sugar. third course capons stuffed with cream, pies of onions, goat. fourth course eagles, pears in hippocras, golden flounders, jelly, watercress. fifth course cream, almonds, walnuts, hazelnuts, pears, sorrel.

title: BANCQUET DE MON SEIGNEUR D'ESTAMPES.
text: for the first course capons in cinnamon broth, hens with herbs, sow s udder, green beans with venison. second course roast the best, peacocks with celery, capon pies, larks in rosé sour wine, capons in must. third course partridges with trimmings. pigeons stewed. venison pies. jellies and creams. fourth course oven cakes, cream fritters. pear pies. sweetened almonds, walnuts and raw pears.

title: BANCQUET POUR MA DAMOYSELLE.
text: table setting popies, candied cherries or feathers, lemons. first course pastries for the hearth with sugar. pigeon pastries. venison with peas. boiled chickens. fresh venison in broth. second course roast. chicken pastries. quail pastries. venison, either as a side dish or for later. third course pigeons with sugar and sour wine. tarts with sugar. tremolectes with sugar. must. mutton banquet. fourth course tarts shaped like arms and dolphins. white jelly and other creamy fritters. pears with sugar. new almonds. for the first ham with sugar, chickens in cloth, strained broth, all chicken sweetened. second service signs with santarelle. peacocks. herons. venison. pockets of. foynes. third service chickens. pigeons. lapperaux. lesches.
